file.titolo: 10 AI PMP Practice Questions and Mindset

domande.domanda: ⚠️ A university's academic integrity office manually reviews flagged essays. The dean proposes licensing an AI detection service to assist the reviewers, worried that some cases are being missed. What should the project manager do first? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript; answer letter inferred from the commentary.

opzioni.A: Pilot the AI service on last semester's essays and compare its judgments with the reviewers' decisions.
opzioni.B: Verify that the risk management plan covers essay review.
opzioni.C: Analyze how often the reviewers make mistakes and what damage would result.
opzioni.D: Evaluate the detection accuracy of the service.

domande.hint: Even though it mentions AI, this is a general PM question: someone wants a solution. Before choosing a tool, understand what is actually happening.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. A pilot means installing the whole system before you know whether the problem exists and how big it is.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The risk management plan does not hold these risks and is not the starting point.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Analyze the problem first (frequency and impact of errors); only then evaluate whether AI is the right solution.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Evaluating the tool starts from the solution instead of the problem.

domande.nota: Answer C inferred from the commentary ('See best answer' = C); option text reconstructed from the transcript.
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript; answer letter inferred from the commentary

domande.domanda: A credit union has finished assessing which member services could benefit from an AI fraud-detection system. The project manager realizes that no one on staff has ever built or run a machine learning model. What should the project manager do next?

opzioni.A: Propose outsourcing the model development to a specialist firm.
opzioni.B: Enroll the current analysts in an intensive machine learning bootcamp.
opzioni.C: Hire a senior project manager with experience delivering AI projects.
opzioni.D: Convene the stakeholders and decide which service to protect first.

domande.hint: If the organization lacks the skills to build the system, who can build it? Also note 'next': the assessment is already done.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. The skills are not available internally, so development goes to someone who has them.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. A single bootcamp will not make the analysts able to build a whole system.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. A senior project manager is not the person who builds the system.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The assessment is already complete: the open issue is how to build the system.

domande.domanda: While developing an AI tool for screening rental applications, the legislature announces a law on automated decision-making that will regulate how such tools work. What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Suspend development until the law takes effect.
opzioni.B: Have a compliance specialist assess what the law would require.
opzioni.C: Update the risk register and the scope to comply with the law.
opzioni.D: Inform the sponsor about the law and review the remaining budget.

domande.hint: Don't wait: build compliance into the project. But first you need to know exactly what the law requires.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. You don't wait: compliance must be built into the project.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. First understand what the law requires: the tool will have to comply.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. This is a later step: assess the impact first, then update the risk register and scope.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. This also comes after the compliance assessment (order: B, then D, then C).

domande.domanda: A construction company adopting a new modular building method wants an AI model that predicts site safety incidents on upcoming projects. The team must choose the training data. Which data should the team use?

opzioni.A: All incident records the company holds, to maximize the sample.
opzioni.B: Records from recently completed projects.
opzioni.C: Synthetic incident data generated to enlarge and balance the sample.
opzioni.D: Records from past projects whose methods and conditions resemble modular construction.

domande.hint: You need plenty of data, but above all data as relevant as possible to this type of project.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Incidents from completely different projects don't help the model.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Recent does not mean similar: relevance matters more than recency.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Synthetic data is generic and doesn't represent the real context.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Data from projects with similar methods and conditions gives the model something concrete to learn from.

domande.domanda: ⚠️ An AI routing model has cut a carrier's fuel spend for two quarters when a veteran operations manager objects to depending on it. How should the project manager respond? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript; answer letter inferred from the commentary.

opzioni.A: Put the model in shadow mode, letting dispatchers route manually until the manager is satisfied.
opzioni.B: Meet with the manager, review the model's results together and keep it in service.
opzioni.C: Present the fuel savings to the client and keep using it.
opzioni.D: Log the objection and proceed as planned.

domande.hint: The model has worked for six months. Which answer directly addresses the concern of the person objecting?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Switching off a model that works is excessive.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Engage the manager directly, review the results together and keep the model running.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. It does not address the manager's concern.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. It ignores the objection instead of handling it.

domande.nota: Option D reconstructed (unclear transcript); answer B inferred from the commentary.
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript; answer letter inferred from the commentary

domande.domanda: A language-learning app's backlog includes a custom pronunciation-scoring feature planned a year ago. A developer notes that new off-the-shelf AI speech models do the same job, probably making the item obsolete. What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Bring the observation to the product owner to decide on the item's remaining value.
opzioni.B: Run a short technical spike comparing a new model with the planned feature.
opzioni.C: Have the team vote on whether the item stays in the backlog.
opzioni.D: Ask the sponsor whether the feature should be dropped from the plan.

domande.hint: Who has the authority to add, remove and prioritize product backlog items?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Only the product owner decides what stays in or leaves the backlog.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The developer has effectively already done this analysis with the observation.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The team does not vote on backlog content.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Deciding backlog content is the product owner's job, not the sponsor's.

domande.domanda: ⚠️ Six weeks after launching a licensed AI demand forecaster, chosen by the team from three vendors, a regional director publicly questions why the company didn't fine-tune its own model to avoid recurring fees. What should the project manager do? — ⚠️ Note: answer letter inferred from the commentary.

opzioni.A: Have the team estimate the cost of an in-house implementation over three years.
opzioni.B: Invite the vendor to present the solution to the director.
opzioni.C: Open a change request to evaluate migrating.
opzioni.D: Go back to the documented requirements and verify that the chosen solution meets them.

domande.hint: The choice was already made by the team. What is the first objective reference for answering criticism of that choice?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. It's a lot of work and premature.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. It doesn't answer whether the choice meets the requirements.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. There is no reason yet to open a change request.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Check the choice against the original requirements: licensing may well have been a requirement.

domande.nota: The answer letter is not spoken in the transcript: D inferred from the commentary ('I would do this first').
domande.motivo_incertezza: answer letter inferred from the commentary

domande.domanda: ⚠️ An external firm is building a customer-service chatbot as a minimum viable product (MVP) over a fixed number of sprints, with payments tied to accepted work. Which set of metrics should the project manager track? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Compute hours consumed and sprints completed.
opzioni.B: The vendor's reported model accuracy scores and the number of iterations in progress.
opzioni.C: Chatbot features accepted and delivered, deliverables rejected and defects found.
opzioni.D: Vendor staffing levels and budget consumed.

domande.hint: With payments tied to accepted work, what matters is value delivered and accepted, not effort spent.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. These only show resource usage, not value delivered.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Vendor-reported figures and iterations in progress are not delivered value.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Accepted features, rejected deliverables and defects measure real value (similar to story points completed per sprint).
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Staffing and budget don't tell you whether work is being delivered and accepted.

domande.nota: Options reconstructed from a fragmented transcript (especially C).
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: ⚠️ A claims department releases the first increment of an AI triage assistant and finds that most adjusters cannot judge when to trust the AI's recommendation and when to override it. What should the project manager do? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Simplify the assistant's interface in the next iteration so it requires less judgment.
opzioni.B: Define the adjusters' training needs and bring this enablement into the project scope.
opzioni.C: Ask Human Resources to run an AI awareness workshop.
opzioni.D: Publish a decision guide describing when to accept or override the recommendation.

domande.hint: The problem isn't that the tool is hard to use, it's that people don't know how much to trust it. Real training is needed, not a sheet of paper.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The problem is not interface complexity.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Proper training and enablement are needed, included in the project scope.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Handing it all to HR means giving away your own work.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. A guide can't cover every scenario (individuals and interactions over comprehensive documentation). Trap question: many pick D.

domande.nota: Option A reconstructed (the transcript reads 'Satisfy the assistant?').
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: On an AI résumé-ranking project in closing, the project manager notes that the team spent weeks of unplanned work on retroactive bias testing, because fairness requirements were not defined at initiation and only surfaced when a client audit flagged skewed results. What should the project manager do to prevent this in the future?

opzioni.A: Require the responsible-AI committee's involvement at the start of every future project.
opzioni.B: Hold a retrospective on why the fairness requirements were missed and update the organizational process assets.
opzioni.C: Add mandatory bias training to the definition of done for all AI deliverables.
opzioni.D: Launch a bias awareness program for all project teams.

domande.hint: At its core this is a missing-requirements problem, not an AI problem. You don't know what future projects will look like: pick the most generic answer that works for all of them.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. It's too AI-specific and imposes a rule on every future project.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. A retrospective on the lesson learned plus updating the organizational process assets (OPAs) applies to every project.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Bias training doesn't fix the missing-requirements problem.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Like C, it's generic training that doesn't address the cause.

domande.domanda: The client expressed concern about the extended timeline for a mobile application project and asked the development team to minimize the number of sprint cycles needed to deliver a usable product. What approach should the project manager take?

opzioni.A: Direct the team to identify and escalate obstacles during the daily stand-up meeting.
opzioni.B: Focus sprint planning on high-risk features to compress the overall iteration count.
opzioni.C: Request the team re-estimate user stories to accelerate the delivery schedule.
opzioni.D: Have the product owner sequence deliverables by business value and establish frequent incremental releases.

domande.hint: How does agile deliver value? Think about the order in which work is done and how often you release.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The daily stand-up only answers three questions (done, doing, blockers); it is not for fixing obstacles and won't reduce the number of sprints.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Features are sequenced by value, not by risk: focusing on high-risk items doesn't compress the iteration count.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Asking for re-estimates shows a lack of trust in the team and is not servant leadership; lower estimates don't change what can be delivered.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. The product owner sequences deliverables by business value and the team releases frequent increments, so the client gets a usable product sooner (an agile principle).

domande.domanda: A project manager receives notice from the primary supplier that new regulatory changes will cause a raw material shortage affecting upcoming project deliverables. What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Consult the legal department about enforcing contractual penalties for non-delivery.
opzioni.B: Identify alternative suppliers capable of meeting the project timeline.
opzioni.C: Remind the supplier of their contractual obligation.
opzioni.D: Evaluate how the raw material shortage will impact the project schedule.

domande.hint: Before acting on the supplier or the contract, what do you need to know?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Penalties are never the first move, and the regulatory change may even void the contractual obligation.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Looking for other suppliers is premature: you don't yet know how much the shortage affects the project.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Reminding the supplier of its obligations doesn't help: the shortage is caused by a regulation, and a contract can't require something against the law.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. First evaluate the impact on the schedule; only then involve legal or the vendor if needed.

domande.domanda: A project manager is finalizing the project management plan and preparing to establish the first approved baseline. Before formal approval, a functional manager submits a request to modify resource allocation and add two deliverables to the project scope. What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Submit the request to the Change Control Board for formal approval.
opzioni.B: Conduct an impact analysis of how the request would affect schedule, cost and scope.
opzioni.C: Decline the request.
opzioni.D: Meet with the functional manager to discuss the request and assess the implications.

domande.hint: The baseline is not approved yet: what isn't needed yet, and what must you understand first?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The baseline isn't approved yet, so the Change Control Board is not involved. Once approved, this would be a decent option.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Analyze how the request affects schedule, cost and scope first, then discuss the results with the requester.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The PM generally has no authority to simply decline a request; never pick 'decline' on the exam.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Decent, but you already know what they want: assess the impact first (B), then go back and discuss it.

domande.domanda: ⚠️ Five changes came to the team's attention during the execution phase and the team cannot agree on how to implement them. How should the project manager handle the situation? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript; answer letter inferred from the commentary.

opzioni.A: Schedule a discussion with the project sponsor to solve the problem.
opzioni.B: Organize a meeting with the team members to review the issue and implement the changes.
opzioni.C: Ensure that all team members and stakeholders understand the change management plan and stick to it.
opzioni.D: Confirm that all required changes are applied to the project and communicate it.

domande.hint: 'Execution phase' signals a traditional project: which document governs changes?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The sponsor hired you to manage project problems, not to solve them for you.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Reviewing the issue is fine, but the team and PM don't decide to implement changes: that bypasses change control.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. On a predictive project changes follow the change management plan (request, assessment, approval).
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Applying all changes without assessment and approval bypasses the sponsor/Change Control Board.

domande.nota: Answer C inferred from 'Follow the change management plan'; text of option B reconstructed.
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript; answer letter inferred from the commentary

domande.domanda: A development team encounters a critical third-party API integration issue that blocks current sprint work. The team identified integration risks during planning but now faces implementation challenges it cannot resolve independently. What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Defer the integration work to the subsequent sprint.
opzioni.B: Facilitate a team session to explore potential solutions.
opzioni.C: Contact the third-party vendor's technical support team.
opzioni.D: Notify the project sponsor of the integration blocker.

domande.hint: Servant leadership: who is best placed to solve a technical problem?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Deferring to the next sprint is kicking the can down the road; fix problems now.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Bring the team together to explore solutions: the team solves problems, the PM facilitates.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Contacting vendor support yourself means choosing the solution independently of the team.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Telling the sponsor doesn't solve the blocker: it's your job (with the team) to solve problems.

domande.domanda: On a distributed project team with daily stand-ups and frequent stakeholder calls, the project manager notices declining participation and limited interaction among team members during virtual sessions. What should the project manager do to address the disengagement?

opzioni.A: Consolidate meetings into fewer, longer sessions to reduce calendar burden.
opzioni.B: Conduct individual conversations with team members and organize team-building activities.
opzioni.C: Redistribute project tasks to balance workloads across the team.
opzioni.D: Authorize a temporary break from sprint work to allow recovery time.

domande.hint: Before changing how work is organized, find out why people disengaged.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Fewer but longer meetings will lead to even more disengagement.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Talking to people individually and running team-building addresses the cause and rebuilds the team.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. On an agile project the team decides who does what, and redistributing work doesn't address the cause.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The team decides when it needs a break; the PM doesn't authorize it and the cause remains.

domande.domanda: A transit authority is developing a new rail system. Six months into construction, the project faces significant delays after inspectors identified multiple violations of local environmental protection ordinances. What should the project manager have done to prevent this situation?

opzioni.A: Hire a dedicated environmental compliance specialist reporting directly to the project manager.
opzioni.B: Request regulatory exemptions given the project's environmental benefits.
opzioni.C: Add schedule buffers based on environmental delay patterns from similar projects.
opzioni.D: Identify all environmental requirements, assess compliance risk and develop mitigation strategies.

domande.hint: 'Should have done' means prevention: before it was an issue, it was a risk.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. A specialist could help, but that person should have helped you do D; it's not the prevention itself.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Requesting exemptions doesn't prevent violations; you must follow the law.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Schedule buffers only absorb delays, they don't prevent the violations.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Know the law before you start: identify the requirements, assess the compliance risk and plan mitigations.

domande.domanda: ⚠️ A manufacturing facility upgrade project has acceptance criteria requiring in-person validation testing with production line operators. Suddenly, government health restrictions prohibit non-essential personnel from entering the facility for the next two months. What should the project manager do? — ⚠️ Note: debatable: the instructor sees more than one valid answer.

opzioni.A: Document the constraint and present alternative approaches to stakeholders.
opzioni.B: Convert the in-person validation sessions to remote video demonstrations.
opzioni.C: Log this as a project risk and develop a contingency plan.
opzioni.D: Remove the validation requirement.

domande.hint: The event has already happened: is it a risk or an issue? And who must approve a change to acceptance criteria?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Document the constraint, look for alternatives and inform the stakeholders. Not perfect, but the best of the four.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Changing how validation is done changes the acceptance criteria and needs approval.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The restriction has already happened, so it is an issue, not a risk.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. In-person validation is required: removing it changes the acceptance criteria without approval.

domande.nota: The instructor calls A 'not the greatest answer, but the best of these four'.
domande.motivo_incertezza: debatable: the instructor sees more than one valid answer

domande.domanda: A project manager oversees a fast-paced software implementation project with multiple planned releases. A developer mentions that several clients are unhappy with features delivered in the last release: they find some functions difficult to use and not fully supporting their business processes. More releases are planned in the coming months. What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Clarify team responsibilities to reduce confusion during future development activities.
opzioni.B: Gather feedback from stakeholders and review their concerns with the team for better understanding.
opzioni.C: Notify the team about the complaints and proceed with the current release roadmap.
opzioni.D: Log the concern in the project records and address it after the remaining releases are complete.

domande.hint: Planned releases signal an agile project. Is the problem with the team or with the clients?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The problem is not role confusion in the team, it's client dissatisfaction.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Gather stakeholder feedback and review it with the team to understand and fix it.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Informing the team and proceeding ignores the complaints.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Postponing until after the releases means never fixing the problem; be proactive.

domande.domanda: A project manager supports an agile team during a backlog prioritization session. A compliance department representative disagrees with the product owner about the priority of a backlog item: the product owner believes other features deliver more business value, while the compliance representative insists the item is required to meet upcoming regulatory standards. What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Support the product owner's authority over backlog prioritization and advise the compliance representative to accept the decision.
opzioni.B: Review historical project records and apply a similar prioritization approach.
opzioni.C: Persuade the product owner to reprioritize the backlog item based on the compliance representative's request.
opzioni.D: Facilitate a discussion between the product owner and the compliance representative to understand both concerns.

domande.hint: The PM is a servant leader: rather than deciding, facilitate.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Technically right on authority, but it forces the outcome and ignores the compliance concern.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Reviewing historical records doesn't address this specific disagreement; only the product owner prioritizes.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. 'Persuade' means pushing people; it's not the PM's job and doesn't resolve the disagreement.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Facilitate a discussion between the product owner and the compliance representative so both concerns are understood.

domande.domanda: A newly assigned project manager discovers that a critical software implementation project lacks essential technical expertise in cloud architecture. The missing skills are causing delays in infrastructure design and deployment planning. What should the project manager do first?

opzioni.A: Identify internal employees with cloud architect expertise who could join the team.
opzioni.B: Distribute the cloud architect tasks among current team members.
opzioni.C: Approve budget expenditure to hire external cloud architect consultants.
opzioni.D: Submit a budget request for cloud architect certification training for current team members.

domande.hint: Which action is the least drastic one to do first?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Look for people with the skill inside the organization first: the least drastic step.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The team lacks the skill, so redistributing the tasks makes no sense.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. A PM can't simply approve spending, and external consultants are costly.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. You first need to know how much and what training is needed, and training takes time.

domande.domanda: A project manager leads a project with team members distributed across four countries. New government regulations suddenly prohibit international business travel for an indefinite period, affecting face-to-face collaboration sessions and design reviews. What should the project manager do next?

opzioni.A: Suspend all project activities until international travel restrictions are lifted.
opzioni.B: Request guidance from the sponsor.
opzioni.C: Direct the team to continue work independently while evaluating collaboration alternatives.
opzioni.D: Stop work indefinitely until virtual collaboration tools are procured and deployed.

domande.hint: Stopping a project is only justified for illegality or safety risks: that's not the case here.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Suspending everything isn't justified by a travel ban.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Asking the sponsor for guidance means giving away your problem.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. The team keeps working while you evaluate collaboration alternatives.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Stopping work indefinitely isn't justified.

domande.domanda: The project manager has received sponsor approval for the project charter and is now meeting with the team to break down deliverables into smaller, manageable components for planning and execution. What technique is the project manager using?

opzioni.A: Resource leveling
opzioni.B: Work breakdown structure
opzioni.C: Decomposition
opzioni.D: Network diagram

domande.hint: Is the answer a technique, or an output/input of planning?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Resource leveling makes sure no resource is over-allocated; it levels the schedule, it doesn't break down deliverables.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The WBS is the output where the decomposed work packages are stored, not the technique itself.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Breaking deliverables into smaller work packages is decomposition.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. A network diagram is an output/input showing activity dependencies, not a technique for breaking down work.

domande.spiegazione: Breaking deliverables down into work packages is decomposition. The WBS and network diagram are outputs/inputs, not techniques; resource leveling ensures no resource is over-allocated.

domande.domanda: A financial services company is restructuring its project management approach across all departments. Leadership is considering implementing agile methodologies to replace traditional waterfall processes. What is the primary reason for adopting agile project delivery?

opzioni.A: Projects will be completed faster, reducing overall delivery timelines.
opzioni.B: Projects will be delivered with minimal organizational risk exposure.
opzioni.C: Projects will deliver incremental value early, based on prioritized features.
opzioni.D: Projects will achieve significant cost reduction through optimized resources.

domande.hint: Which statement is always true of agile, not just 'sometimes'?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not necessarily: agile doesn't guarantee shorter overall timelines.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Not necessarily: agile doesn't guarantee minimal risk exposure.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. With a product owner and a value-ordered backlog, value is delivered early and incrementally.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Not necessarily: cost reduction isn't the primary reason for agile.

domande.spiegazione: With a product owner and a value-prioritized backlog, value is delivered early and incrementally. The other three are not necessarily true.

domande.domanda: A remote software development team reports that the current video conferencing and document sharing platform creates frequent connectivity issues and hinders real-time collaboration. What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Adopt the communication platform currently used by other project teams.
opzioni.B: Escalate the tool selection decision to the sponsor.
opzioni.C: Direct the team to continue using the existing tools.
opzioni.D: Facilitate a team discussion to evaluate and select the appropriate tools.

domande.hint: The team knows best what works for it: what is the PM's role?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Another team's tool may not suit this team.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The sponsor is there for approvals, not to pick the team's tools.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The team is reporting connectivity problems; staying on the tools ignores them.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Facilitate a team discussion so the team evaluates and selects the right tools.

domande.spiegazione: Work with the team to solve the problem: the team knows best what works for its project. Don't impose another team's tool, don't send it to the sponsor, don't ignore the problem.

domande.domanda: A Scrum team is on its first major project after adopting agile. A conflict has developed between a developer and a QA team member about testing approaches, and sprint velocity has dropped. What should the PM do?

opzioni.A: Facilitate individual meetings with each member to understand their perspective and guide them toward resolution.
opzioni.B: Bring the team members together to facilitate problem solving and establish working agreements.
opzioni.C: Analyze the conflict's cause and help the members understand the impact on team performance.
opzioni.D: Schedule the conflict discussion for the next retrospective.

domande.hint: Two people are in conflict and it hurts velocity: which answer actually resolves it now?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Decent (you find the root cause), but bringing them together to agree is better.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Bring the two together, facilitate problem solving and set working agreements so they can work together.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Analyzing the cause and pointing out the impact doesn't resolve the conflict.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Waiting for the retrospective kicks the can down the road.

domande.spiegazione: Bring them together to solve the problem and agree on working agreements. A is decent but B is better; C only analyzes; D kicks the can down the road.

domande.domanda: A project manager notices that team members frequently wait hours for approval on routine technical decisions. The project manager's calendar is filled with stakeholder meetings, creating bottlenecks when team members need authorization to proceed. What should the project manager do to prevent these delays?

opzioni.A: Schedule a biweekly session to address all pending team decisions.
opzioni.B: Analyze workflow data to identify the root causes of decision delays.
opzioni.C: Empower team members with authority to make certain decisions independently.
opzioni.D: Centralize all decision making to maintain consistent project direction.

domande.hint: Beware of answers that set a fixed frequency. Is the root cause already known?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. You can't know whether biweekly is enough; avoid answers with a fixed frequency.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Decent, but the root cause is already known: people wait for the PM's approval.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Routine technical decisions are best made by team members: empower them to decide.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Centralizing decisions keeps the bottleneck you already have.

domande.spiegazione: The root cause is already known (people wait for the PM), so B is already done; technical decisions are best made by team members. Avoid answers that fix a frequency (biweekly): you can't know it's enough. D keeps the bottleneck.

domande.domanda: ⚠️ Your project is behind schedule: only 55% complete against an expected 70%. The total project budget is 210,000 and the actual cost is 162,000. What are the SPI and CPI of this project? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: SPI 0.79 and CPI 0.71
opzioni.B: SPI 0.71 and CPI 0.79
opzioni.C: SPI 1.27 and CPI 1.40
opzioni.D: SPI 0.79 and CPI 1.29

domande.hint: EV = % complete x BAC; PV = % planned x BAC. SPI = EV/PV, CPI = EV/AC.

spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The values are swapped: SPI is EV/PV (0.79) and CPI is EV/AC (0.71).
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Values above 1 come from inverting the formulas (PV/EV, AC/EV); the project is behind and over budget, so both indexes are below 1.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. SPI is right but CPI is wrong: EV (115,500) is less than AC (162,000), so CPI must be below 1.

domande.spiegazione: EV = 55% x 210,000 = 115,500; PV = 70% x 210,000 = 147,000; AC = 162,000. SPI = EV/PV = 0.79 (about 21% behind schedule); CPI = EV/AC = 0.71 (about 29% over budget). Above 1 is good, below 1 is bad.
domande.nota: Options B, C and D are not read in the source video: they were written as plausible distractors (common calculation mistakes). Answer A is from the source.
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: A project team has been working together for about a month. During daily stand-ups, one team member repeatedly mentions having difficulty completing assigned work. What should the PM do?

opzioni.A: Allow the team more time to self-organize and resolve the issue without intervention.
opzioni.B: Assign the unfinished work to a more experienced team member.
opzioni.C: Meet privately with the team member to understand the root cause of the difficulty.
opzioni.D: Facilitate a team discussion to identify ways the group can support the team member.

domande.hint: It's one person's problem, not the whole team's.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Self-organization is good in general, but the problem concerns one member, not the team.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. On an agile project the PM doesn't assign work; the team does.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. With a one-person problem, meet privately with that person to understand the root cause.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Good, but before involving the whole team, try to resolve it with the individual.

domande.spiegazione: It's one person, so resolve it with that person first. A is good in general but not here since the problem isn't the whole team; the PM doesn't assign work on an agile project; D comes before you know whether it's needed.

domande.domanda: ⚠️ A project team is working with an overseas development group to build a software solution. During a status review, the project manager notices schedule delays caused by rework. The rework happens because the development team and the client have different understandings of the client's requirements. What should the PM do? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Arrange a meeting with the PMO to clarify the requirements.
opzioni.B: Escalate the issue to the project steering committee and request a schedule extension.
opzioni.C: Visit the development team's location to pressure them.
opzioni.D: Work with the development team to create prototypes and validate the requirements.

domande.hint: The rework comes from different understandings of requirements: how do you validate them before building?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Meeting is good, but the PMO didn't provide the requirements; the client did.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. You might need an extension later, but solve the problem now and don't give it away.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Visiting is fine, but never pressure people.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Validate requirements before building, e.g. with prototypes or demos the client can confirm.

domande.spiegazione: Validate requirements before building, e.g. with prototypes or demos. The PMO didn't give the requirements; don't give away your problem; never pressure people.
domande.nota: Option B reconstructed from a fragmented transcript.
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: A project manager is assigned to lead the implementation of a new system. Early in the project, the stakeholders have conflicting views of the project's goals and the best ways to complete the work. What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Develop a roles and responsibilities matrix from the charter and ask the sponsor to distribute it to stakeholders for authority.
opzioni.B: Hold scope workshops with the project team to create the WBS, assign the work and instruct the team to follow the schedule.
opzioni.C: Meet with each stakeholder to review their assigned activities and expectations.
opzioni.D: Analyze the disagreement to determine the root cause, then work with each group to clarify their specific roles and responsibilities.

domande.hint: Always analyze the problem before solving it.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. A RACI could help, but handing it to the sponsor doesn't address the conflicting views.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Building the WBS with the team doesn't solve the stakeholders' disagreement.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Reviewing assigned activities doesn't resolve the conflicting views.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Analyze the disagreement to find the root cause, then clarify each group's roles and responsibilities.

domande.spiegazione: Always analyze the problem before solving it. A, B and C take action first without getting to the root cause of the conflicting views.

domande.domanda: A project manager has just started a new project and needs to make sure team members and stakeholders are properly prepared. The project manager finds that the resources have agile experience, but it comes from different agile methods and practices. What should the PM do?

opzioni.A: Make sure the team understands every agile technique.
opzioni.B: Avoid training because the team already has experience.
opzioni.C: Build a shared understanding of agile principles and how they will be used.
opzioni.D: Provide training on one specific agile method.

domande.hint: The answer is in the question: they have agile experience, but from different methods.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The team doesn't need every agile technique; not all will be used.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. You can't assume their experience fits this project; if training is needed, provide it.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Agile principles define agile: build a shared understanding of them and how this project will use them.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Training is good, but one specific method is too narrow; principles matter more.

domande.spiegazione: Agile principles are what define agile, so a shared understanding of them (and of how the project will use them) is best. Not every technique will be used; you can't assume experience; one specific method is too narrow.

domande.domanda: A project manager is leading a new project expected to deliver a product by the end of the year. The vendor informs the project manager that a critical component will not be delivered on time, creating a potential schedule delay. What should the project manager do next?

opzioni.A: Meet with all stakeholders and request approval to extend the deadline.
opzioni.B: Terminate the vendor and select another vendor.
opzioni.C: Add the vendor delay to the next status meeting.
opzioni.D: Record the issue in the issue log and evaluate substitute components.

domande.hint: The component will NOT be delivered on time: is that a risk or an issue?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. You don't yet know the impact; don't ask for an extension first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. 'First/next' is never a drastic action like terminating the vendor.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Informing stakeholders isn't bad, but it doesn't solve anything.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. The late delivery is certain, so it's an issue: log it and look for substitute components.

domande.spiegazione: The delay is certain, so it's an issue (not a risk): log it and look for substitutes. Don't request an extension without knowing the impact; 'first/next' is never a drastic action like firing the vendor; C only informs.

domande.domanda: ⚠️ A project manager is trying to obtain final acceptance for several completed deliverables. One stakeholder is refusing to approve them for reasons that do not appear to be part of the agreed acceptance criteria. What should the project manager do? — ⚠️ Note: debatable: the instructor sees more than one valid answer.

opzioni.A: Use emotional intelligence and negotiation skills to persuade the stakeholder to approve.
opzioni.B: Seek approval from another stakeholder who understands the project deliverables.
opzioni.C: Escalate the issue to the sponsor and request assistance in obtaining the stakeholder's acceptance.
opzioni.D: Document the stakeholder's concern in an acceptance waiver and address it after closure.

domande.hint: You're not looking for the perfect answer, but the best of the four.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Persuading means pushing the stakeholder to accept something they don't want.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Going to someone else ignores the stakeholder; never ignore people.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Not ideal (ideally you'd understand the objection first), but the sponsor, who pays, decides acceptance and can help.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Closing first and fixing later ignores the stakeholder.

domande.spiegazione: Not the ideal answer (ideally you'd understand why the stakeholder objects) but the best of the four: the sponsor, who pays, can help. Don't push people to accept (A), ignore the stakeholder (B) or close first and fix later (D).
domande.nota: The instructor: 'not the best answer in absolute terms, but the best of these four'.
domande.motivo_incertezza: debatable: the instructor sees more than one valid answer

domande.domanda: A project sponsor requests that a new high-value feature be added late in an agile project. The current sprint is already committed and the backlog is full. What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Work with the product owner to prioritize the feature in the backlog.
opzioni.B: Add the feature to the sprint.
opzioni.C: Reject the request.
opzioni.D: Start a new parallel sprint.

domande.hint: Who adds and prioritizes items in the product backlog?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. New features go to the product owner, who adds and prioritizes them in the backlog.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The PM doesn't add work to a committed sprint.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. A PM never simply rejects a request, agile or predictive.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. You don't build a new parallel team/sprint for one feature.

domande.spiegazione: Additions go through the product owner, who adds and prioritizes backlog items. The PM doesn't add work to a committed sprint, never simply rejects a request, and doesn't build a new team for one feature.

domande.domanda: A project manager takes over a project in execution and finds that the team and the customers disagree about whether several delivered features are actually complete, causing repeated rework. What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Establish acceptance criteria with the customers for the remaining features.
opzioni.B: Facilitate an agreement between the team and the customers on a definition of done.
opzioni.C: Review the requirements document and determine which side is correct.
opzioni.D: Implement a formal sign-off step at the end of each feature's development.

domande.hint: Fix the whole problem, not just what lies ahead.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Good, but it only covers the remaining features while previous ones are still being reworked.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. A shared definition of done between team and customers resolves the disagreement on all features.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. It's not a contest about who is right.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. A sign-off at the end is reactive; you need to fix this proactively.

domande.spiegazione: A is good but only covers the remaining features, while the previous features are still being reworked: fix everything, not just what's ahead. It isn't about who is right (C), and D is reactive rather than proactive.

domande.domanda: A stakeholder previously assessed as low interest and low influence has begun requesting frequent detailed updates and pushing for changes to deliverables. What should the project manager do first?

opzioni.A: Update the stakeholder register and revise the engagement approach for the stakeholder.
opzioni.B: Meet with the stakeholder to understand the reason behind their increased involvement.
opzioni.C: Provide the requested updates while maintaining the existing engagement plan.
opzioni.D: Confirm with the sponsor whether the stakeholder's role has formally changed.

domande.hint: Both A and B are good: the keyword 'first' decides.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Right, but second: update the register after understanding why the stakeholder changed.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. First meet the stakeholder to understand the increased involvement, then update the register and engagement plan.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The stakeholder has clearly changed; keeping the existing plan ignores that.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Don't go to the sponsor for help; engage the stakeholder directly.

domande.spiegazione: A and B are both good, but 'first' decides: meet the stakeholder to understand why, then update the register and engagement plan (B, then A). C ignores the change; don't go to the sponsor for help.

domande.domanda: In a retrospective, the team concludes that ambiguous customer requirements are causing most of the rework. The customer is available but rarely engaged during development. What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Schedule regular backlog refinement sessions that include the customer.
opzioni.B: Increase the customer's participation in sprint reviews to gather feedback earlier.
opzioni.C: Ask the product owner to clarify requirements before they reach the team.
opzioni.D: Add explicit acceptance criteria to each backlog item before development starts.

domande.hint: Solve exactly the problem stated: ambiguous requirements because the customer is rarely engaged.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Including the customer in regular refinement sessions solves the engagement problem before the work is built.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Sprint reviews happen after the work is built: too late.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The customer, not the product owner, is the best person to say what's right.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. If requirements are ambiguous, the acceptance criteria will be too.

domande.spiegazione: Answer what the question asks: the problem is the customer's lack of engagement, and refinement sessions engage them. Sprint reviews come after the work is built; the customer, not just the product owner, knows what's right; acceptance criteria will be ambiguous if the requirements are.
domande.nota: Order of options B-D reconstructed from the transcript; answer A confirmed by the instructor.

domande.domanda: A project manager is running a predictive project. The customer requests a scope change that would add significant value but also extend the timeline; the change has not been formally submitted. What should the project manager do first?

opzioni.A: Assess the schedule and cost impact so the customer can make an approval decision.
opzioni.B: Add the change to the project scope since it clearly adds value.
opzioni.C: Ask the customer to submit the request through the change control process.
opzioni.D: Discuss the trade-off between value and timeline with the sponsor.

domande.hint: 'First': the request hasn't even been formally submitted.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Right, but second: you need a formal request to know exactly what to assess.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The PM doesn't have authority to add changes.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Ask the customer to submit a formal change request first; then assess and seek approval.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Possibly later, if needed, but not first.

domande.spiegazione: 'First': the customer must submit a formal change request so you know exactly what they want. Then assess the impact (A) and discuss with the sponsor if needed (D). The PM can't just add changes (B).

domande.domanda: Midway through an agile project, the product owner is frequently unavailable and the team has started making prioritization decisions on its own to avoid stalling. What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Allow the team to continue prioritizing since they understand the work best.
opzioni.B: Escalate the product owner's absence to the sponsor immediately.
opzioni.C: Document the prioritization decisions for the product owner to review later.
opzioni.D: Address availability with the product owner and clarify role expectations.

domande.hint: Everyone sticks to their role. If someone isn't doing theirs, don't do it for them.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Only the product owner prioritizes the backlog.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Address the product owner first instead of going to the sponsor.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The team still makes decisions that aren't theirs to make.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Address availability with the product owner and clarify the role's expectations and value.

domande.spiegazione: Everyone must follow their role: only the product owner prioritizes. If someone doesn't want to do their role, don't do it for them: educate them on its value and confront the problem.

domande.domanda: ⚠️ A key deliverable passed internal quality checks but was rejected by the customer because it did not meet an expectation that was never documented. What should the project manager do? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Explain to the customer that the deliverable met all documented requirements.
opzioni.B: Add the expectation to the requirements and rework the deliverable at no cost.
opzioni.C: Submit a change request to capture the new requirement and assess its impact.
opzioni.D: Meet with the customer to understand the expectation, then determine the next step.

domande.hint: When there's a problem, confront it and find the cause first.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. True, but it doesn't solve the problem: the deliverable is still rejected.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Rework may be needed, but 'at no cost' is wrong: people don't work for free.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Decent and probably the next step, but first understand the expectation.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Meet the customer to understand the expectation, then decide the next step (likely a change request).

domande.spiegazione: When there's a problem, confront it and find the cause: meet the customer first, then probably do C (change request). A doesn't solve the problem; people don't work for free (B).

domande.domanda: ⚠️ During a sprint, a team member completes their assigned work early and asks the project manager what to do next. What should the project manager do? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Assign the team member additional backlog items to put into the sprint.
opzioni.B: Encourage the team member to help others with in-progress sprint work.
opzioni.C: Direct the team member to begin work on items from the next sprint.
opzioni.D: Have the team member start refining backlog items.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The team, not the PM, decides the work, and sprint scope shouldn't change mid-sprint.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. In a cross-functional team, members help each other finish in-progress work, so the sprint may finish early.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. That pulls next-sprint work into the current sprint.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Backlog refinement is the product owner's responsibility.

domande.spiegazione: The team decides the work and sprint scope shouldn't change mid-sprint. Cross-functional team members help each other, so the whole sprint may finish early. C pulls work into the sprint; refinement is for the product owner.
domande.nota: Option D reconstructed (unclear transcript).

domande.domanda: ⚠️ A project sponsor pressures the project manager to report the project as on track at an upcoming steering committee, even though a key milestone is at risk of slipping. What should the project manager do? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Report the project as on track to maintain the sponsor's confidence.
opzioni.B: Report the status accurately and present the risk with options.
opzioni.C: Decline to attend the meeting to avoid presenting misleading information.
opzioni.D: Ask the sponsor to deliver the update on the project's behalf.

domande.hint: Ethics: always tell the full truth, whatever it costs.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Only technically true; it hides a real risk from the steering committee.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Report the status accurately and present the risk with options.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Avoiding the meeting is kicking the can down the road.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Don't hand your job to the sponsor.

domande.spiegazione: Ethics: always tell the truth, whatever it costs. A is only technically true; C kicks the can down the road; don't pass your job to the sponsor.

domande.domanda: ⚠️ A project manager oversees a project that has just entered its final phase. The team is fatigued and the project manager notices a rise in small errors in the work. What should the project manager do? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript; answer letter inferred from the commentary.

opzioni.A: Push the team harder to finish before quality declines.
opzioni.B: Address team fatigue and adjust the pace to sustain quality.
opzioni.C: Ignore the errors since the project is nearly done.
opzioni.D: Reassign the work to a fresh team for the final phase.

domande.hint: Never pick answers that push the team harder.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Pushing the team is unsustainable and against an agile principle.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Address the fatigue and adjust the pace: it tackles the root cause and protects quality.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Ignoring the errors doesn't address the problem.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Replacing the whole team is like firing people.

domande.spiegazione: Never pick answers that push the team harder (unsustainable, against an agile principle). Address the fatigue to protect quality. Ignoring doesn't solve the problem; don't fire a whole team.
domande.nota: Letter B inferred from the commentary (transcript unclear at the end).

domande.domanda: ⚠️ A project manager is planning a project and must decide how to engage a stakeholder group that will be significantly affected by the project outcome but has not yet been consulted. What should the project manager do? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Engage the group only after the product is delivered.
opzioni.B: Assume their needs based on similar projects.
opzioni.C: Limit their involvement to avoid delays.
opzioni.D: Involve the group early to understand their needs.

domande.hint: Never wait to engage stakeholders, and never assume their needs.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Engaging them after delivery doesn't help them.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Never assume needs; ask.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Never limit involvement to avoid delays.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Involve them early to understand their needs (stakeholder engagement plan).

domande.spiegazione: Never wait to engage stakeholders and never assume their needs: engage them from the beginning (stakeholder engagement plan).

domande.domanda: ⚠️ A project manager leads an agile project where the team has grown dependent on the project manager to resolve every minor decision, slowing the team down. What should the project manager do? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Continue making the decisions to keep the project moving.
opzioni.B: Make decisions faster to reduce the slowdown.
opzioni.C: Empower the team to make decisions within agreed boundaries.
opzioni.D: Assign a deputy to handle all team decisions.

domande.hint: Is this an impediment, or a decision the team should be making?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. It does nothing and lets the problem continue.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Faster decisions by the PM risk wrong decisions; the team should be deciding.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. The team is self-organizing: empower it to decide within agreed boundaries.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. A deputy still centralizes decisions instead of the team making them.

domande.spiegazione: The team is self-organizing and self-directing. This is a decision problem, not an impediment: the team should decide, not the PM or a delegate. A just lets the problem go on; B risks wrong decisions.
