spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. A representative still excludes most people.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Reconfirming an agreement doesn't solve it.

domande.spiegazione: Find the core of the problem: people aren't speaking during the meeting, so get all of them to speak. B and C keep them out of the meeting; D only revisits an agreement.
domande.nota: Option D reconstructed ('media ground rules' in the transcript).
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: During a sprint retrospective, several team members say they are exhausted from working late nights to meet sprint commitments. Velocity has remained stable, but two team members hint they may request a transfer. The product owner wants to maintain the current delivery pace to satisfy stakeholders. What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Ask the product owner to reduce stakeholders' expectations immediately.
opzioni.B: Facilitate a discussion to align sprint commitments with a sustainable team capacity.
opzioni.C: Meet with the product owner to assess why work needs to be maintained at the current pace.
opzioni.D: Escalate the burnout risk to the functional manager.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Don't just reduce stakeholders' expectations.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Align sprint commitments with sustainable team capacity.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The distractor: even with a reason, burnout isn't acceptable.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Don't give away your work.

domande.spiegazione: Agile principle: sustainable development. The team should never work at an unsustainable pace. C is the distractor: even if there's a reason, the team can't be burned out. Don't just cut expectations, and don't give away your work (D).

domande.domanda: ⚠️ A project is one week from a fixed launch date. The sponsor asks the project manager to skip the final round of user acceptance testing to guarantee an on-time release, stating that any defects can be fixed after go-live. The quality management plan requires this testing to be done before release. What should the project manager do? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript; debatable: the instructor sees more than one valid answer.

opzioni.A: Skip the testing since the sponsor has the authority.
opzioni.B: Delay the launch date until all testing is complete.
opzioni.C: Increase the budget to complete the testing.
opzioni.D: Have the team perform the testing after the release.

domande.hint: A management plan signals a traditional project. Required means required.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The testing is required by the quality management plan.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Do the required testing even if it delays the launch. Best of the four.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Increasing the budget needs a change request.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Testing after release skips what's required.

domande.spiegazione: A management plan signals a traditional project. The testing is required, so it must be done: if that delays the launch, so be it. Not the greatest answer but the best of the four. Increasing the budget would need a change request.
domande.nota: The instructor: 'not the best answer in absolute terms, but the best of these four'. Options A, C and D reconstructed.
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript; debatable: the instructor sees more than one valid answer

domande.domanda: Midway through a project, a newly appointed department head who was never included in the project communication begins raising objections to design decisions that were approved months earlier. What should the project manager do first?

opzioni.A: Assess the department head's needs and influence.
opzioni.B: Explain that the approved designs cannot be changed.
opzioni.C: Escalate the objections to the sponsor for a decision.
opzioni.D: Submit a change request to incorporate the new objections.

domande.hint: A brand-new stakeholder: what do you do first?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Assess the new stakeholder's needs and influence first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Never say nothing can change.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Maybe later, not first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Maybe later, not first.

domande.spiegazione: A brand new stakeholder: first assess their needs and influence before anything else. Never say nothing can be changed (everything can, with a change request in execution). Escalating or submitting a change request may come later, not first.

file.titolo: 100 Waterfall PMP Questions and Answers (Process Groups Practice Guide)

domande.domanda: You're working on a project to build a new parkland for the community. The person in charge of the parkland design approaches you, as they're not sure what they are supposed to be working on. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Review the project scope statement to see what the team is delivering.
opzioni.B: Review the WBS dictionary to see the detailed description of the scope and the work, and who it is assigned to.
opzioni.C: Review the requirements traceability matrix to see where the scope comes from.
opzioni.D: Review the assumption log to see who we assume should do the work.

domande.hint: Which document describes each work package in detail, including who it is assigned to?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The scope statement describes the scope at a general level, not who does each piece of work.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. The WBS dictionary details each work package: description, assignee, acceptance criteria, cost, schedule and resources.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The RTM links requirements to deliverables; it doesn't say who should work on what.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Never assume: the assumption log records assumptions, not work assignments.

domande.spiegazione: The WBS dictionary gives the detailed description of the work down to the work package level, where it can be assigned (PMBOK 6, p. 162).

domande.domanda: You've taken over as project manager of a project that has had issues delivering on time. You review the earned value management data and find that the schedule performance index (SPI) and cost performance index (CPI) are 0.86 and 1.12 respectively. You advise the project sponsor, who asks you to bring the project back on track within the next two months. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Apply schedule crashing to bring the project back on track.
opzioni.B: Apply fast tracking to bring the project back on track.
opzioni.C: Update the risk register and assign the risk of project failure to an executive with the power to bring it back on track.
opzioni.D: Reduce the project scope to bring the project back on track.

domande.hint: Read the indexes: below 1 is bad, above 1 is good. What do you have spare?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. SPI < 1 means behind schedule, CPI > 1 means under budget: you have money to spend, so crashing (adding money/resources) is the best option.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Fast tracking (doing activities in parallel) is valid and cheaper, but here you have budget to spare, so crashing fits better.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. You are the PM: don't hand the problem to someone else.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. It happens in real life, but cutting scope isn't needed when budget is available to recover the schedule.

domande.spiegazione: SPI 0.86 = behind schedule; CPI 1.12 = under budget. Crashing uses that spare money to compress the schedule (PMBOK 6, p. 215).

domande.domanda: You're working on a change that includes stakeholders at all levels, from frontline workers to senior executives. After performing stakeholder analysis, you and your team group the stakeholders according to their level of influence and the impact the change will have on them. The project sponsor asks what engagement strategy you will use for the frontline workers. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Manage them closely.
opzioni.B: Monitor them only.
opzioni.C: Keep them satisfied.
opzioni.D: Keep them informed.

domande.hint: Frontline workers: how much influence do they have, and how much does the change impact them?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Manage closely is for high influence and high impact.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Monitor only is for low influence and low impact.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Keep satisfied is for high influence (e.g. executives).
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Frontline workers have low influence but are highly impacted: keep them informed.

domande.spiegazione: Impact/influence grid: four quadrants. Low influence + high impact = keep informed (PMBOK 6, p. 512).

domande.domanda: You're working directly with the project sponsor in the initial phase of a brand-new project. The sponsor asks for your help in creating a document that formally authorizes the project, including details such as the cost-benefit analysis, the feasibility study and high-level risks. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Create a milestone chart.
opzioni.B: Create the business case.
opzioni.C: Create the project charter.
opzioni.D: Create the project management plan.

domande.hint: Which document formally authorizes the project?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. A milestone chart is a schedule view, not an authorizing document.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The business case comes before and is an input to the charter.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. The project charter formally authorizes the project and links it to the organization's strategic objectives.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The project management plan is created later, during planning.

domande.spiegazione: The charter formally authorizes the project; business case, cost-benefit analysis and feasibility studies are inputs (PMBOK 6, p. 75).

domande.domanda: You're working as a project manager and your team is about to deliver the completed system to the customer. During the final round of testing, the customer points out that a major piece of functionality is missing, which should have been in scope but was not previously thought of. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Deliver the system to the customer as it is, with the promise to add the functionality later.
opzioni.B: Ask the sponsor to accept the risk and move on.
opzioni.C: Use your project's contingency reserves.
opzioni.D: Use your project's management reserves.

domande.hint: Unforeseen work that is still within scope: which reserve covers it?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Once the project closes, the team may disband and the functionality never gets delivered.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. There is a better, win-win option than simply accepting it.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Contingency reserves cover identified risks (known unknowns).
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Management reserves are held for unforeseen work within the project scope (unknown unknowns).

domande.spiegazione: Cost baseline + contingency (known risks) = budget; + management reserve (unforeseen in-scope work) (PMBOK 6, p. 202).

domande.domanda: You and your team have completed the work on the project, and the customer has confirmed formal acceptance of the product that has been delivered. You set a meeting with your team to document the lessons learned and to release and reassign the personnel as needed. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Gain final sign-off on the risk report with the steering committee.
opzioni.B: Archive all of the project information for future use by the organization.
opzioni.C: Review the project documents for any open risks or issues.
opzioni.D: Ask the customer for a formal contract closure letter.

domande.hint: Which of these is part of the close project or phase activities?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Risk sign-off is not a closure step; risk is essentially zero once delivered.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Archiving project information for future use is a project closure activity.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Risks and issues should have been handled before acceptance.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Contract closure applies to third parties/vendors, not here.

domande.spiegazione: Archiving project information is part of Close Project or Phase (PMBOK 6, p. 123).

domande.domanda: You're working as a project manager on a medium-sized software project. The project sponsor believes that the team has not completed enough work in the last two weeks and comes to talk to you about it. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Review the team's burndown chart to see the flow of work versus what was committed.
opzioni.B: Review the project risk register and raise a risk on project performance.
opzioni.C: Ask the team to work harder, putting in overtime where possible.
opzioni.D: Tell the project sponsor to focus on their area and let you manage the project.

domande.hint: Solve problems with real data before acting.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. The iteration burndown chart shows remaining work against what was committed: real data to check the concern.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Confirm with data first before raising a risk.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Overtime breaks a sustainable pace.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. You must maintain the relationship with the sponsor, who funds the project.

domande.spiegazione: Verify concerns with data. The iteration burndown chart tracks remaining work vs. commitment (PMBOK 6, p. 226).

domande.domanda: You're working on a project that involves the renovation and removal of an old industrial plant. While investigating the area with your team to capture the project scope, you notice there are old chemicals left behind, which hurt your lungs when you breathe them in. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Accept the risk.
opzioni.B: Escalate the risk to your manager.
opzioni.C: Transfer the risk by hiring an external company to remove the chemicals.
opzioni.D: Avoid the risk by working on areas which don't have chemicals.

domande.hint: Genuine danger: who is best placed to deal with it?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The danger is too serious to simply accept.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Not the best option: you can deal with it yourself.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. For genuine danger or high risk, transfer to a specialist third party (like insurance).
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Avoiding the areas isn't realistic: the site must be cleared.

domande.spiegazione: Threat strategies: transferring dangerous/expensive risks to a third party is best here; mitigation through controls would also be good but isn't offered (PMBOK 6, p. 443).

domande.domanda: ⚠️ During user acceptance testing (UAT), a senior user points out a major change needed to the project scope for it to be successful. You realize you may not have enough money or resources to complete your project, but you will need approval to increase either. What will you do next? — ⚠️ Note: debatable: the instructor sees more than one valid answer.

opzioni.A: Review the change management plan for the correct change control process, including the approvers on the change control board.
opzioni.B: Review the configuration management plan to find out who can configure the project scope.
opzioni.C: Review the scope management plan to see how changes to scope should be handled.
opzioni.D: Review the quality management plan to see the rules for user acceptance testing.

domande.hint: You need approval: which plan describes the change control process and the CCB?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. The change management plan defines the change control process and who sits on the CCB.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The configuration management plan says which items are baselined, not who approves.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Close, but the change management plan is specific to change control and approvers.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The quality management plan is about testing, not approvals.

domande.spiegazione: Change mgmt plan = change process and CCB; configuration mgmt plan = baselined items; scope mgmt plan = how scope is defined/validated/controlled (PMBOK 6, pp. 88, 129, 286).
domande.nota: The instructor considers A and C very close.
domande.motivo_incertezza: debatable: the instructor sees more than one valid answer

domande.domanda: A new executive has started in the functional area you're delivering to. They are concerned that the project is not delivering what they need, and they put pressure on you to deliver more than what was originally agreed. You agree to meet and talk through the scope baseline so you are on the same page. What will you gather for the meeting?

opzioni.A: The requirements traceability matrix and the feature Gantt chart.
opzioni.B: The feature list and the current sprint backlog.
opzioni.C: The approved scope management plan.
opzioni.D: The project scope statement, the work breakdown structure (WBS) and the WBS dictionary.

domande.hint: What makes up the scope baseline?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. These are not part of the scope baseline.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. These are agile artifacts, not the scope baseline.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The scope management plan is a process document, not the baseline.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. The scope baseline = scope statement + WBS + WBS dictionary (with work packages).

domande.spiegazione: Scope baseline: scope statement, WBS, WBS dictionary, work and planning packages (PMBOK 6, p. 161).

domande.domanda: You're working on a project where you discover a certain negative risk with a potential impact of $2,000,000. You meet with your project stakeholders, who determine that this is within their risk appetite, provided that you meet a risk threshold of 10%. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Note the acceptable risk level as a threat of $200,000.
opzioni.B: Note the acceptable risk level as a threat of $1.8 million to $2.2 million.
opzioni.C: Note the impact as outside the acceptable risk level of $2,000,000.
opzioni.D: Note the impact as an opportunity of $200,000.

domande.hint: The threshold is a variation around the objective.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. $200,000 is the size of the variation, not the acceptable range.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. A 10% threshold around $2M gives an acceptable range of $1.8M to $2.2M.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Stakeholders said it is within their appetite.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. It's a threat, not an opportunity.

domande.spiegazione: Risk appetite = uncertainty stakeholders accept; risk threshold = acceptable variation around an objective (PMBOK 7, p. 54).

domande.domanda: A risk has been raised in your project around insufficient building materials. One risk response, assigned to the functional manager, suggests using a brand-new material which has not been fully tested before in a building project. Half of your stakeholder group are happy with this risk response, but the other half are not and refuse to sign off on it. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Suggest a quantitative risk approach to give a more accurate financial impact.
opzioni.B: Suggest they proceed with the proposed risk response and ensure it is followed through.
opzioni.C: Suggest a different risk owner, as an executive may have more power to respond to the risk.
opzioni.D: Suggest a different risk response, as responses should be timely, cost-effective, realistic and agreed to by relevant stakeholders.

domande.hint: What characteristics should a good risk response have?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. More analysis isn't needed yet; the response itself is the problem.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. You can't force it while half the stakeholders disagree.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. An executive could force it through, but the disagreement may have good reasons.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. A response must be appropriate, cost-effective, realistic, agreed by stakeholders and owned.

domande.spiegazione: Risk responses should be timely, cost-effective, realistic, agreed by relevant stakeholders and owned by a responsible person (PMBOK 7, p. 54).

domande.domanda: Your project started to go off track due to a large amount of uncertainty in the requirements and resources. At a significant cost, you've managed to rein in these issues. However, your project management office would like you to brainstorm ways to improve with your team, so that it does not happen again. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Ask your team to increase the project contingency reserve to allow for these impacts.
opzioni.B: Ask your team to change the project methodology from waterfall to agile.
opzioni.C: Ask your team to use short feedback loops, continuous improvement and transparent planning.
opzioni.D: Ask your team to check their work twice before sending it to the next part of the process.

domande.hint: How does a team embrace adaptability and resiliency?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. More money doesn't improve the way of working.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Changing methodology doesn't magically remove uncertainty.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Short feedback loops, continuous improvement and transparent planning build adaptability and resiliency.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Possible, but much weaker than C.

domande.spiegazione: Embrace adaptability and resiliency: short feedback loops, continuous learning, inspection and adaptation, transparent planning, prototypes (PMBOK 7, p. 56).

domande.domanda: ⚠️ As your project progresses, many of the business stakeholders are starting to voice their concerns, question some of the changes and even miss key meetings, trying to sabotage your efforts. What will you do next? — ⚠️ Note: debatable: the instructor sees more than one valid answer.

opzioni.A: Communicate the vision and benefits of the change clearly, along with the impact on their work.
opzioni.B: Create an impact/influence chart to determine who should be engaged and how.
opzioni.C: Escalate the matter to your project sponsor and arrange for different stakeholders.
opzioni.D: Map the current state and the proposed future state of the change for the stakeholders.

domande.hint: Resistance to change usually comes from a lack of understanding.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Communicating vision, benefits and impact early reduces resistance and change fatigue.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Useful, but it doesn't address people questioning the change.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Stakeholders usually can't be replaced: work with them.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Close (it's problem solving), but communication is the key to engagement here.

domande.spiegazione: Change management: communicate vision, goals and benefits early, with the impact on work processes (PMBOK 7, p. 59).
domande.nota: The instructor considers A and D very close.
domande.motivo_incertezza: debatable: the instructor sees more than one valid answer

domande.domanda: You're analyzing your stakeholders through an impact/influence chart and have found more than 100 different groups of people and over 3,000 impacted stakeholders. Other parts of your project are starting to fall behind as you try to keep up with such a large number of people. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Ask your project team to engage different groups of stakeholders so everyone is covered.
opzioni.B: Clearly prioritize the stakeholders, then engage and communicate with the highly impacted and influential groups early and often.
opzioni.C: Monitor the stakeholders for signs of stress and respond to the groups most stressed about the project.
opzioni.D: Create a SharePoint page for the changes that any stakeholder can gather information from at any time.

domande.hint: Too many stakeholders to engage effectively: what's the key word?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Splitting the work makes sense, but isn't the specific technique.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. When there are too many to engage effectively, prioritization is key.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. It's a kind of prioritization, but less complete than B.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Good pull communication, but doesn't solve the overload.

domande.spiegazione: Stakeholder engagement: identify, understand and analyze, prioritize, engage, monitor (PMBOK 7, pp. 11-12).

domande.domanda: You're managing a project that has communicated with the customer using mostly pull communication so far. When monitoring the engagement of your stakeholders, you notice a trend: they are not clear on the impacts or benefits of the project. You decide to add push communication to your communication plan. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Create a web page using SharePoint with all the project information your stakeholders can see.
opzioni.B: Push for more funding on your project and communicate this to the project sponsor.
opzioni.C: Push your stakeholders to engage in more two-way communication.
opzioni.D: Send a weekly email to stakeholders with a project update, including the impacts and benefits.

domande.hint: Push = sent to recipients; pull = they fetch it.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. A web page is pull communication.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Right keyword, wrong meaning: funding isn't the issue.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Right keyword, but it isn't push communication.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. A sent email is push communication.

domande.spiegazione: Push: memos, emails, status reports, voicemail. Pull: bulletins, web pages, whiteboards (PMBOK 7, p. 13).

domande.domanda: You have taken over a project with a vendor where scope and requirements have been missed. You notice that miscommunication and mixed messages are common. You set a meeting with your team and the vendor's team, and the meeting is extremely important to get right. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Speak slowly and clearly with the vendor's team, at a louder volume if necessary.
opzioni.B: Confirm they heard your message, determine whether they agree and identify any nuanced or unintended messages they may have received.
opzioni.C: Only communicate with the vendor in writing, so you have a trail of proof if anything goes wrong in the future.
opzioni.D: Prepare a claim for the mishandled scope of your project through the procurement team.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Volume doesn't improve understanding.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Quick feedback loops confirm the message was heard, agreed and correctly interpreted.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Writing loses tone and body language and is more easily misread.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Fix the communication first.

domande.spiegazione: Feedback loops: confirm the message was heard, check agreement, identify nuances (PMBOK 7, p. 13).

domande.domanda: Your stakeholders seem to be engaged. However, there are frequent changes to scope and requirements, causing delays. Issues are often raised and result in multiple rounds of feedback, and you're not sure who or what could be the cause. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Perform root cause analysis on the problem with your project team, to brainstorm.
opzioni.B: Raise a risk in the risk register for the project delay and review responses with your team.
opzioni.C: Review the issue log, risk register and change log for the most frequent requesters, then update your stakeholder engagement approach for those people.
opzioni.D: Ensure your project budget has enough contingency reserve to cover the multiple reviews and delays.

domande.hint: Frequent changes may signal stakeholders who are not aligned. How do you find out who?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Good, but C goes further: it finds the who and acts on it.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. It's an issue already happening, not a risk.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. The logs reveal which stakeholders drive the changes, so you can engage them better.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Don't just throw money at it.

domande.spiegazione: Many changes may mean stakeholders aren't engaged/aligned; issue and risk registers reveal challenges with individual stakeholders (PMBOK 7, p. 15).

domande.domanda: You've been working on a project where the manager leads in a dictatorship style. Over time, the team has stopped making suggestions, sick days and mental health days have become more frequent, and the pace of work has slowed. The manager comes to you for help, and you suggest a servant leadership style instead. What will they do next?

opzioni.A: Serve the team as much as they can, ensuring their every need is met.
opzioni.B: Focus on obstacle removal, encouragement and development opportunities.
opzioni.C: Ensure the team members are serving each other and helping each other succeed.
opzioni.D: Serve the team new ways to do the work and engage them through additional variety.

domande.hint: Servant leadership = removing blockers and growing people.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Sounds good, but servant leaders don't meet every need.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Obstacle removal, diversion shielding, encouragement and development are servant leadership behaviors.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Good practice, but not servant leadership specifically.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Right keywords, wrong meaning.

domande.spiegazione: Servant leaders enable self-organization and autonomy, remove obstacles, shield the team and offer development (PMBOK 7, p. 18).

domande.domanda: You have been allocated to a new project team with members from different parts of the functional business area. It soon becomes clear that very few of them have worked on a project before. There is a lot of miscommunication, and rework is occurring among the team, which is starting to cause delays. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Set a daily stand-up with your team to ensure they update what they completed.
opzioni.B: Review the resource assignment matrix with your team to ensure they are doing their job.
opzioni.C: Help the team set its vision and objectives, roles and responsibilities, and team operations.
opzioni.D: Send your team members on training in their roles to increase their capability.

domande.hint: A newly formed team needs clarity first.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Could help, but doesn't create shared clarity.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Could help, but is control rather than team development.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Vision, roles and ways of working (e.g. a team charter) build a one-team mindset.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Good, but the issue is alignment, not individual skill.

domande.spiegazione: Teams formed across organizations need upfront work: shared vision, clear roles, ways of working (PMBOK 7, p. 18).

domande.domanda: You are nearing the end of a difficult project, where the vendor providing the system to your company has taken longer than anticipated. The deliverables have been quality tested, validated and verified, and your project sponsor is keen to finish the project and close it off. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Review the project management plan and the approved change requests.
opzioni.B: Review the requirements management plan and the requirements traceability matrix.
opzioni.C: Review the procurement agreement and the accepted deliverables.
opzioni.D: Review any outstanding risks and issues.

domande.hint: Closing a project that involved a vendor: which inputs matter?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not the key inputs for closing here.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The requirements management plan is about managing requirements, not closing.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Procurement agreements and accepted deliverables are inputs to Close Project or Phase.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Everything is already tested and accepted.

domande.spiegazione: Inputs to Close Project or Phase include accepted deliverables and procurement agreements (PMBOK 6, p. 124).
domande.nota: Order of options reconstructed from the transcript (the instructor states C and explains the procurement answer).

domande.domanda: You're managing a team through a difficult project, which has been made more difficult by many team members being new, inexperienced and not having the right capability to get the work done. You're getting pressure from your steering committee to improve the performance of your project. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Use Tuckman's ladder of forming, storming, norming and performing with your team.
opzioni.B: Use co-location, a shared knowledge portal, training and team assessments.
opzioni.C: Use conflict management, influencing and emotional intelligence to get your team on side.
opzioni.D: Use brainstorming and root cause analysis to get to the heart of the problem.

domande.hint: Develop Team tools and techniques for raising capability.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Tuckman is a model of team stages, not a capability tool.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Co-location, communication technology, training and team assessments are Develop Team tools.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Good skills, but not targeted at capability.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Good, but the cause (inexperience) is already known.

domande.spiegazione: Develop Team: co-location, interpersonal skills, communication technology, training, team assessments, recognition (PMBOK 6, pp. 340-342).

domande.domanda: You've planned the scope, schedule, cost and resources with your team, and you've also identified a large number of risks within the project. You're in the process of assigning the probability and impact to the risks when one of the risks occurs. Your project sponsor immediately worries about a worst-case scenario. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Use the management reserve for your project to mitigate the risk.
opzioni.B: Review or create the risk response in the risk register, then use the appropriate contingency reserve to implement it.
opzioni.C: Perform quantitative analysis on the risk to ensure you know how much it will cost.
opzioni.D: Accept the risk for now, as the risk analysis is not yet complete.

domande.hint: An identified risk is a known unknown: which reserve?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Management reserve is for unforeseen in-scope work.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Identified risks are covered by contingency reserves through the planned response.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Quantitative analysis is deeper financial analysis, not a response.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. A response is still needed.

domande.spiegazione: Known risks go in the risk register with responses; contingency reserves cover known unknowns (PMBOK 6, p. 440).

domande.domanda: A significant change has been made to the project scope after a serious system flaw was found. This scope change will impact the scope, cost and schedule of the project. You analyze the impacts on each, raise an issue in the issue log and are about to raise a change request. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Review the configuration management plan for the baselined project items.
opzioni.B: Add the detail as a project delivery risk in your risk register.
opzioni.C: Update the change log and implement the changes required.
opzioni.D: Check the change management plan for the change control board members and process.

domande.hint: Who approves, and through which process?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. You already know it needs change control.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. It has already happened: it's an issue, not a risk.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. You can't implement before approval.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. The change management plan defines the process and the CCB's roles.

domande.spiegazione: The CCB reviews, approves, defers or rejects changes; the change management plan documents the process and CCB roles (PMBOK 6, p. 116).

domande.domanda: Five major defects have been found during quality testing, resulting in the scope changing significantly and affecting your schedule and budget. You have analyzed the impacts and raised a change request for each. The change control board has approved two changes, rejected two and deferred one. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Record the outcomes in the change log and communicate the deferred and rejected changes to the change requester.
opzioni.B: Review and reprioritize the project scope to fit the must-have items into delivery.
opzioni.C: Raise a risk for the changes.
opzioni.D: Raise a claim on the affected changes to give them a better chance of approval.

domande.hint: After CCB decisions: record and communicate.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. All outcomes go in the change log; deferred/rejected ones are communicated to the requester.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Changes still go through the change process.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. It has already happened.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Claims are for contested vendor changes.

domande.spiegazione: Outcomes of all change requests are recorded in the change log; rejected/deferred are communicated to requesters (PMBOK 6, p. 120).

domande.domanda: You're working through the scope of a newly kicked-off project. The senior user is unsure how the requirements and scope come together to create a deliverable that will work for him and the functional manager. Your program manager suggests you use decomposition in this circumstance. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Estimate activity resources for who is required to deliver the item.
opzioni.B: Define a project scope for the functional manager.
opzioni.C: Create a work breakdown structure and define the activities in your schedule.
opzioni.D: Create the project charter and the project management plan for a clear view of the project.

domande.hint: Decomposition is a tool of which processes?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. That's not decomposition.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Defining scope isn't decomposition.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Decomposition is a tool of Create WBS and Define Activities.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Good documents, but not decomposition.

domande.spiegazione: Decomposition breaks work into smaller, manageable parts; used in Create WBS and Define Activities (PMBOK 6, pp. 156, 185).

domande.domanda: You have been assigned to take over a project in your organization that has gone off track, with scope creep causing the schedule and cost to increase. You can't quite understand the current cadence and way of working within the team, so you decide to find out their development approach, including any modifications. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Review the project charter, as this was the original agreed document.
opzioni.B: Review the schedule management plan, as this will have the team's cadence schedules.
opzioni.C: Review the project management plan, as this will house the cadence approach.
opzioni.D: Review the stakeholder register for the stakeholders' cadence needs.

domande.hint: Where is the development approach documented?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The charter is high-level authorization.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. It covers the deliverables' schedule, not the team's cadence.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. The development approach (predictive, iterative, agile, hybrid) is in the project management plan.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The register lists stakeholders and their needs.

domande.spiegazione: The development approach and modifications are part of the project management plan (PMBOK 6, p. 88).

domande.domanda: You're working on a complex engineering project where a significant amount of risk has been found with your team and the customer. The functional manager approaches you to ask if she can work with your team to plan the risk responses. You agree to help her update the risk register with:

opzioni.A: Risk triggers, agreed response strategies and residual risks after mitigation.
opzioni.B: Risk contingency reserves, quantitative analysis and financial impact responses.
opzioni.C: The list of risks, their probability and impact, and their overall risk rating.
opzioni.D: Risk owners, assumptions and mitigations.

domande.hint: What does Plan Risk Responses add to the register?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Plan Risk Responses adds agreed strategies, triggers (warning signs) and expected residual risks.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. That's quantitative analysis.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. That's qualitative assessment, not responses.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Close, but A is directly about responses.

domande.spiegazione: Plan Risk Responses updates the risk register with strategies, triggers and residual risks (PMBOK 6, p. 448).

domande.domanda: Your project is nearing completion. You have monitored and controlled quality through testing, and risks through mitigations, throughout the project life. The project sponsor is concerned that she won't know whether the product being delivered has the desired effect on her business area once it is released. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Consult the quality management plan and act in accordance with that process.
opzioni.B: Consult the benefits management plan and act in accordance with that process.
opzioni.C: Consult the business case and act in accordance with it.
opzioni.D: Consult the risk register and act in accordance with it.

domande.hint: Is the sponsor asking about quality, or business value?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. That's about testing.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. The benefits management plan describes how and when benefits are delivered and measured.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The business case explains why, not how benefits are measured.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Risks aren't the point here.

domande.spiegazione: The benefits management plan defines how benefits are delivered and measured; reviewed at closing (PMBOK 6, p. 125).

domande.domanda: You are the project manager on a high-profile software project that involves automation technology never used before in your company. Because of this, your team has no resources to complete that part of the project. The steering committee approves outsourcing this work to a suitable vendor. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Perform a make-or-buy analysis to ensure a correct decision.
opzioni.B: Approach your procurement department for a suitable contract to proceed with, such as cost plus incentive fee.
opzioni.C: Create the procurement statement of work and the source selection criteria.
opzioni.D: Review the current agreements and change requests impacting third-party work.

domande.hint: The buy decision is already made: what comes next in Plan Procurement Management?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Make-or-buy is already decided.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Good, but it comes after the SOW and selection criteria.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. The procurement SOW and source selection criteria are outputs of Plan Procurement Management.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. No agreements exist yet.

domande.spiegazione: Plan Procurement Management outputs: procurement SOW, source selection criteria, bid documents, procurement strategy (PMBOK 6, pp. 464, 477-478).

domande.domanda: You're a project manager working in the initial phases of a project, trying to put together a document for your stakeholders to have your project approved. You remember the 5 Cs of communication from your studies and decide to use them here. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Connect each part of the communication.
opzioni.B: Create a bond between the message sender and the receiver.
opzioni.C: Ensure a clear purpose and expression directed to the needs of the reader.
opzioni.D: Care about the subject and the person.

domande.hint: 5 Cs of written communication: correct, concise, clear, coherent, controlling.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not one of the 5 Cs.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Not one of the 5 Cs.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Clear purpose and expression directed to the reader's needs is one of the 5 Cs.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Not one of the 5 Cs.

domande.spiegazione: 5 Cs: correct grammar and spelling, concise expression, clear purpose, coherent flow, controlling flow of words and ideas (PMBOK 6, p. 363).

domande.domanda: You've been working with the stakeholders in your project for some time, and the communication has been getting more and more tense with each interaction. You perform a stakeholder engagement assessment and discover that the majority of your stakeholders are either resistant or neutral. What will you NOT do next?

opzioni.A: Ensure you're actively listening in each interaction, speaking less and listening more.
opzioni.B: Increase your awareness of cultural and personal differences.
opzioni.C: Identify, set and manage stakeholder expectations correctly.
opzioni.D: Escalate the stakeholder issue to their functional manager to bring them back in line.

domande.hint: NOT question: three answers support the 5 Cs, one doesn't.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect (you would do it). Active listening supports communication.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect (you would do it). Cultural awareness supports communication.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect (you would do it). Managing expectations supports communication.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct (you would NOT do it). Escalation is a last resort; work with them first.

domande.spiegazione: Skills supporting the 5 Cs: active listening, cultural awareness, managing expectations, negotiation/coaching/conflict skills (PMBOK 6, p. 363).

domande.domanda: You have been working on a large database transfer project when the data manager in your organization identifies the aging systems as a threat to your project. You review this with your project team and decide to perform qualitative risk analysis on the threat. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Review the quality of the data.
opzioni.B: Assign a probability of occurrence and an impact to the threat.
opzioni.C: Perform analysis on a range of outcomes.
opzioni.D: Add a risk trigger, a mitigation and an owner to the threat.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not the core of qualitative analysis.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Qualitative analysis prioritizes risks by probability and impact.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Range of outcomes/simulations is quantitative.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. That's Plan Risk Responses.

domande.spiegazione: Perform Qualitative Risk Analysis: prioritize risks by probability and impact (PMBOK 6, p. 419).

domande.domanda: You're managing a project that has formed organically around an important process improvement. You have been given limited resources and a very small budget by the project sponsor. You're planning risk management with your team, but you do not have the resources to complete all the necessary risk tasks. Which step will you remove in such a project?

opzioni.A: Perform qualitative risk analysis.
opzioni.B: Perform quantitative risk analysis.
opzioni.C: Identify risks.
opzioni.D: Plan risk management.

domande.hint: Which step costs the most and is mainly for large or complex projects?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Probability and impact are the backbone of risk analysis.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Quantitative analysis takes extra time and cost and suits large or strategic projects.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Risks must still be identified.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Planning risk management is still needed.

domande.spiegazione: Quantitative risk analysis is not required on every project; most appropriate for large/complex/strategic ones (PMBOK 6, p. 429).

domande.domanda: You are the project manager on a waterfall project and have planned the requirements, scope and schedule with your team. You now need to create the cost estimates for your project. What will you NOT do as part of your cost estimates?

opzioni.A: Include contingency amounts to account for identified risks.
opzioni.B: Include the known cost of project changes and of managing project change.
opzioni.C: Include indirect costs at the activity level, if they are included in the project estimate.
opzioni.D: Include a management reserve for unforeseen scope changes.

domande.hint: NOT question: three items belong in the cost estimates.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect (included). Contingency for identified risks is included.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct (not included). Managing change is part of normal project management, not a cost estimate line.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect (included). Indirect costs are included if part of the project estimate.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect (included, per the source). The management reserve for unforeseen scope is added on top.

domande.spiegazione: Per the source, cost estimates include contingency and management reserves and indirect costs if included in the estimate (PMBOK 6, p. 246).

domande.domanda: You've just taken over as project manager on a difficult waterfall project. Multiple project stakeholders have approached you and asked to make changes to different parts of the scope, cost and schedule of your project. You're trying to figure out which items need change approval and which can just be done. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Review the change management plan for the change approval process.
opzioni.B: Review the scope management plan for how scope changes are managed.
opzioni.C: Review the configuration management plan for the baselined items.
opzioni.D: Review the requirements traceability matrix.

domande.hint: Which plan lists items under configuration control?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. It explains the change process, not which items are baselined.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. It covers how scope is managed, not which items are baselined.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. The configuration management plan identifies baselined items that need change control.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. It links requirements to scope.

domande.spiegazione: Configuration management plan = which items are baselined; change management plan = how changes are processed (PMBOK 6, p. 169).
domande.nota: Order of options reconstructed from the transcript.

domande.domanda: You're new to a project and have been approached by the functional manager. No one has been able to tell them exactly what the project is about and what they need to be aware of, including the high-level scope, schedule, risks and who approved the project in the first place. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Check the project activity list and schedule.
opzioni.B: Hold a sprint review to see what the team has developed so far.
opzioni.C: Review the project charter and identify the stakeholders impacted by the change.
opzioni.D: Visit the project management office to gather organizational process assets.

domande.hint: Which document holds the high-level summary of the project?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. No risks or approvals there.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Only shows an increment.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. The charter contains purpose, high-level requirements, milestones, risks, stakeholders and the approver.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. OPAs are too generic.

domande.spiegazione: The charter holds the high-level information to get up to speed (PMBOK 6, p. 155).

domande.domanda: The project manager on your project recently left, and you agreed to see the project through as it is nearly complete. The deliverables have been accepted, and you just need to communicate the release to any and all affected stakeholders in the way that they agreed. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Review the communications management plan for how communication is managed.
opzioni.B: Review the stakeholder engagement plan to see how they prefer to be engaged.
opzioni.C: Review the stakeholder register for the people you need to communicate to.
opzioni.D: Review the resource management plan for the resources affected by your project.

domande.hint: Where are the agreed communication requirements?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. It describes how communications are planned, structured, implemented and monitored, including stakeholder requirements.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. More about engagement than communication.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Lists who, not how.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. About project resources.

domande.spiegazione: Communications management plan: stakeholder communication requirements, information, reasons, methods (PMBOK 6, p. 377).

domande.domanda: You've been working on a project in your organization for some time. In the latest working group meeting, the project sponsor adds a new executive member to the group. As soon as they arrive, they raise a new scope item that was not in the original plan. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Raise a change request to change the scope baseline.
opzioni.B: Update the stakeholder register with the new stakeholder's details.
opzioni.C: Raise an issue for the scope change in the issue log.
opzioni.D: Update the change log with the initial details of the scope change.

domande.hint: A new stakeholder has just joined: what comes first?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Analyze first: you don't know if the change is valid.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Add and analyze the new stakeholder first (role, influence, requirements).
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Possibly later.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Possibly later.

domande.spiegazione: The stakeholder register holds identification, assessment and classification info; update it when a stakeholder joins (PMBOK 6, p. 514).

domande.domanda: Your project team has been complaining about poor stakeholder engagement in a certain part of the organization for some time. It's now impacting the project schedule, and you may need to use your contingency reserve to crash the schedule and bring it back on track. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Review the cost management plan and access the appropriate contingency reserve.
opzioni.B: Perform root cause analysis on the problem with your team.
opzioni.C: Raise the engagement as a risk and escalate it immediately to the functional manager.
opzioni.D: Change the way of working to agile to increase stakeholder engagement.

domande.hint: Solve the problem before spending money.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Don't spend reserves before analyzing the problem.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Find the root cause first; use reserves only if necessary.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. It's already happening, and escalation isn't first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Agile is not a silver bullet.

domande.spiegazione: Root cause analysis identifies causes for problem solving (PMBOK 6, p. 292).

domande.domanda: You are delivering a brand-new product line into your organization, partly using a third-party system. You've been working with the functional manager and her team to gather their expert judgment throughout development, when they raise a concern that the third-party system is being discontinued and will lose support in the next 12 months. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Update the risk register.
opzioni.B: Ignore the concern.
opzioni.C: Escalate the concern to the sponsor.
opzioni.D: Update the issue log.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. It's a future uncertain event: record it in the risk register.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Never ignore concerns.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Own it first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. It hasn't happened yet.

domande.spiegazione: Risks can be identified at any time and recorded in the risk register (PMBOK 6, p. 409).

domande.domanda: You have joined a car manufacturing company as a new project manager. Senior management has asked you to take the necessary steps to kick-start a project in a corresponding area, designing a new electronic dashboard. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Review the marketplace conditions.
opzioni.B: Create a cost-benefit analysis and a feasibility study for a business case.
opzioni.C: Gather the high-level requirements, scope, milestones and risks for a project charter.
opzioni.D: Start the project through a kickoff meeting immediately and begin gathering resources.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Possibly useful, but doesn't start the project.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Good, but the charter is what kick-starts it.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Develop Project Charter is the first initiating step and authorizes using resources.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Too early without a charter.

domande.spiegazione: The charter formally authorizes the project and gives the PM authority to use resources (PMBOK 6, pp. 25, 81).

domande.domanda: Your project team has just finished defining the scope of the project. They have matched the scope to the original requirements in a requirements traceability matrix, but the team can't agree on what to do next. What will you ask them to do?

opzioni.A: Ask your quality team to verify the scope so the project can proceed.
opzioni.B: Approach the project sponsor for acceptance of the project scope.
opzioni.C: Break down the scope into activities and place them on a project schedule.
opzioni.D: Review the scope management plan for direction on creating the work breakdown structure.

domande.hint: Order: collect requirements, define scope, create WBS.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Quality verifies deliverables later.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Acceptance comes much later.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Scheduling comes after the WBS.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Next is Create WBS, as directed by the scope management plan.

domande.spiegazione: Scope order: collect requirements, define scope, create WBS; the scope management plan describes how (PMBOK 6, pp. 130, 137).

domande.domanda: ⚠️ You've just taken over a project that is approximately halfway through and has used around 75% of its budget. A change to one of the features has been requested after extensive user acceptance testing, and your project team cannot agree on what to do next, or whether changes should be made at all. What will you do next? — ⚠️ Note: debatable: the instructor sees more than one valid answer.

opzioni.A: Check the change management plan for details on how to make changes.
opzioni.B: Check the requirements traceability matrix for how the requirements should be traced.
opzioni.C: Loudly blame the previous project manager for not having a process to deal with this situation.
opzioni.D: Check the scope management plan for details on how to manage the scope.

domande.hint: The question is whether to change at all, not how.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Close, but it explains how to change, not whether scope can change.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Not about a change decision.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Take responsibility.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. The scope management plan says how scope is defined, validated, monitored and controlled.

domande.spiegazione: Scope management plan: how scope is defined, validated, monitored and controlled (PMBOK 6, p. 169).
domande.nota: The instructor considers A and D very close.
domande.motivo_incertezza: debatable: the instructor sees more than one valid answer

domande.domanda: You've been asked to work on a process improvement within your team. The manager has secured a developer to help you automate the process once it's streamlined, but you will need to make sure the developer understands the process thoroughly, including the criteria to test the automation against. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Gather your team and the developer and create a flowchart together.
opzioni.B: Gather your team and the developer and create an affinity diagram.
opzioni.C: Gather your team and perform a cost-benefit analysis for the automation.
opzioni.D: Gather your team and create a quality management plan.

domande.hint: Which tool shows a process step by step?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. A flowchart shows the process start to finish with decision points and participants.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Groups similar ideas.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Doesn't explain the process.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Describes how quality is managed.

domande.spiegazione: Flowcharts show a process with decision points and actors; a Plan Quality tool (PMBOK 6, p. 282).

domande.domanda: You're working on a new project where the design and the project work, including all of the scope and cost, have been planned upfront. However, part of the project relies on a vendor creating a new add-on, which will be subject to multiple changes as the core product is created. What product development life cycle approach will you recommend to the team?

opzioni.A: A predictive (waterfall) approach.
opzioni.B: An iterative approach.
opzioni.C: An incremental approach.
opzioni.D: A hybrid approach, combining pre-planned activities with iterations and ceremonies that promote collaboration and feedback for the changeable parts of the project.

domande.hint: Some parts are fixed, some are evolving.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Doesn't handle the changing part.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. One release refined over iterations.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Delivers increments but doesn't fit the upfront planning.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Hybrid: predictive for known parts, adaptive for evolving parts.

domande.spiegazione: Hybrid life cycle combines predictive and adaptive elements (PMBOK 6, p. 19).

domande.domanda: The project you are managing has defined the scope and created the scope baseline, with the scope statement, the work breakdown structure and the WBS dictionary. The project sponsor is unhappy with the planning process and would like to know how much this scope will cost to deliver. What is the next best action you should take?

opzioni.A: Create the project budget.
opzioni.B: Define and sequence the activities and estimate their durations.
opzioni.C: Create the resource management plan.
opzioni.D: Review the project charter for the high-level project scope, schedule and costs.

domande.hint: You can't cost what you haven't scheduled.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The budget needs activities, durations and resources first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Next is defining activities, sequencing and estimating durations.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Not the next step.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. You're past initiation.

domande.spiegazione: Budget requires activities, durations and resources (PMBOK 6, p. 174).

domande.domanda: You're working on a project charter for the initiating stage of a new project that will deliver a new data system. You approach your enterprise data team and ask them for an estimate to deliver these changes. However, your project sponsor believes a third-party vendor will provide the best solution. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Create the project charter and let the steering committee decide.
opzioni.B: Perform a make-or-buy analysis with a payback.
opzioni.C: Ask the enterprise data team for their lowest quote to ensure they win.
opzioni.D: Take an agile approach to the project and deliver it in increments.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. You need the analysis first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Make-or-buy with payback compares initial and ongoing costs.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. May lead to cutting corners.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Doesn't answer make or buy.

domande.spiegazione: Make-or-buy may include payback, NPV, cost-benefit analysis (PMBOK 6, p. 473).

domande.domanda: You're working on a project where the functional manager is unhappy with the changes being brought to his part of the organization. He argues constantly, misses key meetings and demands multiple sign-offs to slow progress, among other things. The project sponsor asks you to go for a win-win approach to this conflict. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Smooth and accommodate, emphasizing areas of agreement.
opzioni.B: Collaborate and problem-solve with the manager.
opzioni.C: Compromise and reconcile with the manager.
opzioni.D: Force and direct the manager.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Smoothing is lose-win.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Collaborate/problem solve is the only win-win.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Compromise is lose-lose.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Forcing is win-lose.

domande.spiegazione: Conflict: smooth = lose-win; compromise = lose-lose; force = win-lose; collaborate = win-win (PMBOK 6, p. 348).

domande.domanda: You're working on a large multi-year project. You realize that the estimates from a year ago are extremely inaccurate, and the project is now off track. You would like to try a different approach that gives a high-level view of future work and a detailed view of near-term work. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Recommend a decomposition approach.
opzioni.B: Recommend the process in the schedule management plan.
opzioni.C: Recommend an iterative approach to development.
opzioni.D: Recommend a rolling wave planning approach.

domande.hint: Detailed near term, high-level far term.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Decomposition breaks down work but isn't this approach.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. You're trying to change that process.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. About refining a single release.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Rolling wave plans near-term work in detail, future work at a high level.

domande.spiegazione: Rolling wave planning (PMBOK 6, p. 185).

domande.domanda: You're in the initiating stages of a project for a car manufacturer. Their vehicles have been losing market share due to the high price of fuel, and the organization wants to build more fuel-efficient cars. You've been asked to put together a business case outlining the various options, with a specific instruction to perform benchmarking. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Find which competitor products have been benchmarked for future production.
opzioni.B: Compare the specifications of popular branded fuel-efficient cars available in the market with your products.
opzioni.C: Create a project charter to use as a benchmark for your future project management plan.
opzioni.D: Benchmark your current scope, cost and schedule to use as values for project performance.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. A wordplay trap; not benchmarking.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Comparing your products with comparable ones on the market is benchmarking.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Wordplay trap: a charter isn't a benchmark.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. That's baselining, not benchmarking.

domande.spiegazione: Benchmarking compares products, processes and practices with comparable organizations (PMBOK 6, p. 143).

domande.domanda: ⚠️ When reviewing the project performance with your team, you notice the following: Activity A is on the critical path and delayed by 5 days; Activity B is not on the critical path and delayed by 7 days; Activity C is on the critical path and delayed by 3 days; Activity D is not on the critical path and delayed by 2 days. Where will you ask the team to focus their efforts, and in which order, to bring the project back on track? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: B, A, C, D
opzioni.B: A, B, C, D
opzioni.C: A, C, B, D
opzioni.D: C, A, D, B

domande.hint: Critical path first, then the biggest delays.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. B is not on the critical path, so it doesn't come first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. C (critical path) must come before B.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Critical path activities first (A then C, by delay), then the others by delay (B then D).
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Among critical activities, A is more delayed than C.

domande.spiegazione: Address critical path tasks first, then the most delayed (PMBOK 6, p. 210).
domande.nota: Delay values for B, C and D and the option sequences are reconstructed: the transcript only gives A (critical, 5 days) and the answer order A, C, B, D.
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: As your project begins, it becomes clear that most of the business analysts, developers and testers are not familiar with the system they'll be modifying. The project sponsor asks you to address this as a potential future quality issue, and to add a series of training sessions for the team with their associated cost. How will you classify this cost?

opzioni.A: As an appraisal cost.
opzioni.B: As a prevention cost.
opzioni.C: As an internal failure cost.
opzioni.D: As a sunk cost.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Appraisal is auditing/checking work.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Training prevents future quality issues: prevention cost.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Defects caught before release.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Money already spent.

domande.spiegazione: Cost of quality: prevention, appraisal, internal and external failure (PMBOK 6, p. 282).

domande.domanda: You have finished project planning. All baseline documents have been approved and the project team is ready to begin project execution (delivery). Your team has planned and estimated the activity resources required. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Define with the team how to estimate, acquire, manage and use team and physical resources.
opzioni.B: Estimate the team resources and the type and quantities of materials, equipment and supplies necessary to perform the project work.
opzioni.C: Obtain the team members, facilities, equipment, materials, supplies and other resources.
opzioni.D: Monitor the planned versus actual utilization of resources and take corrective action if it goes off course.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. That's Plan Resource Management.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. That's Estimate Activity Resources.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Acquire Resources is the next step, in execution.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. That's Control Resources, later.

domande.spiegazione: Acquire Resources: obtaining team members, facilities, equipment, materials (PMBOK 6, pp. 25, 328).

domande.domanda: You've been working on a large waterfall project for some time, and one of the business analysts working with you has shown interest in taking on higher duties and moving into a project management role. What advice will you give them?

opzioni.A: Work on their soft skills for communication, conflict management and negotiation.
opzioni.B: Ensure they can create a project charter and a project management plan.
opzioni.C: Work on their knowledge and skills in technical project management, leadership, and strategic and business management.
opzioni.D: Work on contracts and procurement.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Important, but only part of the picture.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Can be taught with templates.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. The Talent Triangle: technical PM, leadership, strategic and business management.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Only a small part of PM.

domande.spiegazione: PMI Talent Triangle (PMBOK 6, p. 56).

domande.domanda: You're working as a project manager in an organization with a new project management office (PMO). The PMO advises all project managers to fulfill their numerous roles within their sphere of influence. What is your responsibility toward the organization, as part of your sphere of influence?

opzioni.A: Proactively interact with other project managers on demands for the same resources, funding priorities and the alignment of project goals with the organization.
opzioni.B: Communicate within your project.
opzioni.C: Ensure an understanding of changing market niches and standards.
opzioni.D: Educate other professionals in the organization regarding the value of project management.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Working with other PMs on resources, funding and alignment is the organizational sphere.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. That's the project sphere.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. That's the industry sphere.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. That's across disciplines.

domande.spiegazione: PM's sphere of influence (PMBOK 6, p. 52).

domande.domanda: You have just joined an organization and are about to be allocated to an existing project delivering a new human resources system. You've heard that the project is behind its delivery milestones and is over budget by $40,000 so far, and that there are multiple stakeholders with differing needs. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Create a project management plan outlining the processes for each phase.
opzioni.B: Perform a stakeholder engagement assessment to see who is sabotaging the project.
opzioni.C: Start by understanding how the organization works, including its politics and power.
opzioni.D: Meet with the project sponsor to understand why the project is off track.

domande.hint: You're new to the organization and not yet assigned.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. An existing project already has a plan.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Not assigned yet; stakeholders aren't first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Understand the enterprise environmental factors: how work actually gets done.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The sponsor doesn't manage the project.

domande.spiegazione: Understand internal EEFs, politics and power (PMBOK 6, p. 62).

domande.domanda: You're working in an organization where a large change is affecting multiple departments. You have been asked to manage this change as a project and to staff your project team with people who have sufficient leadership skills. What will you NOT look for in potential candidates?

opzioni.A: People who build trust, balance opposing goals, and apply persuasion and conflict resolution.
opzioni.B: People who give feedback constructively and accept feedback constructively.
opzioni.C: People who can describe the product, goals and objectives of the project.
opzioni.D: People who ensure the work is done their way, to get the fastest approach.

domande.hint: NOT question: which isn't a leadership quality?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect (look for it). Trust and conflict resolution are leader skills.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect (look for it). Feedback is a leader skill.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect (look for it). Communicating the vision is a leader skill.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct (NOT). A 'my way' dictatorship isn't good leadership.

domande.spiegazione: Leader qualities: integrity, vision, collaboration, appropriate influence (PMBOK 6, p. 61).

domande.domanda: You've started as a junior project manager on an internal process improvement project within your existing team. Your project manager asks you to be aware of, and use, the various forms of power available to you. What is the best type of power available to you in this situation?

opzioni.A: Situational power.
opzioni.B: Positional power.
opzioni.C: Coercive power.
opzioni.D: Informational power.

domande.hint: Junior, no position, but you know your team's process.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. You're not in a situation granting power.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. You have no formal position.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. You can't discipline or reward.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. You hold information and expert judgment from your own team.

domande.spiegazione: Forms of power (PMBOK 6, p. 63).
domande.nota: Option order reconstructed: the transcript names the four types but not the answer letter.

domande.domanda: You're working on a new waterfall project where the scope and cost have been planned upfront. As the project progresses, you notice several tasks going off track and falling behind. Luckily, these tasks are not on the critical path and have several days of float, so you can adjust their dates without affecting the overall project. What technique will you use to keep the project on track?

opzioni.A: Resource smoothing.
opzioni.B: Schedule crashing.
opzioni.C: Schedule fast tracking.
opzioni.D: Resource leveling.

domande.hint: Using existing float without moving the end date.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Smoothing uses available float without changing the critical path/end date.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Adds money and resources.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Runs activities in parallel.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Leveling can extend the schedule.

domande.spiegazione: Resource optimization (PMBOK 6, p. 211).
domande.nota: Option order reconstructed from the transcript.

domande.domanda: About a third of your project team have worked on a similar project in the past. They have gathered the requirements and created a high-level scope, and it's now time to estimate the size and effort involved. However, the customer believes things are taking too long and would like to see some progress as soon as possible. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Ask the customer to wait so you can plan the project properly.
opzioni.B: Estimate the scope using parametric estimating.
opzioni.C: Break the high-level scope into smaller parts using a work breakdown structure.
opzioni.D: Estimate the scope using analogous estimating.

domande.hint: Quick estimate from a similar past project.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Serve the customer instead.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Uses a unit rate; not the clue here.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Needed later, but you're asked to estimate now.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Analogous estimating uses similar past projects and is fast.

domande.spiegazione: Analogous estimating (PMBOK 6, p. 324).

domande.domanda: You have been asked to monitor the changes to a product before completing your next project phase. You review the control chart: the data is within the upper and lower control limits, and there is an upward trend of four data points and six points above the average line. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Proceed with the next phase, as the process is within control.
opzioni.B: Delay the next phase and rework the current release, as the process is out of control.
opzioni.C: Ask the project sponsor to validate the released deliverable.
opzioni.D: Proceed with quality testing to verify the created deliverables.

domande.hint: Rule of seven: 7+ points on one side of the mean, 5+ in a trend, or any point outside the limits.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Only 4 points trending and 6 above the mean, all within limits: the process is in control.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. None of the out-of-control rules is triggered.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. A distractor: the question is about reading the control chart, not validation.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. A distractor: verification isn't what the control chart asks you to decide.

domande.spiegazione: Control chart rules: out of control if 7+ points on one side, 5+ in one direction, or any point outside the limits (Green Belt Handbook, p. 404).

domande.domanda: You're in the process of planning the resources required for your project. Work on your project has not started, as your team is not sure what they should be doing. You decide to create the resource management plan with your team. What output do you specifically need from this plan?

opzioni.A: The stakeholder register.
opzioni.B: The project charter.
opzioni.C: The requirements traceability matrix.
opzioni.D: Roles and responsibilities, including the role, authority and competence needed.
