domande.hint: The team doesn't know what to do: which output tells them?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. It captures people involved in the project, not team roles and responsibilities.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The charter already exists and initiates the project.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. It traces requirements to scope, not resources to work.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Roles and responsibilities (role, authority, competence) is the specific output that clarifies who does what.

domande.spiegazione: Resource management plan: roles and responsibilities, with role, authority and competence (PMBOK 6, p. 318).

domande.domanda: A quality assurance manager has been hired externally to test the project and manage defects. She executed the process in the quality management plan with her testing team, and they found a high number of low-impact defects. You need to see where the biggest impacts actually are. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Use a histogram.
opzioni.B: Use a flowchart.
opzioni.C: Use a matrix diagram.
opzioni.D: Use an affinity diagram.

domande.hint: You need to count occurrences per category.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. A histogram is a bar chart counting items (here defects) per category, showing the most common.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. A flowchart shows the steps of a process.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. A matrix diagram shows relationships between groups of factors.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. An affinity diagram groups similar ideas.

domande.spiegazione: Histograms show the frequency of items per category (PMBOK 6, p. 293).
domande.nota: Option order reconstructed: the instructor reads flowchart, matrix, affinity and histogram, then answers A.

domande.domanda: The project you're working on has recently started, and the team has come together from many different parts of the organization, each with their own agenda. There are lots of small conflicts in the team and little work is getting done. The program manager asks you to use your positional power to resolve these conflicts while the team starts to find its rhythm. What will you do?

opzioni.A: Withdraw from the conflicts.
opzioni.B: Force a decision on the conflicts.
opzioni.C: Smooth and accommodate all sides in the conflicts.
opzioni.D: Problem-solve the conflicts with the team.

domande.hint: Positional power and a need for quick results.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Withdrawing doesn't resolve anything.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Forcing uses positional power to resolve conflicts quickly (win-lose), at the cost of other benefits.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Smoothing doesn't use positional power and doesn't fit the urgency.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Second best: collaboration is ideal but takes more time than you have here.

domande.spiegazione: Forcing/directing: pushing a viewpoint at the expense of others; resolves conflicts quickly (PMBOK 6, p. 349).

domande.domanda: During your project, your company was taken over by another, larger company, and the project management office and its policies were changed. The project customer has already formally accepted the deliverables, the project has completed delivery and it is ready to be closed. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Refer to the project charter for the closing procedures.
opzioni.B: Refer to the scope management plan for the acceptance of deliverables.
opzioni.C: Gather the details of the accepted deliverables, any agreements and the procurement documentation in order to close the project.
opzioni.D: The project cannot be closed, as the project outcomes need to be measured and accepted.

domande.hint: Which inputs do you need to close the project?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The charter initiates the project; closing procedures aren't there.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Acceptance has already happened.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Accepted deliverables, agreements and procurement documentation are inputs to Close Project or Phase.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Outcomes can be measured after the project, and deliverables are already accepted.

domande.spiegazione: Close Project or Phase inputs: accepted deliverables, agreements, procurement documentation (PMBOK 6, p. 126).

domande.domanda: One of your stakeholders, who has a very high influence within the company, has raised an urgent change that they want implemented within the next two weeks. You check the change management plan and see that changes can be approved by the project manager. You raise a change request and then review its impact on the project schedule and cost. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Review the configuration management plan to see which documents are baselined.
opzioni.B: Review the schedule and earned value reports for your project.
opzioni.C: Decide on the changes, approve the changes and track the changes.
opzioni.D: Review the requirements traceability matrix for requirement acceptance and sign-off.

domande.hint: In this project, you are the approver.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. You're past that stage: you already know it needs a change request.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Already done: that was the impact review.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Since the PM can approve, the next steps are decide, approve and track the change.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Not related to the change decision.

domande.spiegazione: EV reports are inputs to change control; with impact known, the approver decides, approves and tracks (PMBOK 6, p. 119).

domande.domanda: ⚠️ You're in the process of measuring the outcome of one of your deliverables on the business. The data shows that there seems to be an improvement, but the range of results is very wide; at the same time, you are able to get very clear results. Based on these results, what will you do next? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Low accuracy and high precision: the measuring equipment should be recalibrated.
opzioni.B: Low accuracy and high precision: the deliverable process should be improved.
opzioni.C: High accuracy and low precision: the measuring equipment should be recalibrated.
opzioni.D: High accuracy and low precision: the deliverable process should be improved.

domande.hint: Wide range = low accuracy; very clear results = high precision.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The diagnosis is right, but precision is already good, so measurement isn't the problem.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Results are precise but scattered: improve the process to narrow the range.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Accuracy is low (wide range), not high.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Accuracy is low and precision is high, not the opposite.

domande.spiegazione: Low accuracy = large range; precision = how exact the outcome is (PMBOK 7, p. 54).
domande.nota: Option text reconstructed from the transcript.
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: ⚠️ In the last few months, your project team has had a large amount of conflict finding their roles and place within the team. They're now starting to work together and to adjust their work habits and behaviors to support the team. As a leader, what will you do next? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Help the team work through the storming stage.
opzioni.B: Take the team back to the forming stage.
opzioni.C: Help the team use the norming stage to move into performing.
opzioni.D: Move the team to the adjourning stage.

domande.hint: Tuckman: forming, storming, norming, performing, adjourning.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The conflict (storming) is already behind them.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The team has already formed.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Adjusting behaviors to support the team is norming: help them move into performing.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Adjourning happens when the team is released at the end.

domande.spiegazione: Tuckman ladder (PMBOK 6, p. 338).
domande.nota: Option text reconstructed from the transcript.
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: You have used the project charter and statement to create the project management plan. You present the plan to key stakeholders, including the project sponsor, and you sense a high level of dissatisfaction from the customer executives: they don't believe the project will produce the results they had expected. What should you do next?

opzioni.A: Request a written statement from the customer detailing their concerns.
opzioni.B: Proceed as normal: your project plan will produce a convincing product for the customer.
opzioni.C: Arrange a change request, replan your project where necessary and go ahead with the project work.
opzioni.D: Work together with your customer to create a narrative scope statement outlining the deliverables.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Writing is tempting, but talking together resolves it better.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Proceeding with unconvinced executives will cause problems.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. You don't yet know what the dissatisfaction is about.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Defining the scope statement (description, deliverables, acceptance criteria) together aligns expectations.

domande.spiegazione: Collaborative approach plus the proper Define Scope output: the scope statement (PMBOK 6, p. 154).

domande.domanda: You have planned, executed and monitored a project to completion. The customer has just received the finished product and would like to close the project. However, the customer advises you that they're not happy with the product received, that your team didn't listen when they raised quality concerns, and that they're raising a claim against your company. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Raise a change request for their proposed changes and update the project plan.
opzioni.B: Call their bluff, take the claim to a dispute and then appeal if necessary.
opzioni.C: Review the claims process in the contract and negotiate with them to settle the claim.
opzioni.D: Review the earned value report for any impact on the schedule and cost of your project.

domande.hint: What is the preferred way to handle claims?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The project is essentially finished; this is a claim, not a change.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Disputes and litigation are a last resort.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Follow the contract's claims process and settle through negotiation.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Too late to be useful, and it doesn't address the claim.

domande.spiegazione: Claims administration: the claims process is in the contract; negotiation is the preferred settlement (PMBOK 6, p. 498).

domande.domanda: You're in the process of creating a project charter for your organization to gain resources for an automated process improvement. The project sponsor is also the functional manager in charge of the resources for that area, and she rejects your project charter, noting that you have outlined everything you want from her team but nothing about what her area will get in return. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Rework the project charter to include the benefits management plan and success measures.
opzioni.B: Escalate the project charter to the project sponsor's manager, as this project is important.
opzioni.C: Ask the project sponsor to work agile and start delivering a minimum viable product.
opzioni.D: Begin work on the requirements management plan, as this will show the sponsor how her requirements will be added and tracked.

domande.hint: She needs to see the value for her area.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Benefits, strategic alignment and success measures (ROI, payback) show what she gets.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Escalation is a last resort and may not even be available.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. You can explain the benefits without delivering anything first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. That belongs to planning, after the charter is approved.

domande.spiegazione: The charter ideally includes the benefits management plan and success measures (PMBOK 6, pp. 343-344).

domande.domanda: You're working on a complex, high-value project to replace the telecommunication system across your organization. You've created a request for quote for vendors to respond to, including source selection criteria and a statement of work, and you've already selected a seller based on multiple vendor responses. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Record the new vendor in your stakeholder register and begin engaging them to deliver the project.
opzioni.B: Draft an appropriate contract, such as fixed price incentive fee, to proceed with the implementation.
opzioni.C: Place the approved request for quote in your procurement management plan and proceed with the delivery of the project.
opzioni.D: Approach organizational senior management for approval to award the contract.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. You can't begin delivery before the award.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Tempting (the instructor picked it), but award approval comes first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. You can't proceed with delivery yet.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Complex, high-value, high-risk procurements generally need senior management approval before award.

domande.spiegazione: Conduct Procurements outputs: selected sellers; complex procurements need senior approval before award (PMBOK 6, p. 488).
domande.nota: The instructor initially chose B and got it wrong: a classic trap.

domande.domanda: You have been planning your project using a waterfall methodology and need to estimate the resources required with your team. Your project management office recently stopped using third parties or off-site workers and has mandated on-site resources only. You review the activity list based on your project scope and realize that some essential project resources currently work off-site. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Discuss the available options with the project sponsor.
opzioni.B: Perform alternatives analysis on the impact of both on-site and off-site workers for the project.
opzioni.C: Update the resource management plan with the on-site worker mandate.
opzioni.D: Update the resource calendar with the available people, locations and dates before baselining your project plan.

domande.hint: Analyze before discussing or updating plans.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Good, but you need the analysis before the discussion.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Alternatives analysis finds the best way to perform the work within the constraints.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Comes later, after the options are discussed.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Comes last in the sequence.

domande.spiegazione: Estimate Activity Resources, data analysis: alternatives analysis (PMBOK 6, p. 325). Sequence: B, A, C, D.

domande.domanda: You've been working on a project where the organization wanted only on-site workers, while you believed the project needed specific skills that were only available off-site. You worked through the various options and agreed to use the on-site workers available. As the project progresses, however, it becomes clear that the work is not being done to specification and you really do need the off-site workers. The project is going off track. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Update the issue log and the resource calendar with the resource requirements.
opzioni.B: Use problem solving with your team and negotiation with the project sponsor.
opzioni.C: Gather work performance information from your team and raise a change request.
opzioni.D: Raise a risk in the risk register and brainstorm risk responses with your team.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Logging the issue is fine but doesn't solve it.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Problem solving and negotiation are Control Resources tools to fix it.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Change requests are for impacts on baselined items, not yet here.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. It's already happening: it's an issue, not a risk.

domande.spiegazione: Control Resources: problem solving and negotiation (PMBOK 6, pp. 356-357).

domande.domanda: You're working on a very high-value infrastructure project that is critical to your organization. The team is experienced in this area after working on the project for the past 12 months. During a working group meeting, they mention they're stuck and can't implement part of the project. You raise an issue in the issue log and decide to problem-solve with your team. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Escalate the problem outside your team, as they clearly cannot move forward.
opzioni.B: Review the lessons learned register for lessons from similar past problems.
opzioni.C: Define the problem with data, identify the root cause and generate possible solutions to choose from.
opzioni.D: Raise a risk to project delivery and note the impact and likelihood of the risk.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The team is experienced; outsiders may complicate things.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Possible, but weaker than structured problem solving.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Define with data, find the root cause, generate and choose solutions.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. It's already happening: it's an issue.

domande.spiegazione: Problem solving: define the problem, find root cause, generate solutions, choose and test (PMBOK 6, pp. 295, 356).

domande.domanda: You have created a high-level project charter, which has now been approved. The project sponsor expects you to get to work straight away, but you don't know who to approach or who is available to help you with this project. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Identify stakeholders with an organizational breakdown chart and include them in your project plan.
opzioni.B: Create a RACI (resource assignment matrix).
opzioni.C: Review and update the resource calendar.
opzioni.D: Review the high-level stakeholders in the project charter and begin your project.

domande.hint: After Develop Project Charter comes Identify Stakeholders.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Identify stakeholders next; an organizational breakdown chart shows who is where.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. You can't assign people you haven't identified.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Too early: you don't know who is involved.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The charter's stakeholders are too high-level.

domande.spiegazione: Identify Stakeholders follows the charter (PMBOK 6, pp. 25, 316).

domande.domanda: You have been assigned to address the fast-moving competition that is rapidly taking market share from your company. Your executive manager advises that the company only has 12 months before jobs will be lost, but there are currently no projects to address these concerns. As a project manager, what will you do next?

opzioni.A: Ask the executive manager to come up with project ideas to address the situation.
opzioni.B: Perform benchmarking against various companies for process improvement opportunities.
opzioni.C: Create a project charter with the high-level scope, milestones and cost for approval.
opzioni.D: Create a project business case, including the business need, a situation analysis and solution options.

domande.hint: What must exist before a charter?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Only one input; you have better tools for analysis.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Good, but it feeds the business case and is less complete.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. A charter needs a business case first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. The business case defines the need, analyzes the situation and proposes options.

domande.spiegazione: Business case comes before the charter (PMBOK 6, pp. 30-31).

domande.domanda: You have just started work on a project that has been in development for the past six months. You notice it has been through a large number of project steps you are unfamiliar with, such as concept development, feasibility study, commissioning, milestone review and more. These don't match the normal phases of design, build and test. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Advise the project to reduce and update its phases for less admin and faster delivery.
opzioni.B: Ask the project to adhere to the normal phases of design, build and test, as per the guide.
opzioni.C: Adhere to the project's phases and familiarize yourself with the organization's process.
opzioni.D: Remove the phases altogether and work through waterfall delivery with one big release.

domande.hint: You're new: every organization has its own environment (EEFs).

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. You've just arrived: don't change the process before understanding it.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Phase names vary by organization; imposing the guide's names is dictating.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Respect the enterprise environmental factors and learn the organization's practices first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Removing phases is a drastic, dictated change.

domande.spiegazione: Each organization has its own politics, governance and approvals: adhere to the EEFs and learn its practices (PMBOK 6, p. 20).

domande.domanda: The project management office is looking for your help in hiring and coaching new project managers, and asks you to interview the next candidate for roles in upcoming projects. Speaking with the candidate, you find out they do not have any industry experience. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Ask them whether they prefer waterfall or agile, to see if they work the same way as your organization.
opzioni.B: Ask them whether they would like a different job within the company, with less focus on industry experience.
opzioni.C: Ask them whether they can dictate and command a team to get fast results.
opzioni.D: Ask them what their focus on a project would be: the schedule, selected financial reports or the issue log.

domande.hint: No industry experience doesn't mean no PM skills: test technical project management knowledge.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Methodology labels matter less than understanding the underlying process.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Premature: you haven't assessed their PM skills yet.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Dictatorship gets fast results at the expense of psychological safety and long-term performance.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Schedule, financial reports and issue log are the top focuses of leading PMs: this tests technical PM skills.

domande.spiegazione: Talent Triangle: technical PM, business management and leadership skills; leading PMs focus on schedule, financial reports and issue log (PMBOK 6, p. 58).

domande.domanda: Your project charter has recently been approved, and you are gathering the customer requirements that will form the basis of your project. The project customer advises that they have been burned by previous project deliveries, where the project did not deliver what they really needed. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Create an initial list of requirements as part of a solid requirements management plan.
opzioni.B: Call a focus group with the customer's experts and brainstorm requirements with them.
opzioni.C: Perform benchmarking between the area's process and external organizations.
opzioni.D: Create a requirements traceability matrix to ensure the requirements are tracked properly.

domande.hint: Want to give the customer what they need? Go to the source.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The requirements management plan is about how requirements are managed; you shouldn't write the list yourself.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Direct collaboration through focus groups and brainstorming captures what the customer really needs.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Benchmarking compares processes; it doesn't gather this customer's needs.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Useful for tracking, but first you must collect the requirements from the customer.

domande.spiegazione: Collect Requirements tools: brainstorming, interviews, focus groups, questionnaires, benchmarking (PMBOK 6, p. 138).

domande.domanda: Your deliverables have recently been quality checked by a specialist testing team and passed with flying colors. You take them to the project sponsor for approval so you can move to project closure. The sponsor accepts all the deliverables except two: one she notes as a defect, and one as a missed requirement. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Make the changes as soon as possible to avoid further delays.
opzioni.B: Raise an issue in the issue log, as this will delay your project.
opzioni.C: Raise a change request for the items, along with the reasons for non-acceptance of those deliverables.
opzioni.D: Proceed as normal, as you've delivered them as per the project needs.

domande.hint: Waterfall: changes go through checks and balances.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Changes need to go through the change control process first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. It may become an issue, but the change request comes first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Deliverables not accepted lead to change requests documenting the reasons.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. They have not been accepted, so you can't ignore them.

domande.spiegazione: Validate Scope outputs: change requests for deliverables not formally accepted, with the reasons (PMBOK 6, p. 166).

domande.domanda: You have gathered the customer requirements with your team and are finishing the creation of the scope statement. You need to baseline the project scope to ensure future changes are tracked as necessary. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Take the scope statement to the project sponsor and steering committee for approval.
opzioni.B: Ask the project sponsor to approve the project charter and the project management plan, with the included high-level scope.
opzioni.C: Update the configuration management plan with the scope statement as a baselined document.
opzioni.D: Create the work breakdown structure and the WBS dictionary with your team.

domande.hint: The scope baseline is more than the scope statement.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The scope statement alone isn't the full baseline.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Too high-level for a scope baseline.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The baseline needs more than the scope statement.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. With the scope statement done, create the WBS and WBS dictionary to complete the scope baseline.

domande.spiegazione: Scope baseline: scope statement, WBS, WBS dictionary and work packages (PMBOK 6, pp. 161-162).

domande.domanda: You've been planning your project using a waterfall methodology. The project team has collected the requirements from the customer, who is eager to begin work as soon as possible. You set a meeting with the business analysts in your team to create the scope statement based on these requirements. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Include the scope description, deliverables, acceptance criteria and exclusions.
opzioni.B: Include the scope description, the work breakdown structure and the WBS dictionary.
opzioni.C: Include the scope management plan, the statement of work and the requirements traceability matrix.
opzioni.D: Include the project charter, the project management plan and the accepted deliverables.

domande.hint: Don't confuse the scope statement with the scope baseline.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. These are the contents of the project scope statement.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. That's the scope baseline.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. These are other documents (process, procurement, traceability).
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Important documents, but not the scope statement contents.

domande.spiegazione: Project scope statement: description, deliverables, acceptance criteria, exclusions (PMBOK 6, p. 154).

domande.domanda: You've been assigned to a project that is behind schedule. Some of your team members approach you and ask what they should be working on. You check with your team, and one of your senior analysts recommends you work together to create the work breakdown structure dictionary. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Create a scope breakdown with unique identifier, description and acceptance criteria.
opzioni.B: Work with the senior analyst to create a resource assignment matrix instead, and coach them on the difference between a resource assignment matrix and a WBS dictionary.
opzioni.C: Gather the project scope and break it down into smaller work packages.
opzioni.D: Create a scope breakdown with unique identifier, description and resource requirements.

domande.hint: What does the team actually need to know? Who works on what.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. That's a WBS dictionary: the trap suggested by the analyst.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. A RAM shows who is assigned to each work package, answering the team's question.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Good practice, but doesn't tell people what they should work on.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Also a WBS dictionary variant: still not an assignment matrix.

domande.spiegazione: A RAM shows the connections between work packages/activities and team members (PMBOK 6, pp. 162, 317).
domande.nota: Trick question: the instructor warns about it.

domande.domanda: The project charter has been approved, and you've identified the stakeholders you'll be working with and who will be impacted. As the project progresses, you notice multiple stakeholders who seem to be actively trying to sabotage your project and your efforts. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Review the stakeholder engagement assessment matrix and invite feedback from those who are resistant.
opzioni.B: Remove the people who seem to be slowing your project from your project team.
opzioni.C: Escalate the problem stakeholders to their functional managers for disciplinary action.
opzioni.D: Review the impact/influence matrix to determine how to engage with the stakeholders.

domande.hint: Find who is resistant, then engage them.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. The engagement matrix (unaware, resistant, neutral, supportive, leading) shows who is at risk; then invite their feedback.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. You often can't remove stakeholders: you must bring them on board.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Escalation may win their minds but not their hearts.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Shows power and impact, not who is resistant.

domande.spiegazione: Assess engagement and gather feedback, then use communication and interpersonal skills (PMBOK 6, pp. 521, 527).

domande.domanda: Your project involves nearly a dozen teams dispersed around the country at different sites, with thousands of impacted stakeholders. The executives in these areas are concerned about the changes the project will bring and are starting to push back on your planning efforts. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Create the project charter and arrange for sign-off by the executives.
opzioni.B: Create the communications management plan to ensure their communication needs are met.
opzioni.C: Raise a change request for the project to co-locate all the teams.
opzioni.D: Create the requirements traceability matrix, so you can trace the executives' requirements back to the scope you deliver and keep them engaged.

domande.hint: The project is already under way: how do you meet their information needs?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The project is in progress, so the charter is already approved.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. The communications management plan addresses stakeholders' communication requirements.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Costly, may not be possible and doesn't address the concerns.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Useful, but you still need to communicate in the right way.

domande.spiegazione: Communications management plan: stakeholder communication requirements, timely distribution of information (PMBOK 6, p. 377).

domande.domanda: A number of risks have been raised on your project. You performed qualitative analysis to get a subjective risk rating, but your project customer is not satisfied: they would like you to perform additional qualitative risk analysis beyond impact and likelihood. What will you analyze next?

opzioni.A: Simulation, sensitivity analysis and decision tree analysis.
opzioni.B: Cost of failure, cost of appraisal and cost of prevention.
opzioni.C: Executive needs, political needs and promotion needs.
opzioni.D: Urgency, proximity and strategic impact of the risks.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. These are quantitative analysis techniques.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. That's cost of quality.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. A distractor: not risk parameters.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Other qualitative parameters include urgency, proximity, dormancy, manageability, controllability, detectability, strategic impact.

domande.spiegazione: Assessment of other risk parameters (PMBOK 6, pp. 423-424).

domande.domanda: One of the risks on your project is significantly large and could seriously impact your company if it ever came about. It has captured the attention of high-ranking executives, who have each proposed a response and each think theirs is the best. You decide to settle the argument with a decision tree. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Rate the risks for their probability and impact and get a rating for each.
opzioni.B: Note each of the options on a vertical bar chart for their impact sensitivity on cost.
opzioni.C: Note the various response options with their cost impact and their probability of occurrence.
opzioni.D: Perform an in-depth simulation of all the responses against multiple criteria to test their impact.

domande.hint: A decision tree combines costs and probabilities along branches.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. That's qualitative analysis.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. That's a tornado diagram (sensitivity analysis).
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Options with their cost/benefit and outcome probabilities, to choose the best path.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. That's Monte Carlo simulation.

domande.spiegazione: Decision tree analysis (PMBOK 6, p. 435).

domande.domanda: You've recently become a project manager in a large organization and you're not sure what to expect. Your colleague tells you that the organization is large enough to have a substantial project management office (PMO), and that it is a directive PMO. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Collaborate with the other project managers in the PMO to find a project that suits your skill set.
opzioni.B: Get started on a business case in your work area to initiate a project.
opzioni.C: Await assignment to a project by the PMO.
opzioni.D: Review the project management frameworks, templates and tools mandated for use by the PMO.

domande.hint: Supportive, controlling, directive: which one manages projects directly?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. In a directive PMO you don't choose your project.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. You don't have that autonomy here.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. A directive PMO directly manages projects and assigns project managers.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. That describes a controlling PMO.

domande.spiegazione: PMO types: supportive (templates), controlling (compliance), directive (manages projects, assigns PMs) (PMBOK 6, p. 48).

domande.domanda: ⚠️ The project customer approaches you, as they are worried that the project is not delivering fast enough. You review the project schedule and cost to see how the project is tracking: the actual cost (AC) is $648,000, the earned value (EV) is $601,000 and the planned value (PV) is $629,000. How is the project performing? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Ahead of schedule and under budget.
opzioni.B: Ahead of schedule and over budget.
opzioni.C: Behind schedule and over budget.
opzioni.D: Behind schedule and under budget.

domande.hint: SV = EV - PV; CV = EV - AC.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. EV < PV means behind schedule, and EV < AC means over budget.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. EV < PV means behind schedule.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. SV = 601 - 629 = -28k (behind schedule); CV = 601 - 648 = -47k (over budget).
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. EV < AC means over budget.

domande.spiegazione: Earned value analysis (PMBOK 6, p. 261).
domande.nota: The transcript quotes SV -38,000 and CV -28,000: the values here are recomputed from the figures.
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: The people and resources involved in your project are currently costing a large amount of money, and your project sponsor comments about it frequently. You check how the project is tracking: the planned value (PV) is $840,000, the earned value (EV) is $795,000 and the actual cost (AC) is $755,000. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Use the project contingency reserves.
opzioni.B: Raise a change request to reduce the project scope and bring the cost back on track.
opzioni.C: Reduce the project resources to bring the project cost back on track.
opzioni.D: Add more resources to bring the project schedule back on track.

domande.hint: Check the data, not the perception.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. You're under budget: no need for reserves.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Cost isn't the problem.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Cost isn't the problem, and fewer resources would slow you further.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. SV = -45k (behind), CV = +40k (under budget): you can afford more resources to recover the schedule.

domande.spiegazione: Variance analysis: SV = EV - PV, CV = EV - AC (PMBOK 6, p. 262).

domande.domanda: ⚠️ Team members from other parts of the organization have been assigned to your project at an agreed level of 50% availability. As the project progresses, you notice they are being pulled back into their normal roles, and that your project is falling behind schedule. What will you do next? — ⚠️ Note: debatable: the instructor sees more than one valid answer.

opzioni.A: Talk with the project steering committee and arrange for more resources to assist your project.
opzioni.B: Talk with the functional managers and negotiate clear, written assignments with reliable scheduling priorities.
opzioni.C: Raise a risk to project delivery and assign it to the functional managers.
opzioni.D: Raise an issue in the issue log and bring it up at the next project working group.

domande.hint: Manage it yourself, directly and collaboratively.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Escalation may come later, not first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Direct negotiation with functional managers, with written, reliable commitments.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. It's already happening: it's an issue, not a risk.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Logging is fine, but waiting for the next meeting is too slow.

domande.spiegazione: Interpersonal and team skills: negotiation with functional managers (PMBOK 6, pp. 332-333).
domande.nota: The instructor considers B and D close.
domande.motivo_incertezza: debatable: the instructor sees more than one valid answer

domande.domanda: You've been planning a project with the manager of a functional area who needs to increase their profit by 57% in the next three years, and you're helping him put together a business case. He has come up with 18 different project ideas to reach the goal, but they would take approximately seven years. The manager pushes you to find a way to do them all in three years. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Prioritize the ideas based on impact and cost, noting each as required, desired or optional in the business case.
opzioni.B: Advise the manager that good things take time to deliver.
opzioni.C: Add the appropriate cost for extra resources to your project plan to get all the work done.
opzioni.D: Set a meeting with the functional area experts and ask them to pick the top ideas for delivery.

domande.hint: When everything is a must-have, bring a proper process.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. The business case analyzes options with decision criteria such as required, desired, optional.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Dismissive and unhelpful.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Needs approval, and doesn't prioritize.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. People pick pet projects: prioritize by impact and cost instead.

domande.spiegazione: Business case: situation analysis with criteria (required, desired, optional) (PMBOK 6, p. 31).

domande.domanda: Your project charter has been approved, and your stakeholder analysis reveals multiple impacted, highly paid executives with the power to influence your career. As you approach some of these stakeholders, they raise their concerns about the project, how it's progressing and what it involves. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Perform an impact/influence analysis on all your stakeholders.
opzioni.B: Create your project management plan and review its details regularly with the impacted and influential stakeholders.
opzioni.C: Circulate the signed project charter to anyone who needs convincing that the project is needed.
opzioni.D: Reduce your communication with most stakeholders: they can't resist what they don't know about.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Already done: that's how you identified them.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Developing the plan and reviewing it regularly with them supports engagement.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The charter only authorizes; it doesn't address ongoing concerns.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. It backfires: it's always better to communicate more.

domande.spiegazione: Develop Project Management Plan; review with stakeholders regularly (PMBOK 6, p. 82).

domande.domanda: You have just created your project management plan and are reviewing it with your stakeholders. It includes the subsidiary plans for scope, schedule, cost, resource and quality management. Some stakeholders raise concerns that they cannot see what needs to be baselined, or how project performance and changes will be measured. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Advise your stakeholders that the information they need is in the subsidiary plans.
opzioni.B: Meet as often as needed with your project stakeholders to increase their engagement and acceptance of your project.
opzioni.C: Show them the project budget timeline, with the costs projected on a schedule.
opzioni.D: Create the configuration management plan, the change management plan and the performance measurement baseline with your team, and include them in your project management plan.

domande.hint: Which plan components cover baselines and changes?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Those subsidiary plans don't contain it.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Doesn't answer the baseline question.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Only one part of the picture.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Configuration plan = what's baselined; change plan = how to process changes; PMB = integrated scope-schedule-cost baseline.

domande.spiegazione: Additional project management plan components (PMBOK 6, p. 88).

domande.domanda: Part of your project work needs to be outsourced to a supplier. You are asked to ensure that the cost of the outsourced portion of the project does not exceed $1.2 million, and if the work comes in under cost and ahead of schedule, you may pay additional money to the supplier. What sort of contract will you work with your procurement office to prepare?

opzioni.A: A firm fixed price (FFP) contract.
opzioni.B: A fixed price incentive fee (FPIF) contract.
opzioni.C: A cost plus fixed fee (CPFF) contract.
opzioni.D: A cost plus award fee (CPAF) contract.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. One fixed price, no incentive.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. FPIF has a price ceiling (costs above are the seller's) and incentives tied to agreed metrics.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Cost reimbursable: no ceiling.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. No ceiling, and the award is subjective.

domande.spiegazione: Contract types (PMBOK 6, p. 471).

domande.domanda: You take the completed scope to your project sponsor for acceptance. The sponsor advises that she cannot accept the deliverables, as she doesn't know the outcomes of testing, nor whether the scope met her requirements or needs further changes. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Set a meeting with the project sponsor directly to address her concerns.
opzioni.B: Review the requirements traceability matrix and show the sponsor how each requirement is met by the project scope.
opzioni.C: Review the quality report together with your testing lead and note which items may need change requests, if any.
opzioni.D: Review the project's change requests to show the sponsor whether any corrective actions needed to be made.

domande.hint: Her question is about testing outcomes.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Good approach, but you need the testing data.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Contains little testing information.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. The quality report summarizes control quality findings and corrective action recommendations.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Useful, but not focused on testing outcomes.

domande.spiegazione: Quality reports (PMBOK 6, p. 296).

domande.domanda: Multiple unforeseen events have set your project behind schedule, and in trying to bring it back on track you have spent a considerable amount of money. Now the project sponsor has threatened to stop the project unless they can see how much it will cost by the time it is finished. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Perform a reserve analysis on the remaining contingency and management reserves.
opzioni.B: Create a project estimate at completion (EAC) and compare it to the budget at completion (BAC).
opzioni.C: Calculate the to-complete performance index (TCPI) with your team to meet your project goal.
opzioni.D: Review the cost performance index (CPI) to see how the project cost is tracking.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Doesn't give the total cost.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. EAC forecasts total cost at completion; compare it with the original BAC.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. TCPI is an efficiency index, not a total cost.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. CPI shows efficiency to date, not a final figure.

domande.spiegazione: Cost forecasts: EAC vs BAC (PMBOK 6, pp. 264, 269).

domande.domanda: Your project plan includes an estimate of how long the project will take (via the project schedule), how much it will cost and the resources that will be required. The project sponsor believes the project can be done with around 34% fewer resources. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Dismiss the sponsor's comments as uneducated and proceed with your plan as is.
opzioni.B: Reduce the resources in your project plan so the project can meet the sponsor's expectations.
opzioni.C: Create a basis of estimates with your project team and review it with the sponsor to agree on a way forward.
opzioni.D: Raise a risk to project delivery in the risk register, in case the plan goes ahead with fewer resources.

domande.hint: Direct and collaborative: make estimates transparent.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Loses the sponsor's support.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. You don't know the impact yet.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. The basis of estimates explains assumptions, constraints and ranges so you can agree together.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Doesn't manage the situation now.

domande.spiegazione: Basis of estimates (PMBOK 6, p. 204).

domande.domanda: You're working at Stratus Innovations, where leadership proposes the delivery of a new customer platform that will impact multiple teams. It needs to be released before October next year, and multiple experts from other systems or teams may be involved. Leadership asks how this initiative should be managed. What will you tell them?

opzioni.A: Manage it as a portfolio.
opzioni.B: Manage it as a program.
opzioni.C: Manage it as a project.
opzioni.D: Manage it as part of ongoing operations.

domande.hint: A temporary endeavor, with a deadline, that creates a unique result.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. A portfolio groups projects, programs and operations to achieve strategic objectives; this is a single initiative.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. A program coordinates multiple related projects to obtain benefits not available managing them separately; here there's one initiative.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. A project is a temporary endeavor that creates value through a unique product, service or result: it has a deadline and a defined outcome.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Operations are ongoing, repetitive activities, not a temporary initiative with an end date.

domande.spiegazione: Projects are initiated to create value by producing tangible or intangible deliverables (Standard for PM, p. 12).
domande.nota: Option order reconstructed: the instructor reads portfolio, project, program, operations and answers C (project).

domande.domanda: ⚠️ Daniel is the project manager for Fintrust Solutions, preparing the business case for a new mobile banking platform. As part of the document, he identifies the expected outcomes, including increased transaction revenue, improved customer satisfaction and a better brand reputation. How should Daniel categorize these benefits in the business case? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: All of them are tangible benefits.
opzioni.B: All of them are intangible benefits.
opzioni.C: The revenue increase is intangible; customer satisfaction and brand reputation are tangible.
opzioni.D: The revenue increase is tangible; customer satisfaction and brand reputation are intangible.

domande.hint: Can it be measured directly in financial terms?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Customer satisfaction and brand reputation are hard to express in financial terms, so they are not tangible.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Revenue is money: it can be measured in financial terms, so it is tangible.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. It's the other way around.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Revenue is measurable in money (tangible); satisfaction and reputation are hard to express financially (intangible).

domande.spiegazione: Tangible benefits: profitability, equity, market share. Intangible: brand recognition, customer satisfaction, employee well-being (Standard for PM, p. 14).
domande.nota: Option text reconstructed from the instructor's commentary.
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: You're the project manager at Secure Bank Corporation, implementing a new online banking platform. While developing the project management plan, you identify items such as regulations, organizational culture and IT infrastructure that may influence the project. How should you account for these factors in your project management plan?

opzioni.A: Treat them as enterprise environmental factors.
opzioni.B: Treat them as project risks.
opzioni.C: Include them as part of the scope baseline.
opzioni.D: Treat them as project deliverables.

domande.hint: Conditions not under the team's control that influence the project.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. EEFs are conditions not directly controlled by the team that impact, constrain or direct the project.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. They're existing conditions, not uncertain future events.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. They're not work the project delivers.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The project doesn't produce them.

domande.spiegazione: Enterprise environmental factors (Standard for PM, p. 18).

domande.domanda: Rose is the project manager at TCS, implementing a new internal reporting system. The PMO requires her to use a standard project management plan template and to follow established procedures from previous projects. She reviews these templates and guidelines to ensure consistency with organizational practices. How should Rose classify these templates and procedures?

opzioni.A: Enterprise environmental factors.
opzioni.B: Project deliverables.
opzioni.C: Organizational process assets.
opzioni.D: Project assumptions.

domande.hint: Templates, procedures and knowledge repositories of the organization.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. EEFs are external or internal conditions (regulations, culture, market), not templates and procedures.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. They're inputs used by the project, not outputs.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. OPAs include the plans, processes, templates and knowledge repositories of the performing organization.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. They're established, documented assets, not assumptions.

domande.spiegazione: Organizational process assets (Standard for PM, p. 19).
domande.nota: Option order reconstructed.

domande.domanda: You're the project manager at Build Max Engineering, working on a large infrastructure project. The organization assigns you as the project manager, provides dedicated project resources and gives you full authority over the project budget and decision making. What type of organizational structure are you working in?

opzioni.A: Balanced matrix organization.
opzioni.B: Weak matrix organization.
opzioni.C: Project-oriented organization.
opzioni.D: Functional organization.

domande.hint: Who holds authority over budget and resources?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. In a balanced matrix authority is shared between PM and functional managers.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. In a weak matrix the PM has little authority.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. In a project-oriented organization the PM has high authority over team, resources and budget.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. In a functional organization the functional manager holds authority.

domande.spiegazione: Influence of organizational structures on projects (Standard for PM, p. 22).
domande.nota: Option order reconstructed.

domande.domanda: Liam works as a manager in the sales department at Prime Manufacturing and would like to start a process improvement initiative. The project team members are already within his team, but Liam has no additional budget or authority. What type of organizational structure is Liam working in?

opzioni.A: Weak matrix organization.
opzioni.B: Functional organization.
opzioni.C: Project-oriented organization.
opzioni.D: Balanced matrix organization.

domande.hint: The project is run inside an existing functional team.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Close, but a weak matrix still has some project coordination role.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. In a functional organization the project is done within the functional team, with no dedicated budget or resources.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. There's no high PM authority here.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Authority isn't shared: there's no project budget at all.

domande.spiegazione: Functional organizations: project done within an existing functional team (Standard for PM, p. 22).

domande.domanda: Sophia is the project manager at Tech Bridge Solutions, leading a system implementation project. During planning, she performs activities such as coordination, collaboration and applying expertise, as well as providing support for the delivered product. Which function is NOT associated with projects?

opzioni.A: Providing oversight and coordination.
opzioni.B: Facilitating and supporting.
opzioni.C: Applying expertise.
opzioni.D: Performing ongoing operational support for the delivered product.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. (Associated) Oversight and coordination is a project function.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. (Associated) Facilitating and supporting is a project function.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. (Associated) Applying expertise is a project function.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. (NOT associated) Ongoing operational support is day-to-day operations, not a temporary project.

domande.spiegazione: Functions associated with projects (Standard for PM, pp. 22-26).

domande.domanda: An employee in the organization secures funding for the project, provides strategic direction and helps remove organizational obstacles to ensure project success. What role is this person performing in the project?

opzioni.A: Product owner.
opzioni.B: Project sponsor.
opzioni.C: Project customer.
opzioni.D: Project manager.

domande.hint: Who provides resources and is accountable for enabling success?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The product owner sets direction for an agile team through the product backlog.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. The sponsor provides resources and support and is accountable for enabling success.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The customer receives the benefits but doesn't usually fund or remove organizational blockers.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The PM leads the team delivering the work but doesn't secure funding.

domande.spiegazione: Sponsor (Standard for PM; PMBOK 8, p. 274).

domande.domanda: ⚠️ Roi is part of the project management team at Trans Global Logistics, working on a system upgrade project. The team collaborates with stakeholders and managers to align with organizational objectives and secure resources. While other activities have also been considered, which of the following is something the project management team would do? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Provide duration and cost estimates on the deliverables.
opzioni.B: Coordinate with functional managers for demands on critical resources.
opzioni.C: Verify that the deliverables meet their quality requirements.
opzioni.D: Approve the final product on behalf of the customer.

domande.hint: Project team vs project management team.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Estimating deliverables is done by the project team doing the work.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. The PM team negotiates with other PM teams and functional managers on critical resources and priorities.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Done by the project/quality team.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Acceptance is the sponsor's or customer's role.

domande.spiegazione: Interaction between the PM team and project aspects (Standard for PM, p. 29).
domande.nota: Options C and D reconstructed.
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: You're working with a project sponsor in the early stages of a cloud platform implementation at CSI. As you put the business case together, the sponsor asks when the project will begin delivering value. What will you tell them?

opzioni.A: The project value will be realized after the project is fully completed.
opzioni.B: The project benefits can be realized during the project execution phases.
opzioni.C: The project value will be realized once the benefits are formally measured.
opzioni.D: Value can be realized throughout the project, at the end of the project, or following project completion.

domande.hint: Not only at one point in time.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not only at the end.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. True, but not only during execution.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Measurement confirms value; it doesn't create it.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Value can be delivered throughout, at the end or after completion, whenever deliverables are used.

domande.spiegazione: Focus on value (Standard for PM, p. 41).

domande.domanda: You're the project manager on a chip fabrication project at NG Micro Devices. A functional manager raises concerns about the quality of the deliverables being passed to their department and wants assurance that standards will be consistently met. How will you manage this on your project?

opzioni.A: Quality should be verified through a final inspection before delivery.
opzioni.B: Quality should be integrated into processes to consistently achieve the target quality thresholds.
opzioni.C: Quality should be managed separately from project processes to ensure independence.
opzioni.D: Quality should focus on correcting defects after they are identified.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Inspection catches defects late; it doesn't ensure consistency.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Embedding quality in processes and deliverables keeps a consistent focus on thresholds.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Quality must be part of project processes.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Reactive: defects should be prevented.

domande.spiegazione: Embed quality into processes and deliverables (Standard for PM, p. 43).

domande.domanda: Raphael is managing a government mega project at SGI involving multiple vendors. A conflict arises between vendor teams over shift allocations and rotations, creating tension and affecting productivity. The issue is now starting to affect project deliverables. How should Raphael address this situation?

opzioni.A: Force the vendors to follow the agreed contract terms.
opzioni.B: Let the vendors resolve the issue on their own.
opzioni.C: Facilitate discussions to identify the root causes and agree on a solution.
opzioni.D: Assign your best team member to manage the conflict.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Possible, but forcing doesn't resolve the conflict's cause.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Passive: the PM must be proactive.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Collaboration resolves the conflict and removes friction harming quality and productivity.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. It's the PM's job, not to be delegated.

domande.spiegazione: Be an accountable leader (Standard for PM, p. 48).

domande.domanda: You're in the planning phase of a refinery expansion project at Petrocore Energy Limited. An executive manager raises concerns about increasing staffing costs and several risks identified early in the project. What will you tell them about cost and risk on the project?

opzioni.A: Cost and staffing are highest at the beginning, while risk and uncertainty increase toward project completion.
opzioni.B: Cost and staffing gradually decrease, while risk remains constant.
opzioni.C: Cost and staffing increase as the work progresses and drop near completion, while risk and uncertainty decrease over time.
opzioni.D: Cost and staffing remain stable throughout the project, while risk and uncertainty fluctuate unpredictably.

domande.hint: Think of the classic graph: one curve rises, the other falls.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Inverted: costs start low and uncertainty starts high.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Costs don't decrease from the start, and risk doesn't stay constant.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Costs are low at the start, peak during execution and drop at the end; uncertainty is highest early and decreases.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. There's a predictable pattern.

domande.spiegazione: Impact of variables over time (Standard for PM, p. 59).

domande.domanda: Dr. Mitchell is managing a drug development project at EB Incorporated. The project operates in a highly regulated environment with phase-gate approvals: scope, schedule, cost and risks are defined early, and strict change control with extensive upfront planning is required. Which development approach is being used?

opzioni.A: Adaptive approach.
opzioni.B: Incremental approach.
opzioni.C: Hybrid approach.
opzioni.D: Predictive approach.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Adaptive welcomes change through iterations.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Incremental delivers in increments.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. No adaptive element is described.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Predictive (waterfall) fits when scope can be stabilized early.

domande.spiegazione: Predictive approaches (Standard for PM, p. 61).
domande.nota: Option order reconstructed.

domande.domanda: Jason is leading a mobile application project at Blue Peak Digital Solutions. The team works in short iterations, delivering features regularly and refining its approach based on feedback. One person is responsible for the approved scope and its value to the organization. Which development approach is being used?

opzioni.A: Adaptive approach.
opzioni.B: Predictive approach.
opzioni.C: Hybrid approach.
opzioni.D: Incremental approach.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Adaptive (agile) delivers in iterations, uses feedback; the product owner owns scope and value.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Predictive delivers in one go.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. No predictive element is described.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Incremental delivers increments but without iterative refinement from feedback.

domande.spiegazione: Adaptive approaches (Standard for PM, p. 63).

domande.domanda: Ethan is working on a project at Westgate Group that will deliver a new enterprise platform. The software component has constantly evolving requirements, while the data center infrastructure is built using upfront planning and a formal change control approach. The two parts are brought together in a final sprint at the end. Which development approach is being used?

opzioni.A: Predictive approach.
opzioni.B: Hybrid approach.
opzioni.C: Incremental approach.
opzioni.D: Adaptive approach.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Only the infrastructure part is predictive.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Combines adaptive and predictive elements.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Only part is incremental.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Only the software part is adaptive.

domande.spiegazione: Hybrid approaches (Standard for PM, p. 65).
domande.nota: Option order reconstructed.

domande.domanda: ⚠️ You've just taken over as project manager of the Orion CRM upgrade project, where many stakeholders are not available, others are disengaged and the success criteria are unclear. These conditions are an example of: — ⚠️ Note: debatable: the instructor sees more than one valid answer.

opzioni.A: Project constraints.
opzioni.B: Issues to be managed.
opzioni.C: Leading indicators.
opzioni.D: Lagging indicators.

domande.hint: Signals of what may go wrong in the future.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. They aren't limits on the project.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. They must be managed, but the concept tested is the indicator.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Leading indicators signal upcoming changes or trends that may put performance at risk.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Lagging indicators measure results already achieved.

domande.spiegazione: Leading indicators (PMBOK 8, p. 14).
domande.nota: The instructor considers B close.
domande.motivo_incertezza: debatable: the instructor sees more than one valid answer

domande.domanda: You've been assigned to lead a new patient record system project at CHS. The business case has been approved and the key stakeholders have been identified. Senior leadership wants the project to start immediately and without delay. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Develop the project management plan to define how the project will be executed.
opzioni.B: Hold a kickoff meeting with the team.
opzioni.C: Work with the project sponsor to approve the project charter.
opzioni.D: Perform a make-or-buy analysis to determine the resources to be used.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The plan is developed in planning, after the project is authorized by the charter.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Tempting, but the project isn't authorized yet.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. The charter formally authorizes the project and gives the PM authority over resources.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. A distractor: make-or-buy is a procurement decision, not the next step to start the project.

domande.spiegazione: Initiate Project or Phase (PMBOK 8, p. 17).

domande.domanda: You've been hired to manage a retail expansion initiative. As planning begins, the cost of some materials rises significantly. Senior stakeholders raise concerns about the cost versus the value the project will deliver, and whether it is still worthwhile. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Review the project management plan.
opzioni.B: Review the financial management plan.
opzioni.C: Review the project charter.
opzioni.D: Review the business case.

domande.hint: Which document assesses cost versus benefit?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. It says how the project is managed, not if it's worthwhile.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. It's the process for managing finances.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The charter authorizes the project; it doesn't assess cost versus value.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. The business case is the economic feasibility study.

domande.spiegazione: Business case (PMBOK 8, pp. 17, 116).

domande.domanda: Elijah is initiating a data center expansion project at QGS. Early planning relies on uncertain factors, such as utility availability and the accuracy of vendor timelines. As Elijah documents the initial estimates for cost and duration, what will he NOT do?

opzioni.A: Note the uncertain factors in the assumption log.
opzioni.B: Add the uncertain factors to the issue log.
opzioni.C: Add the uncertain factors to the risk register.
opzioni.D: Add the uncertain factors to the basis of estimates.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. (He would do it) These are assumptions underlying the estimates.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. (He would NOT do it) Issues are events that have occurred; these haven't.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. (He would do it) Uncertainties belong in the risk register.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. (He would do it) They affect the estimates.

domande.spiegazione: Assumption log, risk register and issue log (PMBOK 8, pp. 17, 114).

domande.domanda: ⚠️ You're managing a large infrastructure project at Granite Works Engineering. You've held a kickoff meeting with the project team, and multiple team leads have provided their high-level strategies. You want to put them in a single document that can be changed and configured over time. What will you do next? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Create the configuration management plan.
opzioni.B: Create the project management plan.
opzioni.C: Create the change management plan.
opzioni.D: Update the project charter.

domande.hint: Which document integrates all the subsidiary strategies?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Handles version control, not strategy integration.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. It integrates all subsidiary plans and specifies execution, monitoring and closure.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Defines the change control process.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The charter is high-level and initiates the project.

domande.spiegazione: Integrate and align project plans (PMBOK 8, pp. 18-19).
domande.nota: Option D reconstructed.
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: A project team at Redwood Industrial Systems is preparing to acquire specialized components. They're defining evaluation criteria and contract types, and deciding whether to build internally or outsource the work. No vendors have been contacted yet. What should the project manager do next?

opzioni.A: Issue procurement documents and request proposals from vendors.
opzioni.B: Evaluate vendor proposals and select the best supplier.
opzioni.C: Develop the sourcing strategy, including make-or-buy decisions.
opzioni.D: Advertise the opportunity to gather additional vendors.

domande.hint: First decide whether to outsource at all.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Procurement documents are issued only after the sourcing strategy is defined.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. No vendors have been contacted, so there are no proposals to evaluate.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Plan Sourcing Strategy documents sourcing decisions, the selection approach and make-or-buy.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Advertising comes after deciding to outsource and defining the strategy.

domande.spiegazione: Plan Sourcing Strategy (PMBOK 8, pp. 19-20).

domande.domanda: A project requires outsourcing specialized engineering work. Multiple vendors have expressed interest in submitting a proposal, but each has a different idea of what the project is about. What should the project manager do now to get everyone on the same page?

opzioni.A: Conduct a bidder conference.
opzioni.B: Clarify the source selection criteria.
opzioni.C: Perform a make-or-buy analysis.
opzioni.D: Use advertising for the proposal.

domande.hint: Same information to all prospective sellers.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. A bidder conference gives all sellers the same information and clarifications.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Criteria explain how you'll choose, not what the project is.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Decides whether to outsource.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Ensures fairness of visibility, not shared understanding.

domande.spiegazione: Bidder conferences (PMBOK 8, pp. 19-20, 265).
domande.nota: Option order reconstructed.

domande.domanda: Irene is preparing a large infrastructure project at West Core Development. Different teams propose conflicting approaches for acquiring materials and services, causing delays in procurement planning. Irene needs to align the overall approach, including contract types and supplier selection methods. What should she do now?

opzioni.A: Develop the project bid documents.
opzioni.B: Perform a make-or-buy analysis.
opzioni.C: Develop the statement of work.
opzioni.D: Develop the sourcing strategy plan.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. They don't define the approach.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Decides whether to buy.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Defines the work, not the approach.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. It documents sourcing decisions and the source selection approach.

domande.spiegazione: Sourcing strategy plan (PMBOK 8, pp. 20, 141).

domande.domanda: Ricky is planning a manufacturing project at Trade Corporation. A critical component can be produced internally or sourced from a specialized supplier. Internal stakeholders are pushing to begin work as quickly as possible, and there is limited budget for additional items. What will Ricky do next?

opzioni.A: Develop the procurement management plan.
opzioni.B: Conduct a cost-benefit analysis.
opzioni.C: Perform a make-or-buy analysis.
opzioni.D: Issue a request for proposal.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The process for procurement, not the decision.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Good, but make-or-buy is the specific decision tool.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Make-or-buy analyzes requirements against internal production or purchase.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Only after deciding to buy.

domande.spiegazione: Make-or-buy analysis (PMBOK 8, pp. 19-20, 180).

domande.domanda: Aiden is managing a facilities upgrade at CM Holdings. The project requires standard electrical components with clearly defined specifications. Multiple suppliers are available at different price points, causing confusion and delays in the selection process. What should Aiden do?

opzioni.A: Conduct a bidder conference.
opzioni.B: Issue a request for proposal (RFP).
opzioni.C: Issue a request for information (RFI).
opzioni.D: Issue a request for quote (RFQ).

domande.hint: Standard product, price is the deciding factor.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Specs are already clear.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. RFP is for complex solutions.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. RFI gathers information.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. RFQ is used when price is the main factor and the solution is readily available.

domande.spiegazione: RFQ (PMBOK 8, pp. 20, 248).
domande.nota: Option order reconstructed.

domande.domanda: Rina is executing a warehouse automation project at Grid Line Logistics. Several modifications have been requested throughout the project, and there is now confusion about what should be implemented and in what sequence. What will Rina do next?

opzioni.A: Review the scope statement.
opzioni.B: Review the change log.
opzioni.C: Review the issue log.
opzioni.D: Review the risk register.

domande.hint: Where are change requests and their status tracked?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. May not yet reflect approved changes.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. The change log records changes and their status.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The issue log tracks problems that occurred, not requested changes.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Future risks, not requested changes.

domande.spiegazione: Manage Project Execution; change log (PMBOK 8, pp. 22, 116).

domande.domanda: You're managing a production system upgrade at Ironworks Manufacturing. During execution, your team is delivering outputs, implementing approved changes and tracking performance data. A stakeholder raises concerns about the consistency and reliability of the outputs being produced. What will you do?

opzioni.A: Reassess the scope and quality plans to improve output consistency.
opzioni.B: Ensure the deliverables are produced according to the defined scope baseline.
opzioni.C: Raise these concerns with the steering committee.
opzioni.D: Complete a full analysis of the quality risks being raised.

domande.hint: Execution means delivering per the plan and baseline.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Reviews the processes, not the outputs.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Manage Project Execution ensures deliverables meet scope requirements.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Avoid escalating what the PM can handle within execution.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Slower and less direct.

domande.spiegazione: Manage Project Execution (PMBOK 8, pp. 22-23).

domande.domanda: ⚠️ A project team at CD Solutions is developing a customer analytics platform. Midway through execution, a security officer reports unauthorized access to sensitive project data, which could cause problems with the deliverables in the future. What should the project manager do first? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Record the breach in the issue log.
opzioni.B: Brainstorm ways to handle the security breach with the team.
opzioni.C: Escalate the breach to senior managers within the organization.
opzioni.D: Record the breach in the risk register.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. A problem that has already occurred is an issue: record it in the issue log so it can be tracked and managed before further action.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Right, but only after logging the issue so it can be tracked and managed.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Avoid escalation unless outside your authority.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The breach has already happened: it's an issue, not a future risk.

domande.spiegazione: Issue log (PMBOK 8, pp. 22-23, 123).
domande.nota: Option D reconstructed.
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: Omar is managing a pharmaceutical packaging project at NCL. Quality inspections repeatedly identify defects caused by inconsistent procedures across shifts, leading to rework and delays. Omar wants to address the underlying cause and improve consistency moving forward. What should Omar do next?

opzioni.A: Update the team's work instructions.
opzioni.B: Implement check sheets.
opzioni.C: Assign a quality lead.
