spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Uncontrolled expansion of scope without adjusting time, cost or resources.

domande.spiegazione: Scope creep (PMBOK 8, p. 273).

domande.domanda: Matthew is reviewing several system upgrade proposals. Each option requires a different investment and delivers different financial returns, and the project sponsor would like to prioritize them by return on investment (ROI): Proposal A 45%, Proposal B 90%, Proposal C 135%, Proposal D 110%. Which proposal should be chosen?

opzioni.A: Proposal A (45%).
opzioni.B: Proposal B (90%).
opzioni.C: Proposal C (135%).
opzioni.D: Proposal D (110%).

domande.hint: For ROI, NPV, IRR and BCR higher is better; only payback is better when shorter.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. 45% is the lowest return.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Lower than C and D.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. 135% is the highest ROI.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Good, but lower than C.

domande.spiegazione: ROI = net gain / investment x 100 (PMBOK 8).

file.titolo: 150 PMBOK 7 Scenario-Based PMP Exam Questions and Answers

domande.domanda: You have been assigned to a new project where the work is behind schedule and the team are not working together. The team is relatively new and conflicts are arising. Team members are blaming each other for the work not done, and some people are not showing up to work on the project at all. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Meet with the functional manager of that area to agree on team members' time requirements.
opzioni.B: Meet with your team to set a team charter and define roles and responsibilities.
opzioni.C: Meet with the project sponsor to gain additional funding for resources who can work together.
opzioni.D: Escalate the issue to the steering committee as soon as possible as a project risk.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Time commitments don't address the conflict or blame.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. A team charter and clear roles create a collaborative team environment.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. New people won't guarantee no conflict: managing it is the PM's job.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. It's already happening (an issue) and should be managed before escalating.

domande.spiegazione: Create a collaborative team environment: team agreements, roles and responsibilities (PMBOK 7, pp. 28-29).

domande.domanda: You have recently completed a project for a new product and have been asked to manage it after it's released, to keep it relevant in today's marketplace. However, half of your existing team are rolling off to other projects and the project budget is nearly depleted. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Create a business case and a project charter for your project sponsor to approve.
opzioni.B: Retain as many of your current project staff as possible to continue work on the product.
opzioni.C: Raise a change request for your current project to add scope and continue making changes.
opzioni.D: Secure funding for a stable team, then use current research to form a suite of projects to improve the product.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Fits one specific project, not ongoing product management.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. There's no money left to pay them.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The project is ending: adding scope isn't the way.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Product management uses a stable team, funded over the product life cycle.

domande.spiegazione: Product management considerations (PMBOK 7, pp. 17-19).

domande.domanda: You're delivering a critical change and several key stakeholders in your organization have added seemingly unnecessary steps for you to take, with extra approvals, reports and meetings. They're also restricting the people you need from working on your project in a larger capacity. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Go directly to the people you need, to avoid extra back and forth with the stakeholders.
opzioni.B: Raise a risk in the risk register on the lack of access to sufficient resources.
opzioni.C: Communicate more often with the stakeholders and gain a deeper awareness of their ideas and situation.
opzioni.D: Show your stakeholders the resource assignment matrix and the project roles and responsibilities.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Going behind their backs damages the relationship.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Logging a risk doesn't manage it.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Stakeholders add steps or restrict people when not engaged: communication and awareness help.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. May win minds but not hearts: they still aren't engaged.

domande.spiegazione: Effectively engage with stakeholders (PMBOK 7, pp. 32-33).

domande.domanda: You're managing a project team made up mostly of men. Recently, Jane was hired for her high expertise in the brands that make up your industry. You notice she has been left out of some key meetings and others are overlooking her opinions. You also notice she's paid significantly less than her male colleagues. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Take steps to update her pay to the same range as the others on your project, and ask for her opinion and advice specifically during each meeting, along with others in your team.
opzioni.B: Take the lower pay as a win for your project, as it will help keep costs low; her colleagues don't need to know.
opzioni.C: Ask Jane to write down her knowledge of the industry just in case she leaves.
opzioni.D: No need to rock the boat: this is just how people work in this industry.

domande.hint: Stewardship: fairness in pay, opportunity and treatment.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Respectful engagement includes fair compensation, access to opportunity and treatment.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Unfair and destroys engagement when discovered.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Capturing knowledge is fine but doesn't fix the unfairness.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Accepting the status quo isn't stewardship.

domande.spiegazione: Be a diligent, respectful and caring steward (PMBOK 7, p. 25).

domande.domanda: During one of your working group meetings, a stakeholder raises the concern that the product you're working on will be discontinued in the next 5 months. You were not aware of this, and your project budget has already been approved until the scheduled delivery, which is also in five months. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Keep the project going as it is: the discontinued product isn't your responsibility.
opzioni.B: Set a meeting with your project sponsor to share the information and a recommendation to terminate the project.
opzioni.C: Change the scope of the project to meet a different product, so your project can remain relevant.
opzioni.D: Ask for additional funding to see if you can improve the product instead of discontinuing it.

domande.hint: Value is the primary motivator for a project.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Stewardship means acting on this information.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. If the project no longer aligns with the business need, the organization may terminate it.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. A project is initiated for a specific purpose; changing it entirely needs a new project.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Speculative and may not reverse the decision.

domande.spiegazione: Focus on value (PMBOK 7, p. 35).

domande.domanda: You've collected the requirements for your project and you're creating the scope statement and the work breakdown structure. During this process, you notice some functionality in your database system that would help a different project you're aware of in your project management office. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Place the feature in the other project's backlog and ask them to prioritize it as soon as possible.
opzioni.B: Raise the functionality in your risk register as a threat, with a response to mitigate.
opzioni.C: Add the scope to your project and complete it as soon as possible.
opzioni.D: Raise the functionality in your risk register as an opportunity with a response to exploit, and meet with the other project's team and sponsor to discuss.

domande.hint: Systems thinking: it's a positive risk.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. You can't add to another team's backlog without talking to them.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. It's an opportunity, not a threat.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Your team isn't the expert in that product.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Make the opportunity known and exploit it, collaborating with the other project.

domande.spiegazione: Respond to system interactions (PMBOK 7, pp. 39, 129).

domande.domanda: You're working on a high-profile project. Several high-ranking senior executives want to take the credit for this initiative while limiting the impact on their own resources. This has led to several conflicts and a scope statement that is unclear, leading to a risk of project failure. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Create the scope statement yourself to avoid further conflict.
opzioni.B: Facilitate a discussion with the executives as a neutral third party, focusing on agreed project goals.
opzioni.C: Limit your project resources to the executives until they can agree on a way forward.
opzioni.D: Escalate the issue to the project steering committee and ask them to resolve the problem.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Without their agreement it may never be accepted.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Neutral facilitation helps more than recommendations when senior managers conflict.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Wastes funded resources.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Manage it first before escalating.

domande.spiegazione: Demonstrate leadership behaviors (PMBOK 7, p. 42).

domande.domanda: You're managing a project where the majority of the product has been planned upfront, but an external system is needed from a vendor in partial pieces, where the requirements are unclear. Half of your stakeholders want to use a waterfall approach, and the other half are advocating for an agile approach. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Use an agile methodology: the fixed scope is low risk and you can capture the changes using agile.
opzioni.B: Use a waterfall methodology and ask the team to plan the uncertain scope better.
opzioni.C: Proceed with a hybrid method, with pre-planned scope but agile ceremonies that promote feedback.
opzioni.D: Use a combination of waterfall and agile to capture all the requirements and keep stakeholders happy.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Ignores the upfront-planned part.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Uncertain scope can't simply be planned better.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Hybrid uses predictive and adaptive only where each fits; tailoring is iterative.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Similar, but 'hybrid' tailored to context is the precise answer.

domande.spiegazione: Tailoring (PMBOK 7, pp. 44-46).

domande.domanda: You're working on a project where senior users have been testing the product as parts are released. They have found some missing requirements and defects. Their manager is worried that the project won't deliver a product that is fit for purpose, without defects and within the time frame needed. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Perform some of the testing yourself to ensure a quality product.
opzioni.B: Help every team member focus on quality, from correct acceptance criteria to a developed and tested product.
opzioni.C: Limit testing until the very end of the project, so you can do it all in one go when the product is completely ready.
opzioni.D: Increase the testing on your project and add more testing resources, so no defect goes unnoticed.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The PM is the conductor, not the tester.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Builds quality into processes and deliverables across the team.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Agile tests at all levels throughout.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Throws resources at it without building quality in.

domande.spiegazione: Build quality into processes and deliverables (PMBOK 7, pp. 47-49).

domande.domanda: You are working through the risk assessment with your team, who are having trouble coming up with ideas for risks. You decide to give them some guidance on the types of complexity that might affect your new product. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Ask them to brainstorm qualitative and quantitative risks.
opzioni.B: Ask them to perform the 5 Whys and Ishikawa (root cause) analysis.
opzioni.C: Ask them to brainstorm around possible unwanted human behavior, system behavior, ambiguity and technical innovation impacts.
opzioni.D: Ask them to perform a retrospective to discover what isn't working well and what still puzzles them.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Doesn't guide them on complexity.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Root cause tools for an existing problem.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Complexity comes from human behavior, system interactions, uncertainty, ambiguity and innovation.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Reviews past work, not future risks.

domande.spiegazione: Navigate complexity (PMBOK 7, pp. 50-51).

domande.domanda: You discover a negative risk with a potential impact of $2,000,000. Stakeholders decide it is within their risk appetite, provided a risk threshold of 10% is met. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Note the acceptable risk level as a threat of $200,000.
opzioni.B: Note the acceptable risk level as a threat of $1.8M to $2.2M.
opzioni.C: Note the impact as outside the acceptable risk level of $2,000,000.
opzioni.D: Note the impact as an opportunity of $200,000.

domande.hint: The threshold is a variation around the objective.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. $200,000 is the size of the variation, not the acceptable range.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. A 10% threshold around $2M gives an acceptable range of $1.8M to $2.2M.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Stakeholders said it is within their appetite.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. It's a threat, not an opportunity.

domande.spiegazione: Risk appetite = uncertainty stakeholders accept; risk threshold = acceptable variation around an objective (PMBOK 7, p. 54).
domande.nota: Same question as waterfall-100 id 11.

domande.domanda: A risk has been raised about insufficient building materials. A response assigned to the functional manager suggests using a brand-new, not fully tested material. Half of the stakeholders support it; the other half refuse to sign off. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Suggest a quantitative risk approach to give a more accurate financial impact.
opzioni.B: Suggest they proceed with the proposed response and ensure it is followed through.
opzioni.C: Suggest a different risk owner, as an executive may have more power to respond.
opzioni.D: Suggest a different risk response, as responses should be timely, cost-effective, realistic and agreed by relevant stakeholders.

domande.hint: What characteristics should a good risk response have?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. More analysis isn't needed yet; the response itself is the problem.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. You can't force it while half the stakeholders disagree.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. An executive could force it through, but the disagreement may have good reasons.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. A response must be appropriate, cost-effective, realistic, agreed by stakeholders and owned.

domande.spiegazione: Risk responses should be timely, cost-effective, realistic, agreed by relevant stakeholders and owned by a responsible person (PMBOK 7, p. 54).
domande.nota: Same question as waterfall-100 id 12.

domande.domanda: Your project went off track due to uncertainty in requirements and resources. You reined it in at significant cost, and the PMO asks you to brainstorm with the team how to prevent it happening again. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Ask the team to increase the contingency reserve to allow for these impacts.
opzioni.B: Ask the team to change the methodology from waterfall to agile.
opzioni.C: Ask the team to use short feedback loops, continuous improvement and transparent planning.
opzioni.D: Ask the team to check their work twice before sending it on.

domande.hint: How does a team embrace adaptability and resiliency?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. More money doesn't improve the way of working.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Changing methodology doesn't magically remove uncertainty.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Short feedback loops, continuous improvement and transparent planning build adaptability and resiliency.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Possible, but much weaker than C.

domande.spiegazione: Embrace adaptability and resiliency: short feedback loops, continuous learning, inspection and adaptation, transparent planning, prototypes (PMBOK 7, p. 56).
domande.nota: Same question as waterfall-100 id 13.

domande.domanda: As your project progresses, many business stakeholders voice concerns, question the changes and even miss key meetings, trying to sabotage your efforts. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Communicate the vision and benefits of the change clearly, along with the impact on their work.
opzioni.B: Create an impact/influence chart to determine who should be engaged.
opzioni.C: Escalate to the sponsor and arrange for different stakeholders.
opzioni.D: Map the current state and proposed future state of the change for the stakeholders.

domande.hint: Resistance to change usually comes from a lack of understanding.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Communicating vision, benefits and impact early reduces resistance and change fatigue.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Useful, but it doesn't address people questioning the change.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Stakeholders usually can't be replaced: work with them.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Close (it's problem solving), but communication is the key to engagement here.

domande.spiegazione: Change management: communicate vision, goals and benefits early, with the impact on work processes (PMBOK 7, p. 59).
domande.nota: Same question as waterfall-100 id 14.

domande.domanda: Analyzing stakeholders with an impact/influence chart, you find more than 100 groups and over 3,000 impacted stakeholders. Other parts of the project are falling behind as you try to keep up. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Ask the project team to engage different groups so everyone is covered.
opzioni.B: Clearly prioritize the stakeholders, then engage and communicate with the highly impacted and influential groups early and often.
opzioni.C: Monitor stakeholders for signs of stress and respond to the most stressed groups.
opzioni.D: Create a SharePoint page that any stakeholder can consult at any time.

domande.hint: Too many stakeholders to engage effectively: what's the key word?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Splitting the work makes sense, but isn't the specific technique.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. When there are too many to engage effectively, prioritization is key.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. It's a kind of prioritization, but less complete than B.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Good pull communication, but doesn't solve the overload.

domande.spiegazione: Stakeholder engagement: identify, understand and analyze, prioritize, engage, monitor (PMBOK 7, pp. 11-12).
domande.nota: Same question as waterfall-100 id 15.

domande.domanda: Your project has mostly used pull communication with the customer. Monitoring engagement, you notice stakeholders are unclear on the impacts or benefits. You decide to add push communication. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Create a SharePoint web page with all the project information.
opzioni.B: Push for more funding and communicate this to the sponsor.
opzioni.C: Push stakeholders to engage in more two-way communication.
opzioni.D: Send a weekly email to stakeholders with a project update, including impacts and benefits.

domande.hint: Push = sent to recipients; pull = they fetch it.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. A web page is pull communication.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Right keyword, wrong meaning: funding isn't the issue.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Right keyword, but it isn't push communication.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. A sent email is push communication.

domande.spiegazione: Push: memos, emails, status reports, voicemail. Pull: bulletins, web pages, whiteboards (PMBOK 7, p. 13).
domande.nota: Same question as waterfall-100 id 16.

domande.domanda: You have taken over a project with a vendor where scope and requirements have been missed, and miscommunication is common. You set an extremely important meeting with your team and the vendor's team. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Speak slowly and clearly to the vendor's team, at a louder volume if necessary.
opzioni.B: Confirm they heard your message, determine whether they agree and identify any nuanced or unintended messages.
opzioni.C: Only communicate with the vendor in writing to have a trail of proof.
opzioni.D: Prepare a claim for the mishandled scope through the procurement team.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Volume doesn't improve understanding.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Quick feedback loops confirm the message was heard, agreed and correctly interpreted.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Writing loses tone and body language and is more easily misread.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Fix the communication first.

domande.spiegazione: Feedback loops: confirm the message was heard, check agreement, identify nuances (PMBOK 7, p. 13).
domande.nota: Same question as waterfall-100 id 17.

domande.domanda: Stakeholders seem engaged, but frequent changes to scope and requirements are causing delays, with issues raised and multiple feedback rounds. You're not sure who or what is causing it. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Perform root cause analysis with the team to brainstorm the problem.
opzioni.B: Raise a risk for the project delay and review responses with the team.
opzioni.C: Review the issue log, risk register and change log for the most frequent requesters, then update your engagement approach for them.
opzioni.D: Ensure the budget has enough contingency reserve for the reviews and delays.

domande.hint: Frequent changes may signal stakeholders who are not aligned. How do you find out who?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Good, but C goes further: it finds the who and acts on it.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. It's an issue already happening, not a risk.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. The logs reveal which stakeholders drive the changes, so you can engage them better.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Don't just throw money at it.

domande.spiegazione: Many changes may mean stakeholders aren't engaged/aligned; issue and risk registers reveal challenges with individual stakeholders (PMBOK 7, p. 15).
domande.nota: Same question as waterfall-100 id 18.

domande.domanda: A manager leads in a dictatorship style; the team has stopped making suggestions, sick days have increased and work has slowed. You suggest servant leadership. What will they do next?

opzioni.A: Serve the team as much as possible, ensuring their every need is met.
opzioni.B: Focus on obstacle removal, encouragement and development opportunities.
opzioni.C: Ensure team members serve one another and help each other succeed.
opzioni.D: Serve the team new ways of doing the work and engage them through variety.

domande.hint: Servant leadership = removing blockers and growing people.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Sounds good, but servant leaders don't meet every need.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Obstacle removal, diversion shielding, encouragement and development are servant leadership behaviors.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Good practice, but not servant leadership specifically.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Right keywords, wrong meaning.

domande.spiegazione: Servant leaders enable self-organization and autonomy, remove obstacles, shield the team and offer development (PMBOK 7, p. 18).
domande.nota: Same question as waterfall-100 id 19.

domande.domanda: You have been allocated to a new team with members from different functional areas, few of whom have worked on a project before. Miscommunication and rework are causing delays. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Set a daily stand-up so they update what they completed.
opzioni.B: Review the resource assignment matrix to ensure they are doing their job.
opzioni.C: Help the team set its vision and objectives, roles and responsibilities, and team operations.
opzioni.D: Send team members on training in their roles.

domande.hint: A newly formed team needs clarity first.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Could help, but doesn't create shared clarity.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Could help, but is control rather than team development.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Vision, roles and ways of working (e.g. a team charter) build a one-team mindset.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Good, but the issue is alignment, not individual skill.

domande.spiegazione: Teams formed across organizations need upfront work: shared vision, clear roles, ways of working (PMBOK 7, p. 18).
domande.nota: Same question as waterfall-100 id 20.

domande.domanda: You have collected the requirements for your project, matched them to the project scope, and broken them down into smaller parts and the activities required. In doing this, you notice that the manager of the marketing department has added extra scope that is unrelated to your current project. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Raise the incorrect scope items and their impact, and start an open dialogue with the functional manager.
opzioni.B: Override the marketing manager's decision on scope, as you're the senior project manager.
opzioni.C: Raise a change request for the additional scope and let the change control board (CCB) decide.
opzioni.D: Place the additional scope into the product backlog for the product owner to prioritize.

domande.hint: Maybe it was a mistake or previously approved.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Open dialogue and courage are key to a positive team culture.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Forcing the decision damages the relationship.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. First understand whether a change is even needed.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Talk it through first: it may belong to another project.

domande.spiegazione: Project team culture (PMBOK 7, p. 21).

domande.domanda: Your project team are protected by a union agreement. You notice that they don't know how to use the product you're improving: they're slow to respond and regularly complain about the work. Your project sponsor has had enough and threatens to shut down the project if improvements can't be made. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Set up a new project with different team members and transfer the project work to that team.
opzioni.B: Set a clear project purpose and vision, and pair your team with a customer to show them how they're making a positive difference.
opzioni.C: Tell your project team that they will lose their jobs.
opzioni.D: Create a project Gantt chart, schedule and burndown chart so the work is transparent to all.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not feasible and may produce the same result.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Vision and seeing their impact increase intrinsic motivation.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Threats entrench the behavior.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Transparency doesn't fix low engagement.

domande.spiegazione: Leadership skills: vision and motivation (PMBOK 7, pp. 24-25).

domande.domanda: During a key scope meeting, an argument arises. The business manager accuses the technology manager of not delivering to their needs on past projects, and the technology manager accuses the business manager of changing requirements that impact the delivery schedule. The meeting is at risk, with the stakeholders closed off to any further discussion. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Take the side of the technology manager, as scope that impacts delivery should be controlled.
opzioni.B: Take the side of the business manager, as we should always deliver to the customer's specification.
opzioni.C: Facilitate to keep the communication respectful, focus on the issue in the present, and search for alternatives together.
opzioni.D: Ensure they both agree to the change control process, to avoid disagreements in the future.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Both views have some truth.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Both views have some truth.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Handled well, conflict leads to better decisions.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Useful later, after resolving the present conflict.

domande.spiegazione: Conflict management (PMBOK 7, p. 29).

domande.domanda: You're working on a project where the project team is completely distributed around the country, in multiple sites and including people working from home. Some of the project's team members have not been able to contribute to the project, and there are concerns from the program that the project will fall behind. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Raise a request to the program to co-locate all your project team members as soon as possible.
opzioni.B: Proceed with daily stand-ups and working group meetings with any team members in your area.
opzioni.C: Set team leaders for each area around the country to report back to you as the centralized project leader.
opzioni.D: Use technology to maintain ongoing contact, with audio and video for meetings and a team website to keep all project information available.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Rarely feasible.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Excludes the others.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Keeps silos.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Technology and transparency keep a distributed team connected.

domande.spiegazione: Distributed project teams (PMBOK 7, p. 30).

domande.domanda: ⚠️ You are initiating a project for a sales team where the process will change significantly, even though the outcome of a completed sale will remain the same. The functional manager is concerned about the change and any disruption that it might bring. What will you do next? — ⚠️ Note: debatable: the instructor sees more than one valid answer.

opzioni.A: Kick off the project with multiple deliveries, to deliver small parts and reduce the change impact.
opzioni.B: Kick off the project with a single delivery at the end of the project, when the process change is complete.
opzioni.C: Kick off the project with continuous delivery in mind, to ensure fast delivery to the business.
opzioni.D: Kick off the project using periodic deliveries, delivering value as it's ready.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. A single process is changed as a whole.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Process re-engineering may deliver only near the end when the new process rolls out.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Doesn't fit a single process change.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Doesn't fit a single process change.

domande.spiegazione: Delivery cadence (PMBOK 7, p. 34).
domande.nota: The instructor finds A and B close.
domande.motivo_incertezza: debatable: the instructor sees more than one valid answer

domande.domanda: You're working on a project where the requirements are clear but the solution ideas are uncertain. The product owner and the technical experts can't be sure which ideas will work in practice and which ones won't. The organization can't afford to get this project wrong, as they have previously made mistakes and customers are starting to leave. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Use an incremental approach.
opzioni.B: Use an iterative approach.
opzioni.C: Use a predictive approach.
opzioni.D: Use a hybrid approach.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Releasing increments risks scaring customers.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Iterative captures changing ideas while delivering in one release.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Doesn't refine uncertain solutions.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. No mix of approaches needed.

domande.spiegazione: Development approaches (PMBOK 7, p. 37; Agile Practice Guide, p. 18).
domande.nota: Option order reconstructed.

domande.domanda: You're working on a new product for your organization where the requirements are complex and likely to change a few times as the project progresses. The organization also needs usable parts of the product to be released as fast as possible, to capture some of the market they're aiming for away from their competitors. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Use an iterative approach.
opzioni.B: Use a predictive approach.
opzioni.C: Use an adaptive approach.
opzioni.D: Use a hybrid approach.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Releases only once.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Plans upfront, single delivery.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Adaptive (agile) combines iterative and incremental, refining with feedback.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. No predictive part needed.

domande.spiegazione: Adaptive approach (PMBOK 7, p. 35).

domande.domanda: A new project has been kicked off in your organization following a recent government inquiry into your industry, which found multiple processes with significant regulatory oversight that need to change. The inquiry ordering these changes has given you a due date of 10 months' time before you start incurring penalties. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Proceed with an agile development approach to deliver change as quickly as possible.
opzioni.B: Proceed with a hybrid development approach to respond to changes while planning upfront.
opzioni.C: Proceed with a predictive development approach.
opzioni.D: Proceed with an iterative methodology to improve using feedback.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Documentation and demonstration needs favor predictive.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Possible, but regulation points to predictive.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Significant regulatory oversight may require predictive for process documentation and demonstration.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Possible, but regulation points to predictive.

domande.spiegazione: Considerations for selecting a development approach (PMBOK 7, p. 40).
domande.nota: Option order reconstructed.

domande.domanda: Your organization is moving to an agile way of work. Your project team are strongly opposed to using agile, as they've been burned using iterations when executives used the team's velocity to try to force them to work faster instead of keeping a sustainable pace. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Add extra resources to your team to deliver faster and avoid executives getting involved.
opzioni.B: Proceed with a predictive development approach and deal with the consequences later.
opzioni.C: Ask your team to work with agile velocity and iterations despite their hesitations.
opzioni.D: Suggest the team uses flow-based scheduling, with a Kanban board for visual work.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Doesn't address their concern.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The organization is moving to agile.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Forcing lowers engagement.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Flow-based scheduling doesn't use sprints or velocity; it optimizes delivery on capacity.

domande.spiegazione: Flow-based scheduling (PMBOK 7, p. 45).

domande.domanda: Your team have not worked on projects before and don't know about waterfall, agile or any of the different models. Your project may also have requirements that are certain or uncertain, with varying levels of risk, so you're not sure which approach to use. As you begin this new project, what will you do next?

opzioni.A: Use waterfall and plan everything upfront, so the team have more stability.
opzioni.B: Use general phase definitions such as feasibility, design, build, test, deploy and close.
opzioni.C: Use agile to ensure you can respond to change while your team's capability increases.
opzioni.D: Don't use any project approach: it doesn't matter as long as the work gets done.

domande.hint: Phases common to every life cycle.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Assumes certainty.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. All projects go through these phases: once in waterfall, repeatedly in agile.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Assumes uncertainty.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. A process works better.

domande.spiegazione: Life cycle and phase definitions (PMBOK 7, p. 42).

domande.domanda: You're a project manager in an organization with a directive project management office, and you're currently between projects. The PMO asks you to prepare for an upcoming project in the accounting area by meeting with the functional manager there. You have no team, no scope, no requirements and no timeline as yet. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Ask the functional manager for their wish list of improvements so you can take these to your PMO.
opzioni.B: Create a project management plan so the project scope, budget and schedule are clearer.
opzioni.C: Create a small backlog of work and start your first sprint, then progressively update the backlog as the project progresses.
opzioni.D: Progressively elaborate the vision statement and project charter to define a coordinated approach.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not a basis to start a project.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The project doesn't exist yet.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. No direction yet.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Before initiating, start with a vision statement, charter or business case.

domande.spiegazione: Planning overview (PMBOK 7, p. 52).

domande.domanda: You're working on a project where part of the project delivers a high-value, high-risk component, and another part delivers a routine change to the system. Your project sponsor wants to gain the business value quickly, but your project team want to start with the work they're familiar with first. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Prioritize the high-risk items at the end of the project.
opzioni.B: Prioritize the high-risk items at the start of the project.
opzioni.C: Use an incremental approach and deliver part of the routine and part of the high-risk work in each sprint.
opzioni.D: Plan out the work in detail and secure a scope baseline with formal change controls to reduce the uncertainty.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Risk grows if left late.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Novel or risky work early reduces uncertainty before large investment; routine work can wait.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Doesn't reduce risk early.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Doesn't address uncertainty.

domande.spiegazione: Delivery: last responsible moment (PMBOK 7, p. 54).

domande.domanda: You are working on an agile project where the functional manager you're delivering to only has a high-level idea of the system requirements they'll need. The functional manager suggests a work breakdown structure; however, your team feel it is more suited to a predictive (waterfall) delivery approach. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Create and use a work breakdown structure anyway, as it's just a tool.
opzioni.B: Use rolling wave planning: keep the work at a high level until you're ready to work on it, then plan it in detail.
opzioni.C: Note the high-level themes or epics, decompose them into features, and again into user stories.
opzioni.D: Ask the functional area for more detailed requirements before the project begins.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Possible, but not agile-centric.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Possible, but less specific.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Epics → features → stories is decomposition fitting an incremental approach.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Collaborate to elaborate requirements.

domande.spiegazione: Delivery, decomposition (PMBOK 7, p. 54).

domande.domanda: You're at the beginning of planning a new project. You have researched and gathered the requirements from the area and broken them down into deliverables and activities, which you believe could take 26 weeks to deliver. The project sponsor is asking you for an estimate of how long the project will take. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Tell the project sponsor 26 weeks.
opzioni.B: Tell the project sponsor you'll use an iterative approach where value is delivered until the project stops.
opzioni.C: Tell the project sponsor approximately 24 to 28 weeks.
opzioni.D: Tell the project sponsor approximately 20 to 45 weeks.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Too precise for so little information.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. An estimate is still needed.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Range too narrow at this stage.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Early estimates have a broad range (about -25% to +75%) that narrows as knowledge grows.

domande.spiegazione: Estimating, range (PMBOK 7, p. 55).

domande.domanda: ⚠️ After gathering your project requirements and scope and breaking them down into activities, you need to estimate the project schedule with your team. After some analysis and discussion, your team come up with a range of 53 to 75 days across all tasks. What will you do next? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Note it as high accuracy and low precision.
opzioni.B: Note it as low accuracy and high precision, and ensure estimates become more accurate as the project unfolds.
opzioni.C: Note it as high confidence and low precision.
opzioni.D: Note it as low confidence and high precision.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. A wide range is low accuracy.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Wide range = low accuracy; days = precise units.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Mixes concepts.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Mixes concepts.

domande.spiegazione: Estimating: accuracy, precision, confidence (PMBOK 7, p. 54).
domande.nota: Option text reconstructed.
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: You are working on a business case, knowing that your industry is undergoing significant change at the moment and that there could be many different impacts on your project benefits before the project is fully delivered. Your project sponsor asks you for the best estimate of benefits you can give under the circumstances. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Ask your team for a probabilistic estimate.
opzioni.B: Ask your team for a deterministic estimate.
opzioni.C: Ask your team for an absolute estimate.
opzioni.D: Ask your team for a relative estimate.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Ranges with probabilities (e.g. confidence levels) suit uncertain numbers.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. A single specific number.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. A specific actual number.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Compares items; for user stories.

domande.spiegazione: Presenting estimates (PMBOK 7, p. 57).

domande.domanda: You've noted 9 epics for delivery as part of your most recent project. Your team have broken these epics down into user stories and would like to see the effort involved for these deliverables. You ask your team to find the smallest user story, size it as 1, and then determine the size of the other cards based on how they compare to that original card. What approach are you taking?

opzioni.A: Relative estimating with your team.
opzioni.B: Deterministic estimating to determine the effort.
opzioni.C: Absolute estimating.
opzioni.D: Probabilistic estimating.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Sizing in comparison to other estimates.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. A single point value.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Actual units.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Ranges with probabilities.

domande.spiegazione: Relative estimating (PMBOK 7, p. 57).

domande.domanda: You're working on a project where a competitor is also working on a similar feature, and being first to market will have a significant impact on this year's profit. Your product owner would like to measure how quickly story cards are being completed once they start being developed. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Measure lead time.
opzioni.B: Check the Gantt chart.
opzioni.C: Measure cycle time.
opzioni.D: Check the schedule network and precedence diagram.

domande.hint: From start of work to done.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Lead time runs from request to delivery.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Not this.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Cycle time is the elapsed time for one unit through the process.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. For critical path and dependencies.

domande.spiegazione: Flow-based estimating (PMBOK 7, p. 58).
domande.nota: Option order reconstructed.

domande.domanda: You're working on a project that has recently moved to a more agile way of work. The team have not completely taken on the Scrum approach, however, and are comfortable working with a more flow-based approach, moving user stories across a Kanban board. You want an estimate of how much work can be completed in the next three months, based on the team's existing progress. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Multiply the velocity by the number of remaining user stories.
opzioni.B: Multiply the cycle time by the throughput.
opzioni.C: Multiply the lead time by the schedule performance index.
opzioni.D: Multiply the planned value by the actual value.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Velocity is Scrum.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Flow-based estimates come from cycle time and throughput.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. A distractor.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. EVM, not flow.

domande.spiegazione: Flow-based estimating (PMBOK 7, p. 58).

domande.domanda: ⚠️ Your product owner wants to bring the next feature forward so that it is done in parallel with the current feature, but still released in the existing feature order. You make the necessary adjustments to the product backlog and decide to adjust the product roadmap, which you have visualized as a Gantt chart. What will you do next? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Use a schedule lead and change the features to finish-to-start.
opzioni.B: Use a schedule lag and change to finish-to-finish.
opzioni.C: Use a schedule lead and change the features to finish-to-finish.
opzioni.D: Use a schedule lag and change to start-to-start.

domande.hint: Bring forward but keep finish order.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. FS doesn't allow parallel work.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. A lag delays, not brings forward.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Lead brings it forward; FF keeps the delivery order.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. A lag delays.

domande.spiegazione: Schedule lead and lag (PMBOK 7, p. 59; PDM PMBOK 6, p. 190).
domande.nota: Option text reconstructed.
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: You're working on a project where you have been completing the deliverables in sequence, and the project work is starting to fall behind. The project sponsor asks you to speed up the work and reduce the time for the project to be delivered, but also makes it very clear that there is no more money to use when speeding up the work. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Use schedule crashing.
opzioni.B: Use schedule fast tracking.
opzioni.C: Use leads and lags.
opzioni.D: Use resource leveling.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Crashing adds cost.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Fast tracking performs sequential activities in parallel.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Too unspecific.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Leveling may lengthen the schedule.

domande.spiegazione: Fast tracking and crashing (PMBOK 7, p. 59).
domande.nota: Option order reconstructed.

domande.domanda: After reviewing your project schedule, you notice you are three weeks behind and the schedule needs to be compressed. Your project does not have enough budget to crash the schedule. You check with the lead for each area and review the schedule to see whether they can fast track their deliverables. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Fast track the activities with discretionary dependencies.
opzioni.B: Fast track the activities with industry-regulated dependencies.
opzioni.C: Fast track the activities with external dependencies.
opzioni.D: Fast track the activities with mandatory dependencies.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Based on project preferences: might be modifiable.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Regulatory needs can't be changed.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Usually can't be modified.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Usually can't be modified.

domande.spiegazione: Dependencies and compression (PMBOK 7, p. 60).
domande.nota: Option order reconstructed: discretionary is read last but the transcript gives 'A'.

domande.domanda: Your team are new to agile and have previously been working with waterfall. Your key customer asks you for a project schedule. The project team believe that a project schedule belongs to the old waterfall way of working and that they shouldn't have to create one. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Create a project Gantt chart to visualize the activities within the project.
opzioni.B: Determine the project's planned versus actual value instead of working with a schedule directly.
opzioni.C: Advise the customer that you don't need to plan ahead in an adaptive way of work.
opzioni.D: Ask your team to develop a high-level release plan, like a product roadmap, showing the features to be included in each upcoming release.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Possible, but less agile-centric.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Variance, not a schedule.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Agile still plans.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Adaptive planning uses a high-level release plan with features per release.

domande.spiegazione: Adaptive schedule planning (PMBOK 7, p. 61).

domande.domanda: ⚠️ You're working in a project team that has recently moved to an agile way of work. Your business analysts want to gather the requirements and solutions, match them to the scope, and create a work breakdown structure for the whole deliverable. Your product owner says this will take too long and is not agile enough for their needs. What will you do next? — ⚠️ Note: debatable: the instructor sees more than one valid answer.

opzioni.A: Ask your team to review the scope management plan for the proper process.
opzioni.B: Break the deliverable down into smaller pieces so you can deliver them faster.
opzioni.C: Ask your team to time-box work on the highest-priority items in the backlog, update the estimates and then reprioritize them as necessary.
opzioni.D: Review the project charter for the high-level scope, then use it to begin delivery quickly.

domande.hint: Time boxes on a prioritized backlog.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not adaptive.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Pieces must be usable and prioritized.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Adaptive approaches use time boxes and a prioritized backlog.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Still needs proper planning.

domande.spiegazione: Time boxes (PMBOK 7, p. 62).
domande.nota: The instructor finds B and C close.
domande.motivo_incertezza: debatable: the instructor sees more than one valid answer

domande.domanda: While reviewing the current progress of your project with your project sponsor, they notice that the system solution is missing a critical piece that will impact the benefits of the project. The project sponsor approves the scope. Your project has a planned value of $520,000 and an actual cost of $535,000. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Work with the PMO to unlock the project's management reserves for the extra work.
opzioni.B: Ask the product owner to reprioritize the backlog and see if the new work will fit.
opzioni.C: Perform the work within your normal budget, as your project is on track.
opzioni.D: Raise a change request for the changes and gain approval from the change control board.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Management reserves cover unexpected in-scope work, often managed by the PMO.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Bumps other work; not clearly agile.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. You're over budget (AC > PV).
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The sponsor already approved it.

domande.spiegazione: Budget, management reserve (PMBOK 7, p. 62).

domande.domanda: You're in the planning stages of an agile project where the functional manager and senior users have provided the high-level requirements and scope. You have been asked to put together a project team that will be able to deliver quickly. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Select project team members from each city to ensure diversity of knowledge within the team.
opzioni.B: Put together a resource management plan outlining the resources required.
opzioni.C: Ask your PMO for currently available resources and assign them to the work.
opzioni.D: Select a small team that can work in the same area, so they can solve problems as they arise.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Distribution slows collaboration.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. No strategy yet.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Availability isn't the criterion.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Small co-located teams benefit from osmotic communication.

domande.spiegazione: Project team composition (PMBOK 7, p. 64).

domande.domanda: You're putting together a project team to deliver an accounting system to offices around the country. The accounting system you're moving to has not been used by anyone in your organization before. The project is quite high risk and the delivery needs to be right the first time. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Select a small team that can work in the same area, so they can solve problems as they arise.
opzioni.B: Use a predictive project approach and source part of your team externally.
opzioni.C: Train existing internal staff in the new system, then have them work on the project.
opzioni.D: Perform a make-or-buy analysis on the different software options.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Nobody internally knows the system.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Outside skills weighed against cost; single high-risk delivery suits predictive.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Slow and adds team-forming issues.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Already decided.

domande.spiegazione: Project team composition (PMBOK 7, p. 63).

domande.domanda: You're putting together a project plan for a change that affects nearly 10,000 stakeholders in your organization. You have identified, analyzed and prioritized the affected stakeholders, and you're now putting together a communication plan to ensure the right engagement. What would you NOT include in your plan?

opzioni.A: Why information should be shared with the stakeholders.
opzioni.B: The best way to provide them with the information.
opzioni.C: How stakeholders can make changes to the communication plan.
opzioni.D: When and how often the information is needed.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. (Include) Part of planning communication.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. (Include) Part of planning communication.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. (NOT) Stakeholders give feedback; the team maintains the plan.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. (Include) Part of planning communication.

domande.spiegazione: Communication planning: who, why, when, how, what (PMBOK 7, p. 64).

domande.domanda: You put together a resource plan for a large amount of physical inventory to be purchased from overseas. You ordered the inventory during project execution; however, global supply chains were impacted and the shipment was delayed by three months, significantly impacting your project. What should you have done differently?

opzioni.A: Hired a resource manager to take care of the resource tasks on your project.
opzioni.B: Planned strategically about the timing from order to delivery to usage, managing resource risks and their responses.
opzioni.C: Ensured there were means to track the inventory from arrival on site to the delivery of an integrated product.
opzioni.D: Sourced the inventory locally to reduce the impact of global supply chains.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Doesn't address timing risk.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Teams needing significant materials plan timing, bulk vs storage and global logistics.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Tracking doesn't manage the risk.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. It had to be bought overseas.

domande.spiegazione: Physical resources (PMBOK 7, p. 65).

domande.domanda: You are halfway through your agile project when a significant change to the project scope is needed, after it was found that the project would not be able to deliver the benefits it had promised. You check your project budget and there are contingency and management reserves available. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Take the project scope change to the change control board for approval.
opzioni.B: Use the available contingency reserves to make the appropriate change to the project scope.
opzioni.C: Review the change management plan for the change control process.
opzioni.D: Reprioritize the backlog, including the new scope, and begin work on the highest-priority item straight away.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Agile uses backlog reprioritization instead of formal control.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Contingency is for risks.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Not agile.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. In agile, changes are handled by reprioritizing the backlog.

domande.spiegazione: Changes (PMBOK 7, p. 66).

domande.domanda: You have recently taken over a project that is behind schedule and slightly over budget. You raise an issue at the steering committee meeting, where they advise that there is no additional funding available and the project must finish on time. You believe you can optimize the project process to bring it back on track. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Add additional people and resources to the project to speed it up.
opzioni.B: Use the project's contingency reserve to source the resources you need.
opzioni.C: Perform project activities in parallel, completing multiple items at once instead of one at a time.
opzioni.D: Use lean production methods to reduce non-value-added activities, and retrospectives for the team to suggest improvements.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Adds cost and complexity.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Reserves are for risks.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Fast tracking isn't process optimization.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Lean and retrospectives optimize project processes.

domande.spiegazione: Project processes (PMBOK 7, p. 71).

domande.domanda: Your project management office is optimizing all the projects within its portfolio. They ask for your advice on tracking the type of work each team member is doing and how long it takes, suggesting that team members categorize and record their work in addition to doing the work itself. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Ask your team to record and categorize their work, as it's important.
opzioni.B: Recommend an automated reporting tool where possible, as categorizing the work is non-value-added.
opzioni.C: Recommend an automated reporting tool because recording their work is value-added.
opzioni.D: Ask your team to ignore the request and focus on delivering customer value only.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Adds waste.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Respect the PMO while keeping processes efficient and effective.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Recording isn't value-add for the customer.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Don't ignore the PMO.

domande.spiegazione: Project processes (PMBOK 7, p. 72).

domande.domanda: You're working on an agile project as a Scrum Master. A functional manager from the business, who has worked with some people in your development team before, approaches them directly to see if they can add a feature to the product in their current sprint. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Adjust the sprint backlog to allow for the additional feature.
opzioni.B: Adjust the product backlog to add the customer requirement.
opzioni.C: Ask the manager to speak with the product owner about the product priorities, then protect the team from direct requests in the future.
opzioni.D: Ask the manager to create a change request so it can go through the proper process.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The PO prioritizes.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The PO decides what goes in.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Protect team focus; the PO is the single point of prioritization.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Not agile.

domande.spiegazione: Maintain project team focus (PMBOK 7, p. 73).

domande.domanda: Part of the project management plan is a detailed communications plan listing the project's stakeholders, their communication needs and how information will be communicated. While this is being signed off by the project sponsor, you receive many ad hoc requests for information from new stakeholders. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Review the communications management plan to include the stakeholders, with the information they need and their communication preferences.
opzioni.B: Create an information radiator and ask the stakeholders to pull the information they need.
opzioni.C: Ignore the new requests, as you've already captured all the stakeholders you need in your plan.
opzioni.D: Ask the new stakeholders to review your communications management plan to see how you're distributing information.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Many ad hoc requests mean planning didn't meet needs.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Good, but the plan needs updating.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Never ignore.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. It's our job to update it.

domande.spiegazione: Project communications and engagement (PMBOK 7, p. 72).

domande.domanda: ⚠️ You're working on a high-value construction project to include smart home components in multi-million-dollar buildings. After completing a make-or-buy analysis, you find it will cost $700,000 to make a new system or $500,000 to buy it from a vendor. You prepare a procurement management plan to purchase it. What will you do before conducting the procurement? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Work with your project team to complete as much as possible in-house.
opzioni.B: Work with the contracting professionals in your organization to develop the RFP, the statement of work, and the terms and conditions.
opzioni.C: Adjust your stakeholder register to include the new vendor and add the scope to your WBS dictionary.
opzioni.D: Work with your project team to develop an RMP, an SMP and a list of resources.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. You decided to buy.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. PM and technical team work with contracting professionals on bid documents.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Wrong order.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. A distractor.

domande.spiegazione: Working with procurements (PMBOK 7, p. 74).
domande.nota: Option D seems invented as a distractor.
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: A missing item has been uncovered in the project scope that your project team cannot deliver. The item is not complex and seems to be readily available from various sources. You are ready to move to source selection and choose a vendor that will meet your needs. What will you do before sending out bid documents to vendors?

opzioni.A: Prepare a request for proposal (RFP) for vendors to provide a solution to your needs.
opzioni.B: Prepare a request for quote (RFQ) to determine the best price from the vendors.
opzioni.C: Prepare a request for information (RFI) to gather more information and viable sources from the market.
opzioni.D: Review the procurement management plan for your project's procurement process.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. RFP is itself a bid document.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. RFQ is itself a bid document.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. RFI gathers market information before sending bid documents.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Decent, but RFI comes first.

domande.spiegazione: The bid process (PMBOK 7, p. 75).

domande.domanda: You're working on a project where part of the work is planned carefully upfront and another part is subject to change. You negotiate the terms and conditions with a vendor, including cost, delivery and payment dates. The vendor is concerned about the confusion that might occur between pre-planned and changeable work. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Use a firm fixed price contract to ensure the cost is fixed but the scope can remain flexible.
opzioni.B: Use a time and materials contract to ensure only the time and materials used are paid for.
opzioni.C: Adjust your project plan to suit either a predictive or an adaptive approach, to reduce the confusion.
opzioni.D: Use a master agreement for the overall contract, with the adaptive work placed in an appendix.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Fixes scope and price.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Doesn't separate the two parts.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The project needs both.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Changes to adaptive scope happen without affecting the overall contract.

domande.spiegazione: Contracting (PMBOK 7, p. 76).

domande.domanda: You're working on an agile project where there are vastly differing levels of product knowledge within your team. The Scrum Master suggests you try to gain knowledge by osmosis, because project information may be lost when only communicating by email. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Co-locate the team to capture the benefit of each person's tacit knowledge.
opzioni.B: Refer to the organizational process assets to capture the team's explicit knowledge.
opzioni.C: Refer to the project's knowledge management system and capture the project's explicit knowledge.
opzioni.D: Create a process to capture the team's tacit knowledge.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Co-location captures tacit knowledge from surroundings.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Explicit, not osmosis.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Explicit, not osmosis.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Co-location is the way.

domande.spiegazione: Explicit and tacit knowledge (PMBOK 7, p. 77).

domande.domanda: You're working as a product owner and have placed high-level information about the product in the product backlog, with the highest-priority feature at the top. The senior users informing the project are unable to clearly articulate their requirements, and they're concerned that the product will not truly meet their needs. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Proceed with the highest-priority item during the first sprint.
opzioni.B: Work with the customer to create mock-ups and prototypes to discover what works for them.
opzioni.C: Ask your stakeholders to submit a change request and update the project scope accordingly.
opzioni.D: Begin breaking down the work into user stories to place into the sprint.

domande.hint: 'I'll know it when I see it'.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Requirements unclear.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Prototypes, demos, storyboards and mock-ups evolve requirements.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Not about change.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Needs clear requirements first.

domande.spiegazione: Evolving and discovering requirements (PMBOK 7, p. 83).

domande.domanda: You are gathering requirements for a new feature in a customer management system. The product owner has given a user interface feature as the next highest priority, and you're co-located with the team who will receive the benefits. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Show the customer team how the new user interface will look, as they will be using it.
opzioni.B: Communicate the requirements to the developers with a coherent, logical flow of ideas.
opzioni.C: Elicit the requirements into user stories, using acceptance criteria that are clear, verifiable and traceable.
opzioni.D: Show the mock-up or prototype to the developers and ask them to develop based on that.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not enough to build.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Part of the 5 Cs, not elicitation.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Requirements should be clear, concise, verifiable, consistent, complete and traceable.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. A prototype may lack detail.

domande.spiegazione: Requirements elicitation (PMBOK 7, p. 83).

domande.domanda: You're working in an agile team who are trying to break down the project requirements and scope. They have created a scope statement and a work breakdown structure, but they're not sure how this will work now that they're using sprints and user stories. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Assign activities to each of the scope items in the work breakdown structure and place them on a Gantt chart.
opzioni.B: Create a product roadmap with the team using the lowest, most detailed level of the work breakdown structure.
opzioni.C: Group the work by large themes of customer value, shown as epics, then break them down into smaller user stories to complete in each sprint.
opzioni.D: Ask the team to trace the requirements properly using a requirements traceability matrix.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Traditional.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Roadmaps are at feature level.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Epics too big for a sprint, broken into stories.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Not the question.

domande.spiegazione: Scope decomposition (PMBOK 7, p. 84).

domande.domanda: Your project team are trialling an agile way of work, and the product owner has a clear vision for the product. There is confusion in the team about how much work should be done on a user story before it's taken to the sprint review, and how they will know that a story is complete. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Refer to the user story's acceptance criteria and your team's definition of done.
opzioni.B: Review the user story with multiple users to ensure it's correct.
opzioni.C: Ask the product owner to sign off on the completed user story.
opzioni.D: Ensure quality testing on the user story is completed and passed.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Acceptance criteria and DoD describe completion.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Could be part of DoD.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Could be part of DoD.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Could be part of DoD.

domande.spiegazione: Completion of deliverables (PMBOK 7, p. 85).

domande.domanda: You've been working closely with the quality manager of your project, planning the budget for the project phase that's due to begin in the next two months. They mention the need to budget for appraisal costs to avoid quality issues in the future. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Ensure there's enough budget for training.
opzioni.B: Ensure there's enough budget for a quality tester to verify the deliverables against the agreed specifications.
opzioni.C: Ensure there's enough budget to create a quality assurance plan.
opzioni.D: Ensure there's enough budget to allow for rework or rectification when defects are found.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Prevention.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Appraisal covers verification and audits.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Prevention (quality planning).
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Failure cost.

domande.spiegazione: Cost of quality (PMBOK 7, p. 89).

domande.domanda: ⚠️ Your agile project has recently had multiple quality issues. Project features have been prioritized by the product owner and broken down into user stories. What will you do to help reduce the cost of quality issues the most? — ⚠️ Note: debatable: the instructor sees more than one valid answer.

opzioni.A: Quality test each user story against its acceptance criteria before release.
opzioni.B: Advise the team that any quality defects will come out of their bonus.
opzioni.C: Perform testing all in one go at the end, to reduce the cost of testing resources.
opzioni.D: Ensure a triad of developer, tester and customer is involved during requirements and design.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Good, but later and costlier.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Harsh and disengaging.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Most costly.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Fixing at requirements/design is cheapest (20x build, 50x test, 150x production).

domande.spiegazione: Cost of change (PMBOK 7, p. 90).
domande.nota: The instructor finds A and D close.
domande.motivo_incertezza: debatable: the instructor sees more than one valid answer

domande.domanda: You're working in an agile team, and executives in the area you're delivering to are asking for a large set of reports to be created every two weeks, showing how the project is tracking and updating them on costs and benefits. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Collect the planned value versus earned value to show the executives any variance from the plan.
opzioni.B: Co-locate the team with the executives so they can answer any questions as they arise.
opzioni.C: Suggest a demonstration of the features developed during each sprint instead, plus a burndown chart of future product releases.
opzioni.D: Create the desired reports for the executives to keep them happy.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not agile-centric.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Possible, not best.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Agile demonstrates value delivered and uses information radiators.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Reports for their own sake.

domande.spiegazione: Measurement performance domain (PMBOK 7, p. 94).

domande.domanda: Multiple features have been released, but they are not having the effect the product owner believes they should. Your team are using key performance indicators (KPIs) to track performance, and you agree to move to more leading indicators. What could you use as examples of leading indicators on your project?

opzioni.A: An increase in customer usage once the feature is released, such as sales and repeat purchases.
opzioni.B: Stakeholders who are not engaged, and the lack of a risk management process.
opzioni.C: The velocity of work completed in each sprint, and the cycle time of the user stories.
opzioni.D: The schedule variance between planned and actual time taken.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Lagging.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Leading indicators predict changes: no risk process, disengaged stakeholders, unclear success criteria.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Lagging.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Lagging.

domande.spiegazione: Leading indicators (PMBOK 7, p. 96).

domande.domanda: You're working in an agile project team that has increased in size and complexity since the project began. Reviewing the throughput of work with your team, you notice fewer and fewer user stories being completed, and the roadmap of features scheduled to go live is being pushed out. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Place a limit on the work in progress and work with the team to reduce the cycle time.
opzioni.B: Increase meetings with the team.
opzioni.C: Ask the team to work overtime until the number of features reduces.
opzioni.D: Put a pull system in place, where the team can pull work only when they are ready.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. WIP limits avoid multitasking and context switching.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Adds overhead.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Unsustainable.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Without WIP limits, more work gets pulled.

domande.spiegazione: What to measure, delivery (PMBOK 7, p. 99).

domande.domanda: You're working on an agile project where the project customer wants a reliable way to measure project performance, and you first need a baseline. What measures will you show your customer as part of your agile project?

opzioni.A: Team velocity.
opzioni.B: Start and finish dates.
opzioni.C: The rate of features completed.
opzioni.D: Schedule and cost variance.

domande.hint: Fixed cost and time, variable scope.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Internal team measure.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Not value.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Agile tracks features delivered with a stable team.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Cost and time are fixed.

domande.spiegazione: Baseline performance (PMBOK 7, p. 100).

domande.domanda: The product owner has worked with a team of senior users to gather feature ideas. They now have a list of more than 50 ideas for your team to develop, which is far too many to complete in the time frame you have. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Start work on the smallest features first.
opzioni.B: Ask the product owner to go back to the users and ask for a shortened list.
opzioni.C: Workshop the features with a wider audience to get a diverse view on their priority.
opzioni.D: Ask the product owner to prioritize the features using cost to benefit, then deliver them in priority order until the time or money runs out.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Value first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Prioritize instead.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Messy; the PO decides.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. POs prioritize by business value (cost-benefit, ROI, NPV).

domande.spiegazione: Business value (PMBOK 7, p. 102).
domande.nota: Option order reconstructed.

domande.domanda: Your agile project team has only recently formed. The product is still unclear, and there have been disagreements and minor conflicts over the past two weeks as the team find their rhythm. You would like things to improve, but you can't quite pinpoint or address the problem. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Hold a workshop with your team and ask them why they're unhappy.
opzioni.B: Have the team complete a Net Promoter Score with comments, and ask for improvement ideas at the next retrospective.
opzioni.C: Raise the issue with their line managers and ensure everyone is working on it.
opzioni.D: Have the team pair up so they can learn from each other.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. May become complaining.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. NPS/satisfaction measures plus retrospectives capture improvements.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Handle it yourself.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Possible later action.

domande.spiegazione: Measuring stakeholders (PMBOK 7, p. 103).
domande.nota: Option order reconstructed.

domande.domanda: Your project has faced serious impacts in getting materials, with supply chains disrupted by a global pandemic, and is currently three weeks behind schedule. You take this information to the next project steering committee meeting, where they advise they need more information on how much the project will end up costing. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Use the current budget with no deviations until it runs out.
opzioni.B: Use the project burndown chart to see the burn rate of the project funds.
opzioni.C: Use regression analysis to see the current rate of spending and where the final cost will end up.
opzioni.D: Use the project's estimate at completion (EAC) to show the steering committee the most likely final cost.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. No forecast.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Shows work, not cost.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. May work, but not best.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. EAC (e.g. BAC/CPI) forecasts the most likely final cost.

domande.spiegazione: Forecasts (PMBOK 7, p. 104).
