domande.domanda: You're working on an agile project where the project sponsor and executive managers require lengthy reports each week on how the project work is going. This takes you and the project team a considerable amount of time and reduces the time spent creating the actual product. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Reuse most of the information each week so the time spent on the reports is reduced.
opzioni.B: Suggest the leaders come to the sprint review and gather any information they need from the information radiator.
opzioni.C: Ask your project sponsor to wait until a steering committee meeting for the information.
opzioni.D: Share your working project schedule and budget with the executives instead of creating the reports.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Still waste.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Sprint reviews show work done; radiators let anyone pull information.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Less transparency.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Less live.

domande.spiegazione: Information radiators (PMBOK 7, p. 108).

domande.domanda: You're working on a project where the team has planned as much as they can upfront, and you would like them to move to a more agile way of work. Currently the work is hidden: the team catches up only once a week in a working group, and it's hard to see what each person is working on and to keep track of it. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Ask your team to report on their work in a written status update each day so you can keep track.
opzioni.B: Have more working group meetings so you're always up to date on what the team is working on.
opzioni.C: Ask the team to move their work to a central, visible task board, like a Kanban board, and have a short meeting each day to discuss progress on their cards.
opzioni.D: Remove the team meetings altogether and trust your team to get the work done.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Non-value-add.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Overhead.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Task boards plus a 15-minute daily stand-up.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Communication still needed.

domande.spiegazione: Visual controls, task boards (PMBOK 7, p. 109).

domande.domanda: You're working on a hybrid project where the majority of the work has been planned upfront. The team manages their work via a Kanban board and reports on progress and blockers each day. As the project evolves, stakeholders have added more and more scope to the product, with one executive raising an urgent feature that needs to be added. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Limit the number of cards in 'ready' or 'to do', and ask the product owner to work with the stakeholders' requests, noting the need to swap the new item for an existing one.
opzioni.B: Match the number of user stories to the team's velocity to ensure a sustainable pace.
opzioni.C: Work with the stakeholder to raise a change request and note the outcome in a change log.
opzioni.D: Review the impact of the scope change with the stakeholder using the WBS dictionary.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. WIP limits and PO prioritization manage scope.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Not the issue.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. It's addition, managed by prioritization.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. A distractor.

domande.spiegazione: Kanban board (PMBOK 7, p. 110).

domande.domanda: You're working as a product owner in an agile team where the main measure of project success is the number of features delivered into production. Over the past six months the team have delivered the highest number of features your organization has ever seen; however, customers are starting to complain about issues and bugs in the product. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Ask the team to work harder to deliver more features and fix the product issues.
opzioni.B: Adjust the product metrics to include customer satisfaction and quality measures.
opzioni.C: Add a slack card of five points to the sprint backlog to deal with the technical debt.
opzioni.D: Remove customer comments and feedback completely until you've finished delivering all the features.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Unsustainable.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. What you measure influences behavior: balance it.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Good, but doesn't fix the cause.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Hides the problem.

domande.spiegazione: Measurement pitfalls, Hawthorne effect (PMBOK 7, p. 112).

domande.domanda: You've been working on a project for the past eight months. Your project team have been approached by multiple stakeholders for reports on various performance measures about the project and the product area. A large amount of their time is now spent creating these reports for others, and they've escalated this issue to you. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Ask the project stakeholders to stop interacting with your team.
opzioni.B: Spend a portion of your project budget to automate the reports for your stakeholders.
opzioni.C: Work with the team and the stakeholders to only measure things that will facilitate a decision, help avoid an issue or increase project performance.
opzioni.D: Invite your stakeholders to your sprint reviews so they can see a working feature in practice.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Engagement still needed.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Possible, but doesn't question what's measured.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Only measure what enables learning, decisions or improvement.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Good, but partial.

domande.spiegazione: Growing and improving (PMBOK 7, p. 114).

domande.domanda: You're working on a project where there is a significant amount of uncertainty about the requirements. There is also a legislative change coming, and no one knows what it will mean for your industry. As the project manager, how do you deal with this uncertainty?

opzioni.A: Perform additional planning for your project to improve your view on scope management.
opzioni.B: Hold additional retrospectives to capture challenges and improvements from your team.
opzioni.C: Create a risk assessment of all possible project risks, with their risk ratings and owners.
opzioni.D: Gather information, prepare for multiple outcomes, and build team resilience through processes and training.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Can't plan away uncertainty.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Not for this.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Partial.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Responses: gather information, multiple outcomes, set-based design, resilience.

domande.spiegazione: General uncertainty (PMBOK 7, p. 118).

domande.domanda: You're working on a project with a vendor where there is significant ambiguity involved. There are multiple options the team could go with, and many possible outcomes with varying degrees of impact. To improve the situation, what will you do next?

opzioni.A: Use experiments, prototypes and progressive elaboration to work your way through it.
opzioni.B: Ask your team for additional reporting on the different options so you can make an informed decision.
opzioni.C: Add all the different options into your project scope so all your bases are covered.
opzioni.D: Work more closely with your senior users so they can inform you of the product requirements.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Progressive elaboration, experiments and prototypes resolve ambiguity.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Doesn't resolve.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Still ambiguous.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Good practice, not direct.

domande.spiegazione: Ambiguity (PMBOK 7, p. 120).

domande.domanda: You're working on a project to improve some software that has been in production for over 17 years and has been modified extensively over that time. It also integrates with many other systems within your organization, and you cannot decide which features to deliver first. How will you deal with the complexity?

opzioni.A: List the possible features you can deliver and prioritize them by cost over benefit.
opzioni.B: Simulate decoupling the connected parts to simplify the number of variables, then reframe your view by brainstorming with a diverse set of stakeholders.
opzioni.C: Provide an incentive for whichever project team member can solve this complex problem.
opzioni.D: Form a business case for a third-party system to replace the existing complex system and transfer the risk of delivery.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Good practice, not complexity handling.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Systems-based decoupling/simulation and reframing with diverse views.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Not a method.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. May increase complexity.

domande.spiegazione: Complexity (PMBOK 7, p. 121).

domande.domanda: You're working on a project that requires a very particular programming skill set that is not very common. It's also the hottest job market the industry has seen in two decades, so people are hard to come by and leave often. The programming language is also evolving at a quick pace. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Develop the product from scratch in a more common programming language.
opzioni.B: Ask your whole team to learn the programming skill set to cover the risk.
opzioni.C: Use alternatives analysis to gather different options, and ensure a sufficient cost reserve to help complete your project.
opzioni.D: Raise a risk to project completion for the threat related to team members' skill sets.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Drastic.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Not feasible quickly.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Alternatives analysis and cost reserves address volatility.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Partial.

domande.spiegazione: Volatility (PMBOK 7, p. 122).

domande.domanda: Your project team have found a significant data vulnerability in one of the features planned in your product backlog: customer data is exposed without password access. This feature is partially made by a third-party vendor, and the relationship is owned by a functional manager in your organization. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Avoid the risk and wait for the third-party vendor to fix the vulnerability.
opzioni.B: Transfer the risk by asking a different vendor to create the feature with no vulnerability in its design.
opzioni.C: Escalate the risk to the manager with the appropriate authority to act on the response.
opzioni.D: Accept the risk and move on to other features, so the work continues to get done.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Too passive for this severity.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Slow and not yours to decide.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Escalate when outside project scope or PM authority.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Too severe to accept.

domande.spiegazione: Threat responses (PMBOK 7, p. 123).

domande.domanda: You brainstorm risk responses with your project team and project sponsor and decide you cannot transfer a certain high-impact risk. You also can't avoid the risk, and there is no one in the organization to escalate it to. Your project sponsor agrees that you should actively accept the risk. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Develop a contingency plan that would be triggered if the event occurred.
opzioni.B: Shift the ownership to a third party to manage the risk and bear the impact if it does occur.
opzioni.C: Act to eliminate the threat or protect the project from its impact.
opzioni.D: Take action to reduce the probability of its occurrence and the impact of the threat.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Active acceptance includes a contingency plan.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Transfer.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Avoid.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Mitigate.

domande.spiegazione: Threat responses (PMBOK 7, p. 123).

domande.domanda: You're working on a project to build a new customer database system for an engineering team. While working on the requirements, you realize that this system could also work for other teams in your organization, and the effort to add those teams is actually quite small. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Work with the other teams and their managers to escalate the opportunity.
opzioni.B: Work with the other teams and their managers to exploit the opportunity.
opzioni.C: Work with the other teams and their managers to enhance the opportunity.
opzioni.D: Work with the other teams and their managers to accept the opportunity.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. For opportunities outside PM authority.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Exploit acts to ensure it occurs.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Only raises probability.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Does nothing.

domande.spiegazione: Opportunities (PMBOK 7, p. 125).

domande.domanda: You're working as a product owner in an agile team. During a recent risk review, the team uncovered various risks that will impact your project, and you brainstormed risk responses together. The project customer would like the risks to be mitigated as soon as possible. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Ask your team to work on the risk responses and get them done as soon as possible.
opzioni.B: Ignore the risks initially: some might dissipate over time and only the important ones will be left.
opzioni.C: Assign the risk responses to all the stakeholders around your project team to share the load.
opzioni.D: Prioritize the risks by comparing the expected monetary value of each risk to the anticipated return on investment.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Ignores other priorities.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Risks may grow.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. May lack expertise.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. EMV vs ROI incorporates responses into normal prioritization.

domande.spiegazione: Risk-adjusted backlog (PMBOK 7, p. 126).

domande.domanda: You're planning a project where supply chains have been impacted, and the requirements are complex and intertwined with other areas of the business. Your project sponsor asks you to manage these risks before the project moves to execution. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Move to project execution so you can work through the risks as they happen.
opzioni.B: Move to an agile way of work so you can deliver faster and also deal with the complexity.
opzioni.C: Note the risks with appropriate controls and add a contingency reserve to the project budget.
opzioni.D: Assign a management reserve to deal with the risks before moving to project execution.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Too late.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Doesn't remove risk.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Contingency reserve is for identified risks.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. For unknown events.

domande.spiegazione: Management and contingency reserves (PMBOK 7, p. 127).

domande.domanda: You're working on an agile project, delivering a usable feature every few weeks. The project sponsor comes from a waterfall background and is concerned that there is not enough focus on risk. They would like to hold a regular risk review with a wide group of stakeholders. What will you suggest instead?

opzioni.A: There is no need for a separate meeting, as risk is everyone's responsibility in an agile team.
opzioni.B: Use daily stand-ups to report blockers early, and fortnightly demonstrations of the product to catch any stakeholder dissatisfaction.
opzioni.C: Use the Kanban board to see the work and how it flows.
opzioni.D: Hold the risk meeting, but only with the immediate project team, to avoid unnecessary participants.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Partly true, but weak.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Stand-up blockers and demos surface threats and opportunities.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Partial.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Excludes useful stakeholders.

domande.spiegazione: Risk review (PMBOK 7, p. 127).

domande.domanda: Your project management office has no prescribed way of working, so they're working with a vendor who supplies an Extreme Programming (XP) framework at a significant cost. However, projects are still running behind schedule, over budget and with low customer satisfaction. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Tailor the approach to suit the organization, the operating environment and the project needs.
opzioni.B: Use a waterfall approach instead to ensure proper planning.
opzioni.C: Switch to Scrum instead, as it's a more popular framework.
opzioni.D: Tighten the controls around the project environment with a more directive PMO approach.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Tailoring fits the approach to the context.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Still needs tailoring.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Popular isn't best.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Not the cause.

domande.spiegazione: Tailoring overview (PMBOK 7, p. 132).

domande.domanda: Your project management office is in the middle of a company-wide ways-of-working transformation. They have taken a popular project framework and are tailoring it to the organization, with branded templates and processes that meet their existing governance requirements. You've been asked to help finalize the process. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Gather feedback from the functional business areas to ensure the process meets their needs.
opzioni.B: Roll out the new way of working to the PMO as a pilot, then to the rest of the organization.
opzioni.C: Enable a process for tailoring based on size and complexity, and implement ongoing improvement.
opzioni.D: Form a working group made up of executives and project professionals.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Partial.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Partial.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Select approach, tailor for organization and project, implement ongoing improvement.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Partial.

domande.spiegazione: The tailoring process (PMBOK 7, p. 137).

domande.domanda: You're the manager of a PMO in a large organization that has recently undertaken a company-wide ways-of-working transformation. You need to select an initial development approach for your projects, which you will then tailor further to suit them. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Use the framework that best engages your executive team through easy-to-use graphics and presentations.
opzioni.B: Select the most popular current framework to keep up with what other organizations are doing.
opzioni.C: Select multiple development approaches as a baseline for your organization.
opzioni.D: Use a suitability filter to assess the most appropriate development approach.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Looks, not fit.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Popular isn't fit.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Complex.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Suitability filters show predictive, hybrid or adaptive fit.

domande.spiegazione: Select initial development approach (PMBOK 7, p. 138).

domande.domanda: Your organization is starting to move to an agile way of work and is setting up a Value Delivery Office (VDO) to complement the existing project management office (PMO). The executives in the area have begun working through what the function looks like and the roles and responsibilities that might exist, and they approach you for help. What will you tell them?

opzioni.A: A VDO is responsible for the value delivered and owns the programs within the organization.
opzioni.B: A VDO focuses on coaching project teams, building adaptive skills and capabilities, and mentoring sponsors and product owners to be more effective.
opzioni.C: A VDO is responsible for allocating agile resources, such as Scrum Masters and product owners, effectively to project teams.
opzioni.D: A VDO creates the organizational framework to be used on each project throughout the company.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. PMO-like.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. A VDO enables rather than oversees.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Directive PMO-like.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Directive PMO-like.

domande.spiegazione: Value Delivery Office (PMBOK 7, p. 141).

domande.domanda: You've been planning a project for the last two months, gathering requirements and scope and assigning tasks to a schedule. As you get closer to the execution phase, you need to decide what delivery approach you will use. The requirements are likely to change and require a medium amount of compliance, but the product can be released in one go. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Use a predictive delivery approach.
opzioni.B: Use an incremental delivery approach.
opzioni.C: Use an adaptive (agile) delivery approach.
opzioni.D: Use an iterative delivery approach.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Plans upfront.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Releases increments.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Releases increments with feedback.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Iterative improves with feedback and delivers once.

domande.spiegazione: Tailor for the project (PMBOK 7, p. 141).

domande.domanda: You've been asked to make a process improvement in the accounting area of your organization. You have been assigned a small team of nine people, each with all the skills needed to complete the project. The team is co-located and has unlimited access to the project customer. How will you tailor your delivery approach?

opzioni.A: Use a predictive delivery approach.
opzioni.B: Use an adaptive (agile) delivery approach.
opzioni.C: Use an incremental delivery approach.
opzioni.D: Use a hybrid delivery approach.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not needed.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Adaptive fits small, cross-functional, co-located teams close to the customer.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Partial.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. No predictive part.

domande.spiegazione: Tailor for the project team (PMBOK 7, p. 141).

domande.domanda: You have been working for some time as a project manager in an organization where an agile-centric delivery approach and way of working have been selected and tailored for the organization. Over the past few months, as you begin new projects, you notice several things are not working and could be improved. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Review the product backlog to see the flow of features going through the teams.
opzioni.B: Look into issues, threats and quality assurance statistics.
opzioni.C: Suggest a retrospective with your PMO leaders to determine ongoing improvement opportunities.
opzioni.D: Review a control chart and a value stream map to see non-value-added activities and remove waste from the process.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Partial.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Partial.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Retrospectives find ongoing improvements.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Good tools, but part of problem solving.

domande.spiegazione: Tailoring diagnostics (PMBOK 7, p. 151).

domande.domanda: You have been working on a project to deliver a new customer data system and notice that the work is starting to slow down: fewer user stories are appearing in your sprint backlog because they are not ready. You hold a retrospective with your team and discover that there are long delays waiting for requirements and acceptance criteria approvals. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Streamline approval decisions through fewer people, such as a product owner authorized to make decisions up to certain value thresholds.
opzioni.B: Ask your team to place the user stories in the sprint backlog, reducing the need for customer approval.
opzioni.C: Note the long delays as a risk to your project, with a high likelihood as it's already happening.
opzioni.D: Escalate the issue to the functional manager to ensure approvals happen quickly.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Tailoring suggestion for approval delays.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Excludes the customer.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. It's an issue.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Doesn't fix the process.

domande.spiegazione: Common situations and tailoring suggestions (PMBOK 7, p. 151).

domande.domanda: You have been assigned to take over an existing project as the previous project manager leaves for another opportunity. Working with your team, you notice a large amount of work in progress all at once, with team members working on multiple items at a time and constantly context switching between tasks. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Add more people to the project.
opzioni.B: Use value stream mapping and Kanban boards to visualize the work and brainstorm solutions with your team.
opzioni.C: Ask your team to work overtime to cover the extra work and bring it all back in line.
opzioni.D: Review the scope of the project and reduce items with low impact on customer satisfaction.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Complicates communication.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Visualize work, identify issues, propose solutions.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Unsustainable.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Good practice, not the cause.

domande.spiegazione: Common situations and tailoring suggestions (PMBOK 7, p. 151).

domande.domanda: The product owner has prioritized the product backlog of features, and the team creates user stories with estimates and places enough of them to fill a two-week sprint. You notice that the pieces being completed are being rejected by the customer for defects and missed requirements. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Create the project scope from scratch with the project team and customers, so it's correct.
opzioni.B: Hold an iteration zero planning sprint with your project team to set it up for success.
opzioni.C: Add more feedback loops, such as shoulder checks, peer review, unit testing and system testing.
opzioni.D: Hold less frequent customer demonstrations, so they only see the product when it's correct.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Excessive.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Delays flow.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. More verification loops and QA steps.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Less feedback.

domande.spiegazione: Common situations and tailoring suggestions (PMBOK 7, p. 151).

domande.domanda: Your project team has started to find its rhythm, yet you notice that they seem disengaged and are dragging their feet on normal tasks. You check your project budget and note that the team are all paid fairly for the market and within the same range for their roles. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Look for ways to reward the team members with bonuses above their normal pay rate.
opzioni.B: Move team members around to different roles frequently so they experience job variety.
opzioni.C: Give the team a paid day off.
opzioni.D: Establish ways for the team to grow and advance.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Fades quickly.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Loses expertise and flow.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Fades quickly.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. With hygiene factors met, motivators are achievement, growth, advancement.

domande.spiegazione: Hygiene and motivational factors (PMBOK 7, p. 158).

domande.domanda: You're working as a project manager on a regulatory change for your organization. You notice that the team are not communicating as well as they could be, and you put together a plan to improve team communication by increasing its effectiveness and richness. What will you do?

opzioni.A: Include methods that handle multiple information cues, facilitate rapid feedback and use natural language.
opzioni.B: Include methods to escalate issues quickly, with executives open to anything the team needs.
opzioni.C: Include ways to get sign-off in writing, so it can be recorded and reviewed later when needed.
opzioni.D: Include communication that ensures everyone gets a voice and input into decisions.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Media richness: multiple cues, rapid feedback, personal focus, natural language.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Not richness.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Less rich.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Good, but not richness.

domande.spiegazione: Effectiveness of communication channels (PMBOK 7, p. 157).

domande.domanda: ⚠️ Your deliverables have been signed off by the product owner and are ready to be released to the customer: the financial analytics team of your organization. The new system will be quite a change from their normal day-to-day work, but the team already have the desire to use it. What will you do next? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Share the vision and the why behind the change.
opzioni.B: Use training and education to show them the new processes and systems.
opzioni.C: Give them unlimited hands-on practice so they can get used to the new system.
opzioni.D: Include rewards, recognition, feedback and measurement.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Awareness, already there.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. After Desire comes Knowledge.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Ability, later.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Reinforcement, last.

domande.spiegazione: ADKAR model (PMBOK 7, p. 161).
domande.nota: Option A reconstructed from the commentary ('do they need a vision and the why?').
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: You are leading a large organizational change that affects more than 1,000 people across multiple teams. You've engaged with the senior managers of the area, created a brief vision statement summarizing the change and a strategy to realize the vision, and you communicate the vision throughout the change process. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Release multiple usable features to the affected teams so they can get used to the change gradually.
opzioni.B: Anchor the changes into the corporate culture by telling success stories and recognizing people.
opzioni.C: Address any obstacles to the change, including outdated processes and people's resistance.
opzioni.D: Set goals for continued improvement on the change throughout the organization.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Too early.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Last step.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. After communicating the vision comes removing obstacles.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Later step.

domande.spiegazione: Kotter's 8-step process (PMBOK 7, p. 162).

domande.domanda: You're a project manager assessing the risk of future releases with your team. You have a clear set of requirements from your customer; however, there is a range of possible correct solutions and a range of known unknowns. How will you approach this situation?

opzioni.A: Use current best practices to make decisions.
opzioni.B: Use emergent practices that allow you to probe the environment, sense the situation and respond with action.
opzioni.C: Assess the facts, analyze the situation and apply known good practices.
opzioni.D: Act where there is some stability and take steps to try to stabilize the situation.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Obvious domain.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Complex domain (unknown unknowns).
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Complicated: known unknowns, range of correct answers.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Chaotic domain.

domande.spiegazione: Cynefin framework (PMBOK 7, p. 164).

domande.domanda: You've been asked to initiate a project to deliver a new system. The requirements are not clear and it will take some time to uncover them. The system has been used by some team members but not all, and there is a medium level of uncertainty around it. How will you approach this project?

opzioni.A: Release small usable features and improve your approach based on feedback.
opzioni.B: Do additional planning upfront to ensure every component is thought of.
opzioni.C: Split the team in two and work on different parts of the system to simplify it.
opzioni.D: Form a business case for starting from scratch with new, easier-to-use technology.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Agile works best in complicated and complex zones.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Doesn't resolve uncertainty.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Adds silos.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Long and unnecessary.

domande.spiegazione: Stacey matrix (PMBOK 7, p. 165).

domande.domanda: Your project team came together from different parts of the organization and were formally introduced to each other. Now you notice some conflict in the team: some people don't respect others' decisions, they're not working together well, and there are some personality clashes. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Help team members get to know each other and their names.
opzioni.B: Help the team understand their roles and responsibilities and form a regular rhythm of meetings, collaboration and work.
opzioni.C: Help the team jockey for position within the team and foster healthy conflict.
opzioni.D: Help the team complete the project work and disperse onto other things.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Forming, already done.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Moves the team from storming to norming.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Unhealthy competition.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Adjourning.

domande.spiegazione: Tuckman ladder (PMBOK 7, p. 166).

domande.domanda: You have formed a new project team and worked through the purpose and mission of the project with them. You then expanded on who is on the project team and the skills and abilities each person brings. You would like to foster a high-performing culture and ensure the team is able to deliver as soon as possible. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Work through changes to the project team and the project, such as deliverables and stakeholders.
opzioni.B: Decompose the high-level plan into greater detail, including a detailed schedule or backlog.
opzioni.C: Define a plan to achieve the project goals, including milestone schedules, release plans and high-level budgets.
opzioni.D: Clarify the goals of the team and what you are there to deliver.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Later (renewal).
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Later (implementation).
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Later (commitment).
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. After orientation and trust building comes goal clarification.

domande.spiegazione: Drexler/Sibbet Team Performance Model (PMBOK 7, p. 167).

domande.domanda: ⚠️ Your team members have raised an issue: they believe the current project scope will not reach the intended project goal of increasing customer retention. You take their concerns to the project sponsor, who controls the project's funding and resources. The sponsor dismisses them and directs you to proceed with the scope currently set. What will you do next? — ⚠️ Note: debatable: the instructor sees more than one valid answer.

opzioni.A: Problem-solve with the sponsor and find a resolution.
opzioni.B: Compromise with the sponsor so each party gets a little of what they want.
opzioni.C: Accommodate the sponsor to maintain harmony and goodwill.
opzioni.D: Force the issue so the sponsor accepts the change.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Good, but the sponsor already decided.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Lose-lose.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. With a powerful sponsor and a relationship to keep, accommodating may be appropriate.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Win-lose, damaging.

domande.spiegazione: Thomas-Kilmann conflict model (PMBOK 7, pp. 168-169).
domande.nota: The instructor finds A and C close.
domande.motivo_incertezza: debatable: the instructor sees more than one valid answer

domande.domanda: A functional manager raises a concern that they have not been engaged correctly and that, as a result, the program is missing some key requirements. You believe you've captured all the items required. Your program manager asks you to handle the situation and approach it from a win-win perspective. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Escalate the decision to the steering committee to ensure your point of view is heard.
opzioni.B: Demonstrate integrity, find mutual trust and look at the situation from their point of view.
opzioni.C: Give some leeway in your approach so the functional manager can add their requirements.
opzioni.D: Get your requirements baselined first, then compete with the manager to ensure a win.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not win-win.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Win-win needs character, trust and their perspective.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Lose-win.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Win-lose.

domande.spiegazione: Negotiation (PMBOK 7, p. 169).

domande.domanda: You have been planning a project to deliver a process change for the past four weeks. The requirements and scope have been signed off by the business owner, and the team is moving into delivery and execution. The work begins in line with the project plan and scope. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Monitor and control the project work.
opzioni.B: Execute the project work.
opzioni.C: Plan the project work.
opzioni.D: Formally sign off the project.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Executed work must be monitored and controlled.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Already happening.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Already done.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Not finished yet.

domande.spiegazione: Process groups (PMBOK 7, p. 170).
domande.nota: Option order reconstructed.

domande.domanda: You're working as a product owner. While sales and revenue have increased over the past eight months, the overall profit has decreased by 17%. Your executive manager asks you to address the situation. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Stop the current work and set a planning session with your team to address the situation.
opzioni.B: Ask your team to work overtime on the current features in your backlog to get the work done.
opzioni.C: Perform benchmarking with a similar but non-competing company, and add any process improvements to your product backlog.
opzioni.D: Look for opportunities to partner with other products in your organization and increase your sales further.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Don't stop work.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Unsustainable.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Benchmarking finds process gaps reducing cost.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Ignores rising costs.

domande.spiegazione: Benchmarking (PMBOK 7, p. 175).

domande.domanda: You have been given authority to manage the upcoming features your team will release. You don't have a high enough level of expertise in the product, so you gather senior users from the product area to create a feature list. Each stakeholder wants their feature to be delivered first. How will you prioritize them and move forward?

opzioni.A: Go with the features wanted by the top-level executives first, to avoid issues later on.
opzioni.B: Perform a MoSCoW analysis with the stakeholders.
opzioni.C: Perform a root cause analysis and go with the features that address the root cause.
opzioni.D: Use a cost-benefit analysis and compare the time needed to recover the project cost (payback period).

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. HiPPO.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Everyone says 'must have'.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. For specific problems.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Cost-benefit and payback are accepted ways to prioritize value.

domande.spiegazione: Business justification methods (PMBOK 7, p. 175).

domande.domanda: You're creating a business case and a project charter with a small initial project team. You have a high-level feature decomposed into smaller release milestones, and you'd like to note a high-level schedule using Wideband Delphi (a high-level version of planning poker). What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Hold a round of cards with points on them, where each team member places their cards in the center for the total estimate.
opzioni.B: Ask subject matter experts to complete multiple rounds of estimates individually, comparing and explaining the highest and lowest estimates in each round.
opzioni.C: Show the wide-band, high-level range from the lowest to the highest estimate for each feature.
opzioni.D: Find the business functionality for each feature and estimate the effort based on that.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not the method.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Multiple rounds with explanations of extremes.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Wordplay trap.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Function points.

domande.spiegazione: Wideband Delphi (PMBOK 7, p. 178).

domande.domanda: ⚠️ You have been asked to help facilitate a senior planning meeting in your organization. High-level executives have presented the strengths and opportunities of the organization, painting a rosy picture. Revenue has fallen recently, and the chief executive asks you to balance their analysis with a more complete view. What will you do next? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Add your organization's competitors and compare their products.
opzioni.B: Showcase the pipeline of upcoming work.
opzioni.C: Add in the background and abilities of the executive team that will allow the organization to deliver.
opzioni.D: Brainstorm and capture the weaknesses of the organization and the threats to it.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Partial.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Not relevant.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Not relevant.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Completes SWOT.

domande.spiegazione: SWOT analysis (PMBOK 7, p. 175).
domande.nota: Option B is truncated in the transcript ('showcase the pipeline of upcoming...'): ending reconstructed.
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: You are adding an essential feature to your product roadmap. Your team believe they can complete the feature in six weeks; however, the feature is quite large and a bit more complicated than normal. One of your lead developers says they worked on a similar feature in another company and it took around 4 months to complete. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Use relative estimating.
opzioni.B: Use analogous estimating and place the feature at around 4 months to complete.
opzioni.C: Use parametric estimating.
opzioni.D: Use function point estimating to show the amount of business functionality in the feature.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. For stories.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Uses experience on a similar item.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. No parameters.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. No data.

domande.spiegazione: Analogous estimating (PMBOK 7, p. 178).

domande.domanda: You have a prioritized backlog of features and have decomposed the next feature to be delivered into user stories. The team would like to estimate the effort involved in those user stories but are unsure how to proceed. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Ask each team member to add their own estimates as they complete the acceptance criteria.
opzioni.B: Estimate the effort for the overall feature and reduce the need for individual story estimates.
opzioni.C: Help the team perform relative estimating together, sizing the stories in points relative to the smallest piece.
opzioni.D: Base the estimates on cost per hour, and add them after the work is done to ensure they're correct.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Loses team input.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Story estimates needed for velocity.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Most common for stories, often Fibonacci.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Not estimation.

domande.spiegazione: Relative estimating (PMBOK 7, p. 178).

domande.domanda: You are halfway through your current two-week sprint and the work is progressing well. However, you notice that there's not enough work ready and elaborated for when the next sprint begins. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Hold a backlog refinement meeting and work with the team to identify the work that could be accomplished.
opzioni.B: Raise the issue as a blocker in the daily stand-up and ask your team to swarm around the problem.
opzioni.C: Raise the issue in the next retrospective and take an action for the team.
opzioni.D: Place the cards on the Kanban board so the team can see the work and get started.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Refinement elaborates and prioritizes work for the next iteration.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Takes people off work.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Too late.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Not ready yet.

domande.spiegazione: Backlog refinement (PMBOK 7, p. 179).

domande.domanda: You have completed a make-or-buy analysis on your project and found that part of your deliverable is best created by an external vendor. You work with your project team to create the procurement strategy, the source selection criteria and the statement of work. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Gather the seller proposals, including technical details and price.
opzioni.B: Meet with prospective sellers to ensure all vendors have a common understanding of the procurement.
opzioni.C: Perform source selection analysis on what you want from prospective vendors.
opzioni.D: Create the procurement agreement for the third-party vendor to provide their specified services.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Too early.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Bidder conferences ensure common understanding before bids.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Already done.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Too early.

domande.spiegazione: Bidder conference (PMBOK 7, p. 179).

domande.domanda: One of the stakeholders on your project has raised a change request after some of the deliverables contained defects and a missed requirement. Your project has a formal change control process, as opposed to a more agile, prioritized product backlog. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Gather feedback from other stakeholders to see if they also need the change.
opzioni.B: Note the change in the change log, then place the requested item in the next sprint.
opzioni.C: Take it to the change control board, then communicate the decision to approve or reject the change.
opzioni.D: Raise the request as an issue that will affect your project schedule and budget.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Already raised.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Skips control.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. The CCB approves or rejects; decisions are communicated.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Not the process.

domande.spiegazione: Change control board (PMBOK 7, p. 179).

domande.domanda: Your agile project has recently gained some new stakeholders after a department restructure. They complain to you that they're not seeing enough traction in the work delivered through the project, and they're worried it will not meet their requirements. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Invite them to the daily stand-up so they can see the work that happens on a daily basis.
opzioni.B: Invite them to iteration planning so they can choose what the team works on.
opzioni.C: Invite them to the retrospective so they can raise their issue and come up with a solution.
opzioni.D: Invite them to the iteration (sprint) review so they can see the usable increment the team delivers.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Team event.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. PO prioritizes.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Team process.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Reviews demonstrate work to customers and stakeholders.

domande.spiegazione: Iteration review (PMBOK 7, p. 179).

domande.domanda: You have recently taken over a project. Your project team tell you that a regulatory approval has not been granted yet, and it might block development of your project in the next 5 months. You check your project's documentation but cannot see any mention of this. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Hold a risk review meeting, capture it as a risk and ensure an adequate risk response.
opzioni.B: Hold a retrospective with your team to capture the challenges the team is facing.
opzioni.C: Adjust your product roadmap to reflect the changes to the time frame of that deliverable.
opzioni.D: Escalate the regulatory approval to the project steering committee.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Risk reviews identify new risks and check responses.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Not for this.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Not known yet.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Manage first.

domande.spiegazione: Risk review (PMBOK 7, p. 180).

domande.domanda: ⚠️ You're an agile project manager holding daily stand-ups with your team. You notice people accusing other team members of not doing their job, and there are some tasks that are not mentioned anywhere and that no one is responsible for. The team's velocity has slowed over the last three sprints. What will you do next? — ⚠️ Note: debatable: the instructor sees more than one valid answer.

opzioni.A: Refer to the team charter, the team roles and the agreed ways of managing conflict.
opzioni.B: Raise it as an issue in the next retrospective and come to a solution with the team.
opzioni.C: Assign team roles to the people you think are best suited.
opzioni.D: Work with your team to size user stories correctly so velocity improves.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The missing tasks aren't in it.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Retrospectives improve the team's process.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Not collaborative.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Not the cause.

domande.spiegazione: Retrospective (PMBOK 7, p. 180).
domande.nota: The instructor finds A and B close.
domande.motivo_incertezza: debatable: the instructor sees more than one valid answer

domande.domanda: You're managing a large construction project. Due to some delays, the project schedule has been pushed back by one week. As a result, one of the project risks has increased slightly but is still within acceptable limits. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Hold a risk review to update the risk response and owners.
opzioni.B: Raise a change request for the change to the project schedule.
opzioni.C: Capture the change in your project reporting and take it to the next status meeting.
opzioni.D: Update the sprint backlog to reflect the delayed work.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not needed.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Within limits.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Status meetings exchange progress information.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Not agile here.

domande.spiegazione: Status meeting (PMBOK 7, p. 180).

domande.domanda: You are an agile project manager, and over the last three months your team has delivered 3 features to improve a customer app. Your product owner needs to know whether the features are having the desired effect. It's a large organization and multiple measures are available. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Ask them to gather the team velocity and throughput over the past three months.
opzioni.B: Ask them to gather the cost-benefit ratio over the past six months.
opzioni.C: Ask them to gather the Net Promoter Score (NPS) over the past six months.
opzioni.D: Ask them to gather the average app availability and uptime.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Internal.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. For prioritization.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. NPS gauges customer satisfaction and loyalty.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Operations.

domande.spiegazione: Net Promoter Score (PMBOK 7, p. 181).

domande.domanda: You are a project manager in an agile team developing new features for an app. An executive stakeholder with high influence in the organization approaches you and asks you to add a feature that they like; they've also asked their friends, who think it's a good idea too. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Place the feature in the product backlog and prioritize it using cost versus benefit.
opzioni.B: Raise a change request to add the new feature into the scope baseline.
opzioni.C: Gather the requirements for the new feature and ask your team to elaborate on it.
opzioni.D: Analyze the impacts on your project schedule and cost, and add the feature to your project scope.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Data-driven prioritization.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Analyze first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Decide first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Decide first.

domande.spiegazione: Prioritization schema (PMBOK 7, p. 181).

domande.domanda: Your project team are gathering solution ideas for a particular customer requirement that is prioritized to be worked on next. The item is complicated, and they've been trying to find a way forward for the past three weeks. There is not enough work ready for the upcoming sprint. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Start work on the item in the next sprint anyway, and elaborate it as the sprint begins.
opzioni.B: Arrange for the right people to elaborate the issue with a spike, time-boxed to two days.
opzioni.C: Deprioritize the item until the team can figure out the issue.
opzioni.D: Adjust the project schedule to reflect the extra time taken on elaboration.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not ready.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. A spike is a short research story in a fixed time box.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. It's top priority.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Solve first.

domande.spiegazione: Spike and time box (PMBOK 7, p. 181).

domande.domanda: Your project team have planned the requirements, scope, schedule and cost for constructing a new building for your organization. As your project is funded and about to begin execution, an executive from another area approaches you and asks if you can also help them deliver a website. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Raise the request as an issue in your project's issue log.
opzioni.B: Add the website to your project scope and adjust your project scope, schedule and cost.
opzioni.C: Raise a change request for the added scope and review the impact on your project schedule and cost.
opzioni.D: Offer to help them create a business case for the new idea and get funding for a new project.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not an issue.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Different team and scope.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Wrong project.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. A business case precedes a new project charter.

domande.spiegazione: Business case (PMBOK 7, p. 184).

domande.domanda: You're working on an agile project and planning your product backlog for the next three to six months. You have high-level features and feature ideas from various parts of your organization, from frontline staff to executives to customer research. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Break down each feature into epics and user stories, then size the work with your team.
opzioni.B: Add all of the items into your product backlog and work on the ones from the managers first.
opzioni.C: Work with the requesters and your technical experts to create a business model canvas for each feature.
opzioni.D: Perform precedence diagramming on each feature to determine the dependencies.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Too detailed too early.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. HiPPO.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. One-page summary of value, customers, infrastructure and finances.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Too early.

domande.spiegazione: Business model canvas (PMBOK 7, p. 184).

domande.domanda: You're working in a new agile team where the work has started to slow, and there is uncertainty and low team engagement. You set aside time to create a team charter with your team, agreeing on roles and responsibilities and the team cadence. What else will you do?

opzioni.A: Set a team goal for them to be more engaged in the work over the next three months.
opzioni.B: Create a product vision statement showing the value you're bringing and the why behind the work.
opzioni.C: Ask the team to contribute more to all pieces of work during each team meeting.
opzioni.D: Raise it as a people issue for your project and manage it with the project steering committee.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Vague.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. A vision states purpose and inspires contribution.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Pressure.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Manage first.

domande.spiegazione: Project vision statement (PMBOK 7, p. 184).

domande.domanda: You're integrating a third-party system as part of your project. The developers on your team have not worked on this system before, but they believe the language and layout are the same, so they should be able to work with it. Adding a bit of time for the uncertainty, they give a high-level estimate of five weeks. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Note the estimate of five weeks and update the assumption log with the technical assumption that the language and layout are the same.
opzioni.B: Don't add the estimate yet: break the integration down into user stories and use a bottom-up approach.
opzioni.C: Check the estimate using parametric estimating to increase its accuracy.
opzioni.D: Gather your whole team and customers together and estimate using Wideband Delphi or planning poker.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. The assumption log records assumptions and constraints.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Possible, more effort.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. No parameters.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Heavy for now.

domande.spiegazione: Assumption log (PMBOK 7, p. 185).

domande.domanda: Your agile project has delivered 3 features so far and is halfway through delivering the latest improvement. During a brainstorming session, one of your customers comes up with a new feature idea. You check it: the benefit is high and the complexity is low. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Add money to your budget to accommodate the additional feature as soon as possible.
opzioni.B: Elaborate on the feature, break it down into user stories and estimate them.
opzioni.C: Place the item in the backlog and reprioritize it to be next.
opzioni.D: Create a business case for the new feature, outlining the benefits and costs involved.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Agile: fixed budget.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Prioritize first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Backlog items are ordered by priority.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Not for agile.

domande.spiegazione: Backlog (PMBOK 7, p. 185).

domande.domanda: One of the senior users testing your product has found that it is missing a key requirement he had assumed would be there. It was not noted in the project scope, which has already been baselined. You check the impact on cost and schedule, raise a change request on his behalf and take it to the change control board, where it is approved. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Ask your team to elaborate the requirement and turn it into user stories.
opzioni.B: Place the new requirement into the sprint backlog for the next sprint.
opzioni.C: Add the missed requirement to the issue log and problem-solve with your team to ensure it doesn't happen again.
opzioni.D: Note the outcome in the change log and communicate it to your stakeholders.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. After communicating.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. After elaborating.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Later.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. The change log records changes and status.

domande.spiegazione: Change log (PMBOK 7, p. 185).

domande.domanda: You're working on a hybrid project to replace an ageing customer system, which has just had a feature upgrade release. During the daily stand-up, the senior developer raises a concern that the system no longer seems able to connect to some parts of the organization. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Re-plan the project to ensure the correct scope is worked on so it will connect to the organization.
opzioni.B: Raise it in the issue log, assign it to a responsible party and work with them to find a resolution.
opzioni.C: Raise the concern as a risk and brainstorm risk responses.
opzioni.D: Escalate the issue to the technical manager so they can resolve it.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Premature.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Issues are logged and assigned for resolution.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Already happened.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Assign the right party.

domande.spiegazione: Issue log (PMBOK 7, p. 185).

domande.domanda: You're working on an agile project where your project team have raised multiple risks to project delivery, some of which may significantly impact your cost and schedule. Your program manager asks you to manage them using a risk-adjusted backlog. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Adjust your risk register to include the work not completed if the risks are triggered.
opzioni.B: Adjust your backlog velocity so that your end date is not impacted by the raised risks.
opzioni.C: Gather risk mitigation responses from your retrospectives and assign them to an owner.
opzioni.D: Place at least one risk response in each sprint to manage and close the risks.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not a backlog.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Not this.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Partial.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. A risk-adjusted backlog includes actions for threats and opportunities.

domande.spiegazione: Risk-adjusted backlog (PMBOK 7, p. 185).

domande.domanda: You're delivering a project to a functional area in your organization. The project is highly complex and there are many risks to project delivery. The functional manager would like to see the biggest risks that are assigned to her. What will you do?

opzioni.A: Show her the risk-adjusted backlog.
opzioni.B: Show her the risk register.
opzioni.C: Show her the risk management plan.
opzioni.D: Show her the qualitative risk assessment.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not clearly agile.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Records owners, probability, impact and responses.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Process.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. No owners.

domande.spiegazione: Risk register (PMBOK 7, p. 185).

domande.domanda: Your project has been in progress for the past six months. Someone you have not met before approaches you and says he hasn't been engaged sufficiently, even though he believes his team is highly impacted by the project. He advises he may block the project as a result. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Perform a stakeholder engagement assessment with this stakeholder.
opzioni.B: Add him to the stakeholder register, including his salary and interest information.
opzioni.C: Add him to the stakeholder register, including his impact and influence information.
opzioni.D: Raise a risk to project delivery due to the nature of his actions.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Good, but record him first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Irrelevant data.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. The register records assessment and classification.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Manage first.

domande.spiegazione: Stakeholder register (PMBOK 7, p. 185).

domande.domanda: ⚠️ You are a product owner on an agile project and you've created a product backlog of features in priority order for delivery. You ask the team to break down the first feature into user stories and estimate their effort. What will you do next? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Create an iteration plan with your team.
opzioni.B: Create the product roadmap with your team.
opzioni.C: Hold a sprint review.
opzioni.D: Begin daily stand-ups with your team.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Matches estimated work to velocity.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Already past.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. After the sprint.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. After planning.

domande.spiegazione: Iteration plan (PMBOK 7, p. 186).
domande.nota: Option C is unclear in the transcript: reconstructed as the sprint review.
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: You have worked with your project customer to create a list of features that will bring the most value to them. They would like to see when some of this value will be delivered, and the expected outcomes of each feature. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Show the features at the next sprint review so the customer can see what they look like.
opzioni.B: Place the features on a release plan and show it to the customer.
opzioni.C: Check the features against the velocity chart to see when they might be delivered.
opzioni.D: Place the features into the next sprint plan and show it to your customer.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Only past work.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Sets expectations for dates, features and outcomes.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. An input.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Only one sprint.

domande.spiegazione: Release plan (PMBOK 7, p. 186).

domande.domanda: You're in the planning stages of your project, where you need to find out exactly what the project customer needs so you can find a solution. Your business analysts are new to their roles and aren't sure what their process will be. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Ask the business analysts to begin writing user stories.
opzioni.B: Create the project management plan to outline how the project will be delivered.
opzioni.C: Work with the business analysts to create a requirements management plan.
opzioni.D: Create a work breakdown structure of the project scope.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. No process yet.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Too broad.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Describes how requirements are analyzed, documented and managed.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. One step only.

domande.spiegazione: Requirements management plan (PMBOK 7, p. 186).

domande.domanda: You're working on a new software application with a lot of complex interdependencies. The senior user providing and testing most of the requirements is concerned that some of those dependencies will cause errors upon release if they're not caught. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Ask the senior user for a written list of all his requirements, then check whether they're included in the project scope.
opzioni.B: Raise a risk on the software complexity with the project team.
opzioni.C: Create an affinity diagram with the senior user.
opzioni.D: Review the test plan with the senior user.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not testing.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Partial.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Groups ideas.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Describes what, how and when is tested.

domande.spiegazione: Test plan (PMBOK 7, p. 186).

domande.domanda: You're planning your project and have captured the requirements from the project customer. You ask your team to plan the project scope, but they need to see exactly what needs to be delivered and how each part relates to the others. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Create a product breakdown structure with your team.
opzioni.B: Create the requirements traceability matrix with your project team.
opzioni.C: Create the risk breakdown structure with your project team.
opzioni.D: Create the scope management plan with your project team.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Hierarchical tree of deliverables in whole-part relationship.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Traces requirements.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Risks.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Process.

domande.spiegazione: Product breakdown structure (PMBOK 7, p. 187).

domande.domanda: You've just finished breaking down, with your project team, the scope that will meet your customer's requirements. Your program manager wants to control the project scope, so that any changes go through the proper process. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Create the change management plan to see how changes will be managed.
opzioni.B: Baseline the project scope and note it in the configuration management plan.
opzioni.C: Create the scope management plan with a rule minimizing changes.
opzioni.D: Create a responsibility assignment matrix limiting the roles who can approve project scope changes.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Needs a baseline first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Baselines are noted in the configuration management plan.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Process only.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Partial.

domande.spiegazione: Baselines (PMBOK 7, p. 188).

domande.domanda: You have planned and begun the current sprint, in which the project team have committed to delivering and releasing a particular feature. You need to see how the team are tracking towards their sprint goal. What will you do?

opzioni.A: Check the Kanban board.
opzioni.B: Check the velocity chart.
opzioni.C: Review the sprint burndown chart.
opzioni.D: Perform a sprint review with the team.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Less direct.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Past sprints.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Compares ideal trend with work remaining.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. After the sprint.

domande.spiegazione: Burndown chart (PMBOK 7, p. 188).

domande.domanda: Your agile project has recently been merged into a larger program, and the program manager is reviewing how the project is tracking. She asks you how much has been completed in design, and also how much has been completed in development, testing and sign-off. What will you do?

opzioni.A: Show her the sprint Kanban board.
opzioni.B: Take her through the team's product backlog.
opzioni.C: Show her the team's cumulative flow diagram.
opzioni.D: Show her the team's velocity chart.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. One sprint only.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. No stages.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Shows features completed over time by stage.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Totals only.

domande.spiegazione: Cumulative flow diagram (PMBOK 7, p. 188).

domande.domanda: The features developed by your agile team have added some complexity to your website, as they were delivered quickly with no time to refactor the code. You believe the user stories are moving more slowly now as a result, but you can't be sure. What will you do?

opzioni.A: Check the team's cycle time chart.
opzioni.B: Shadow the developers to observe the work they're doing.
opzioni.C: View the product roadmap for the proposed release dates.
opzioni.D: Review the points in the sprint backlog against the velocity of the last three sprints.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Shows average cycle time over time.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Not data.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Release dates.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Team-level only.

domande.spiegazione: Cycle time chart (PMBOK 7, p. 189).

domande.domanda: You're working on an agile project with a full product roadmap for the next 6 months. Your project team are not sure what the next feature does or how they should turn it into user stories. What will you do?

opzioni.A: Review the scope baseline.
opzioni.B: Perform story mapping with your team.
opzioni.C: Perform sprint planning with your team.
opzioni.D: Perform a retrospective with your team.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not agile.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Holistic view of features, broken into stories by functionality.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Needs stories first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Not for this.

domande.spiegazione: Story map (PMBOK 7, p. 190).

domande.domanda: ⚠️ You're a program manager on a large-scale agile program where each project team has its own Scrum Master. You need to know the rate at which work is flowing through each team, so you can see whether there are any blockers or issues and whether the teams will remain on track. What will you do? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Raise your query at the Scrum of Scrums so each team knows what they need to do.
opzioni.B: Attend each team's sprint review at the end of each sprint.
opzioni.C: Review the schedule management plan for managing the schedule.
opzioni.D: Review each team's velocity chart, showing the work committed versus completed in each sprint.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Indirect.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Demos only.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Process.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Tracks the rate deliverables are produced and accepted.

domande.spiegazione: Velocity chart (PMBOK 7, p. 190).
domande.nota: Option D is not read in the source video: text reconstructed from the answer and the explanation.
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: Your project has been executing for the past five months and, due to an organizational change, a new project sponsor has come on board. He asks where the project is up to and whether it's on track. You tell him, but he wants more information. What will you do?

opzioni.A: Show him the signed project charter.
opzioni.B: Show him the project management plan, including the schedule management plan.
opzioni.C: Review the current and previous status reports with the sponsor.
opzioni.D: Invite him to the next sprint review so he can see the progress made.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Start of project.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Process.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Status and progress since last report, with forecasts.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Partial.

domande.spiegazione: Status report (PMBOK 7, p. 190).

domande.domanda: Your agile project needs a third-party vendor to help complete the work. The product owner has multiple features on their roadmap, which may change or be reprioritized over time, making the scope of your project uncertain. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Ask your product owner to fix the features and scope so the project is more certain.
opzioni.B: Create a cost plus incentive fee contract with your procurement team.
opzioni.C: Create a firm fixed price contract with your procurement team.
opzioni.D: Use the external vendor funding to create a project team in-house and complete the project.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not agile.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Cost-reimbursable suits ill-defined or changing scope.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Fixed scope needed.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Complex and uncertain.

domande.spiegazione: Cost-reimbursable contracts (PMBOK 7, p. 191).

domande.domanda: Your project is releasing a number of upgrades to a commercial building over the next 12 months. Material costs have changed a lot recently, and you need to budget for the materials required; however, the volume of materials may change significantly as the project evolves. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Create an indefinite delivery, indefinite quantity (IDIQ) contract for the materials.
opzioni.B: Create a firm fixed price contract for the materials.
opzioni.C: Ensure a sole supplier for your materials.
opzioni.D: Ensure multiple suppliers for your materials.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Quantity within limits over a fixed period.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Needs known quantity.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Doesn't address quantity.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Doesn't address quantity.

domande.spiegazione: Agreements and contracts (PMBOK 7, p. 191).
domande.nota: Option order reconstructed.

domande.domanda: You've completed a make-or-buy analysis and agreed to hire a third-party vendor to complete part of your product. You've created the statement of work and have a list of acceptable sellers that meet the source selection criteria. The work is not complex and the sellers understand the scope. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Send a request for proposal (RFP).
opzioni.B: Send a request for information (RFI) to the sellers you like.
opzioni.C: Send a request for quotation (RFQ).
opzioni.D: Hold a bidder conference to ensure all sellers are on the same page.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. For complex.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Info already known.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Requirements are ready: just need price.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Already understood.

domande.spiegazione: Bid documents (PMBOK 7, p. 192).

domande.domanda: Your project is new and the team have just come on board. There have been multiple disagreements, and the work is slow as they try to understand where they fit in the project and the team. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Create a project charter.
opzioni.B: Create a definition of ready.
opzioni.C: Create a project management plan.
opzioni.D: Create a team charter.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Authorizes project.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Work readiness.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Management processes.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Records team values, agreements and guidelines.

domande.spiegazione: Team charter (PMBOK 7, p. 192).

domande.domanda: You've created a high-level view of the features your project will deliver and prioritized them in the product backlog. The development team is ready to start work, but they don't know where to start, as the information is too high level. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Ask the team to begin with the highest-priority item first.
opzioni.B: Help the team break the features down into user stories that can fit into a sprint.
opzioni.C: Hold a retrospective with the team to understand what's blocking them.
opzioni.D: Reprioritize the features into an order that makes sense for the developers.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Still too high-level.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Stories have enough detail to work on.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. After a sprint.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Doesn't add detail.

domande.spiegazione: User story (PMBOK 7, p. 192).

domande.domanda: You're working as an agile project manager. The executive manager who will own the product you're delivering (potentially the product owner) would like to focus primarily on set processes and tools to manage the project. What will you recommend to them instead of set processes and tools?

opzioni.A: Focus on the definition of success as defined by the project manager.
opzioni.B: Focus primarily on the individuals and interactions involved.
opzioni.C: Focus primarily on the scope of the project.
opzioni.D: Focus primarily on the schedule of the project.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Success is defined by the product owner/customer the team is serving, not by the project manager.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. The Agile Manifesto values individuals and interactions over processes and tools: projects are run by people, and interactions (stand-ups, retrospectives) make or break them.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. A primary focus on scope belongs to a traditional (waterfall) approach, not to agile.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. A primary focus on schedule belongs to a traditional (waterfall) approach, not to agile.

domande.spiegazione: Projects are run by people: interactions make or break them. Agile Practice Guide.

domande.domanda: The executive management in your organization has assembled a new team and dictated that they will use agile for their product development. As the project progresses, there is confusion about the product scope and about what 'done' looks like. As an agile project manager, what will you recommend to the executive team?

opzioni.A: Select a person from each part of the organization to assist, to ensure diversity.
opzioni.B: Have the functional manager select their friends or favorite team members.
opzioni.C: Encourage a self-organizing team to form, including the people who asked for the requirements and the outcomes in the first place.
opzioni.D: Hire external consultants to run the project and create the product.
