spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Diversity matters, but people picked from across the organization may not be interested in or invested in the product.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Favorites are not necessarily the best people for the job.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Agile encourages self-organizing teams built around the people who created the requirements and want the outcome: higher ownership and product expertise.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. External consultants usually don't know the business and need a long ramp-up time.

domande.spiegazione: Agile encourages self-organizing teams of the people who own the need. Agile Practice Guide.

domande.domanda: You're running an agile project and you meet with the team for the next sprint planning meeting. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Negotiate the scope and costs of the project with the project sponsor.
opzioni.B: Walk through the three questions with the team: what did I do yesterday, what will I do today, and is anything blocking me?
opzioni.C: Have the development team demonstrate the working feature to the product owner, who marks it as complete.
opzioni.D: Have the product owner share the updated backlog, and the team discuss it to ensure a shared understanding.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Scope and cost are discussed before the agile team forms; cost is usually fixed.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Those are the three questions of the daily stand-up, not of sprint planning.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. That is the sprint review (demonstration), held at the end of the sprint.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. In sprint planning the product owner brings the prioritized backlog and the whole team discusses it to reach a shared understanding of what will be worked on.

domande.spiegazione: Sprint planning: prioritized backlog + shared understanding.

domande.domanda: You're a project manager working on an agile project, and you want your team to maximize the value they bring to the customer. What can you eliminate in order to maximize project value?

opzioni.A: Daily stand-ups.
opzioni.B: Unnecessary features.
opzioni.C: Sprint reviews.
opzioni.D: Testing.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Stand-ups give visibility and keep everyone on the same page.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Unnecessary features are waste. Value is also maximized by eliminating partially done work, delays, extra processes, task switching, waiting, handoffs and defects.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Sprint reviews provide feedback on the product and must be kept.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Testing ensures quality items are released and must be kept.

domande.spiegazione: Eliminate waste to maximize value.

domande.domanda: You're working on a project and the team has recently moved to an agile way of working. One of the team members is confused about Scrum and what typically happens after the sprint review. What will you tell them happens next?

opzioni.A: Hold a sprint retrospective with the team.
opzioni.B: Perform backlog refinement with the product owner.
opzioni.C: Perform story card elaboration with the three amigos (business/product owner, developers and testers).
opzioni.D: Hold a daily scrum.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. The sprint retrospective is held with the whole team after the sprint review and before the next sprint planning, to gather lessons learned and improve.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Backlog refinement usually happens before iteration planning.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Story card elaboration also happens before iteration planning.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The daily scrum happens every day, not specifically after the sprint review.

domande.spiegazione: The retrospective gathers lessons learned for the next sprint.

domande.domanda: You're working in an agile team and preparing the agile team charter (the team's agreement on its way of working). You work with the team to ensure the charter answers four questions. Two of them are 'Why are we doing this project?' and 'Who benefits from the project?'. Which are the other two?

opzioni.A: When will the project end? What do we do with the product?
opzioni.B: What does done mean for the project? How are we going to work together?
opzioni.C: How much risk is on the project? What is the project scope?
opzioni.D: How many defects are allowed in the product? How many testers are there?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. These are not team charter questions.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. According to the Agile Practice Guide, the team charter covers why we're doing the project, who benefits, what done looks like, and how we will work together.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Risk and scope are classic project management questions that go into the project management plan.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. These don't go into the team charter: quality is everyone's responsibility.

domande.spiegazione: Agile Practice Guide.

domande.domanda: You're working with a new agile project manager and explain that agile favors value-based measurements instead of predictive measurements on a project. What is an example of value-based measurements?

opzioni.A: Earned value management and the schedule performance index.
opzioni.B: Variance analysis and estimate to complete.
opzioni.C: The feature burndown chart, features delivered and customer satisfaction.
opzioni.D: Variance at completion and the cost performance index.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. These are predictive measurements from a traditional (waterfall) methodology.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. These are predictive measurements found in the PMBOK Guide.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Agile's primary measurement is value delivered: features delivered, feature burndown and customer satisfaction.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. These are predictive (earned value) measurements.

domande.spiegazione: Agile measures value delivered.

domande.domanda: Agile Unified Process (AUP) is an auxiliary agile method that performs more iterative cycles across seven key disciplines and incorporates the associated feedback before formal delivery. Which of the following is NOT one of the seven key disciplines within a release of the Agile Unified Process?

opzioni.A: Discipline in the high-level model.
opzioni.B: Discipline in managing stakeholder expectations.
opzioni.C: Discipline in testing.
opzioni.D: Discipline in configuration management.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect: this IS a discipline. Building a high-level model first is a common agile practice.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct: this is NOT a discipline. Agile focuses on transparency to ensure customer needs are met, not on specifically managing stakeholder expectations.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect: this IS a discipline. Testing is very important in agile.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect: this IS a discipline. Configuration management merges and tests code regularly to see if anything breaks.

domande.spiegazione: Agile Practice Guide.

domande.domanda: You're leading a coaching session with your project team on the additional agile and lean frameworks that have contributed to the agile way of working. Which frameworks will you share with the team?

opzioni.A: The project management plan and the project charter.
opzioni.B: The Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe) and Large-Scale Scrum (LeSS).
opzioni.C: Working group meetings and post-mortem project meetings.
opzioni.D: Flowcharting and affinity diagrams.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. These are predictive project documents, not frameworks.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Agile and lean frameworks include SAFe, LeSS, Scrum of Scrums, DSDM, as well as Kanban, Extreme Programming (XP) and Scrum (Agile Practice Guide).
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. These are traditional project meetings.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. These are analysis tools (used, for example, by business analysts), not agile or lean frameworks.

domande.spiegazione: Agile Practice Guide.

domande.domanda: Crystal was introduced by Alistair Cockburn in his book 'Crystal Clear' and created at IBM in 1991. It is a framework that focuses on individuals and their interactions as opposed to processes and tools: not a set process, but a guideline for the team to collaborate and communicate. Which of the following is NOT one of the core beliefs of Crystal?

opzioni.A: Technologies change techniques.
opzioni.B: People change functions.
opzioni.C: Cultures change norms.
opzioni.D: Distances change communication.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect: this IS a core belief. The technologies available change the techniques the team uses (e.g. video conferencing vs. same-room stand-ups).
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct: this is NOT a core belief of Crystal.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect: this IS a core belief. An organization's culture changes the team's norms.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect: this IS a core belief. Co-located and distributed teams communicate very differently.

domande.spiegazione: Crystal beliefs underpin stand-ups, collaboration, retrospectives.

domande.domanda: You're working on a project in the role of Scrum Master and have set a meeting with the team and the product owner to refine the product backlog. What should the team do in this meeting?

opzioni.A: Estimate and refine the work items.
opzioni.B: Prioritize the work items.
opzioni.C: Add features to the product backlog.
opzioni.D: Identify fixes.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. The product owner adjusts the priority; the team estimates and refines the items, adding more detail each time.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Prioritization is done by the product owner, who should always come with a prioritized list.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Features are added before prioritizing and before this meeting.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Fixes can come at any time; that is not the purpose of backlog refinement.

domande.spiegazione: PO prioritizes; team estimates and refines.

domande.domanda: You're working with a team that would like to become agile. The functional manager asks you what the difference between Kanban and Scrum is. What will you tell them?

opzioni.A: Kanban teams plan their work in sprints or iterations.
opzioni.B: There are no work-in-progress limits in Kanban.
opzioni.C: Kanban teams work on the project as a whole.
opzioni.D: Kanban teams employ a pull system.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Planning in sprints is typical of Scrum.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Work-in-progress limits are what Kanban is all about.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Kanban teams work in increments, not on the product as a whole.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. In Kanban, completing an item triggers someone to pull the next item onto the board, and WIP limits cap how much work is in progress.

domande.spiegazione: Kanban: pull system and WIP limits.

domande.domanda: You're working on a new project with an agile product development team that has self-formed and chosen a Scrum Master called Jeremy. Jeremy immediately sets a meeting with the team to explain and flesh out their team charter. What has made Jeremy a good choice for Scrum Master?

opzioni.A: He likes to work within set processes.
opzioni.B: He has been with the company for more than five years.
opzioni.C: He shows servant leadership and engages the team in team decisions.
opzioni.D: He sticks to the plan and does not change.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Agile values interactions over processes and tools.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Tenure may make him good at his job, but not necessarily a good Scrum Master.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. He engages the team in decisions, starting with the charter and ground rules: servant leadership rather than command and control.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Agile teams respond to change rather than rigidly following a plan.

domande.spiegazione: Servant leaders engage rather than command.

domande.domanda: You're managing a project as an agile project manager. A business representative for the product you're delivering asks how many defects were found in the latest round of testing. You don't know the answer off the top of your head. What should you do?

opzioni.A: Guess the number of defects and then change the subject.
opzioni.B: Tell the business partner you will send them an email with the information.
opzioni.C: Take them to the team area where the information radiator with the project information is displayed.
opzioni.D: Ask the business partner to call the Scrum Master to get the correct answer.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. It happens in real life, but it isn't transparent or agile.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Agile prefers face-to-face interaction and self-service information over email.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. The information radiator (physical or online) shows velocity, Kanban board, backlog, burndown, latest test results and retrospective results to anyone who wants them.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Information should be available to everyone, not held by one person.

domande.spiegazione: Information radiators enable transparency.

domande.domanda: You're working in a company that is moving from a waterfall methodology to agile. You mention to the business unit manager that, using agile, the team will be better prepared to respond to change and meet customer needs. Why is this?

opzioni.A: The agile team works directly with a business owner or representative to constantly prioritize the value delivered.
opzioni.B: The agile team delivers the product all in one go.
opzioni.C: The agile team is for developers only, so development will improve.
opzioni.D: The business partners review statuses and ask for recommendations.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Working almost daily with the business (face to face rather than through documents or emails) lets the team constantly reprioritize to deliver the right value.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Agile delivers in small increments and features, not all in one go.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Agile can be used by anyone: it's a way of working, not only for technical work.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The business tells the team what to work on and what value it wants delivered.

domande.spiegazione: Face to face with the business beats documents.

domande.domanda: In agile life cycles, two kinds of planning occur: release planning and iteration planning. In release planning, business representatives such as the product owner establish and prioritize the user stories for the release (the product backlog), working with the team to refine larger user stories into collections of smaller ones. Which description below is INCORRECT regarding iteration planning and backlog preparation?

opzioni.A: The backlog is the ordered list of all the work, presented in story form, for a team.
opzioni.B: The coach encourages the team to work alone, so that no one bothers them.
opzioni.C: The facilitator encourages the team to work in triads of developer, tester, and product owner or business analyst.
opzioni.D: The triad discusses and writes the stories, then places enough stories into an iteration and enough features for a first release.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect (this statement is correct). The backlog is the ordered list of all work in story form.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct (this statement is INCORRECT). Agile teams collaborate continuously; working alone goes against agile principles.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect (this statement is correct). This is the 'three amigos', a core agile practice.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect (this statement is correct). This is good practice for iteration and release planning.

domande.spiegazione: Agile Practice Guide.

domande.domanda: Behavior-Driven Development (BDD) allows a developer to focus on testing the code based on the expected behavior of the software, and it is a method of writing user stories and their acceptance criteria. What is the correct format for BDD acceptance criteria?

opzioni.A: Make, buy and do.
opzioni.B: Tell, show and repeat.
opzioni.C: Find, create and perform.
opzioni.D: Given, when, then.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. This is not a BDD format.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. This is not a BDD format.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. This is not a BDD format.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Given a certain situation, when something happens, then we want this outcome. It's used especially when outlining user story cards for an iteration.

domande.spiegazione: BDD acceptance criteria use Given-When-Then.

domande.domanda: ⚠️ Every project has characteristics around requirements, delivery, change and goals. Understanding the different types of life cycle allows you to choose the right one for the circumstances of your project. What is the correct description of a waterfall (predictive) approach? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Predictive: fixed requirements, activities performed once for the entire project, single delivery.
opzioni.B: Predictive: variable requirements, activities repeated until correct, single delivery.
opzioni.C: Predictive: fixed requirements, activities repeated until correct, frequent smaller deliveries.
opzioni.D: Predictive: variable requirements, activities performed once for the entire project, frequent smaller deliveries.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. A predictive (waterfall) life cycle has fixed requirements, activities performed once for the whole project, and a single 'big bang' delivery.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Variable requirements and repetition until correct describe an iterative approach.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Waterfall doesn't repeat activities or deliver frequently.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Waterfall has fixed requirements and a single delivery.

domande.spiegazione: Agile Practice Guide.
domande.nota: All four options start with 'predictive'; the exact wording of B, C and D is reconstructed from the commentary.
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: ⚠️ Every project has characteristics around requirements, delivery, change and goals. Understanding the different types of life cycle allows you to choose the right one for your project. Agile is made up of iterative and incremental approaches. What is the correct description of an iterative approach? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Fixed requirements, activities repeated until correct, single delivery.
opzioni.B: Dynamic requirements, activities repeated until correct, single delivery.
opzioni.C: Dynamic requirements, activities repeated until correct, multiple deliveries.
opzioni.D: Fixed requirements, activities performed once, multiple deliveries.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Iterating towards success means requirements keep changing: they are not fixed.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Iterative methods have dynamic requirements, repeated with feedback until correct, but delivered only once.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Multiple deliveries combined with iteration describe agile, not purely iterative.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Fixed requirements performed once don't describe iteration.

domande.spiegazione: Agile Practice Guide.
domande.nota: Option text reconstructed from the commentary.
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: The agile team charter is also a social contract. Which of the following is NOT usually part of an agile team charter?

opzioni.A: Team values, such as sustainable pace and core hours.
opzioni.B: Working agreements, such as what 'ready' and 'done' mean.
opzioni.C: Ground rules, such as only one person talking in a meeting.
opzioni.D: The schedule performance index (SPI) and cost performance index (CPI) for the project.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect: this IS part of the charter. Sustainable pace and core hours are typical team values.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect: this IS part of the charter. Definitions of ready and done are key working agreements.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect: this IS part of the charter. Ground rules belong to the team's agreement.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct: this is NOT part of it. SPI and CPI are earned value metrics from predictive projects; the charter focuses on the vision, the why and the team's way of working.

domande.spiegazione: Charter focuses on vision, why and ways of working.

domande.domanda: You're working with a team that is new to agile, and you're using Scrum to manage the project. The business representative is confused about the difference between a sprint review and a sprint retrospective. What will you tell them?

opzioni.A: Sprint reviews demonstrate the work completed in the sprint; sprint retrospectives look at all the work completed in the project.
opzioni.B: Sprint reviews discuss what was worked on in the sprint; sprint retrospectives are done at the end of the project as a lessons-learned opportunity.
opzioni.C: Sprint reviews review the lessons learned; sprint retrospectives look at the history of the product retrospectively.
opzioni.D: Sprint reviews are for product demonstrations; sprint retrospectives are for lessons learned.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The first half is right, but retrospectives look at the iteration, not all the work in the project.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Retrospectives are held at the end of every iteration, not only at the end of the project.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. This mixes up the two events.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Reviews demonstrate the product to the business/customer; retrospectives ask what went well, what didn't go well and what we learned.

domande.spiegazione: Review = demo; retrospective = process improvement.

domande.domanda: You're working on an agile project as a team member and begin gathering the product requirements. What is the overall first question you should ask and use as a guide for your work?

opzioni.A: How long will the project last?
opzioni.B: What is the business value?
opzioni.C: How much is the budget?
opzioni.D: How many team members will participate?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. A valid question, but not the first one on an agile project.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Agile projects center on delivering business value; the business risk and the impact of not doing the project should also be considered.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. A valid question, but not the core purpose.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. A valid question, but not the first one.

domande.spiegazione: Also consider business risk of not doing the project.

domande.domanda: The agile team, for which you're the project manager, has determined several key features to deliver to the customer. How should these features be tackled by the team?

opzioni.A: The features should be prioritized, tested and delivered incrementally.
opzioni.B: The features should be delivered quickly, whether or not they are complete, to gather feedback.
opzioni.C: The features should be delivered according to the project plan.
opzioni.D: All the features should be delivered at the end of the project.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Agile combines incremental delivery and iterative development: value is continuously prioritized and delivered in complete, tested increments the customer can use.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Agile is fast, but quality is everyone's responsibility: features must be complete and usable.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Following a plan for everything is a waterfall approach.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Delivering everything at the end is a waterfall approach.

domande.spiegazione: Quality is everyone's responsibility.

domande.domanda: You're working on an agile project and the project team has just finished an iteration. All tasks for the iteration are complete and you're ready to move on to the next iteration, but you're not sure what the team should work on. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Follow the project plan developed early in the project.
opzioni.B: Follow the project management office, which has already determined how the project should progress.
opzioni.C: Ask the product owner, who continuously prioritizes the backlog.
opzioni.D: Ask the project coach or team leader to determine the next iteration.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Following an early project plan is a waterfall approach.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. A PMO dictating the path is a waterfall approach.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. The product owner represents the customer and continuously prioritizes the backlog by value.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Prioritizing features is the product owner's role, not the coach's.

domande.spiegazione: Work from the PO-prioritized backlog.

domande.domanda: While you're meeting with the customers or business owners, they introduce several pieces of new functionality into the product backlog. The deadline for the product cannot be changed. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Tell the team to work overtime in order to deliver the project.
opzioni.B: Stand by your team and tell the customers the project will not be delivered on time.
opzioni.C: Make sure the customers understand that lower-priority features may drop off the project completely.
opzioni.D: Agree with the customers to put all new items into a separate category that will be completed if time allows.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Agile requires a sustainable pace: overworking burns the team out.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Agile keeps delivering value; it doesn't simply declare the deadline missed.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. In agile, cost, quality and schedule are often fixed while scope varies: higher-value features are delivered and lower-priority ones may drop off.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. A decent idea, but agile handles this through prioritization of business value.

domande.spiegazione: Accept late change; keep a sustainable pace.

domande.domanda: ⚠️ Every project has characteristics around requirements, delivery, change and goals. Understanding the different types of life cycle allows you to choose the right one for the circumstances of your project. What is the correct description of an incremental project management approach? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Fixed requirements, activities performed once, multiple deliveries.
opzioni.B: Dynamic requirements, activities repeated until correct, one large delivery.
opzioni.C: Dynamic requirements, activities performed once for a given increment, frequent smaller deliveries.
opzioni.D: Dynamic requirements, activities repeated until correct, frequent smaller deliveries.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Close, but incremental work has dynamic requirements.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Incremental delivers in multiple deliveries, not one large delivery (and 'repeated until correct' is iterative).
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Each increment goes through the whole process once and is delivered in frequent, smaller deliveries.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Repeating until correct plus frequent deliveries describes agile (iterative + incremental), not purely incremental.

domande.spiegazione: Agile Practice Guide.
domande.nota: Option D is not clearly read in the source: written as a plausible distractor.
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: There are certain core practices common to the various agile frameworks, used by any team that calls itself agile. Which of the following is NOT a core agile practice?

opzioni.A: Team iteration planning.
opzioni.B: Collaborative user story creation between the business/customer, developers and testers.
opzioni.C: Demonstrations and reviews of the features.
opzioni.D: Autocratic leadership to ensure the work gets done.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect: this IS a core agile practice.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect: this IS a core agile practice.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect: this IS a core agile practice.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct: this is NOT a core practice. Agile prefers servant leadership, which builds psychological safety; autocratic leadership is a top-down, one-person affair.

domande.spiegazione: Agile Practice Guide.

domande.domanda: Poor specifications are often a major reason for project failure. In agile development, user stories are written with the developers, testers and business representatives, with frequent reviews to ensure they are right. Which of the following is NOT correct regarding collaborative user story creation?

opzioni.A: A user story addresses both functional and non-functional requirements.
opzioni.B: The project sponsor must sign off on all user stories in advance.
opzioni.C: A user story includes acceptance criteria for the feature.
opzioni.D: Acceptance criteria must be estimable, small and testable.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect (this statement is correct).
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct (this statement is NOT correct). Developers, testers and the business agree on the story criteria; the stories are not signed off by the sponsor. The product owner grooms the backlog.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect (this statement is correct).
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect (this statement is correct).

domande.spiegazione: PO, not sponsor, owns the backlog.

domande.domanda: In continuous integration, configuration management, compilation, software build, deployment and testing are wrapped into a single, automated, repeatable process. Because of this, defects in the code are:

opzioni.A: Not an issue, making it an ideal method.
opzioni.B: Detected more quickly, because the team constantly integrates, builds and tests its work.
opzioni.C: Integrated into the work as part of test-driven development.
opzioni.D: Collected and fixed in an iteration at the end of the project to avoid delay.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Defects are still an issue and must be watched for.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. CI merges code into a test environment with automated regression tests, so defects are found and fixed more quickly.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Test-driven development (test first, then code) is a separate practice that happens before integration.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Defects should be found and fixed as you go, not saved for the end.

domande.spiegazione: CI + automated regression = faster defect finding.

domande.domanda: Agile has certain core practices used by any team working in an agile way. Which of the following is NOT a core agile practice?

opzioni.A: The whole team approach, where anyone who is needed is brought into the project team.
opzioni.B: Early and frequent feedback, so everyone shares a common understanding of the product.
opzioni.C: Daily stand-ups to report progress and raise blockers.
opzioni.D: Reporting to executives to ensure they're happy with your project.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect: this IS a core practice. External dependencies are brought into the team where possible.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect: this IS a core practice.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect: this IS a core practice.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct: this is NOT a core practice. Executives are rather included in demos/reviews and can see burndown charts and the backlog on information radiators.

domande.spiegazione: Agile Practice Guide.

domande.domanda: You're working on an agile project. As an agile project manager, you look at the product backlog and ensure that several features or minimum viable products (MVPs) can be scheduled for delivery throughout the duration of the project. Why is that a good idea?

opzioni.A: To show executives that the development team is making progress.
opzioni.B: To keep the project duration short.
opzioni.C: To deliver multiple features so users can test the product for quality and give feedback.
opzioni.D: To enable the business to get value quickly as the features are delivered.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. A side effect, not the core reason.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The project may still run for a while; that's not the reason.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Partly true for an MVP, but not the core reason.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. MVPs are usable features delivered incrementally, so business value is gained more quickly and feedback can be gathered along the way.

domande.spiegazione: MVPs deliver value incrementally.

domande.domanda: You're working on a complex software project and see that the team uses a whiteboard and writes tasks on cards or sticky notes. The business representative seems put off by the use of these low-tech tools on such a high-profile technology project. What will you tell them?

opzioni.A: The team is using low-tech tools so that low-tech people can understand them.
opzioni.B: A whiteboard is actually a complex tool; they just don't know it yet.
opzioni.C: The team is using the principle of visual management: a physical board makes the work transparent to anyone who needs the information.
opzioni.D: The team will drop everything and develop a new software-based Kanban board to avoid embarrassment.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. It has some benefits, but it's not the core reason.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Reverse psychology, not the reason.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Visual management is a lean principle borrowed into agile: key information is accessible at a glance in the team area. A Kanban board is a low-tech, high-touch tool.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Agile prefers individuals and interactions over tools.

domande.spiegazione: Kanban board: low tech, high touch.

domande.domanda: Agile teams practice frequent verification and validation during and at the end of each iteration through demonstrations and reviews. Which of the following is NOT a benefit of demos and reviews?

opzioni.A: They enable the team to catch mistakes and mismatched customer expectations early.
opzioni.B: They keep everyone busy and give them something to do.
opzioni.C: They're easy to manage, since there are multiple feedback loops.
opzioni.D: They reduce cost overruns, as mistakes are found early before additional tasks are built on a faulty foundation.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect: this IS a benefit.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct: this is NOT a benefit. Busy work adds no value to the project.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect: this IS a benefit.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect: this IS a benefit.

domande.spiegazione: Demos give early feedback.

domande.domanda: You're on an agile software implementation project with a very short deadline. How do agile teams shorten the time between identifying a defect and resolving it?

opzioni.A: Continuous integration.
opzioni.B: Daily builds and smoke tests.
opzioni.C: Usability testing.
opzioni.D: Exploratory testing.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. CI merges the code into a working build at least once a day and runs automated tests, so less time passes before a problem is identified.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Not the core agile practice for this.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Important, but not the core practice that shortens defect detection.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Important, but not the core practice that shortens defect detection.

domande.spiegazione: CI shortens defect detection time.

domande.domanda: With all the different methods of testing software or a product deliverable, when should the team determine the acceptance test criteria for the feature or story card?

opzioni.A: When the first iteration is complete.
opzioni.B: During estimation and elaboration of the card with the product owner, business analysts and development team.
opzioni.C: Before the product or feature is prioritized.
opzioni.D: At the end of the project.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Acceptance criteria are needed before delivering the iteration.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Acceptance criteria are defined before development, during elaboration, often in Given-When-Then (BDD) format.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Items are prioritized first, then the prioritized ones are elaborated and estimated.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Far too late.

domande.spiegazione: Acceptance criteria precede development.

domande.domanda: ⚠️ Every project has characteristics around requirements, delivery, change and goals. Understanding the different types of life cycle allows you to choose the right one for your project. What is the correct description of an agile approach? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Dynamic requirements, activities repeated until correct, frequent small deliveries.
opzioni.B: Fixed requirements, activities performed once, single delivery.
opzioni.C: Dynamic requirements, activities repeated until correct, single large delivery.
opzioni.D: Fixed requirements, activities repeated until correct, frequent small deliveries.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Agile has dynamic requirements, repeated until correct, delivered in frequent smaller deliveries (Agile Practice Guide).
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. This is predictive (waterfall).
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. A single large delivery is iterative, not agile.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Agile requirements are dynamic, not fixed.

domande.spiegazione: Agile Practice Guide.
domande.nota: Option text reconstructed from the commentary.
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: Continuous integration wraps software build, deployment and testing into a single, automated, repeatable process. What does it do with the changes made to the software?

opzioni.A: It merges all the changes and separates each feature into its own development pool.
opzioni.B: It ensures no code is changed.
opzioni.C: It integrates all changed components regularly, at least once a day.
opzioni.D: It enables new features for the product backlog.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. It merges changes together, it doesn't separate them.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Code keeps changing; CI integrates those changes.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. CI merges all changes and tests them automatically, discovering defects on a daily basis.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Not related to CI.

domande.spiegazione: CI finds defects daily.

domande.domanda: Crystal is one of the original frameworks that contributed to agile. It is designed to scale and recognizes that each project may require a slightly tailored set of practices based on its size and complexity. What are the core values of Crystal?

opzioni.A: People, interaction and community.
opzioni.B: Finding people, building people and leading people.
opzioni.C: Building products, buying products and selling products.
opzioni.D: Profit, persistence and power.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Like agile (individuals and interactions over processes and tools), Crystal centers on people, interaction and community.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Promising from an agile view, but not Crystal's core values.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Not related to agile.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Not specific to agile people and interactions.

domande.spiegazione: Crystal (Cockburn, 1990s).

domande.domanda: Crystal is designed to scale and recognizes that each project may require a slightly different, tailored set of practices based on its size and complexity. What are some of the ways Crystal scales?

opzioni.A: Crystal Blue, Indigo and Violet, based on the number of features.
opzioni.B: Crystal Clear, Yellow, Orange and Red, based on the number of people involved.
opzioni.C: Crystal Metal, Wood and Water, based on the flow of story cards through the Kanban board.
opzioni.D: Crystal High, Low and Medium, based on the dollars spent on the project.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. These are not Crystal names.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Crystal Clear (0-8 people), Yellow, Orange and Red, based on people involved, money involved and the criticality/risk of the project.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. These are not Crystal names.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Money is a factor, but these are not Crystal names.

domande.spiegazione: Crystal Clear for 0-8 people.

domande.domanda: You're working through an agile project with your team meeting daily in a stand-up. What is NOT one of the reasons agile teams use daily stand-ups?

opzioni.A: To micro-commit to the team.
opzioni.B: To uncover and remove blockers.
opzioni.C: To ensure work flows freely through the team.
opzioni.D: To report to the executive team.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect: this IS a reason.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect: this IS a reason.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect: this IS a reason.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct: this is NOT a reason. Executives are welcome to attend (agile is open), but stand-ups are not specifically for reporting to them.

domande.spiegazione: Stand-ups serve the team.

domande.domanda: You're the project manager on an agile project that is halfway through. The project sponsor is starting to raise concerns that the project will not be completed in the allotted time. What will you do to gather the information needed to answer the sponsor?

opzioni.A: Review the Kanban board and the current work in progress.
opzioni.B: Check the product backlog for remaining features.
opzioni.C: Review the team velocity, the product burndown chart and other key performance indicators.
opzioni.D: Hold a team meeting and log everyone's status.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Possible, but it may only show one iteration.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Shows how much is left, but not how long it will take.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Velocity (rate of progress) and remaining work, shown visually on a burndown chart, give the most reliable answer.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Not an agile way to gather this information.

domande.spiegazione: Agile KPIs: velocity and remaining work.

domande.domanda: You're attending a kickoff meeting with the agile team and the business owners. The Scrum Master recommends using MoSCoW to help prioritize the work with the product and business owners. How does MoSCoW prioritize the product backlog?

opzioni.A: Using priority 1, 2, 3 and 4.
opzioni.B: Using low, medium and high.
opzioni.C: Using must have, should have, could have and won't have.
opzioni.D: Using multiple dots that people can assign to the features they like.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not MoSCoW.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Not MoSCoW.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. MoSCoW labels items must have, should have, could have and won't (or would like to) have.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. That is multi-voting with dots, another prioritization technique (others: monopoly money, Kano analysis, fist of five).

domande.spiegazione: Other techniques: dot voting, monopoly money, Kano, fist of five.

domande.domanda: Agile teams use different methods to manage their work in progress (WIP). The business sponsor believes that removing the WIP limits will help the team take on more work and get the product delivered faster. What will you tell the business sponsor?

opzioni.A: You'll remove the work-in-progress limits to push as much work through as possible.
opzioni.B: You'll dictate overtime and no holidays for the team to get things done.
opzioni.C: Work-in-progress limits ensure the team focuses on one main thing at a time and avoid the time cost of switching tasks.
opzioni.D: Work in progress can be seen on the Kanban board, so it doesn't matter what the limit is.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Counterintuitively, it would slow the team down.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. It may work for a while, but it burns the team out and has the opposite effect.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Work is taken on according to velocity; multitasking and context switching reduce effectiveness.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The board shows WIP, but the limit is what protects focus.

domande.spiegazione: Work is taken on by velocity; WIP limits protect focus.

domande.domanda: You're working on an agile team that includes many stakeholders who have not worked on an agile project before. Several stakeholders have valid concerns about some agile methods. As a servant leader or project coach, what will you do to make them more comfortable with the process?

opzioni.A: Educate the stakeholders, address their concerns and keep them engaged.
opzioni.B: Tell them it has worked in the past, so it will work here too.
opzioni.C: Dictate to the stakeholders that this is how all future projects must be executed.
opzioni.D: Go back to a waterfall-style project management method.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. A servant leader includes people in decisions and grows them through education and coaching.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Dismissive, and not servant leadership.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. 'Those convinced against their will are of the same opinion still.'
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Waterfall has its place, but here the goal is to coach and bring everyone along.

domande.spiegazione: Grow people through coaching.

domande.domanda: You're working on an agile project with stakeholders who are keen to know why it is so important to incorporate multiple touchpoints with them before, during and after iterations. What will you tell them?

opzioni.A: To raise and manage changes and to identify potential risks and issues.
opzioni.B: To inform stakeholders of the development team's direction.
opzioni.C: To ensure business executives hear about the team's value through multiple meetings.
opzioni.D: To have them invest more time in the project so they are more committed.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Frequent touchpoints ensure features are reviewed regularly, meet expectations, and that changes and risks are raised early.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Direction comes from the product owner's prioritized backlog.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Agile isn't about reporting to executives through meetings.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Not the reason for frequent interaction.

domande.spiegazione: Frequent touchpoints catch changes early.

domande.domanda: Teams use daily stand-ups to micro-commit to each other, uncover and remove blockers, and ensure that work flows smoothly through the team. What is NOT true about stand-ups?

opzioni.A: They are often time-boxed to 15 minutes.
opzioni.B: The team walks through the Kanban or task board.
opzioni.C: The team facilitator, or anyone in the team, can facilitate.
opzioni.D: Only people in the project team can attend.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect (this is true).
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect (this is true).
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect (this is true). The Scrum Master should encourage others to facilitate and grow their skills.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct (this is NOT true). Agile teams are open and transparent: anyone can attend, learn, watch or contribute.

domande.spiegazione: Transparency.

domande.domanda: Features in an agile project are usually completed in the form of multiple user stories. When a feature is complete, the team periodically demonstrates the working product to the customer. When do these demonstrations or reviews happen?

opzioni.A: Only at the end of a project, when the stakeholders are available.
opzioni.B: Often at the end of an iteration, or when enough features have been completed into a coherent set.
opzioni.C: Often at the start of a project.
opzioni.D: Often when the team wants to, as they're so busy working anyway.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. They happen at the end of each iteration.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Sprint reviews/demos occur at the end of an iteration or when enough cards/features form a set that can be showcased.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Nothing has been developed yet.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The team must prioritize this time with the customer.

domande.spiegazione: Sprint reviews demonstrate working product.

domande.domanda: Disciplined Agile is a process decision framework that blends various agile techniques. Which of the following principles is NOT part of Disciplined Agile?

opzioni.A: People first: enumerating roles and organization elements at various levels.
opzioni.B: Learning oriented: collaborative improvement.
opzioni.C: Self-promotion: working to improve your own personal brand.
opzioni.D: Goal driven: tailoring processes to achieve specific outcomes.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect: this IS a principle. People first is a big part of agile.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect: this IS a principle. Growth mindset, feedback, iterative improvement.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct: this is NOT a principle. Agile works transparently with all stakeholders in mind: the team serves each other and removes blockers.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect: this IS a principle. Tailoring the approach to the circumstances.

domande.spiegazione: Team serves each other; information transparent.

domande.domanda: Disciplined Agile is a process decision framework that blends various agile techniques. Which of the following principles are from Disciplined Agile?

opzioni.A: Learning oriented, goal driven and scalable.
opzioni.B: Implementing, iterating and integrating.
opzioni.C: Excellence, guidance and cadence.
opzioni.D: Making, doing and being.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Learning oriented, goal driven and scalable are key Disciplined Agile principles and general agile themes.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Sounds fancy but doesn't match agile approaches.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Not Disciplined Agile principles.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Not Disciplined Agile principles.

domande.spiegazione: Disciplined Agile.

domande.domanda: Dynamic Systems Development Method (DSDM) is one of the founding methods with an input into agile. It was designed to add more rigor to the rising iterative methods of the 1990s, such as Crystal. Which of the following is a principle of the DSDM framework?

opzioni.A: Focus on the business need and deliver on time.
opzioni.B: Add every feature and stop when it's done.
opzioni.C: Find all the defects or don't approve the release.
opzioni.D: Push fast delivery over quality so we can learn from our mistakes.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. DSDM focuses on the business need and delivers on time: scope is variable while the schedule is set, so features are managed through the backlog.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Features are prioritized; some may drop off.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Quality matters, but you can't stop a release for defects you don't know about.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Learning from mistakes is important, but not at the expense of quality.

domande.spiegazione: DSDM: constraint-driven delivery.

domande.domanda: You're working with developers in an agile team who are using a test-driven development (TDD) approach. They ask whether they should operate using something called 'red, green, refactor'. What are they referring to?

opzioni.A: No code is developed during a red status, some code is developed during a green status, and new features are taken in during refactor.
opzioni.B: A traffic-light approach to bringing in new features.
opzioni.C: Only releasing features when they are given the green light.
opzioni.D: A test is written first and fails, then passes once the solution is developed, and then the code can be refactored or streamlined.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Refactoring means cleaning up existing code, not taking in new features.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. It doesn't relate to refactoring or testing.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Not the meaning.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Red-green-refactor is the TDD cycle: fail, pass, then streamline the code.

domande.spiegazione: Red-green-refactor is the TDD cycle.

domande.domanda: You're an agile project manager working with the product owner of the agile team. Several key deliverables have been identified and listed in the product backlog. What will the agile team do next?

opzioni.A: All deliverables should go live only at the end of the project.
opzioni.B: The tasks should be delivered but not tested, to get value to the customer as quickly as possible.
opzioni.C: The tasks should be prioritized, developed and tested incrementally.
opzioni.D: The tasks should be planned carefully and delivered according to their plan.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Agile delivers in increments to get feedback.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Quality is everyone's responsibility: increments are tested.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Agile develops and delivers in features or increments, prioritized and tested for each increment.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Planning matters, but agile values responding to change over following a plan.

domande.spiegazione: Deliver features incrementally.

domande.domanda: A team new to agile has worked closely with the product owner and identified the highest-value features of the project. What is one reason to break these features down into increments and deliver them as soon as possible?

opzioni.A: To get all the work out of the way so the team can relax.
opzioni.B: So the project life cycle can be shortened.
opzioni.C: So the product owner can report to her executive manager that work is being done.
opzioni.D: To reduce the risk of the feature no longer providing value for the customer.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not the reason.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The time frame is usually fixed.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Agile is about the team and the customer, not personal reporting.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. The longer a feature takes to deliver, the higher the risk it no longer provides the intended value: value-driven delivery.

domande.spiegazione: Value-driven delivery.

domande.domanda: You're an agile project manager working closely with the Scrum Master and the agile team. The Scrum Master mentions that agile works differently with risk compared to a traditional project, and sets a meeting with you and the team to talk through agile risks. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Ensure the team notes and schedules high-risk activities early in the project so they are mitigated quickly.
opzioni.B: Ensure the team identifies risks, places them in a register and mitigates them by the end of the project.
opzioni.C: Ensure the team keeps the risk register to itself so other stakeholders don't think less of the project.
opzioni.D: Ensure risk is only captured around people, because an agile team prefers individuals and interactions over processes and tools.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Prioritizing high-risk features first reduces future risk for the project.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. A decent approach, but agile works on the risks first, not by the end.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Hiding risks has adverse effects.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Risk covers the whole project, not just people.

domande.spiegazione: Agile front-loads risk.

domande.domanda: You're a project manager on an agile project that requires an external third party to develop software for one of your features. You've worked with the team to gather the requirements and the backlog of product features, and you begin working with your procurement department on a contract for the vendor. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Request that the contract be one that accommodates changes to product scope.
opzioni.B: Go back to the business and ask them to deliver the feature.
opzioni.C: Raise a risk to the delivery of your project based on the external vendor.
opzioni.D: Find an existing time and materials contract in the organization's process assets.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Agile works with changing scope and cost (fixed schedule and quality), so the contract must accommodate changing requirements.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Possible, but not the best answer.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Partly valid, but it doesn't address the contract.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. T&M accommodates change, but without clear limits there is no incentive to deliver.

domande.spiegazione: Contracts must accommodate changing requirements.

domande.domanda: ⚠️ Dynamic Systems Development Method (DSDM) is one of the founding methods with an input into agile, designed to add rigor to the rising iterative methods of the 1990s such as Crystal and Scrum. It is best known for constraint-driven delivery: cost, quality and time are set at the beginning, and then formal prioritization of one element is used to meet those constraints. Which element is it? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Scope, delivering the features the customer values most first and the lower-priority ones if time allows.
opzioni.B: Single delivery, which ensures everything is correct and approved before the project goes live.
opzioni.C: Stakeholders, which ensures everyone is involved in gathering scope, quality and cost requirements.
opzioni.D: Cost, which ensures the project closes once funds are depleted.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Agile methods work with variable scope while cost, quality and schedule are often fixed: the opposite of predictive, which fixes scope upfront.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Agile delivers features incrementally, not in a single delivery.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The whole team is involved, but stakeholders are not the variable being prioritized.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Cost is one of the fixed constraints.

domande.spiegazione: Opposite to predictive, which fixes scope.
domande.nota: Option A wording reconstructed from the commentary.
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: Agile projects have short iterations, so the team receives early and continuous feedback on product quality throughout the development cycle. With frequent customer feedback, agile teams can incorporate most new changes into the product and the process before the end of the project. What is NOT one of the benefits of this approach?

opzioni.A: Avoiding requirement misunderstandings that might not be detected until later in the development cycle, when they are more expensive to fix.
opzioni.B: Clarifying customer feature requests and making them available for the customer to use early.
opzioni.C: Discovering, isolating and resolving quality problems early.
opzioni.D: Having one big release at the end of the project that everyone can celebrate.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect: this IS a benefit.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect: this IS a benefit.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect: this IS a benefit.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct: this is NOT a benefit. A single release is a waterfall approach; agile releases increments to gather feedback.

domande.spiegazione: Agile releases increments.

domande.domanda: Enterprise Scrum is a framework designed to apply the Scrum method at an organizational level, not just within a single product development effort. What is NOT part of leadership within Enterprise Scrum?

opzioni.A: Extending the use of Scrum across all aspects of the organization.
opzioni.B: Role-playing the role of Scrum Master before the first iteration.
opzioni.C: Generalizing Scrum techniques so they apply easily at the various levels.
opzioni.D: Scaling the Scrum method with supplemental techniques as necessary.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect: this IS part of Enterprise Scrum.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct: this is NOT part of it. You may choose to do it, but Enterprise Scrum is about scaling Scrum across and within teams.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect: this IS part of Enterprise Scrum.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect: this IS part of Enterprise Scrum (tailoring the approach).

domande.spiegazione: Enterprise Scrum scales Scrum across teams.

domande.domanda: You're an agile project manager tasked with evolving your part of the organization into agile. What is NOT something you would do when making this change?

opzioni.A: Treat the change as an agile project, with its own backlog of changes the team could introduce based on perceived value.
opzioni.B: Treat each change as an experiment, tested for a short period to determine its suitability or the need for further refinement.
opzioni.C: Use Kanban boards to track progress, showing new approaches in use as done and things to be tried as in progress.
opzioni.D: Direct the teams to take on agile in one go, moving ahead without wavering.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect: you WOULD do this. Prioritizing the highest value first is perfectly agile.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect: you WOULD do this. It's the iterative approach.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect: you WOULD do this. Using agile to deliver agile.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct: you would NOT do this. A big-bang change is a waterfall approach; agile is incremental.

domande.spiegazione: Use agile to implement agile.

domande.domanda: Extreme Programming (XP) is a software development method based on frequent cycles. It is known for popularizing a holistic set of 12 primary practices, later expanded with secondary practices. Which of the following does XP require?

opzioni.A: Sitting together as a whole team in an informative workspace.
opzioni.B: Writing reports for the executive team.
opzioni.C: Rotating roles so everyone gets experience in something they like.
opzioni.D: Developing all changes for a single release.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Agile core practices include the whole team approach and an informative workspace (visual management: Kanban, burndown charts, backlogs).
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Executives are invited to the informative areas instead.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Agile prefers T-shaped people (generalizing specialists) with one deep specialty.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Agile delivers in increments.

domande.spiegazione: XP is a core agile input.

domande.domanda: You're an agile project manager working with the project sponsor in the beginning stages of an agile project. The sponsor would like your help creating the project charter. You tell them you will also create a team charter for your agile team, which will include the project sponsor. What does this mean?

opzioni.A: You'll capture the team values, communication guidelines and decision-making process separately from the project purpose, requirements and summary schedule.
opzioni.B: You'll create a project plan with scope, schedule, cost and quality outlines to follow.
opzioni.C: You'll take over from the project sponsor and direct the team on future customer requirements.
opzioni.D: You'll defer to the team for all queries, in the way of a servant leader.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. An agile PM charters both the project (business case, purpose, high-level requirements, stakeholders, risks) and the team (agreements and how the team will operate, created by the team for the team).
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. That describes a project management plan.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The team works through the agile approach, prioritizing value.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Everyone should have input; this doesn't describe a team charter.

domande.spiegazione: Team charter: by the team, for the team.

domande.domanda: You're working with the team on the team charter. You've outlined the project vision and mission, agreed meeting times and accepted team behavior. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Ask the team to get to work straight away, because agile teams move swiftly.
opzioni.B: Send the team charter to the project sponsor for sign-off so the project can begin.
opzioni.C: Agree on and include the definition of done for team features and tasks.
opzioni.D: Set a meeting in two weeks' time so you can continue developing the charter iteratively.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Agile works quickly, but doesn't rush in before defining done.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The sponsor may be part of the team, but doesn't need to sign off the team charter: it's an agreement among the team.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. The definition of done tells the team when a task is complete and they can pull the next one, so everyone agrees what success looks like.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Waiting two weeks is too slow.

domande.spiegazione: Definition of done is part of the charter.

domande.domanda: You're working on an agile project, gathering requirements from the business stakeholders with the product owner. During the discussion, different people seem to have different understandings of what the feature will look like. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Ask the stakeholders to elaborate their ideas better and set another meeting in a week's time.
opzioni.B: Park the feature for now and begin work on a feature that is better elaborated.
opzioni.C: Draw a storyboard prototype of the requirement so all stakeholders can see it, adjust it on the fly and agree.
opzioni.D: Give your understanding of the feature and ask the stakeholders to agree or disagree.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Agile keeps people close and communicating; waiting a week is too slow.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Possible in real life, but agile prefers communicating and resolving it in the moment.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. A wireframe or storyboard builds consensus on the content and flow: a rough increment everyone can see, feel and touch.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. A facilitation technique, but a visual prototype iterated together works better.

domande.spiegazione: A storyboard is a rough increment everyone can see.

domande.domanda: You're working as a project manager with an agile project team. The project sponsor sits on another floor and prefers to communicate by email only. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Make sure you communicate with the project sponsor by email only, so they are comfortable.
opzioni.B: Stop communicating with the project sponsor until they come to at least a few project meetings.
opzioni.C: Ask the project sponsor to co-locate with the agile team for a few days a week, to ensure face-to-face communication and access to the visual project information.
opzioni.D: Set meetings with the project sponsor so you can update them personally.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. It may happen in real life, but it isn't the best agile answer.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. That's avoiding the situation.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Co-location allows fast questions and feedback, reading body language, and access to Kanban boards and burndown charts in the team area.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Better than email, but co-location is the agile answer.

domande.spiegazione: Face to face includes body language.

domande.domanda: As an agile project manager, you understand the need to operate with openness and transparency with your team and stakeholders. How will you encourage knowledge sharing throughout the project?

opzioni.A: Tell your team what to do during work hours so they can learn from you.
opzioni.B: Write process documents for the team to read in their spare time.
opzioni.C: Make key information visible in the team area and ensure all impacted stakeholders are invited to the daily stand-up, retrospectives and even iteration planning.
opzioni.D: Form a key group of executive stakeholders to share project information with and ensure your good reputation within the company.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. That's dictating, not servant leadership.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Agile values individuals and interactions over processes and tools.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Agile teams make project information visible and accessible to all, and keep their ceremonies open.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. It serves your personal brand rather than the team.

domande.spiegazione: Agile makes information accessible to all.

domande.domanda: You've been working in an agile team for some time, and an executive from the business area asks how the team has delivered so consistently over the past year. You tell him you're using Extreme Programming (XP). Which primary XP practices contributed to the team's success?

opzioni.A: Real customer involvement, team continuity and a sustainable pace.
opzioni.B: Executive reports, testing and continually raising defects.
opzioni.C: Pivoting frequently, long meetings and one final delivery.
opzioni.D: Finding the right product, the right people and the right price.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. These are XP primary practices. Agile encourages them through stand-ups, backlog grooming with the real customer/product owner, and planning to the team's velocity.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Executive reports are not a main agile factor.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Long meetings and one final delivery are waterfall.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. It rolls off the tongue, but isn't part of agile.

domande.spiegazione: Plan to velocity to avoid burnout.

domande.domanda: You're working with a seasoned agile team that is very familiar with Extreme Programming (XP). They walk through a set of principles they frequently use. What is NOT one of the primary practices of XP?

opzioni.A: Planning with user stories.
opzioni.B: Test-first programming.
opzioni.C: Incremental design.
opzioni.D: First in, best dressed.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect: this IS an XP practice (stories placed into the iteration from the product backlog).
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect: this IS an XP practice (test fails, then code, then test passes).
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect: this IS an XP practice (design and release in increments).
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct: this is NOT an XP practice: it's just a saying.

domande.spiegazione: XP has 12 primary practices.

domande.domanda: You're testing the product being delivered in increments by an agile team. You notice that no defects have been passed on to the end user, and that the team is working with Extreme Programming (XP). Which XP practices led to this result?

opzioni.A: Regular refactoring and daily deployment of an integrated code base.
opzioni.B: Having real users test the product when it's released.
opzioni.C: Moving team members around to different roles for a shared experience.
opzioni.D: Making sure the team does exactly what the Scrum Master says.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. XP uses continuous integration (daily deployment of a single code base with automated regression tests) and regular refactoring, so defects are picked up quickly.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. A good practice, but not what prevents defects reaching users.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Agile prefers T-shaped members who keep their deep specialty.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The Scrum Master guides and removes blockers; it's not their job to dictate.

domande.spiegazione: XP technical practices.

domande.domanda: You're an agile project manager working with an agile coach and planning the next sprint with the team. The agile coach advises you to build some slack into the sprint. What does this mean?

opzioni.A: Using the messaging service Slack to communicate as a team.
opzioni.B: Allowing the best performers in the team to slack off as a reward for their hard work.
opzioni.C: Adding a card for refactoring code that can be replaced if an emergency comes up.
opzioni.D: Creating a burndown chart and a burnup chart together.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not that kind of slack.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Slacking off adds no value.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. A refactoring card keeps the code clean and can be swapped out if an emergency arises: that's slack in the sprint.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Not related to slack.

domande.spiegazione: Slack protects the sprint from emergencies.

domande.domanda: The team is planning its first sprint on an agile project. They have worked with the product owner, who has gathered a backlog of features in priority order. As an agile project manager, what must you do to ensure you can plan future sprints correctly?

opzioni.A: Find the best performer in the team, so you know who you can rely on.
opzioni.B: Find your team's velocity over the next few sprints so you can set a sustainable pace.
opzioni.C: Set a working group meeting to gain executive buy-in.
opzioni.D: Create the project management plan and draw out the schedule in advance.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Agile is about the whole team, not individuals.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Sprints are planned to the team's velocity (average completed per sprint). You need to complete at least one sprint to know it.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Executives should be invited to team ceremonies instead.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. That's a predictive approach.

domande.spiegazione: Plan to average velocity.

domande.domanda: You're an agile project manager and your organization is moving from waterfall to an agile way of working. After reading the Agile Manifesto, the functional manager you're working with mentions 'individuals and interactions over processes and tools' and asks how you will achieve it. What do you tell them?

opzioni.A: Create ceremonies such as the daily stand-up, iteration planning, demos/reviews and retrospectives that encourage team interaction.
opzioni.B: Create a process for the team to review that shows the way of work.
opzioni.C: Ask the project sponsor to interact with the team by sharing some of their journey.
opzioni.D: Ensure the tools the team works with are state-of-the-art software solutions.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Agile ceremonies are designed to encourage interaction, and co-location enables fast decisions and ownership.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. That's process over individuals and interactions.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. A nice idea, but not specifically agile.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Agile can be very low tech: a whiteboard and sticky notes are enough.

domande.spiegazione: Collaboration enables fast decisions.

domande.domanda: You're an experienced functional manager who has been asked to lead an agile project team; your executive manager calls the role 'project coach' or 'Scrum Master'. Agile leadership may be different from what you're used to. What leadership style will you embody?

opzioni.A: Servant leadership.
opzioni.B: Directive leadership.
opzioni.C: Visionary leadership.
opzioni.D: Laissez-faire leadership, taking a hands-off approach and letting the team self-organize.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. An agile leader is primarily a servant leader: removing blockers, helping the team problem-solve and growing their skills.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The team should grow and make decisions collaboratively.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Agile also requires getting into the detail.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Close, but a leader still needs to be involved and guide the team through its ceremonies.

domande.spiegazione: Agile leaders are servant leaders.

domande.domanda: You're working as an agile project manager in a new project team. Many team members are despondent and do not show up for the meetings and ceremonies you have set. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Raise a risk in the risk register around project goals and ask the project sponsor to mitigate it.
opzioni.B: Hold a coaching session with the team on the what and the why behind the agile ceremonies, and ensure each meeting has a clear outcome, time and agenda.
opzioni.C: Cancel all meetings for now and write documentation for the team on what you'd like them to do.
opzioni.D: Make the decisions yourself and dictate the outcomes to the team.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. A waterfall-style response that hands the problem to someone else.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. An agile leader coaches the team, starts with why, removes blockers and ensures interaction.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Agile prefers interaction over documentation.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Dictating won't get the results the customer, business or team need.

domande.spiegazione: Agile leaders coach and remove blockers.

domande.domanda: You're an experienced project manager used to a directive leadership style, where people do exactly as you say. Now you're working in an agile team where that style is not accepted. What is one thing you can change to move to a more servant leadership style?

opzioni.A: Ensure the executive team makes all the decisions.
opzioni.B: Ensure stakeholders collectively agree on and share decisions.
opzioni.C: Defer to the product owner and the business to make all the decisions.
opzioni.D: Find an extremely competent person in the project team and delegate all decisions to them.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. That's still a directive style.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Agile fosters team empowerment through collective agreement and shared decisions, where the team and stakeholders reach decisions together.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Developers, testers and analysts must also give input.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. One person deciding still isn't collaborative.

domande.spiegazione: Agile fosters team empowerment.

domande.domanda: You're working on the requirements for the next iteration and a decision needs to be made by the team. The product owner suggests a show of hands to indicate who is for or against the decision. As the agile project manager, you object. Why?

opzioni.A: Agile is about software: the team should use software to vote on the decision.
opzioni.B: The decision may not go in your favor, so it's best to make it yourself.
opzioni.C: Decisions should take time to work through and should not be voted on quickly.
opzioni.D: By making the votes visible, team members may be influenced by others in the team, especially executives, without the benefit of discussion.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Agile can use low-tech tools.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The best overall outcome matters more than your own view.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. A fast decision can also be a good one.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. A simple for/against vote gives no discussion, and visible votes are easily swayed (e.g. by your manager). Fist of five or anonymous voting help.

domande.spiegazione: Visible votes invite bias.

domande.domanda: Your project team would like to add a few key agile processes to become more agile. The project manager mentions performing root cause analysis when problems appear on features, focusing on the features that bring in the most revenue through pay-per-use, and daily stand-ups. Which agile method is she most likely referring to?

opzioni.A: Scrum.
opzioni.B: Extreme Programming (XP).
opzioni.C: Kanban.
opzioni.D: Iteration planning.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Scrum doesn't include pay-per-use.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. XP has 14 secondary practices, including root cause analysis, pay-per-use, daily stand-ups and shrinking teams.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Kanban is about WIP limits and visualization.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Iteration planning is common to most agile techniques, not a method.

domande.spiegazione: XP secondary practices.
