The product owner, who has been with you since the beginning, has taken another job, and a new teammate with very little experience joins as product owner. Which of the following will you NOT tell them about the product owner role?

opzioni.A: The product owner represents the customer and generates, maintains and prioritizes the backlog, to ensure the highest business value without creating waste.
opzioni.B: The product owner must have previous experience in agile to work in the team.
opzioni.C: The product owner may work with stakeholders, customers and the team to define the product direction and rank the work based on business value.
opzioni.D: Product owners typically have a business background and bring deep subject matter expertise to their decisions.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect: you WOULD say this.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct: you would NOT say this. Agile can be coached; what matters is deep expertise in the business/customer domain being served.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect: you WOULD say this.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect: you WOULD say this.

domande.spiegazione: PO role.

domande.domanda: The Agile Unified Process (AUP) performs more iterative cycles across seven key disciplines and incorporates the associated feedback before formal delivery. Which of the following is NOT a principle that guides the AUP disciplines?

opzioni.A: Tailoring the approach to fit.
opzioni.B: The team knows what it is doing.
opzioni.C: Collective agreement of scope before delivery.
opzioni.D: Focus on high-value activities.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect: this IS a principle. You tailor the approach to the situation.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect: this IS a principle, often achieved with generalizing specialists.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct: this is NOT a principle. Scope is arranged by the product owner; not everyone has to agree before delivery.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect: this IS a principle (grooming the backlog for value).

domande.spiegazione: AUP mirrors agile.

domande.domanda: The 12 clarifying principles of agile were defined to give more clarity to the Agile Manifesto and its core values. Which of the following is one of the 12 clarifying principles?

opzioni.A: Our highest priority is to satisfy the customer through early and continuous delivery of valuable software.
opzioni.B: Our highest priority is to ensure executive buy-in by delivering high-value items.
opzioni.C: Our highest priority is to reduce the impact of change by keeping information to a minimum.
opzioni.D: Our highest priority is to plan thoroughly and execute with discipline.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. The first principle: early and continuous delivery of value, applicable to any knowledge work, not only software.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Executive buy-in matters, but it isn't a principle.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The opposite: agile wants transparency and to embrace change.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Thorough upfront planning is predictive.

domande.spiegazione: Agile applies to any knowledge work.

domande.domanda: You're working with a new agile team and have reviewed the team velocity over the past three iterations. The maximum number of points completed was 35 and the fewest was 25. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Push the team to complete five more than the maximum, and roll over any incomplete cards to the next iteration.
opzioni.B: Set 35 as the work-in-progress (WIP) limit and adjust it in future iterations if the team is able to pull more work in.
opzioni.C: Add more people to the team to complete the work, because 35 is not enough.
opzioni.D: Reduce the number of features in the backlog to suit the team velocity.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Goes against a sustainable pace: the team burns out.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Once velocity is known, set a WIP limit for future iterations so as not to overburden the team.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. More people means more communication channels and complexity.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Prioritize the backlog instead; only the sprint backlog must fit the velocity.

domande.spiegazione: Don't overburden the team.

domande.domanda: You're the product owner in an agile team with a backlog of features to be developed. Each feature is assigned a dollar value representing its return on investment. You would like a risk-adjusted backlog. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Note the risk impacts in dollars against the return in dollars, then reprioritize the backlog.
opzioni.B: Adjust the backlog to focus on the largest features first.
opzioni.C: Capture the known risks for each feature, then place cards to control those risks and prioritize them in the backlog.
opzioni.D: Create a risk register for the project and have it signed off by the risk owners.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Possible, but in practice risk response cards are created.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Size isn't the criterion.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. A risk-adjusted backlog contains risk response tasks prioritized against the normal features.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. A waterfall approach.

domande.spiegazione: Risk-adjusted backlog.

domande.domanda: You're an agile project manager analyzing the risk for each feature in your backlog by assigning a probability and an impact score to each risk, then multiplying them to calculate risk severity. How will the team handle the items with the highest risk?

opzioni.A: Place all the high-risk items in a dedicated risk iteration.
opzioni.B: Schedule them later in the project.
opzioni.C: Schedule them earlier in the project to reduce the risk impact over time.
opzioni.D: Change the requirements to reduce or remove the risk.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The team should keep delivering value the whole time.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Risks cost more the later they're dealt with.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Risk is highest early in the project: completing high-risk items first significantly reduces risks and unknowns later.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The requirements may still be needed; manage the risk instead.

domande.spiegazione: High risk first.
domande.nota: Option order reconstructed from the commentary.

domande.domanda: The Scrum Master tells you that agile builds problem solving into its process in a number of ways, using transparency tools and ceremonies. Which of the following is NOT something designed to reveal and solve problems?

opzioni.A: Retrospectives.
opzioni.B: Writing user stories.
opzioni.C: Iteration demonstrations and reviews.
opzioni.D: Raising blockers in the daily stand-up.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect: this IS designed for it (what went wrong, what still puzzles us).
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct: this is NOT specifically designed for it. Writing stories is useful and can reveal problems, but it isn't its purpose.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect: this IS designed for it (the customer may see it's not what they want).
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect: this IS designed for it.

domande.spiegazione: Transparency tools.

domande.domanda: The whole team approach brings everyone needed into the project team and is an important part of creating the right cross-functional team. The team facilitator is a key member of the whole team. What is NOT correct regarding the team facilitator role?

opzioni.A: The team facilitator or servant leader can be called project manager, Scrum Master, project lead, team coach or portfolio manager.
opzioni.B: The team facilitator must have a degree in business.
opzioni.C: All agile teams need servant leadership on the team.
opzioni.D: Team members should build up their own servant leadership skills of facilitation, coaching and removing blockers.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect (this is correct).
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct (this is NOT correct). No degree is needed: the role is to remove blockers and facilitate problem solving, and anyone in the team can perform it.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect (this is correct).
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect (this is correct).

domande.spiegazione: Anyone can facilitate.

domande.domanda: You're rearranging a current agile team, and you know agile teams are cross-functional. What sort of team members will you select as you rearrange the team?

opzioni.A: Generalizing specialists: T-shaped people with one deep specialty and a wide range of experience in other skills.
opzioni.B: Team leaders with a specialty in leadership, so everyone can lead.
opzioni.C: Risk specialists.
opzioni.D: Don't add team members: you should shrink the team.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Agile teams are made up of generalizing specialists (T-shaped people).
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Everyone should lead, but that's not what's needed.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. You may need some, but not all members.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. XP mentions shrinking teams over time, but it's not always right.

domande.spiegazione: Generalizing specialists.

domande.domanda: You're helping the organization set up a new agile team and making sure they consider the whole team approach. What is NOT correct regarding the whole team approach?

opzioni.A: The whole team approach means involving everyone with the knowledge and skills necessary to ensure project success.
opzioni.B: The team should be relatively small: successful teams have been observed with as few as three people and as many as nine.
opzioni.C: Team members are often 100% dedicated to delivery, because when switching or multitasking people make more mistakes and lose 20-40% of their productivity.
opzioni.D: Team members should not be multi-skilled, as this can distract from the clarity of their role.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect (this is correct).
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect (this is correct).
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect (this is correct): context switching causes a large productivity loss.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct (this is NOT correct). The whole team approach wants multi-skilled, T-shaped people with at least one deep specialty.

domande.spiegazione: Whole team approach.

domande.domanda: You're having trouble selecting team members for a new agile team in a new organization. What is NOT true about cross-functional team members in the whole team approach?

opzioni.A: Cross-functional teams consist of team members with all the skills necessary to produce a working product.
opzioni.B: Teams do not need to use visual management because they're already good at what they do.
opzioni.C: In software development, cross-functional teams are made up of designers, developers, testers and any other required roles.
opzioni.D: Cross-functional team members are critical because they can deliver finished work in the shortest possible time, with higher quality and without external dependencies.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect (this is true).
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct (this is NOT true). Agile teams use visual management (Kanban, burndown, velocity charts) regardless of skill level.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect (this is true).
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect (this is true).

domande.spiegazione: Visual management always.

domande.domanda: There are three main types of role in an agile team. The team includes representatives for the product owner, cross-functional team members, and the team:

opzioni.A: Creator.
opzioni.B: Facilitator.
opzioni.C: Runner.
opzioni.D: Enabler.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not an agile role.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. The team facilitator (Scrum Master, coach, iteration manager, servant leader) raises and removes blockers, ensures flow and problem-solves with the team.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Not an agile role.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Removing blockers enables the team, but the role is the facilitator.

domande.spiegazione: Team facilitator.

domande.domanda: You're working through the iteration with your agile team and having trouble completing one of the story cards in the sprint. It depends on something else being done, and the contact is away. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Raise a blocker at the next daily stand-up so the team can swarm around the problem and solve it quickly.
opzioni.B: Bring the piece of work in-house so you don't have to worry anymore.
opzioni.C: Ask the product owner to remove that feature for now; you can revisit it later.
opzioni.D: Add cost to the budget and find a third party to complete the work.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Blockers are raised at least daily at the stand-up so the team can swarm, get help from any experts needed and move on.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Fits the whole team approach, but may not be possible or immediate.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Value should keep its normal priority.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The last resort.

domande.spiegazione: Raise blockers daily.

domande.domanda: The product owner representing the business on your agile project is used to a more dictatorial style of leadership. You explain that servant leadership is used in agile to ensure a safe and open environment. Why is this important to product development?

opzioni.A: So the agile team lead knows who to blame.
opzioni.B: So the team can accurately count the defects.
opzioni.C: So the team feels free to ask for help, admit to problems or failures, and improve.
opzioni.D: So the entire team can push work onto each other if they know they have time.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Agile removes blockers instead of blaming.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Defects should be visible to everyone anyway.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Psychological safety lets people be vulnerable and admit problems; otherwise mistakes stay hidden until release.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The Kanban board already makes work transparent.

domande.spiegazione: Psychological safety.

domande.domanda: Feedback, in many different forms, is one of the most important parts of successful agile product delivery. Which of the following is an agile method for gathering and using feedback to improve?

opzioni.A: Having a once-weekly working group meeting.
opzioni.B: Conducting sprint reviews or demonstrations that include all stakeholders.
opzioni.C: Sending out project reports to project stakeholders to view.
opzioni.D: Asking stakeholders for feedback only when development is blocked.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Once a week isn't enough.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Demonstrating the usable increment each iteration gathers feedback far sooner than at the end (retrospectives are another way).
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. A report doesn't gather feedback.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Agile wants feedback all the time.

domande.spiegazione: Also retrospectives.

domande.domanda: You're working on an agile project where the business representative is pushing for more and more features to be delivered in each iteration. You know what they're asking is not possible based on your team's current velocity. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Show them the team velocity and the points allotted to the cards in the backlog, then ask them to prioritize the features at the next sprint planning.
opzioni.B: Add more members to the team.
opzioni.C: Ask for another business representative who understands the technology better.
opzioni.D: Remove some of the features yourself and see if anyone notices.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. This gives the business control over what's delivered, within the boundaries of what the team can do.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Not the solution.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Educate them and work within the agile system instead.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Tempting, but not transparent.

domande.spiegazione: Prioritize within capacity.

domande.domanda: You're working on a traditional waterfall project, and the organization wants to move to an agile way of working. The functional manager wants the benefit of certain agile tools they've heard about, to uncover potential problems before they occur. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Write the change into your project management plan and circulate it with project stakeholders.
opzioni.B: Set a weekly working group meeting to discuss the project.
opzioni.C: Jump straight into iteration planning.
opzioni.D: Make the product backlog, the iteration Kanban board and the velocity chart all visible in a co-located team area.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not agile.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Not agile.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Maybe, but jumping straight in may scare people.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Visual management integrates seamlessly even in waterfall (a hybrid approach): everyone sees progress, blockers and when things go off course.

domande.spiegazione: Visual management detects problems.

domande.domanda: The Agile Manifesto has 12 clarifying principles added to it to help projects and teams understand the agile values. Which of the following is a correct clarifying principle?

opzioni.A: Tailor the project approach to suit the project and the team.
opzioni.B: Ensure executive buy-in.
opzioni.C: Deliver working software frequently, from a couple of weeks to a couple of months, with a preference for the shorter timescale.
opzioni.D: Ensure complete planning.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Good practice, but not one of the 12 principles.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Executives can be invited to stand-ups, demos and retros, but this isn't a principle.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. One of the 12 clarifying principles.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. That's a waterfall approach.

domande.spiegazione: 12 principles.

domande.domanda: The Agile Manifesto has 12 clarifying principles added to it to help projects and teams understand the agile values. Which of the following is a correct clarifying principle?

opzioni.A: Business people should dictate to the development team what to do.
opzioni.B: Developers can code and release products on a schedule that suits them, for complete autonomy.
opzioni.C: Business people and developers mustn't work together.
opzioni.D: Business people and developers must work together daily throughout the project.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Agile uses servant leadership, not dictation.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. There are schedules to meet: that's why work is time-boxed.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The opposite.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. The product owner (representing the business/customer) works daily with the developers throughout the project.

domande.spiegazione: 12 principles.

domande.domanda: The Agile Manifesto has 12 clarifying principles added to it to help projects and teams understand the agile values. Which of the following is a correct clarifying principle?

opzioni.A: Build projects around a core idea, then brainstorm frequently to get the job done.
opzioni.B: Find the right executive to support you and ensure they tell you the product requirements.
opzioni.C: Deliver frequently, whether an item has been tested or not.
opzioni.D: Build projects around motivated individuals; give them the environment and support they need, and trust them to get the job done.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Close, but agile also delivers in increments, not just brainstorms.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Requirements come from the people who use the product.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Quality is everyone's responsibility, and testing is part of it.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Build around motivated people (those who own or use the product), with T-shaped team members, removing blockers and ensuring flow.

domande.spiegazione: 12 principles.

domande.domanda: The 12 clarifying principles also match up with the best advice for projects, leadership and communication. Which of the following is a correct clarifying principle when it comes to project communication?

opzioni.A: The most efficient and effective method of conveying information to and within a development team is face-to-face conversation.
opzioni.B: Communication is always done in writing, to make sure there is proof.
opzioni.C: Agile teams ensure downward communication only, so the executive in charge directs the product features and the work.
opzioni.D: When communicating, use various forms such as telephone, writing and face to face, to ensure variety.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Face to face gives fast answers and picks up non-verbal nuances; co-located teams also gain information by osmosis.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Written communication loses tone and is easily misinterpreted.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Agile communication is horizontal, among peers.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Variety is nice, but face to face is still best.

domande.spiegazione: Osmotic communication.

domande.domanda: ⚠️ The Agile Manifesto has 12 clarifying principles added to it to help projects and teams understand the agile values. Which of the following is one of them? — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: Union representatives must attend key team meetings.
opzioni.B: Working software is the primary measure of progress.
opzioni.C: Finding risks is the only way to avoid failure.
opzioni.D: Learning new things helps keep a team engaged.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. No union involvement is needed.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Working software (or product), as increments and features delivered with feedback, is the primary measure of progress.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Not true.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Sometimes true, but not a principle.

domande.spiegazione: 12 principles.
domande.nota: Option A is only partially read in the source ('union attendance'): its wording is reconstructed.
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: You're new to your agile project and the team is working through the forming stages. How do you help the team improve as the project progresses?

opzioni.A: Ensure the team holds a project post-mortem and captures the lessons learned by the end of the project.
opzioni.B: Hold a retrospective with the whole team at the end of each iteration and build the lessons learned into each new iteration.
opzioni.C: Ask the product owner to show the team where they can improve.
opzioni.D: Rotate tasks and roles during each iteration.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. A post-mortem comes at the end, too late to help the team as it forms.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Retrospectives at the end of each iteration (what went well, what didn't, what did I learn, what still puzzles me) feed actions back into future iterations quickly.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Improvement is a whole-team activity.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. You'd lose people's expertise in their areas.

domande.spiegazione: Retros.

domande.domanda: You're the agile project manager working through the product requirements with the product owner and the executive project sponsor. The sponsor raises concerns that the development team doesn't fully understand the requirements. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Show them the project management plan, with the scope statement listed in the scope baseline.
opzioni.B: Ask the team to create a high-level prototype of the requirements, then discuss and review it with all stakeholders.
opzioni.C: Show the team the project schedule outlining the delivery dates.
opzioni.D: Hold a retrospective to gather feedback and improve.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. That's for a predictive project.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Agile uses visual mock-ups or prototypes (storyboards, wireframes, models) to quickly reach a shared understanding and consensus.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Not related.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Could help, but isn't about shared understanding of scope.

domande.spiegazione: Visual prototypes.

domande.domanda: The Scrum Master on your agile project asks you for the total lead time of a particular feature. You add up the cycle time of all the cards that contributed to that feature. What two other factors must you take into consideration?

opzioni.A: Time for testing the code and time for merging the code.
opzioni.B: Meeting times and lunch times.
opzioni.C: Value-added time and non-value-added time.
opzioni.D: Time for testing and time for documenting.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Part of the picture, but not the concept asked.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Not the concept.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Lead time (a Lean concept) must include value-added time (contributes to the customer outcome) and non-value-added time (waiting, handoffs, blockers, context switching).
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. These can be essential non-value-added time, but not the answer.

domande.spiegazione: Lean waste.

domande.domanda: When working in an agile team, it's common to use prototypes, demonstrations and reviews, wireframes and storyboards to elicit feedback from the customer or product owner. What is the benefit of using these tools?

opzioni.A: The development team doesn't have to create the real thing.
opzioni.B: The team can get together and have another meeting.
opzioni.C: It allows the users to create new forms that will be required for the new system.
opzioni.D: It allows the product owner to discuss and agree on requirements with their stakeholders.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The work still has to be done.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. More communication, not more meetings.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Not related.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Stakeholders can discuss and agree on requirements and features before money is spent on actual development.

domande.spiegazione: Prototypes gather feedback.

domande.domanda: You're finishing up the first iteration of your agile project and have set a retrospective for the whole team. One team member asks why you have this meeting and whether they really need to attend. What will you tell them?

opzioni.A: It helps the team prioritize product features for the next iteration.
opzioni.B: It allows the team to blame others when things go wrong.
opzioni.C: It's an opportunity for the whole team to look at their way of working and improve.
opzioni.D: It showcases part of the product so everyone can see what was delivered.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. That's iteration (sprint) planning.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Agile removes blockers instead of blaming.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Everyone's feedback is needed: what went well, what didn't, what did I learn, what still puzzles me. Actions feed back into the process.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. That's the sprint review/demonstration.

domande.spiegazione: Retros.

domande.domanda: You're in the beginning stages of a new project where the organization would like to use agile to manage the work. The executive manager asks how the team will make quality everyone's responsibility, leverage the various skill sets within the team and remove reliance on external inputs. Which agile method is she describing?

opzioni.A: Servant leadership.
opzioni.B: Sprint planning.
opzioni.C: The daily stand-up.
opzioni.D: The whole team approach.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Good, but not what's described.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. It's a ceremony.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. It's a ceremony.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. The whole team approach brings all necessary people (cross-functional, T-shaped) into the team, ideally co-located, reducing handoffs and silos.

domande.spiegazione: Whole team approach.

domande.domanda: You've been working on an agile project for some time and have been blocked by the need for expertise from another team. What do you do to overcome organizational silos?

opzioni.A: Work with the managers of the team members you need, to have them dedicate the necessary individuals to your cross-functional team.
opzioni.B: Raise a change request for review by the project change control board, as the work will be delayed.
opzioni.C: Raise an issue in the issue log for review and management by the project team.
opzioni.D: Work with the risk team to raise a project risk, assign an owner to it and create controls.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. The whole team approach brings the necessary members and skills into the team, reducing silos and handoffs.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. An old-school waterfall approach.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. An old-school waterfall approach.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. An old-school waterfall approach.

domande.spiegazione: Reduce silos.

domande.domanda: The 12 agile clarifying principles also match up with the best advice for workflow and getting things done. Which of the following is a correct clarifying principle when it comes to project workflow?

opzioni.A: Agile does not use processes, as it prefers individuals and interactions over processes and tools.
opzioni.B: Agile processes engage and support the team by ensuring sponsors, developers and users all get what they want.
opzioni.C: Agile processes promote sustainable development: the sponsors, developers and users should be able to maintain a constant pace indefinitely.
opzioni.D: Agile processes help get as much work done as possible: when the team thinks it can't go further, agile pushes them to go the extra mile.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. It echoes a manifesto value, but it isn't a principle (agile still has processes).
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. You can't always get what you want.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Sustainable pace: avoid frequent task switching or pushing too much work into an iteration, which burns people out and slows progress.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Pushing beyond velocity causes burnout, sick days and disengagement.

domande.spiegazione: Sustainable pace.

domande.domanda: The 12 agile clarifying principles also match up with the best advice for quality. Which of the following is a correct agile clarifying principle when it comes to project quality?

opzioni.A: Continuous flow ensures work is done at a reasonable pace and defects are caught.
opzioni.B: Testing is done at all levels, from unit testing to end-to-end testing.
opzioni.C: Continuous attention to technical excellence and good design enhances agility.
opzioni.D: Quality is everyone's responsibility in an agile team, meaning everyone will test the product.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Continuous flow (from Toyota) is good, but it doesn't ensure defects are caught.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. A correct practice, but too detailed: not a clarifying principle.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Of these, only continuous attention to technical excellence and good design is one of the 12 principles.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Quality is everyone's responsibility, but that doesn't mean everyone tests.

domande.spiegazione: 12 principles.

domande.domanda: The 12 agile clarifying principles also match up with the best advice for keeping things simple in a project. Which of the following is a correct clarifying principle?

opzioni.A: Simplicity is only possible when the team first understands how complex the system is.
opzioni.B: Simplicity is part of every project: everyone naturally simplifies the work as part of their role.
opzioni.C: Simplicity reduces cost in a project, by ensuring executives are always simplifying the process and the system.
opzioni.D: Simplicity, the art of maximizing the amount of work not done, is essential.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. A nice statement, but not a principle.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Ideal, but in reality simplicity is hard to achieve.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Executives aren't in the detail of the work.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. This is the clarifying principle (as simple as possible, but no simpler).

domande.spiegazione: 12 principles.

domande.domanda: The Agile Manifesto has 12 clarifying principles to help you understand the agile values; they are also best practice for improving the team over time. Which of the following is a correct clarifying principle?

opzioni.A: The team will meet daily to build a supportive network of workers.
opzioni.B: At regular intervals, the team reflects on how to become more effective, then tunes and adjusts its behavior accordingly.
opzioni.C: Features are regularly improved through refactoring of the code.
opzioni.D: The project sponsor regularly swaps team member roles to keep everyone learning and growing.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Stand-ups are great, but this isn't a principle.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. This principle becomes the team retrospective in practice.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Good practice, but not a clarifying principle.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Agile prefers pairing up and T-shaped members.

domande.spiegazione: 12 principles.

domande.domanda: Which of the following is NOT an agile clarifying principle?

opzioni.A: Our highest priority is to satisfy the customer through early and continuous delivery of valuable software.
opzioni.B: Ensure delivery timelines are met at all costs.
opzioni.C: Welcome changing requirements, even late in development; agile processes harness change for the customer's competitive advantage.
opzioni.D: Deliver working software frequently, from a couple of weeks to a couple of months, with a preference for the shorter timescale.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect: this IS a principle.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct: this is NOT a principle. In agile, time and cost are often fixed but scope is flexible and prioritized by the product owner.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect: this IS a principle.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect: this IS a principle.

domande.spiegazione: 12 principles.

domande.domanda: You're going through a retrospective with your team at the end of the sprint, and the team has raised an issue that is slowing down their work. The Scrum Master guides the team through an exercise called the Five Whys. What is its purpose?

opzioni.A: To ask who, what, where and when to find the cause of the problem.
opzioni.B: To ask why the issue happened, then why again for each answer, until the cause is found.
opzioni.C: To ask why the team is working on each feature, to give the team purpose.
opzioni.D: To allocate five whys to each story card, so the team knows the reason for working on it.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The technique asks 'why' repeatedly.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. The Five Whys is a Lean (Toyota) problem-solving technique to get to the root cause.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. It's for root cause, not purpose.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Story cards should have a 'why', but that's not the Five Whys.

domande.spiegazione: Five Whys.

domande.domanda: The Scrum Master in an agile team has asked the team to do a self-assessment. What is the focus of this self-assessment?

opzioni.A: How often the team meets during the week.
opzioni.B: How many story cards the team has completed.
opzioni.C: How much yearly bonus the team should receive.
opzioni.D: How the team performs and delivers together.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not the focus.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. That's velocity.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Not related to agile.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. It gauges how the team performs together and its results, identifying what works and where to improve; the team then problem-solves and celebrates.

domande.spiegazione: Self-assessment.

domande.domanda: You're working in an agile team and the business representative would like an idea of the risk associated with a particular feature. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Show the business representative the risk management plan from your project management plan.
opzioni.B: Ask the development team if they like the feature.
opzioni.C: Hold a pre-mortem, where each team member writes down reasons they think the task or feature might fail, so these can be discussed.
opzioni.D: Check your gut feel for the feature and, if it doesn't feel right, look into it more deeply.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. A waterfall approach.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Developer input matters, but this isn't about risk.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. A pre-mortem brainstorms reasons for failure before they happen; ideas are shared round-robin and can be grouped in an affinity diagram.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Not a structured approach.

domande.spiegazione: Pre-mortem.

domande.domanda: You're the agile team leader working through a team retrospective. An issue experienced by the team is raised. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Perform fishbone (Ishikawa) analysis.
opzioni.B: Perform Kano analysis.
opzioni.C: Perform regression analysis.
opzioni.D: Perform multi-vari chart analysis.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Get to the root cause: the fishbone (Ishikawa) diagram brainstorms causes into buckets such as people, information, process and system.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Kano is for customer value.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Regression is for trends in data.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. A chart similar to a control chart, with variable inputs.

domande.spiegazione: Fishbone.

domande.domanda: You've been hired to lead a new project team as an agile project manager. When you come on board, you learn that the organization uses a hybrid model. What does this mean?

opzioni.A: The team is a hybrid of developers, designers and business users, to get the best return on investment.
opzioni.B: The product you're developing will use both electricity and fuel for power, like a hybrid car.
opzioni.C: A combination of predictive (e.g. a project plan prepared in advance) and adaptive (e.g. iterations, backlogs, Kanban) project methods will be used.
opzioni.D: A hybrid team environment of physical and software reporting boards will be used.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Sounds good, but not the idea.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Very funny, but no.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Hybrid combines predictive (pre-planned scope, quality, schedule, risk) with adaptive elements (prioritized backlog, Kanban, iterations, retrospectives).
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. It's about project methods, not boards.

domande.spiegazione: Hybrid approach.

domande.domanda: You're the product owner in an agile team, working with the developers to create story cards to place in the product backlog. In the three Cs of user story creation, what do you do first?

opzioni.A: Create the card: the physical or software media describing the user story.
opzioni.B: Confirm the acceptance criteria.
opzioni.C: Have a conversation with the team to flesh out the requirements.
opzioni.D: Catch defects before they're developed by working with quality testers before and after.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. The three Cs: Card, then Conversation (PO and developers on how it will be used), then Confirmation (acceptance criteria / definition of done).
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Confirmation comes last.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Conversation is second.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Not one of the three Cs.

domande.spiegazione: 3 Cs.

domande.domanda: You're working on the product backlog with your agile project team, creating user stories to be prioritized. Which of the following is the best answer for what should go into a user story card?

opzioni.A: The key risks of the project and the feature being developed, with their owners and mitigations.
opzioni.B: A wireframe of the feature to be developed that developers can work with.
opzioni.C: The requirement, its criticality, the expected development and test duration, and the acceptance criteria for that story.
opzioni.D: The benefit of the feature, so key stakeholders are aware of what they'll get.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. That belongs to the risk log or risk cards.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Useful, but not in every story card.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Story cards should have the requirement, criticality, test/estimate details and clear acceptance criteria.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Useful, but not in every story card.

domande.spiegazione: Story card.

domande.domanda: You're an agile project manager and have begun creating user stories with your team to go into the product backlog. You've created the card and added the requirement, its criticality and the acceptance criteria. What will you do next?

opzioni.A: Place the card on the Kanban board so the team can clearly see the future work.
opzioni.B: Have a conversation with the developers about how the software will be used, then confirm the acceptance criteria and the definition of done.
opzioni.C: Prioritize the card in the upcoming sprint backlog to ensure the work gets done.
opzioni.D: Advise the project sponsor and risk manager of the feature details to ensure risks are captured.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Probably needs iteration planning first.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Following the three Cs (card, conversation, confirmation), then it can be placed in the backlog for the upcoming sprint.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The card isn't complete yet.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. A separate process.

domande.spiegazione: Card, conversation, confirmation.

domande.domanda: A project manager is planning the construction of a new public library. The community and the project stakeholders are having difficulty agreeing on the key features to include in the final design. What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Facilitate a workshop to gather input from all stakeholders.
opzioni.B: Define the difference between essential and non-essential features.
opzioni.C: Involve a design consultant to mediate the stakeholder discussions.
opzioni.D: Identify the root cause of the stakeholders' inability to agree on the project scope.

domande.hint: There's a problem: do you understand it yet?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. An action taken before understanding why the stakeholders can't agree.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. An action, and choosing what's essential isn't the PM's job: it belongs to the product owner, sponsor or customers.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Brings in other people without understanding the root cause of the problem.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Look for the root cause: understand the problem before solving it.

domande.spiegazione: Mindset: no actions without understanding the problem. Before solving a problem ask how it came about, what's going on and whether there are multiple solutions. A, B and C have something in common: they're all actions.

domande.domanda: A project manager convenes an emergency session with the software development team to address significant bugs that are delaying the project's delivery. The product owner suggests conducting a root cause analysis (RCA) to identify the underlying issues. What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Collaborate with the team to discuss the RCA suggestion and decide collectively on the next step.
opzioni.B: Encourage a lead developer to take charge of the RCA to foster team autonomy.
opzioni.C: Coordinate with the quality assurance lead to refine the testing processes based on the RCA outcome.
opzioni.D: Organize the session so that all team members contribute their insights and potential solutions.

domande.hint: 'Product owner' = agile: the team is self-directing.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Bring the suggestion to the team and let them decide whether to do it.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Never do this: it gives your work away and leaves the team on its own.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Brings more people in and assumes the RCA will be implemented.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Not bad, but vague: the team seems to be coming up with its own solutions instead of addressing the RCA.

domande.spiegazione: The product owner tells you it's agile. When someone suggests something the team should do, let the team decide: on an agile project the team is self-leading and self-directing, and decides how and with what methods to do the work. You're not a dictator.

domande.domanda: Reviewing the launch of a new e-commerce platform, the project manager discovers that the finance department is concerned about not being involved in the cost estimates and about the potential impact on the project's returns. What should the project manager do first?

opzioni.A: Amend the stakeholder engagement plan to better integrate finance in future planning.
opzioni.B: Document the exclusion of the finance team as a risk to project success.
opzioni.C: Maintain the project timeline and plan a financial review before the final phase.
opzioni.D: Organize a meeting with the finance team to understand their concerns.

domande.hint: 'First', and a stakeholder has a concern.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. You'd be amending the plan before understanding their concern.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Before documenting a risk, you have to understand it.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. 'Maintain' means doing nothing, and the timeline may be affected.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Meet them first to understand the concern, so you know what action to take next.

domande.spiegazione: Similar to question 1. The choices share a theme, but one is uniquely different: before acting (amending plans, documenting risks), meet the stakeholders and understand their concern. Never do nothing.

domande.domanda: As part of a project to integrate a new security feature into an online shopping platform, stakeholders are concerned during planning that they don't understand the integration process. What should the project manager do to improve the stakeholders' understanding of the integration?

opzioni.A: Schedule regular demonstration sessions during each sprint to show progress and integration steps.
opzioni.B: Arrange for the technical team to provide a detailed explanation before each sprint begins.
opzioni.C: Organize a training session to educate stakeholders on the technical aspects of the integration.
opzioni.D: Provide detailed documentation on the integration process before each sprint.

domande.hint: In agile, what happens every sprint?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Sprint reviews/demonstrations show what's been done and how it works.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Stakeholders don't need detailed technical explanations.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Customers don't need to be educated on technical aspects: that's for team members.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Customers don't want detailed documentation and may not understand it.

domande.spiegazione: Simple if you know agile: every sprint has a sprint review. Customers care about functionality, not the technical details: if you build me a website, I don't need to know the coding language, only that it works.

domande.domanda: ⚠️ A project manager is preparing for the sprint planning session for a new feature in a healthcare system. The meeting aims to determine the amount of work for the upcoming sprint. Which two pieces of information are essential to make the meeting productive and efficient? (Choose two.) — ⚠️ Note: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript.

opzioni.A: An updated risk assessment.
opzioni.B: Product marketplace goals.
opzioni.C: Team performance metrics (velocity).
opzioni.D: A detailed product backlog.
opzioni.E: The current phase-based project timeline.

domande.hint: Input to sprint planning: what the work is and how fast the team works.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Not an input to decide how much work goes into the sprint.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. More about sales and marketing.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Velocity tells the team how much it can do per sprint, based on how fast it worked before.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. The product backlog (with user stories) is where the team picks the work for the sprint.
spiegazioni_opzioni.E: Incorrect. Agile projects don't have phases and timelines laid out like that: they build by backlog priority.

domande.spiegazione: Sprint planning: the team decides what and how much work to do in the next sprint (output: the sprint backlog). It needs the product backlog and its velocity.
domande.nota: Multiple-choice question (choose two). The option letters are not read in the source video: options reconstructed from the transcript; answer (velocity + product backlog) is from the source.
domande.motivo_incertezza: options/text partly reconstructed from the transcript

domande.domanda: A project manager is leading a biotechnology research project characterized by significant ambiguity and unpredictability. It has been suggested to introduce a system to gauge the quality of the project outputs effectively. Which hybrid technique should the project manager use to ensure quality assurance?

opzioni.A: Combine weekly sprints with quarterly external audits to validate project standards.
opzioni.B: Merge traditional milestone reviews with agile sprint demonstrations.
opzioni.C: Adopt pair programming and customer feedback sessions.
opzioni.D: Integrate continuous integration tools with formal quality control checkpoints.

domande.hint: The ultimate test of quality is customer satisfaction.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Quarterly, and it doesn't involve the customer.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Sprint demos are good, but it's unclear how long the milestone reviews are.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Pair programming (from XP: one writes, one checks the code) reduces bugs, and customer feedback makes the product satisfying.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Tools and checkpoints, but it doesn't bring customers in.

domande.spiegazione: Quality means meeting customer satisfaction. The best way to make a product customers like is to involve them during development and get their feedback. Pair programming catches bugs as code is written.

domande.domanda: A project manager oversees a software development project where the team has prioritized building a new user authentication system in the current sprint. Midway through the sprint, two developers want to divert their efforts to optimizing database queries, anticipating future performance bottlenecks. What should the project manager do next?

opzioni.A: Allocate time for the developers to present their optimization proposal at the next sprint planning meeting.
opzioni.B: Reinforce the importance of adhering to the sprint's primary goal of completing the authentication system.
opzioni.C: Request a special session to assess the potential impact of the database optimization on future sprints.
opzioni.D: Support the developers' initiative by allocating a small portion of their time to preliminary work on the database.

domande.hint: Once a sprint starts, don't change the work.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Allocating time takes it away from the sprint goal.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Keep them on track to finish the sprint goal.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Again takes time away from the sprint goal.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Makes them work on something that isn't the sprint goal.

domande.spiegazione: Tough: it tests agile principles. Once a sprint starts, do the sprint work: don't change the team or the work. If the team thinks the optimization is needed, it can go into the product backlog for a future sprint.

domande.domanda: A project manager is overseeing the development of an enterprise resource planning (ERP) system and has decided that a combination of Scrum and Kanban would be most effective. However, the product owner is unsure how to begin organizing and prioritizing work. What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Guide the product owner in developing and optimizing a comprehensive product backlog.
opzioni.B: Have team members explain the integration of Scrum and Kanban principles to the product owner.
opzioni.C: Recommend that the project team use visual management tools to improve workflow.
opzioni.D: Teach the product owner how to map out process flows to better understand task sequences.

domande.hint: If someone doesn't know how to do their role, teach them.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Organizing and prioritizing work happens in the product backlog: work with the product owner on it.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Don't give it away: this is part of your job.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The team shouldn't prioritize work: that's the product owner's job.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Good, but it doesn't teach prioritization.

domande.spiegazione: Exam objective: train people. If someone doesn't know how to do something, don't do it for them or have someone else do their role: teach them. Prioritizing work is all about the product backlog.

domande.domanda: A project manager is leading a team on a critical marketing campaign for a major product launch. After unexpected last-minute changes, the team worked overtime to meet tight deadlines. The sponsor has allocated a monetary award to recognize the team's efforts. Based on project management practice, what is the most appropriate action?

opzioni.A: Distribute the entire award to the team member who worked the longest hours.
opzioni.B: Organize a team-building retreat to enhance morale for future projects.
opzioni.C: Use the award to fund professional development opportunities that benefit the team in future projects.
opzioni.D: Decide how to distribute the award based on informal feedback from the team.

domande.hint: Rewards must be fair and public.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Working the longest hours doesn't mean doing the most work: throwaway answer.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Not a bad answer, but C benefits them more in future projects.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Helps them learn and benefits the whole team in the future.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Informal feedback isn't a fair, transparent system.

domande.spiegazione: Tough. Any reward system must be fair and public. Between a retreat and professional development, development benefits the team more in future projects.

domande.domanda: A project manager is overseeing the construction of a new community recreation center that needs to be built quickly to meet the community's expectations. The team is skilled, stakeholders are engaged and the community is excited about the new facility. What should the project manager do to prioritize time to completion?

opzioni.A: Assign more resources to critical tasks without consulting the team.
opzioni.B: Develop a milestone-based plan ensuring regular stakeholder involvement and communication.
opzioni.C: Monitor progress daily and integrate team input to ensure alignment with project goals.
opzioni.D: Request an extension of the project deadline from the sponsor.

domande.hint: Stakeholder involvement is the key to success.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Never do something without consulting the team doing the work.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Milestones keep the project on schedule, and stakeholder involvement keeps it on track.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Daily monitoring takes up a lot of time.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. No need for an extension unless you're going to overrun.

domande.spiegazione: Trick question. Stakeholder engagement is the key to success on projects and to many exam answers; a milestone-based plan keeps the schedule.

domande.domanda: A project manager has begun a complex airport expansion project. Although the project is in the initiating phase, the sponsor keeps asking for concrete dates for the most important project milestones. When will the project manager be able to provide the requested information?

opzioni.A: After the initial risk assessments are completed to estimate timelines.
opzioni.B: At the end of the planning phase, once the detailed schedule and risk assessments are completed.
opzioni.C: During execution, when the project is under way and progress can be measured.
opzioni.D: Once the project charter is signed, since it outlines the initial milestones.

domande.hint: Initiating is high level: concrete dates come from planning.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. An initial risk assessment doesn't give concrete information.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Planning is when you build the detailed schedule (expert judgment, bottom-up estimates, WBS): concrete dates come from there.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. You don't need to wait for execution: that's the point of planning.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. A signed charter authorizes the project, but the real planning work hasn't been done yet.

domande.spiegazione: In initiating everything is high level (scope, schedule, budget, risk in the charter): you can't give concrete dates. The objective of planning is to determine the best schedule.

domande.domanda: A project manager oversees a large infrastructure project in a hierarchical organization. Team members are used to receiving direct instructions, and their performance reviews are based on task completion percentage. After discussing with the sponsor, the project manager realizes some tasks must be reassigned to meet the next milestone. This change could be seen as a negative reflection on the current assignees' performance. What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Assign the tasks to the most skilled member without further discussion.
opzioni.B: Hold a meeting to explain the changes and collaborate on reassigning the tasks.
opzioni.C: Privately ask a senior member to take over the tasks and inform the others of the reassignment.
opzioni.D: Send an email to the team outlining the task changes and the reasoning behind them.

domande.hint: Confront the problem; never hide anything.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Don't decide by yourself: work with the team.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Meet the team, explain the changes and decide collaboratively.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Never give away your work, and don't do things behind people's backs.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Similar to B, but an email is worse than collaborating with the team.

domande.spiegazione: Mindset: confront your problems, don't hide anything from anyone, and bring people into decisions. B and D are similar, but working collaboratively is better than sending an email.

domande.domanda: A project manager is leading a city park renovation. During a status meeting with city officials, the project manager gives an update on a significant deliverable, and some officials claim they were never informed about it. What should the project manager do next?

opzioni.A: Confirm whether the scope statement has been updated to include the deliverable.
opzioni.B: Meet with these officials to review the communication plan and clarify the deliverables.
opzioni.C: Check these officials' attendance records at prior project meetings.
opzioni.D: Review the project documents to ensure the deliverable was communicated.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. First meet them and check they understand what the deliverable is.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Meet the officials, review the communication plan and clarify the deliverables.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Looks malicious, as if you want to prove they didn't show up.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Before reviewing documents, meet them.

domande.spiegazione: When something negative is going on, meet and talk to people. If an option seems malicious or likely to hurt the project (checking attendance to 'prosecute' them), it's not the answer.

domande.domanda: A project manager oversees the construction of a new office building. A key stakeholder complains they never received the structural integrity test status report. When the project manager provides it, the stakeholder notices that an important aspect of the structure was not tested. Which tool should the project manager have used to prevent this situation?

opzioni.A: Communication log.
opzioni.B: Requirements traceability matrix.
opzioni.C: Stakeholder register.
opzioni.D: Quality management plan.

domande.hint: 'Prevent': which document records a stakeholder's communication needs?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The log records communications that already happened: it doesn't prevent anything.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Traces who gave which requirement: not the problem here.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Records who the stakeholders are and their communication requirements.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Says how to meet quality requirements, but the problem is a report not received.

domande.spiegazione: Tough. The keyword is 'prevent'. The main complaint is that the stakeholder never got the report. The stakeholder register records each stakeholder's communication requirements; the communications management plan describes what, when and how communication happens.

domande.domanda: A project manager oversees development of a new healthcare facility. The team is struggling to understand some critical aspects of the project scope. A senior subject matter expert (SME) from headquarters is available for one week. What should the project manager do to benefit from the SME's presence?

opzioni.A: Conduct a workshop with the SME to address the team's challenges.
opzioni.B: Discuss with the SME the specific scope issues the team is facing.
opzioni.C: Arrange for the SME to provide training sessions to the team.
opzioni.D: Have the SME review the project documentation for alignment.

domande.hint: Collaborative: who needs to understand the scope?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. A workshop with just you and the SME doesn't include the team.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Again, the team isn't involved.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. The SME trains the team so they understand the scope better.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Nothing says there's an alignment problem.

domande.spiegazione: Be collaborative: if you leave the team out and decide by yourself, it's not servant leadership. With an SME available for only a week, use them to train the team.

domande.domanda: A project manager is leading an agile project to develop a new customer relationship management (CRM) system. Midway through, the team receives feedback from the legal team about new data protection laws the project may need to comply with. Which two actions should the project manager take next? (Choose two.)

opzioni.A: Direct the product owner to prioritize data protection features in future sprints.
opzioni.B: Request detailed information about the new laws from the legal department.
opzioni.C: Have the legal team implement the compliance measures.
opzioni.D: Plan the immediate integration of compliance requirements to mitigate any legal issues.
opzioni.E: Conduct an impact analysis with the team to understand how the law affects the project.

domande.hint: Before acting: understand the law and its impact.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. An action: maybe later, once you know the law and its impact.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. First find out what the law is about.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. You can't implement compliance measures without knowing how they affect the project.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. An action before understanding the impact.
spiegazioni_opzioni.E: Correct. Before implementing anything, understand how it affects the project.

domande.spiegazione: Choose two, 'next'. Don't take action straight away: assess the situation. First learn about the law (B), then analyze its impact (E); only after that talk to the product owner or plan integration.
domande.nota: Multiple-choice question (choose two). The instructor first says 'B and C', then confirms B and E.

domande.domanda: A project manager is initiating a new software development project for a client known for vague requirements and challenging communication. Previous interactions with this client have led to misunderstandings about scope. What strategy should the project manager implement to prevent this?

opzioni.A: Apply a phased development approach to validate scope at each milestone.
opzioni.B: Collaborate with the product owner to establish a clear minimum viable product (MVP).
opzioni.C: Enhance team-client communication protocols to ensure better clarity and feedback.
opzioni.D: Implement a strict deliverable schedule to force clarity and client interaction.

domande.hint: How do you beat vague requirements?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Milestones can take a long time: you want something quicker.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Give the client a product to use: they'll tell you what to change, update or remove.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Good, but giving them a product beats just communicating.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Never force people: negative answer.

domande.spiegazione: The exam likes MVPs. Eliminate the negative option (force). C is good, but better than talking to the client is giving them something to use and getting their feedback: the way to beat vague requirements is a minimum viable product.

domande.domanda: In the middle of a software development project following a predictive life cycle, a significant portion of the software is set for incremental delivery to the client. The experienced team responsible for this portion wants to take on more of the decision-making traditionally handled by the project manager after each delivery. What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Schedule a meeting with senior management to seek guidance on adjusting the decision-making process.
opzioni.B: Support the team's initiative to take on decision-making responsibilities while retaining final approval authority.
opzioni.C: Maintain the traditional structure in which the project manager makes all decisions regardless of the team's readiness.
opzioni.D: Consult the sponsor to explore delegating key post-delivery decisions to the team.

domande.hint: Predictive project: who keeps final approval?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Never go to senior management for guidance: they hired you to run the project.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Support the team while keeping final approval, as fits a predictive project.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. 'Maintain' means doing nothing for the question.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The sponsor is senior management: never give away your work.

domande.spiegazione: The mindset eliminates going to senior management or the sponsor. 'Maintain the current structure' does nothing. Support the team, but on a predictive project you keep the final decision.

domande.domanda: A project manager oversees development of a new software tool. Although the tool isn't finished, the product owner decides to release an early version, the minimum viable product. A key stakeholder, the vice president of marketing, is unhappy with the limited features in the launch. What should the project manager do to ensure better satisfaction with future releases?

opzioni.A: Work with the team and stakeholders to adjust future release timelines based on expectations.
opzioni.B: Set up a process where stakeholders can provide feedback before future releases are finalized.
opzioni.C: Take control of communication with the stakeholders to ensure everyone understands.
opzioni.D: Ask the sponsor to resolve the disagreement between the product owner and the vice president of marketing.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Work with the team and stakeholders: collaborative.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Good, but you'd set up the process yourself without the team.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Taking control isn't servant leadership on an agile project.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Never go to the sponsor to do your work.

domande.spiegazione: By now you'll notice the theme: always work and collaborate with people. An MVP means agile, so be a servant leader: B is good but you'd be doing it alone.

domande.domanda: A project manager oversees an agile project to develop a new mobile app in a large tech company. The project manager planned to use email for all project communications, but the product owner suggests using a specialized project management tool that integrates better with agile workflows. What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Evaluate how the new communication tool could affect current timelines and workflow before making a decision.
opzioni.B: Update the communications management plan to fully adopt the product owner's preferred tool and inform the team.
opzioni.C: Have the team test the proposed tool on a small part of the project before deciding whether to implement it across the team.
opzioni.D: Continue using email for major announcements, but use the new tool for daily agile interactions with the team.

domande.hint: Bring the team in and let them decide.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. You'd evaluate and decide by yourself.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Imposes the tool, bypassing the team.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. The team tests it and decides whether it's good to implement.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Nothing really changes, and you're deciding everything yourself.

domande.spiegazione: The mindset eliminates almost every choice. In A, B and D you decide by yourself: not servant leadership. Have the team try it and decide.

domande.domanda: During development of a new cloud-based analytics platform, the team raises concerns about certain product backlog items that are hard to implement because of technical and resource limitations. What should the project manager recommend the product owner do?

opzioni.A: Prioritize and address the impediments based on their impact on the platform's most valuable features.
opzioni.B: Conduct a risk assessment to evaluate how the impediments might affect the project timeline.
opzioni.C: Implement a phase-based approach to solve the issues, starting with those that impact the current sprint.
opzioni.D: Remove those items and add new ones.

domande.hint: What is the product owner responsible for?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. The product owner is responsible for prioritizing the backlog: change the priorities based on the impact.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. A risk assessment is done by you and the team, not the product owner.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Nothing in the question concerns the current sprint.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Never just remove high-value items because of problems: try to solve them first.

domande.spiegazione: Read carefully: it asks what the product owner should do. The product owner prioritizes the backlog, so the answer is about prioritization.

domande.domanda: A project manager new to agile is overseeing development of a software tool. Having seen other projects stumble without a well-defined scope and completion criteria, leading to continuous scope expansion, the project manager wants to prevent similar issues. What proactive step should the project manager take to establish clarity and prevent scope creep?

opzioni.A: Create a detailed timeline with milestones to monitor progress and control changes.
opzioni.B: Introduce a rigorous change management process to evaluate and approve additional features.
opzioni.C: Promote regular synchronization meetings to discuss the schedule and which work to do first.
opzioni.D: Organize workshops with all stakeholders to collaboratively create the project charter and clearly define the definition of done.

domande.hint: Agile: what clarifies when work is complete?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Traditional schedule control, not clarity on the work.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Agile doesn't have a rigorous change management process.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Not bad, but it's about the schedule, not the scope.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. The definition of done tells the team when the work meets the required criteria.

domande.spiegazione: Since it's agile, rigorous change control and controlling changes aren't the answer. Nothing addresses clarity of the work better than an MVP and a definition of done.

domande.domanda: During a project, it becomes apparent that team members from different departments have different perspectives on what the project's final outcome should be. What should the project manager do first?

opzioni.A: Facilitate a session to revisit and clarify the project goal with the entire team.
opzioni.B: Meet with the sponsor to ensure alignment with the project objectives.
opzioni.C: Make sure the project outcome is aligned with the project charter and scope statement.
opzioni.D: Assign the department heads responsibility for resolving the issue.

domande.hint: Bring people together and solve the problem.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Bring everyone together so they all understand the goal.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The sponsor already knows the objectives: this is about team members.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Doesn't address the problem between team members.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The problem is with team members, not department heads.

domande.spiegazione: Mindset: bring people together and solve problems. Don't run from a problem, don't kick the can down the road, don't give it away and never do nothing.

domande.domanda: A project manager is overseeing construction of a new manufacturing facility when an economic downturn may suddenly threaten the project's viability. What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Adjust the project's financial forecast to account for the economic downturn.
opzioni.B: Suggest to the sponsor that the project be postponed.
opzioni.C: Redirect some project resources to support other essential projects.
opzioni.D: Identify and document the new risk and create mitigation strategies.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. An action: on a traditional project, changing plans requires a change request.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Never go to the sponsor and never postpone a project just like that.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Redirecting resources basically shuts the project down.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. It's a risk: record it in the risk register and plan mitigation.

domande.spiegazione: Read carefully: 'may' or 'might' means a risk; something that will happen or has happened is an issue. Don't take action right away: on a traditional (construction) project, changes need a change request.

domande.domanda: A project manager is starting a highway expansion project. The state transportation department has requested an initial environmental impact assessment, after which it will decide whether to continue. A team member suggests planning the full project based on past trends. What should the project manager do first?

opzioni.A: Advise the team member to focus on the current deliverable.
opzioni.B: Review the charter to confirm the high-level scope.
opzioni.C: Develop a detailed plan for the entire project based on history.
opzioni.D: Confirm with the stakeholders and plan the full project scope.

domande.hint: Initiating, and the go/no-go decision depends on the assessment.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Shuts the team member down: never do nothing.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Review and confirm the high-level scope while waiting for the assessment.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. You have to wait for the assessment.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. An action: you can't plan the full scope before the assessment.

domande.spiegazione: Very tricky: it tries to push you into doing something you shouldn't. You're in initiating and must wait for the assessment, so assess and review first: confirm the high-level scope.

domande.domanda: ⚠️ A project manager is overseeing the upgrade of an old manufacturing system to a new automated solution aligned with organizational process changes. The project charter is approved and the PMO has provided templates for all new projects. What should the project manager prioritize? — ⚠️ Note: debatable: the instructor sees more than one valid answer.

opzioni.A: Align the project plan with the organization's strategic goals, working closely with senior management.
opzioni.B: Develop a training and communications management plan to enhance collaboration with the team.
opzioni.C: Create a detailed budget and schedule regular reviews with the finance team.
opzioni.D: Collaborate with the operations department to minimize disruption during the upgrade.

domande.hint: The charter is approved: next you plan, and with whom?

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Senior management doesn't help you build detailed plans.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Collaborate with the team, and the way to collaborate is good communication.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. You build the budget with your team, not the finance department.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. You plan with your team, not the operations department.

domande.spiegazione: With the charter approved, the next step is planning, with the team. It's not about whether the choice is amazing: is it better than the other three? The game is choosing the best answer, not the correct one.
domande.nota: The instructor: 'not the best answer in absolute terms, but the best of these four'.
domande.motivo_incertezza: debatable: the instructor sees more than one valid answer

domande.domanda: A project manager has just completed development of a new city park and is preparing to transition the project to the city maintenance department. Before closing the project, what should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Verify that all project deliverables were met according to the project plan.
opzioni.B: Conduct a final inspection with the sponsor to ensure all tasks in the WBS are complete.
opzioni.C: Ensure all project documentation is completed and archived.
opzioni.D: Conduct a final performance review with the stakeholders.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Part of closing: before it comes inspection and scope validation.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Validate scope (inspection with the customer/sponsor) comes before closing.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Part of closing.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Project performance review: part of closing.

domande.spiegazione: Many people get this wrong: it says BEFORE closing. On a traditional project, before closing comes control quality, then validate scope, where the customer and sponsor verify the work. One of its tools is inspection, and the output is accepted deliverables.

domande.domanda: A project manager needs to prioritize multiple projects within a portfolio and requires accurate budget estimates. The process must follow agile principles to ensure a reliable financial plan. How should the budget for each project be estimated?

opzioni.A: Calculate the cost from the team's individual task estimates, considering the current workload.
opzioni.B: Leverage the combined expertise of the sponsor, product owner and agile coach to derive budget estimates.
opzioni.C: Use analytical software to model potential costs based on predictive analysis and historical data.
opzioni.D: Have the product owner conduct a thorough requirements analysis with the team to forecast the project budget.

domande.hint: In agile, cost is mostly people.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Agile cost depends on the team: how much you pay people, for how long and for how many sprints.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The real cost lies in how much you pay the workers, not in their expertise.
