Case study I
A large financial services organization has initiated a project to replace its legacy Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system with a new cloud-based platform. The project has an approved budget of $12 million and a planned duration of 18 months. The project sponsor and the Project Management Office (PMO) have assigned a project manager to lead the effort.
The organization has an executive steering committee that oversees all projects exceeding $5 million. The steering committee includes the chief information officer, the chief financial officer, and the head of business operations. The PMO has established standard templates and phase-gate review processes for all major projects.
During the project initiation, the project manager develops the project charter in collaboration with the sponsor. The charter is approved, and the project manager is granted authority to allocate organizational resources.
Question 2 (Case Study I)
The development team, which has experience with adaptive approaches, asked to self-govern their sprint planning and daily coordination meetings. The steering committee denied the request, insisting that all scope changes must go through formal change control, even for low-impact adjustments.
What should the project manager have done differently to avoid this situation?

opzioni.A: Submitted a formal change request to the steering committee with a detailed business case for self-governance.
opzioni.B: Avoided using any adaptive development practices on a project governed by a structured governance model.
opzioni.C: Aligned the steering committee earlier on tailoring decisions, including the appropriate level of self-governance for adaptive workstreams.
opzioni.D: Assigned a dedicated governance compliance officer to monitor the team's adherence to structured governance rules.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Submitting a formal change request to the steering committee, accompanied by a detailed business case for self-governance, is reactive rather than preventive. The question asks what the PM should have done to avoid the situation. By the time a formal change request is needed, the disagreement has already occurred. The better approach is to establish governance expectations upfront.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Predictive and adaptive approaches are not mutually exclusive. Many organizations successfully use Agile teams within structured governance frameworks. The solution is tailoring and alignment, not avoiding adaptive practices.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Agile or adaptive projects are designed to be self-governing, meaning that the teams involved have the autonomy to make decisions and manage their work without heavy bureaucracy and oversight. The issue is not that the team wants self-governance. The issue is that governance expectations were never aligned. The project manager should have worked with the steering committee early in the project to define which decisions the team could make independently, which changes required formal approval, and how adaptive practices would coexist with organizational governance. This proactive tailoring would likely have prevented the conflict.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Assigning a dedicated governance compliance officer to monitor the team's adherence to structured governance rules focuses on enforcement rather than on resolving the underlying mismatch between governance expectations and the team's operating model. Adding oversight may increase bureaucracy, and it does not address the root cause: the lack of agreement on the team's level of autonomy.

domande.spiegazione: Agile or adaptive projects are designed to be self-governing, meaning that the teams involved have the autonomy to make decisions and manage their work without heavy bureaucracy and oversight. The issue is not that the team wants self-governance. The issue is that governance expectations were never aligned. The project manager should have worked with the steering committee early in the project to define which decisions the team could make independently, which changes required formal approval, and how adaptive practices would coexist with organizational governance. This proactive tailoring would likely have prevented the conflict.

domande.domanda:
Case study I
A large financial services organization has initiated a project to replace its legacy Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system with a new cloud-based platform. The project has an approved budget of $12 million and a planned duration of 18 months. The project sponsor and the Project Management Office (PMO) have assigned a project manager to lead the effort.
The organization has an executive steering committee that oversees all projects exceeding $5 million. The steering committee includes the chief information officer, the chief financial officer, and the head of business operations. The PMO has established standard templates and phase-gate review processes for all major projects.
During the project initiation, the project manager develops the project charter in collaboration with the sponsor. The charter is approved, and the project manager is granted authority to allocate organizational resources.
Question 3 (Case Study I)
A technical risk involving data migration has materialized into an issue. The project manager attempted to escalate to the steering committee but was told that operational risks should first go to a lower-level working group that does not yet exist.
What should the project manager do next?

opzioni.A: Record the issue in the issue log, implement a workaround, and defer formal escalation until the next steering committee meeting.
opzioni.B: Halt project work until the necessary escalation paths are established to prevent a recurrence of the same issue.
opzioni.C: Escalate the issue to the steering committee with an impact analysis, noting the absence of a working group as a governance gap requiring resolution.
opzioni.D: Update the risk register without escalating, since operational issues are outside the steering committee's purview.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Deferring escalation may unnecessarily increase the issue's impact. The project manager should not wait for the next meeting when the established escalation path is unavailable.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Halting project work until the necessary escalation paths are set is an extreme response. Governance gaps should be addressed, but stopping project work is rarely justified unless there is a significant safety, legal, or compliance concern.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. The project manager has already discovered that the prescribed escalation path does not exist. That is a governance issue in itself. The project manager should not allow a materialized issue to remain unresolved simply because the organization has not established the required working group. By escalating with an impact analysis, the project manager ensures decision-makers understand the issue's impact, highlights the governance gap, and seeks resolution from the appropriate authority.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The risk has already occurred and is now an issue, so it belongs in the issue management process rather than being treated solely as a risk. Additionally, the steering committee needs to address the governance gap preventing proper escalation.

domande.spiegazione: The project manager has already discovered that the prescribed escalation path does not exist. That is a governance issue in itself. The project manager should not allow a materialized issue to remain unresolved simply because the organization has not established the required working group. By escalating with an impact analysis, the project manager ensures decision-makers understand the issue's impact, highlights the governance gap, and seeks resolution from the appropriate authority.

domande.domanda:
Case study I
A large financial services organization has initiated a project to replace its legacy Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system with a new cloud-based platform. The project has an approved budget of $12 million and a planned duration of 18 months. The project sponsor and the Project Management Office (PMO) have assigned a project manager to lead the effort.
The organization has an executive steering committee that oversees all projects exceeding $5 million. The steering committee includes the chief information officer, the chief financial officer, and the head of business operations. The PMO has established standard templates and phase-gate review processes for all major projects.
During the project initiation, the project manager develops the project charter in collaboration with the sponsor. The charter is approved, and the project manager is granted authority to allocate organizational resources.
Question 4 (Case Study I)
The PMO requires weekly status reports, biweekly change-request reviews, and monthly steering committee presentations. The project manager estimates that governance activities consume nearly 20% of the team's capacity, delaying actual delivery work.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Accept the PMO requirements as mandatory organizational process assets and continue without changes.
opzioni.B: Request that the PMO tailor the governance requirements for this specific project.
opzioni.C: Limit governance activities, except for the monthly steering committee presentation, to reduce overhead.
opzioni.D: Hire additional project administrative staff to handle governance reporting so the team can focus on delivery.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Accepting excessive governance requirements without tailoring contradicts the principle of value-driven project management.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. According to PMBOK 8th Edition, page 104: "Too few processes can lead to ineffective project management, while employing more processes than required is costly and wasteful. Thus, tailoring leads to optimum and effective project management that can deliver direct and indirect value to organizations." Project governance should be tailored to the context in which the project operates. This includes tailoring reporting frequency, approval thresholds, and governance intensity based on project risk profile, scale, and development approach.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Too much governance risks wasting resources, while too little may lead to issues with strategic alignment and project performance. Eliminating all governance activities except one monthly meeting removes essential monitoring and control mechanisms, increasing project risk.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Tailoring is about adapting processes to be more efficient, not adding resources to accommodate inefficient processes. Adding administrative staff increases project cost without addressing the root cause (excessive, untailored governance requirements).

domande.spiegazione: According to PMBOK 8th Edition, page 104: "Too few processes can lead to ineffective project management, while employing more processes than required is costly and wasteful. Thus, tailoring leads to optimum and effective project management that can deliver direct and indirect value to organizations." Project governance should be tailored to the context in which the project operates. This includes tailoring reporting frequency, approval thresholds, and governance intensity based on project risk profile, scale, and development approach.

domande.domanda:
A mobile banking project is in its sixth two-week sprint. During the sprint review, the product owner rejects a new "transaction search" feature because search results take 6–8 seconds (acceptance criteria required 3 seconds), and the merchant name search uses internal payee codes instead of customer statement names.
What should the project manager do first?

opzioni.A: Document the rejection in the issue log.
opzioni.B: Facilitate a root cause analysis to understand why the acceptance criteria were misinterpreted.
opzioni.C: Rework the feature to meet both acceptance criteria.
opzioni.D: Add two new user stories to the next sprint’s backlog for merchant name correction and query optimization.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Documenting the rejection may be appropriate later, but it does not address the immediate problem. The primary concern is understanding why the team delivered functionality that did not meet the agreed acceptance criteria. Simply recording the issue does not help the team learn or improve.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Before any corrective action can be taken, the project manager must understand why the gap occurred: whether due to unclear acceptance criteria, technical constraints, unvalidated assumptions, or stakeholder expectations not properly communicated. Facilitating root cause analysis with both parties ensures the response addresses the actual cause, not just the symptom.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The feature will likely require rework, but this is not the first step. Immediate rework without analysis is reactive. Reworking without root cause analysis risks repeating the same errors.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Creating additional backlog items may ultimately be part of the solution, but it assumes the team already knows how to address the problem. Before adding new work, the team should understand why the acceptance criteria were not met, whether the feature should be corrected through rework, as a defect, a technical improvement, or as a new backlog item, and whether there are broader process issues affecting the understanding of requirements.

domande.spiegazione: Before any corrective action can be taken, the project manager must understand why the gap occurred: whether due to unclear acceptance criteria, technical constraints, unvalidated assumptions, or stakeholder expectations not properly communicated. Facilitating root cause analysis with both parties ensures the response addresses the actual cause, not just the symptom.

domande.domanda:
A project manager oversees an agile project for developing a mobile application for a fast-paced startup. The project involves a cross-functional team comprising developers, designers, and testers. As the project progresses, the project manager encounters various challenges, including technological complexities, stakeholder communication gaps, and collaboration issues.
What should be the project manager’s primary focus to ensure the team remains aligned with agile principles?

opzioni.A: Ensuring the team delivers new features as frequently as possible.
opzioni.B: Establishing accurate and detailed plans to guide the team's work and minimize communication and quality issues.
opzioni.C: Implementing rigorous quality control measures to ensure the application meets the highest standards of performance and usability.
opzioni.D: Prioritizing the delivery of features that directly contribute to the client's goals and provide tangible value to end-users.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Delivering features frequently enables rapid feedback and adaptation, which is indeed crucial in agile projects. However, the agile team should primarily focus on delivering value with each new feature rather than solely on delivery frequency.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Creating detailed, accurate plans is common in predictive projects, not in agile projects.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Implementing quality control measures does not directly address the mentioned challenges. Besides, agile calls for progressive elaboration and continuous improvements; the first of the agile 12 principles states: “Our highest priority is to satisfy the customer through the early and continuous delivery of valuable software.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Delivering value should always be the agile team’s top priority, as it represents one of the agile manifesto principles: “working software over comprehensive documentation”. From the client’s perspective, value represents the benefit derived from using a product or a service.

domande.spiegazione: Delivering value should always be the agile team’s top priority, as it represents one of the agile manifesto principles: “working software over comprehensive documentation”. From the client’s perspective, value represents the benefit derived from using a product or a service.

domande.domanda:
An organization hires an external agile coach as part of its transformation project. In the final report, the agile coach notes that measures should be taken to enable agile teams to be cross-functional.
How should the organization proceed with the agile coach recommendation?

opzioni.A: Allow individuals to collectively determine the best way to achieve the sprint's goal.
opzioni.B: Allow individuals to take part in guiding the product direction.
opzioni.C: Assign individuals who possess the necessary skills to produce a functioning product.
opzioni.D: Empower individuals to approve the potentially shippable product increment.

domande.spiegazione:
A cross-functional team must possess the competencies needed to independently create a product or service, without relying on members outside the team.
Option A: A self-organizing team is one in which individuals collectively determine the best way to accomplish the sprint goal.
Options B & D: The product owner is mainly responsible for guiding the product direction and approving the potentially shippable product increment.

domande.domanda:
To promote adaptability and minimize disruptions, a project manager decides to adopt an Agile development approach that allows the project team to work in a continuous flow rather than using iteration-based cycles.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Implement daily stand-up meetings to enhance communication and collaboration.
opzioni.B: Encourage self-organization and decision-making within the team.
opzioni.C: Break down project deliverables into smaller, manageable increments.
opzioni.D: Use a Kanban framework to optimize workflow and identify bottlenecks.

domande.spiegazione: The Kanban method involves pulling work into the system only when the team is capable of handling it. The Kanban method prioritizes productivity and efficiency through its workflow approach. The Kanban Method is less prescriptive than some agile approaches and less disruptive. A Kanban board helps the team further improve its effectiveness by visualizing the flow of work and making impediments easily visible (Agile Practice Guide, pages 13 & 31).

domande.domanda:
A project manager is leading a software development project using an agile framework. In the current iteration, the team encounters a technical challenge related to integrating a third-party API into the system. To address this challenge, the team decided to allocate time for a spike to look into the issue.
Based on the iteration burndown chart below, during which period of the iteration did the team take the spike?
⚠️ Nell'esportazione Udemy manca l'immagine (grafico/tabella) a cui fa riferimento la domanda.

opzioni.A: A
opzioni.B: B
opzioni.C: C
opzioni.D: D

domande.spiegazione: A spike is a time-boxed activity aimed at addressing a technical challenge or mitigating risks. Spikes usually result in a temporary slowdown or pause in the team's velocity as they allocate time for research or exploration. Analyzing the provided burndown chart, you can observe slow progress at the beginning of the iteration, a brief pause from Day 2 to Day 4, and a resumption of the downward trend. This deviation indicates the time allocated for the spike to address the technical challenge.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is leading the development of a new software project. The project manager wants to adopt an approach that produces key deliverables at various stages of the project.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Create a detailed project schedule with key milestones to track progress against the plan.
opzioni.B: Deliver incremental results that can be added to the subsequent results.
opzioni.C: Organize frequent review meetings with project stakeholders to gather feedback and adjust project direction.
opzioni.D: Adopt an iterative approach in order to deliver the highest business value earlier.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Creating a detailed project schedule with key milestones means adopting a predictive approach and only delivering at the end of the project.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Delivering partial results at various intervals refers to the incremental approach. In this type of development approach, the project is divided into increments delivered sequentially, avoiding the need to wait until everything is complete to create a solution.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Organizing review meetings to gather feedback and adjust project direction is a main aspect of the iterative approach. The iterative approach focuses on correctness. It typically includes multiple essays and one acceptable deliverable at the end of the project.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Delivering the highest business value earlier is the aspect of the incremental approach, not the iterative approach. The incremental approach focuses on speed, while the iterative approach focuses on correctness.

domande.spiegazione: Delivering partial results at various intervals refers to the incremental approach. In this type of development approach, the project is divided into increments delivered sequentially, avoiding the need to wait until everything is complete to create a solution.

domande.domanda:
By the end of the third iteration, the project manager delivered the website to the customer and signed a maintenance contract to fix any issues that might occur. On the first day of the maintenance contract period, the customer reported an error on the contact page when using a smartphone. After verifying the issue with the project team, the project manager realized that testing the contact feature on mobile devices had been omitted.
What should the project manager do next?

opzioni.A: Reopen the project and fix the error since testing the contact feature on mobile was omitted.
opzioni.B: Ask the sponsor to submit a formal change request with an earlier date so it can be considered part of the project.
opzioni.C: Request from the project team to fix the issue according to the maintenance contract.
opzioni.D: Do nothing since the error was discovered after the formal closure of the project.

domande.spiegazione: An escaped defect is one that was not detected by the project team but rather discovered by the customer or end-user after the product is released. These defects are usually covered by a maintenance contract. Therefore, the project manager should request that the project team fix the issue in accordance with the maintenance contract.

domande.domanda:
The following chart was presented during a retrospective meeting.
Which of the following statements is true regarding this chart?
⚠️ Nell'esportazione Udemy manca l'immagine (grafico/tabella) a cui fa riferimento la domanda.

opzioni.A: This burnup chart shows that there is work left at the end of the sprint
opzioni.B: This burnup chart shows that the planned work is completed before the end of the sprint
opzioni.C: This burndown chart shows that there is work left at the end of the sprint
opzioni.D: This burndown chart shows that the planned work is completed before the end of the sprint

domande.spiegazione: This burndown chart shows that there is work left at the end of the sprint. In fact, 3 story points remain to be completed to finalize all planned work for the exhibited 7-day sprint.

domande.domanda: A project manager works on a software project. During the last retrospective meeting, several topics were discussed. Which of the following topics can be discussed in such a meeting?

opzioni.A: How to decompose a complex user story into manageable tasks
opzioni.B: Which user stories should be prioritized in the next sprint
opzioni.C: How to fix the regression of a product feature
opzioni.D: Whether the standup timing is suitable for all team members

domande.spiegazione:
During the sprint retrospective, the project manager should identify what went well and what can be improved in the next sprint. A possible topic is the timing of the standup. If team members are showing dissatisfaction with the current schedule, then the retrospective meeting is the right event to discuss the issue.
Options A & B: The sprint planning meeting is the right meeting for discussing which tasks should be prioritized in the next sprint and how to decompose user stories into manageable tasks.
Option C: Dedicated project team meetings and Backlog refinement meetings should address product development topics, including ways to fix regressions.

domande.domanda:
This is the first time the project manager has adopted the Scrum framework for the project execution. One of the team members asks the project manager when a Sprint is considered completed.
What should be the project manager’s response?

opzioni.A: When all product backlog items are completed.
opzioni.B: When all the tasks in the sprint are completed.
opzioni.C: When the sprint’s defined timebox ends.
opzioni.D: When all product backlog items meet the Definition of Done (DoD).

domande.spiegazione:
A sprint is considered complete only when it reaches the end of its duration/timebox, which is usually 1 to 4 weeks.
Option B: In some cases, the sprint ends without finishing all of the assigned tasks, so this can’t be the criterion for sprint completion.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is facing challenges due to a key stakeholder. The project manager collaborated with this stakeholder on previous projects, during which the latter frequently changed requirements and caused trouble when those requirements were not met.
How should the project manager deal with this issue?

opzioni.A: Adopt an Agile approach
opzioni.B: Involve the concerned stakeholder right from the start
opzioni.C: Ask the concerned stakeholder to mend their ways
opzioni.D: Inform management about the issue

domande.spiegazione:
The project manager should involve the key stakeholder from the very beginning of the project to help reduce and uncover risks, as well as increase their “buy-in.”
Option A: While implementing an agile approach may benefit the project, it does not address stakeholder management. If the question were “What’s the appropriate approach for the project?”, adopting an agile approach would be the right answer, given the frequently changing requirements.

domande.domanda:
In a mid-sized technology company, the executive leadership has recognized the need to adapt to changing market dynamics and improve project delivery efficiency. As a result, they have initiated a company-wide transformation to adopt Agile methodologies. The project manager, assigned to lead this transformation, faces several challenges in facilitating the organization's shift to Agile practices; employees have varying levels of experience with the Agile approach, so there is resistance to change from some stakeholders who are accustomed to traditional project management approaches and are skeptical about the benefits of Agile. Additionally, the company operates in a highly regulated industry with stringent compliance requirements, which must be addressed during the Agile transformation process.
What should the project manager do next? (Select two)

opzioni.A: Dismiss reservations and skepticism about this transformation since resistance to big changes is natural.
opzioni.B: Establish a cross-functional Agile transformation team comprising representatives from different departments to ensure alignment, collaboration, and inclusivity throughout the transformation process.
opzioni.C: Conduct a comprehensive organizational assessment to evaluate the organization’s suitability for adopting the Agile approach.
opzioni.D: Develop a tailored Agile training program to address the diverse needs and skill levels of employees.

domande.spiegazione:
Establishing a cross-functional Agile transformation team comprising representatives from different departments to ensure alignment, collaboration, and inclusivity throughout the transformation journey empowers employees to drive change initiatives and address specific challenges unique to their respective areas. It also recognizes the importance of collaboration and inclusivity in driving organizational change and encourages employees to take ownership of the Agile transformation process, leading to more sustainable and successful outcomes.
Developing a tailored Agile training program is essential for addressing the diverse needs and skill levels of employees. By offering customized training sessions and ongoing support, the project manager can ensure that all employees receive the necessary knowledge and guidance to embrace Agile practices effectively.
Option A: Ignoring feedback and concerns from employees and stakeholders who express reservations or skepticism about the Agile transformation, and dismissing their input as resistance to change, may lead to disengagement and morale issues among team members, hindering collaboration and cooperation in the Agile transformation process.
Option C: An organizational assessment to evaluate the organization’s suitability for adopting the Agile approach might have already been completed, since the decision to transform to Agile had already been made.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is leading a rebranding project using a predictive approach for the planning phase and an Agile approach for work execution. The project manager receives an email from a key stakeholder requesting an estimation of the project completion date. To estimate the completion date, the project manager considers the team’s average velocity (20 story points) and that the project still has 205 remaining user story points to complete.
How many iterations will it take to complete the project?

opzioni.A: 10 iterations
opzioni.B: 11 iterations
opzioni.C: 12 iterations
opzioni.D: Cannot be determined

domande.spiegazione: If the team maintains an average velocity of 20 story points per iteration, it would take 11 iterations to complete the remaining 205 story points. (205 story points / 20 story points = 10.25 iterations). Since the timebox for an iteration should not be changed, the project team will need 11 iterations to complete the remaining work.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is managing a software development project. To ensure the project’s agile team is cross-functional, the project manager hires an experienced designer. A few days later, the designer informs the project manager that he’s unable to do his work properly because the subscription plan for the design application he’s using doesn’t include all the features he needs. Therefore, the designer requests an upgrade to the subscription plan.
What should the project manager do next?

opzioni.A: Ask the designer to raise the issue during the next retrospective meeting
opzioni.B: Tell the designer to be self-reliant by dealing with the situation and finding turnarounds
opzioni.C: Explain to the designer that his current subscription plan is sufficient for fulfilling his assigned tasks
opzioni.D: Reach out to the appropriate stakeholder to upgrade the designer’s subscription plan

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Retrospective meetings are set up to improve processes and not to remove impediments.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. In an agile work environment, the project manager should listen to the impediments their team members face and act to resolve them. If the designer’s subscription plan cannot be upgraded, the project manager should explain this and ask the designer to explore alternatives, such as using complementary applications that provide the functionality he needs to perform his work.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Agile teams are self-organized, i.e., they decide how they should perform their work. Thus, forcing the designer to use a limited subscription plan is inappropriate. Furthermore, since the designer is experienced, he can clearly identify his needs; therefore, the Scrum master or project manager should cater to the designer’s job requirements rather than argue with the designer.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. As a servant leader, the project manager should reach out to the appropriate stakeholder in order to upgrade the designer’s subscription plan.

domande.spiegazione: As a servant leader, the project manager should reach out to the appropriate stakeholder in order to upgrade the designer’s subscription plan.

domande.domanda:
During sprint planning for an e-commerce platform project, the Agile team decomposed a user story focused on improving the checkout process into 4 tasks. While implementing the story, a developer discovered an additional technical task required to complete the functionality.
What should the team member do?

opzioni.A: Update the user story and work on the new task
opzioni.B: Report the issue to the Scrum Master
opzioni.C: Ask the product owner to approve the new task
opzioni.D: Add the task to the product backlog

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. In Agile, the sprint backlog is emergent, and the team can modify tasks to achieve the sprint goal. The team owns the sprint backlog and the tasks needed to deliver the committed user stories. Implementation-level tasks are a team responsibility; adding or adjusting tasks to complete a story is normal and expected. The practical next steps the team member should take: Add the task to the sprint backlog, estimate the required effort, raise the discovery in the daily stand-up so the team is aware and can re-plan or reassign work, and track the change on the burndown chart and monitor impact on the sprint goal. If the new task threatens the sprint goal, the team member can inform the Product Owner so that the scope or priorities can be renegotiated.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The situation doesn’t involve any issue. The team member can add, adjust, or remove tasks in order to deliver the user story according to its acceptance criteria.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The new task doesn’t require the product owner's approval since it’s a technical component of an agreed-upon user story.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. If the task represents a new feature or doesn’t contribute to validating the user story, it should be added to the product backlog. In the described scenario, however, the task is an integral part of the user story.

domande.spiegazione: In Agile, the sprint backlog is emergent, and the team can modify tasks to achieve the sprint goal. The team owns the sprint backlog and the tasks needed to deliver the committed user stories. Implementation-level tasks are a team responsibility; adding or adjusting tasks to complete a story is normal and expected. The practical next steps the team member should take: Add the task to the sprint backlog, estimate the required effort, raise the discovery in the daily stand-up so the team is aware and can re-plan or reassign work, and track the change on the burndown chart and monitor impact on the sprint goal. If the new task threatens the sprint goal, the team member can inform the Product Owner so that the scope or priorities can be renegotiated.

domande.domanda:
At a trade show, a prospect stops at the stand of a company that specializes in selling and installing network security appliances. The prospect asks the representative if their company can provide and set up 10 firewall hardware devices in 5 weeks, recommending an incremental approach to deliver 2 firewalls per week. The prospect adds that an external security expert will conduct a penetration test and that final acceptance will be granted only after all cyberattacks are detected and prevented.
What is the prospect defining in the above scenario? (Select two)

opzioni.A: The required delivery schedule and penetration testing as the Definition of Done.
opzioni.B: The testing requirements as part of the Quality Assurance process.
opzioni.C: The firewall performance and testing expectations as part of the technical requirements.
opzioni.D: The testing requirements as part of the Quality Control process.

domande.spiegazione:
A Definition of Done (DoD) is a checklist of the required criteria for considering a product ready for delivery (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 39). In this scenario, the prospect specifies completion conditions: Delivery schedule (2 firewalls per week) and final acceptance after penetration testing confirms that all simulated attacks are detected and prevented. These statements define what “done” means from the customer’s perspective: clear, measurable acceptance criteria that the project team must meet before a deliverable is considered finished. Therefore, the prospect is directly outlining the Definition of Done.
Quality Control involves monitoring and verifying that deliverables meet the specified requirements and acceptance criteria (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 23). The prospect mentions that an external security expert will conduct a penetration test and that final acceptance depends on the successful detection and prevention of all attacks. This testing and validation activity is a Quality Control process that confirms the product works as intended through inspection, testing, and verification before acceptance.
Option B: Quality Assurance (QA) focuses on process-oriented actions, ensuring that proper methods, procedures, and standards are followed to produce quality outcomes (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 23). In this scenario, the prospect does not describe preventive or process-oriented activities such as documentation, configuration standards, or testing protocols. Instead, the description focuses on verifying outputs rather than controlling or auditing the process, which falls under Quality Control, not Quality Assurance.
Option C: Technical requirements specify functional and nonfunctional product requirements, such as WiFi support, storage, number of LANs, etc. The scenario does not detail these technical characteristics; rather, it defines how and when deliverables will be delivered and tested for acceptance.

domande.domanda:
A project is underway to develop a new claims processing system for a regional insurance cooperative. The system will serve six regional offices, each representing different market sizes and member demographics. Four smaller regional offices have raised concerns that the project team consistently prioritizes features requested by the two largest offices, leaving the specific regulatory and operational needs of the smaller offices underrepresented. The cooperative's operations director has proposed that the team dedicate a fixed 30% of each sprint's capacity to features requested by smaller offices.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Accept the operations director's proposal and commit to reserving 30% of each sprint's capacity for backlog items originating from the four smaller regional offices.
opzioni.B: Reject the fixed-capacity proposal and instead facilitate a prioritization workshop with representatives from all six regional offices.
opzioni.C: Analyze the backlog to identify which features are truly essential for the smaller offices to meet their regulatory obligations, and prioritize those items regardless of the 30% target.
opzioni.D: Propose a compromise where the team reserves 30% of capacity for smaller office items on a trial basis for three sprints, with a review to assess whether the allocation is delivering value.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Accepting the operations director's proposal creates an arbitrary allocation rule that may not align with business value or project objectives. Reserving a percentage of sprint capacity could result in lower-priority work being selected simply because it originates from a particular group. While the proposal attempts to address perceived fairness, it may reduce the team's ability to maximize value delivery.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Agile teams should prioritize work based on value, risk, stakeholder needs, and business objectives, rather than predetermined allocations of development capacity. In this scenario, the concern is not simply that smaller offices are receiving fewer features. The underlying issue is that stakeholders perceive the prioritization process as unfair or unbalanced. Before changing capacity allocations, the project manager should facilitate collaboration among stakeholders to establish a shared understanding of priorities and ensure all voices are heard. A prioritization workshop allows representatives from all six offices to openly discuss competing needs, clarify regulatory and operational requirements, evaluate business value and urgency, build consensus on backlog priorities, and improve stakeholder engagement and transparency.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Analyzing the backlog to identify which features are truly essential for the smaller offices to meet their regulatory obligations places the project manager in the role of determining priorities. In Agile environments, backlog prioritization should involve the Product Owner and relevant stakeholders rather than being driven solely by the project manager's analysis.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Proposing a compromise in which the team reserves 30% of capacity for smaller office items on a trial basis for three sprints relies on an arbitrary allocation of capacity. Even as a trial, the proposal assumes that fairness is best achieved through quotas rather than collaborative prioritization. Agile teams should continuously prioritize based on value and stakeholder needs, rather than on predetermined percentages.

domande.spiegazione: Agile teams should prioritize work based on value, risk, stakeholder needs, and business objectives, rather than predetermined allocations of development capacity. In this scenario, the concern is not simply that smaller offices are receiving fewer features. The underlying issue is that stakeholders perceive the prioritization process as unfair or unbalanced. Before changing capacity allocations, the project manager should facilitate collaboration among stakeholders to establish a shared understanding of priorities and ensure all voices are heard. A prioritization workshop allows representatives from all six offices to openly discuss competing needs, clarify regulatory and operational requirements, evaluate business value and urgency, build consensus on backlog priorities, and improve stakeholder engagement and transparency.

domande.domanda:
An Agile project manager is leading a software development project. The product is designed to process sensitive customer data and must comply with strict data privacy regulations by launch date. Midway through development, the compliance officer reminds the team that these regulatory requirements have not yet been addressed. The development team informs the compliance officer that they plan to complete all compliance tasks in a final sprint at the end of the release.
What should the Agile project manager do?

opzioni.A: Add a final sprint at the end of the release schedule to handle all regulatory tasks.
opzioni.B: Ask the compliance officer to submit a change request for review during the next sprint planning session.
opzioni.C: Track compliance risks separately and monitor them until development is complete.
opzioni.D: Work with the product owner to integrate regulatory compliance work into the product backlog and deliver it incrementally.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Adding a final compliance sprint at the end of development increases the risk of delays, missed deadlines, and last-minute defects. If compliance is not built into the product early on, it may require major rework, undermining the value of iterative delivery. This approach also fails to meet regulatory expectations, which often require ongoing validation.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. While involving the compliance officer is important, submitting a change request is inaccurate, as this is an agile project, not a predictive one.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Tracking compliance risks without taking action is passive risk management. It fails to address the root issue; compliance must be proactively embedded in the product. Simply monitoring risks without integrating them into the development process does not ensure compliance or effectively mitigate risk.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Working with the product owner to integrate regulatory compliance into the product backlog and deliver it incrementally ensures that compliance is built in, not bolted on. By breaking down compliance tasks into user stories and delivering them in each sprint, the team can continuously validate compliance, reduce technical debt, meet audit and regulatory standards, and avoid last-minute surprises. This approach supports the Agile principle of Built-in quality, in which quality is integrated into every stage of the development process rather than being an afterthought.

domande.spiegazione: Working with the product owner to integrate regulatory compliance into the product backlog and deliver it incrementally ensures that compliance is built in, not bolted on. By breaking down compliance tasks into user stories and delivering them in each sprint, the team can continuously validate compliance, reduce technical debt, meet audit and regulatory standards, and avoid last-minute surprises. This approach supports the Agile principle of Built-in quality, in which quality is integrated into every stage of the development process rather than being an afterthought.

domande.domanda:
While reviewing iteration performance data, a project manager notices that one developer consistently delivers fewer story points per iteration than other team members. This developer tends to select the most complex, high-risk tasks and consistently produces work with zero defects. The other team members complete simpler, lower-risk tasks with higher point counts.
What should the project manager do first?

opzioni.A: Reassign the developer to simpler tasks to increase their story point velocity and improve team metrics.
opzioni.B: Review the story point estimation process for complex tasks.
opzioni.C: Coach the developer to select a balanced mix of simple and complex tasks.
opzioni.D: Replace the developer with someone who can deliver more story points to meet the iteration goal.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Reassigning the developer to simpler tasks may temporarily increase velocity but would deprive the project of the developer's expertise on complex, critical work. Assigning the most skilled developer to simple tasks while leaving complex work to others reduces the project's overall value. This treats the metric (story points) as the goal rather than value delivery.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. When a developer consistently handles the most complex work yet shows low output in points, the likely explanation is that those tasks were underestimated during planning. Estimation accuracy depends on the quality of input data and assumptions. The project manager should first investigate the estimation process itself to determine whether it underestimated complex tasks and story points relative to their actual effort and risk, before drawing conclusions about individual performance.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Coaching the developer to select a mix of tasks assumes the issue is the developer's task selection. However, the developer is deliberately choosing complex tasks. Plus, Agile teams are typically self-managing: the project manager (or Scrum Master) should be cautious about directing individuals on which tasks to select unless there is a demonstrated team problem, which is not the case here.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Replacing the developer is an extreme, punitive response. Building an Empowered Culture emphasizes developing team members rather than replacing them at the first sign of performance variance. There is no indication that the developer is incompetent; they are delivering zero-defect, complex work.

domande.spiegazione: When a developer consistently handles the most complex work yet shows low output in points, the likely explanation is that those tasks were underestimated during planning. Estimation accuracy depends on the quality of input data and assumptions. The project manager should first investigate the estimation process itself to determine whether it underestimated complex tasks and story points relative to their actual effort and risk, before drawing conclusions about individual performance.

domande.domanda:
Over the last three iterations, a project manager observes that testing time has progressively increased, consuming a growing share of each iteration. The team has already implemented basic test automation, but testing still takes 40% of the iteration capacity, up from 20% three iterations ago. The increased testing effort is threatening the team's ability to meet iteration goals.
What should the project manager do first?

opzioni.A: Increase the frequency and depth of backlog refinement to improve the clarity and testability of stories.
opzioni.B: Implement additional test automation tools to accelerate test execution for upcoming iterations.
opzioni.C: Dedicate an entire iteration to testing to eliminate the accumulated test backlog.
opzioni.D: Introduce pair testing to distribute the testing workload among more team members.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Poorly defined requirements lead to downstream issues. When testing time progressively increases, it typically signals that stories are entering sprints poorly defined, with unclear acceptance criteria or insufficient detail. Backlog refinement supports the continuous review and elaboration of backlog items to ensure they are well understood and testable before sprint planning. Strengthening backlog refinement addresses the root cause by reducing downstream testing complexity and rework.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Implementing additional test automation tools may seem like a logical solution, but the team already has basic automation in place. Adding more tools without addressing why testing requirements are increasing treats the symptom, not the root cause.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Dedicating an entire iteration to testing may temporarily reduce the backlog, but it does not prevent the backlog from accumulating again. This option is reactive and does not address why testing time has increased.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Pair testing distributes workload but does not reduce the total testing effort required. If stories are poorly defined, they will still require extensive testing regardless of how many people perform them.

domande.spiegazione: Poorly defined requirements lead to downstream issues. When testing time progressively increases, it typically signals that stories are entering sprints poorly defined, with unclear acceptance criteria or insufficient detail. Backlog refinement supports the continuous review and elaboration of backlog items to ensure they are well understood and testable before sprint planning. Strengthening backlog refinement addresses the root cause by reducing downstream testing complexity and rework.

domande.domanda:
After three iterations of progressively increasing test duration, a project manager facilitated intensive backlog refinement sessions to address the issue of poorly defined stories with unclear acceptance criteria. The team is now completing the third iteration since the intervention. The project manager needs to determine whether the actions taken were effective and whether the intervention successfully reduced testing time.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Check the business value delivered per story to confirm that higher-value stories are being prioritized.
opzioni.B: Assess the time required to resolve iteration impediments, to confirm that blockers are being addressed faster.
opzioni.C: Check the number of stories completed per iteration, comparing the three iterations before the intervention to the three iterations after.
opzioni.D: Check the total number of items remaining in the backlog to confirm that the backlog is not growing.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Checking the business value delivered per story does not measure whether the intervention was successful. The problem being addressed was the increasing testing duration caused by unclear requirements. Prioritizing higher-value stories does not indicate whether backlog refinement improved story quality or reduced testing delays. This metric measures prioritization effectiveness rather than the effectiveness of the intervention.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Assessing the time required to resolve iteration impediments relates to impediment management, not backlog refinement quality. The intervention targeted unclear acceptance criteria and poorly defined stories. While impediments can affect delivery performance, the scenario provides no indication that blockers were the primary cause of the testing problem. The project manager should measure outcomes directly related to the issue that prompted the intervention.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. When a team implements a process improvement, the project manager should evaluate whether the intervention produced the intended outcome by examining relevant performance metrics before and after the change. If the refinement sessions were effective, stories should now be better understood before development begins, reducing rework, clarification discussions, and testing delays. One indicator of improved flow and efficiency would be an increase in the number of stories completed per iteration when compared with the period before the intervention. The project manager should therefore compare performance before and after the change to determine whether the intervention improved delivery outcomes.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Backlog size is not a reliable measure of intervention effectiveness. The backlog may grow or shrink for many reasons, including the addition of new requirements, changes in business priorities, stakeholder requests, and product roadmap updates. A stable or shrinking backlog does not necessarily indicate that testing duration has improved or that story refinement has been more effective.

domande.spiegazione: When a team implements a process improvement, the project manager should evaluate whether the intervention produced the intended outcome by examining relevant performance metrics before and after the change. If the refinement sessions were effective, stories should now be better understood before development begins, reducing rework, clarification discussions, and testing delays. One indicator of improved flow and efficiency would be an increase in the number of stories completed per iteration when compared with the period before the intervention. The project manager should therefore compare performance before and after the change to determine whether the intervention improved delivery outcomes.

domande.domanda:
Halfway through the current iteration, the progress report reveals that the agile project is off track. The project manager didn’t expect that since he carefully sequenced and assigned all project work to meet the iteration goal.
What should the project manager have done differently to avoid this issue?

opzioni.A: Train the team on how to implement the agile approach
opzioni.B: Encourage the team to record their progress using the reporting system
opzioni.C: Set up a contingency reserve
opzioni.D: Encourage the team to self-organize to ensure their buy-in

domande.spiegazione: Since he’s leading an agile project, the project manager should have empowered his team to be self-organized through handling iteration tasks selection and prioritization, rather than solely taking care of work sequencing and assignment. This ensures a high level of buy-in from the team. Encouraging the team to self-organize typically results in a highly motivated staff, as it allows them to exercise autonomy in choosing the most efficient way to accomplish their work.

domande.domanda:
A product owner sends a document including all the product backlog items to the project manager. The project manager informs the product owner that these product backlog items should be prioritized throughout the project.
What should the project manager recommend?

opzioni.A: The business analyst and project manager collaborate to define the priorities of the product backlog items.
opzioni.B: The team prioritized the product backlog items by size: smaller items at the top and larger items at the bottom.
opzioni.C: The product owner places the most valuable items at the top.
opzioni.D: The sponsor decides the priority of product backlog items based on the need.

domande.spiegazione: Ordering Product Backlog items is one of the Product Owner’s responsibilities, though they may delegate it to others. Regardless, the Product Owner remains accountable. The most valuable product backlog items should be placed at the top.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is leading a software development team to build a new e-commerce platform for a client. While selecting the appropriate development approach for this project, the project manager wants to ensure he’s choosing one that allows him to define the interactions the client wishes to perform and break them down into smaller workpieces for development.
Which development approach should the project manager choose?

opzioni.A: Behavior-Driven Development (BDD)
opzioni.B: Test-Driven Development (TDD)
opzioni.C: Feature-Driven Development (FDD)
opzioni.D: Continuous Integration

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Behavior-Driven Development (BDD) entails employing scenarios and specifications to drive the creation of automated tests.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Test-Driven Development (TDD) involves writing tests before writing code, then refactoring the code to improve it.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Feature-Driven Development (FDD) consists of defining the interactions the client wishes to perform and breaking them down into smaller pieces of work for development.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Continuous Integration involves frequently integrating work into the whole and then retesting to ensure everything still works as intended.

domande.spiegazione: Feature-Driven Development (FDD) consists of defining the interactions the client wishes to perform and breaking them down into smaller pieces of work for development.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is assigned to an Agile software development project. The project is almost complete when the client requests an additional feature not included in the initial requirements. The project is already nearing its budget limit, and accommodating the new requirement would require new funds.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Immediately incorporate the new requirement since agile prioritizes customer satisfaction and flexibility.
opzioni.B: Negotiate with the client to prioritize the new requirement against other features and functionalities.
opzioni.C: Decline the client's request for the new requirement due to budget constraints.
opzioni.D: Escalate the request to the CCB for a decision on whether to prioritize it.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The project manager should not immediately incorporate the new requirement, taking into consideration the impact and implementation requirements of the new feature.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. The project manager should negotiate with the client to prioritize the new requirement against other features and functionalities in the product backlog. Agile advocates responding to change and satisfying the client, but this should be balanced against the project's budget constraints, given that budgets are fixed in Agile projects.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The project manager should not decline the client's request for the new requirement due to budget constraints, as it will lead to client dissatisfaction, which goes against agile principles of satisfying the customer and welcoming changing requirements, even late in development (Agile Practice Guide, page 98).
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Escalating the request to the CCB is inaccurate, since the scenario involves an agile project rather than a predictive one.

domande.spiegazione: The project manager should negotiate with the client to prioritize the new requirement against other features and functionalities in the product backlog. Agile advocates responding to change and satisfying the client, but this should be balanced against the project's budget constraints, given that budgets are fixed in Agile projects.

domande.domanda:
A project manager was assigned to lead a new project. Wondering about the project completion date, the product owner asks the project manager: “How many story points do you expect to complete per sprint?”
In order to provide the product owner with an accurate response, the project manager should:

opzioni.A: Estimate the sprint velocity based on the team members’ input.
opzioni.B: Complete multiple sprints in order to be able to answer the product owner’s question.
opzioni.C: Rely on their own judgment as an experienced project manager to estimate the team's velocity.
opzioni.D: Engage the team in estimating their velocity based on their previous agile projects.

domande.spiegazione:
Typically, the project manager should rely on the team's historical velocity data to set a reasonable, achievable number of story points per sprint, based entirely on the team’s capacity and what they can accomplish.
Options A & C: When a new team has no historical data, the sprint forecast can be done based on your experience with similar projects, along with collaborative estimations from the entire team, to determine how many story points they can potentially deliver in the first sprint.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is initiating an agile software development project. In past projects, this client has frequently changed direction mid-project, leading to misunderstandings about scope, deliverables, and expectations, and to vague requirements and inconsistent communication, resulting in rework, delays, and frustration.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Break the project into sequential phases, with formal scope validation at the end of each phase.
opzioni.B: Work with the product owner to define an MVP early on the project.
opzioni.C: Establish a structured communication plan with daily check-ins and detailed reporting.
opzioni.D: Set firm delivery deadlines and milestones, and require the client to sign off before any work begins.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Breaking the project into sequential phases reflects a predictive or waterfall approach, which does not fit either this scenario or the client's behavior of frequently changing direction and providing vague requirements. Sequential phases would lock the team into rigid deliverables and make it harder to adapt to changes, leading to even more rework and dissatisfaction.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Collaborating with the product owner to define a Minimum Viable Product (MVP) directly addresses the challenge of vague requirements by focusing on delivering the smallest set of features that provides tangible business value. This helps build something concrete for the client to respond to, gather early feedback, refine requirements iteratively, and reduce rework and misalignment. This is the most effective way to anchor an ambiguous project in shared understanding.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. While improved communication is important, simply adding more check-ins and reports will not resolve the fundamental issue of vague and shifting requirements. It may increase administrative work without improving clarity or alignment.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Firm deadlines and upfront sign-offs assume that requirements are stable, which is not the case in this scenario. It would make the project inflexible, resulting in scope disputes and possibly project failure.

domande.spiegazione: Collaborating with the product owner to define a Minimum Viable Product (MVP) directly addresses the challenge of vague requirements by focusing on delivering the smallest set of features that provides tangible business value. This helps build something concrete for the client to respond to, gather early feedback, refine requirements iteratively, and reduce rework and misalignment. This is the most effective way to anchor an ambiguous project in shared understanding.

domande.domanda:
A project manager adopts an agile approach to develop credit card fraud detection software. The project team consistently struggles to complete all the user stories allocated for each sprint. Despite their efforts, they frequently fall short of achieving the sprint goals, leading to frustration and concerns about project progress.
What is the most probable reason for the project team's inability to complete all sprint backlog items?

opzioni.A: Insufficient collaboration and communication within the team, leading to misunderstandings and inefficiencies in task execution.
opzioni.B: Inadequate sprint planning, resulting in unrealistic or overly ambitious sprint goals that are challenging to achieve within the allocated time frame.
opzioni.C: Lack of the needed expertise or skills among team members, leading to delays in implementing user stories and meeting sprint objectives.
opzioni.D: External disruptions, such as changes in requirements, impacting the team's ability to deliver on time.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Collaboration and communication are indeed essential, but they may not be the primary reason for the team's inability to complete sprint story points. Even with effective collaboration, poor sprint planning can still lead to challenges in meeting sprint objectives.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Inadequate sprint planning is the most likely reason the team failed to complete all sprint story points. Unrealistic or overly ambitious sprint goals can lead to underestimation of effort and result in incomplete work by the end of the sprint.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. While a lack of technical expertise or skills could potentially contribute to delays, it is less likely to be the primary reason for consistently missing the sprint goal. Agile teams are typically cross-functional, meaning they include all the skills and expertise needed to deliver project deliverables without external dependencies.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Changing requirements during the sprint can impact the team's ability to complete the sprint backlog items. However, according to the scenario, there are no changes, and the team has consistently struggled to complete the user stories of each sprint.

domande.spiegazione: Inadequate sprint planning is the most likely reason the team failed to complete all sprint story points. Unrealistic or overly ambitious sprint goals can lead to underestimation of effort and result in incomplete work by the end of the sprint.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is leading the implementation of a Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system for a large e-commerce company. A detailed product roadmap is created, outlining the different features to be developed over the next year. As the team prepares to implement advanced customer segmentation algorithms, they are unsure what this feature's functionality is.
What should the project manager do next?

opzioni.A: Perform value stream mapping.
opzioni.B: Perform story mapping with the team.
opzioni.C: Perform sprint planning with the team.
opzioni.D: Create a use case for the feature.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Value stream mapping involves analyzing the end-to-end process of delivering value to the customer. While valuable for understanding the overall flow of value creation, it does not directly address the immediate need to understand the upcoming feature's functionality and to define user stories. Value stream mapping is more focused on process improvement rather than user story definition.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. A story map is a visual model of all the features and functionality desired for a given product, created to give the project team a holistic view of what they are building and why. Story mapping directly addresses the team's uncertainty about the upcoming feature and facilitates the creation of achievable user stories. Therefore, it's the most suitable option for guiding the team to understand and break down the feature.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Sprint planning involves selecting and prioritizing user stories from the product backlog for implementation in the upcoming sprint. Therefore, it can’t be performed until the functionality of the upcoming feature is clarified and its user stories are defined.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Creating a use case shows the scenario of interactions between the feature and the user. Use cases typically describe normal flows as well as exception flows, in which the scenario diverges from the normal flow. This technique does not address the team's described need.

domande.spiegazione: A story map is a visual model of all the features and functionality desired for a given product, created to give the project team a holistic view of what they are building and why. Story mapping directly addresses the team's uncertainty about the upcoming feature and facilitates the creation of achievable user stories. Therefore, it's the most suitable option for guiding the team to understand and break down the feature.

domande.domanda:
When reviewing the velocity chart, the project manager noticed that the team's velocity was inconsistent. While searching for the root cause, the project manager notices that one team member has a very slow performance compared to the other members, which is negatively impacting the whole team’s performance.
How should the project manager address this issue?

opzioni.A: Plan training sessions for the concerned team member
opzioni.B: Acquire a more competent resource
opzioni.C: Mentor the concerned team member
opzioni.D: Reassign the concerned team member to another project

domande.spiegazione:
When a team member’s performance is negatively affecting the project's overall progress, the project manager should intervene immediately. Mentoring can help the team member enhance their performance. It’s among the project manager’s responsibilities to serve as a guide in identifying and assisting the team members with their learning needs to ensure better productivity and performance. By offering sufficient support and attention, the team member will respond positively by working harder, which will naturally lead to better performance. A mentor should, however, continue to observe the team member’s performance and provide feedback to help them refine and improve their work.
Option A: Since training the team member would take time, mentoring them would be a more suitable option for this urgent issue.

domande.domanda:
An agile team is working on an e-commerce website project. After a slow start and many disputes, team members are starting to get along and support each other’s needs.
In which area of the Tuckman ladder does this team currently exist?
⚠️ Nell'esportazione Udemy manca l'immagine (grafico/tabella) a cui fa riferimento la domanda.

opzioni.A: Area A
opzioni.B: Area B
opzioni.C: Area C
opzioni.D: Area D

domande.spiegazione: Getting over the storming stage (area B) means the team has resolved its conflicts, and a sense of unity is beginning to take shape. During the norming phase (area C), a sense of cohesion and unity emerges, a common consensus develops, and personal differences begin to diminish. Team performance has improved at this point as members have become more goal-oriented. However, if disagreements resurface, the team can slide back into the storming phase (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 211). Please note that on the real PMP exam, you may be asked to answer this type of question by clicking on the correct area in the image.
domande.motivo_incertezza: immagine della domanda non presente nell'esportazione

domande.domanda:
A project manager has implemented a practice where team members take turns facilitating daily stand-up meetings to promote collaboration and ownership. Each team member is assigned a rotating role to facilitate the stand-up meeting for a designated period, typically one week. However, one team member consistently fails to properly facilitate stand-up meetings, acting flustered, failing to engage other team members, and doing most of the talking.
What should the project manager do next?

opzioni.A: Temporarily reassign the facilitation role to maintain meeting quality.
opzioni.B: Provide immediate feedback at the end of each stand-up, so all team members can learn how to facilitate the meeting effectively.
opzioni.C: Discuss the facilitation challenges privately and provide guidance on how to improve.
opzioni.D: Observe a few more stand-ups before intervening to give the team member time to improve naturally.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Assigning the responsibility of facilitating stand-up meetings to another team member does not address the root cause of the problem. It could also lead to resentment among team members, disrupt team dynamics, undermine the learning culture, and reduce opportunities for skill development.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. This issue is personal and performance-related and is best handled privately. Providing feedback publicly at the end of each stand-up meeting can create tension, embarrass the team member, and discourage openness.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. The project manager should help the struggling facilitator improve rather than replacing or publicly criticizing them. Private coaching sessions allow the project manager to provide support, guidance, and feedback to help the team member overcome any hardships they’re facing in their role as a facilitator. Servant leaders should support the team through mentoring, encouragement, and support. Sometimes, team members may not have knowledge or experience in specific roles or functions. Servant leaders who may have more exposure or training in techniques can support the team by providing training (Agile Practice Guide, page 37). The coaching session should focus on identifying obstacles or challenges the team member faces and collaboratively developing strategies to overcome them.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The project manager should not observe a few more stand-ups before intervening. Inaction risks reinforcing poor habits and lowering team morale or efficiency. The issue has already become a pattern since the team member “consistently” fails to properly facilitate stand-up meetings, so timely feedback and support are necessary.

domande.spiegazione: The project manager should help the struggling facilitator improve rather than replacing or publicly criticizing them. Private coaching sessions allow the project manager to provide support, guidance, and feedback to help the team member overcome any hardships they’re facing in their role as a facilitator. Servant leaders should support the team through mentoring, encouragement, and support. Sometimes, team members may not have knowledge or experience in specific roles or functions. Servant leaders who may have more exposure or training in techniques can support the team by providing training (Agile Practice Guide, page 37). The coaching session should focus on identifying obstacles or challenges the team member faces and collaboratively developing strategies to overcome them.

domande.domanda:
During the sprint planning meeting, the product owner and the cross-functional team members agreed on which backlog items would be executed in the next sprint.
Who commits to delivering a potentially shippable increment by the end of the sprint?

opzioni.A: The cross-functional team
opzioni.B: The Scrum master
opzioni.C: The product owner
opzioni.D: The entire Scrum team

domande.spiegazione:
When sprint planning is complete, the cross-functional team members acknowledge their commitment to the business value to be delivered by the end of the sprint. The sprint goal and the sprint backlog embody this commitment (Essential Scrum by Rubin, Kenneth S, page 346).
Option B: The Scrum master helps maintain the Scrum processes, and neither selects nor executes sprint backlog items.
Option C: The product owner doesn’t deliver business value by the end of the sprint; instead, they own the product backlog and manage, maintain, and prioritize its items. Keep in mind that the Product backlog represents the work required to create the entire product, while the Sprint backlog is a subset representing the work to be executed in the current sprint.

domande.domanda:
A project manager brings in overseas contractors for one month to maintain momentum while some team members are unavailable. The contractors have strong technical skills and successfully completed six complex backend stories in the first sprint. However, they struggle with the usability requirements for the user interface, leaving several frontend stories unaddressed. The product owner is concerned about the incomplete work and the potential impact on the release timeline.
What should the project manager do first?

opzioni.A: Engage a business analyst with frontend expertise to translate usability requirements into detailed technical specifications that contractors can implement.
opzioni.B: Redirect all usability-related stories to the remaining local team members and allow the contractors to continue working independently on technical stories.
opzioni.C: Facilitate a discussion with the product owner to clarify the usability requirements.
opzioni.D: Look for a contractor who has stronger experience in both backend and frontend development.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Engaging a business analyst introduces an intermediary before confirming that a clarification problem actually exists. Agile favors direct communication between the team and the Product Owner rather than immediately creating additional documentation or relying on intermediaries. While a business analyst might eventually provide value, the first step should be to clarify requirements collaboratively.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Redirecting all usability-related stories to the remaining local team members treats the symptom rather than the cause. Immediately redistributing work could create bottlenecks and reduce team flexibility without understanding the underlying issue. The project manager should identify root causes before restructuring work assignments.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. When team members struggle to implement a requirement, the first step is to ensure that everyone has a common understanding of what is needed. This scenario suggests the immediate problem may not be technical ability but rather a lack of clarity or shared understanding regarding the usability expectations. The project manager should facilitate a discussion between the Product Owner and the team to clarify user experience expectations, acceptance criteria, design standards, customer needs, definition of done for usability-related stories, etc.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Looking for a contractor with stronger experience in both backend and frontend development assumes the problem is a resource capability issue, without sufficient evidence.
