domande.spiegazione: A Cost Performance Index (CPI) below 1 indicates that the project is experiencing cost overruns, meaning that the actual cost of work performed is higher than planned. A Schedule Performance Index (SPI) above 1 indicates that the project is ahead of schedule, meaning that work is being completed at a faster rate than anticipated (PMBOK 8th Edition, pages 208-209). Therefore, the project manager should take corrective actions to get the cost back on track.

domande.domanda:
The procurement manager who is assigned to a construction project meets with the project manager to assess the final performance of the project’s primary vendor. This involved discussing the multiple issues that they experienced with this vendor, including late delivery and budget overruns. The procurement manager and the project manager also analyzed what they could have done differently and what they did well when addressing the vendor issues when they occurred.
What activity are the procurement manager and the project manager engaged in?

opzioni.A: Collaborating on an open claim with the vendor
opzioni.B: Generating a work performance report
opzioni.C: Confirming the formal acceptance of the vendor’s work
opzioni.D: Capturing lessons learned

domande.spiegazione: The procurement manager and the project manager are discussing lessons learned in engaging with this particular vendor and also in activities associated with managing the vendor’s performance. This includes identifying what went well and what could have been done differently, which will benefit future projects (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 269).

domande.domanda:
While controlling the project execution, the project manager uncovers scope creep caused by a key stakeholder. When checking the Stakeholder Engagement Assessment Matrix, the project manager finds out that the stakeholder is classified as “leading”.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Nothing, since the scope creep was caused by a key stakeholder.
opzioni.B: Reverse the scope change since the project manager didn’t approve it.
opzioni.C: Take the scope creep to the change control board.
opzioni.D: Nothing, since changes made by leading stakeholders could only have a positive impact on the project.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Any change to the scope baseline, even if initiated by a key stakeholder, must follow the formal approval process.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Undoing the changes without referring to the CCB means the project manager is going to perform additional work that is not part of the scope, resulting in further scope creep. That’s why they need approval from CCB.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. The scope creep needs to go through the formal channel by reporting it to the change control board and deciding with them on the appropriate course of action.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Any change to the scope baseline, even if initiated by a leading stakeholder, must follow the formal approval process.

domande.spiegazione: The scope creep needs to go through the formal channel by reporting it to the change control board and deciding with them on the appropriate course of action.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is leading a team of engineers to build a packaging machine. The machine went through exhaustive internal verification. After receiving the machine, the client sent an email to the project manager asking whether it met the requirements or not.
What should the project manager do next?

opzioni.A: Send an engineer to the client’s site to double-check the product
opzioni.B: Perform the control quality process and use the contingency reserve to fix any unidentified issues
opzioni.C: Collaborate with the client to get their signature approving that the product complies with requirements
opzioni.D: Confirm that the product was internally tested and formally close the project

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. In this situation, the client just asked whether the product meets the requirements or not and didn’t report any problems.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The control quality process is supposed to be performed before the product is shipped.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. At this stage, the project manager should work with the client to get their signature as approval that the product complies with requirements (validate scope process). Thus, the proper next step is to go over all of the product specifications with the client to formally validate them and get their signature approving that the product complies with requirements in order to finally close the project.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Confirming that the product has been internally tested on your part is not sufficient since the client must validate that the product meets their requirements.

domande.spiegazione: At this stage, the project manager should work with the client to get their signature as approval that the product complies with requirements (validate scope process). Thus, the proper next step is to go over all of the product specifications with the client to formally validate them and get their signature approving that the product complies with requirements in order to finally close the project.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is preparing a status report for the project sponsor. The report shows a Schedule Performance Index (SPI) of 0.8 and a Cost Performance Index (CPI) of 1.1. 40% of project work is completed against a planned 50%. The project has a fixed regulatory deadline that cannot be extended.
What should the project manager do first?

opzioni.A: Reassure the sponsor that the project is performing well since the CPI of 1.1 indicates the project is under budget.
opzioni.B: Analyze the root causes of the schedule variance and evaluate options for schedule recovery.
opzioni.C: Use the surplus funds to accelerate the schedule through overtime or additional resources.
opzioni.D: Report the current status to the sponsor and recommend accepting the schedule variance since the project is under budget.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Reassuring the sponsor that the project is performing well focuses only on cost performance and ignores the significant schedule variance. The project manager should showcase honesty and transparency: downplaying a schedule variance of this magnitude violates these principles. The sponsor needs to know the true status to make informed decisions.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. An SPI < 1.0 indicates that the project is behind schedule. A CPI > 1.0 indicates that the project is under planned cost. The SPI of 0.8 means the project is only achieving 80% of the planned schedule progress. With only 40% complete against 50% planned and a fixed regulatory deadline, this variance is significant and requires immediate attention. The project manager should analyze root causes, evaluate schedule recovery options (crashing, fast tracking, or scope adjustment), and prepare a recovery plan before meeting with the sponsor.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Requesting additional budget to accelerate the schedule may be a valid recovery option, but it is premature without first understanding the root cause of the schedule variance. The schedule delay may be due to factors that additional budget cannot solve (e.g., regulatory approvals, resource unavailability, scope creep).
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Reporting the status and accepting the variance is passive and fails to demonstrate accountability. The project manager should take ownership and propose solutions, not simply accept variances. With 60% of the work remaining and a fixed deadline, the project manager should be actively pursuing recovery options.

domande.spiegazione: An SPI < 1.0 indicates that the project is behind schedule. A CPI > 1.0 indicates that the project is under planned cost. The SPI of 0.8 means the project is only achieving 80% of the planned schedule progress. With only 40% complete against 50% planned and a fixed regulatory deadline, this variance is significant and requires immediate attention. The project manager should analyze root causes, evaluate schedule recovery options (crashing, fast tracking, or scope adjustment), and prepare a recovery plan before meeting with the sponsor.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is planning a cryptocurrency conference. The Ministry of Finance, which is the conference sponsor, limited the number of attendees to forty. One day prior to the event, the project manager got a call from the ministry office requesting to add two other subject matter experts to the conference attendees list. Luckily, the conference room has a seating capacity of fifty people. However, the project manager needs to rearrange lodging, catering, coffee breaks, gift packages, etc., accordingly.
What should the project manager do first?

opzioni.A: Issue a change request to address the ministry’s request
opzioni.B: Accept the ministry’s request and increase the number of attendees since the conference hasn’t started yet
opzioni.C: Accept the ministry’s request and increase the number of attendees since the request is issued by the sponsor
opzioni.D: Refuse to increase the number of attendees since the event is only one day away

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. When a critical key stakeholder requests a change, the project manager should treat it with high priority and issue a change request to the Change Control Board (CCB) in order to add their request to the scope.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Even though the conference hasn’t started yet, the project execution has already begun since the project team has contacted suppliers, reserved attendees’ accommodations, booked the conference room, etc.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The project manager should not immediately increase the number of attendees because this will be considered scope creep.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. In the described situation, the project manager is able to address the stakeholder’s request. So, it’s not appropriate to decline the change request under the pretext that the conference date is only one day away.

domande.spiegazione: When a critical key stakeholder requests a change, the project manager should treat it with high priority and issue a change request to the Change Control Board (CCB) in order to add their request to the scope.

domande.domanda:
A project manager calculates the early & late start and finish dates of his project activities. One of the activities has the following representation.
What is this activity's float? [Dati ricostruiti dalla spiegazione: ES = 4, EF = 20, LS = 12, LF = 28]
⚠️ Nell'esportazione Udemy manca l'immagine (grafico/tabella) a cui fa riferimento la domanda.
domande.spiegazione: Float, Total float, Slack, or activity float represent how long an activity can be delayed without causing a delay in the project completion date. On a critical path, the total float is zero (PMBOK 8th Edition, pages 160-161). You can calculate an activity float by subtracting the Early Start date of the activity from its Late Start date: (12 - 4 = 8 days), or by subtracting the Early Finish date of the activity from its Late Finish date (28 - 20 = 8 days).

domande.domanda:
A project manager is managing an e-commerce project using a predictive approach. The customer reached out to the project manager requesting the addition of a new feature to allow users to rate the products they purchased.
Knowing that this feature may involve some security risks, what should the project manager do next? (Select two)

opzioni.A: Inform the customer of the potential risks to convince them to change their mind.
opzioni.B: Ask the customer to submit a change request.
opzioni.C: Protect the team from distractions by asking the customer to put off the change until they finish the project.
opzioni.D: Evaluate the change and its associated risks with the team.

domande.spiegazione:
Since the project manager is adopting a predictive approach, he should ask the customer to submit a change request that will be evaluated by him and his team. The change request evaluation should cover analyzing its associated risks and implications. After gathering all information, the Change Control Board (CCB) will decide to either accept the change or reject it. The project manager is usually a member of the CCB. In this case, the project manager may influence the decision based on the conducted analysis. But, he cannot do this without assessing the change with his team first (PMBOK 8th edition, pages 29-30).
Option C: The customer may not accept postponing the change. The concept of protecting the team from distraction or external interference doesn’t exist in the predictive approach; it’s rather common in the Scrum framework, more specifically during sprint execution.

domande.domanda:
Before announcing the completion of the project execution, the project manager of a construction project reviews deliverables and performs a site walkthrough.
What is the project manager performing in this scenario?

opzioni.A: An inspection
opzioni.B: A handing over
opzioni.C: An audit
opzioni.D: A scope validation

domande.spiegazione:
During an inspection, the project manager reviews deliverables and performs a site walkthrough if applicable (PMBOK 8th edition, page 174).
Options B & D: The project manager here is neither validating the scope with the customer nor handing over deliverables to them.
Option C: Audits are carried out to determine if project activities comply with organizational and project policies, processes, and procedures (PMBOK 8th edition, page 148). In other words, audits are performed on processes while inspections are performed on products.

domande.domanda:
The most recent project of Kitchen Plus Inc. involves the creation of an automatic dicer with industry-exclusive characteristics. Based on the information provided by the project team, the current Schedule Performance Index (SPI) is 1.10, while the Cost Performance Index (CPI) is 0.80.
What should the project manager do to balance out the performance of both the schedule and the budget?

opzioni.A: Crash the schedule by adding more resources to critical activities
opzioni.B: Fast-track the longest activities that fall on the critical path
opzioni.C: Level out resource usage to further spread out costs over time
opzioni.D: Nothing, since the project is performing as expected

domande.spiegazione:
Based on the performance indexes provided, the project is 10% ahead of schedule while being over budget. Leveling out resource usage is a strategy used to spread out costs over time. This helps reduce unexpected spikes of spending, albeit it may lead to lengthening the schedule (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 193).
Options A & B: Crashing or fast-tracking are two schedule compression techniques. So, it’s pointless to use them in the described situation since the project is ahead of schedule (PMBOK 8th Edition, pages 196-197).

domande.domanda:
A project manager is managing a project with a distributed team, a limited budget, and tight deadlines. The project manager wants to avoid any scope creep and keep the team focused on delivering a product that meets requirements.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Ask the project team to skip small requirements so that they can only focus on the big and important ones.
opzioni.B: Ensure that all alterations to the scope are authorized through a formal process.
opzioni.C: Prevent stakeholders from directly interacting with the project team.
opzioni.D: Scope creep cannot be avoided in a predictive project; therefore, the project manager should adopt an agile approach instead.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Requirements shouldn’t be skipped, small or big.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. The project manager can avoid scope creep by adhering to the agreed-upon change management process. Change management processes have to be set up front and should be very straightforward. Essentially, when a change is suggested, it should be reviewed, approved or rejected, and then incorporated into the project plan if it’s approved (PMBOK 8th edition, page 151).
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Often, it’s not appropriate to prevent the stakeholders from communicating with the project team.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Not all projects are fit for the agile approach; therefore, it’s not appropriate to change the project’s development approach just to prevent scope creep.

domande.spiegazione: The project manager can avoid scope creep by adhering to the agreed-upon change management process. Change management processes have to be set up front and should be very straightforward. Essentially, when a change is suggested, it should be reviewed, approved or rejected, and then incorporated into the project plan if it’s approved (PMBOK 8th edition, page 151).

domande.domanda:
One year into managing a construction project, and during the completion and closure process, the project manager faces a key stakeholder’s refusal to sign off on the deliverables due to non-compliance claims.
What should the project manager do next?

opzioni.A: Issue a change request to fix the deliverables
opzioni.B: Conduct a lessons learned meeting with the key stakeholder
opzioni.C: Check the contract’s dispute resolution clause
opzioni.D: Conduct a variance analysis

domande.spiegazione: Variance analysis is a technique used at the end of a project or phase in order to identify any deviation in deliverables or differences between actual and planned behaviors. This method is used to determine the cause and magnitude of the difference between baseline and actual performance and to retain control over the project (PMBOK 8th edition, page 211).

domande.domanda: Due to high levels of uncertainty, the project manager opts for the rolling wave method for project planning. How is this method useful in this case?

opzioni.A: It will help the project manager determine which activities are more important to prioritize.
opzioni.B: It will help the project manager organize the project’s activities and tasks.
opzioni.C: It will help the project manager determine the sequencing of a large number of activities.
opzioni.D: It will help the project manager reach the proper level of detail in each work package at the right time.

domande.spiegazione:
Rolling wave is a project planning method that consists of a gradual elaboration of details to the Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) over time. Near-term deliverables are decomposed into individual components (work packages) that are broken down to the greatest degree of detail. Long-term deliverables, on the other hand, are identified more broadly. In this way, rolling wave planning allows work to progress on current and near-term deliverables while the planning for potential work packages continues (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 196).
Options A, B, C: The Rolling wave method is used to address uncertainty rather than prioritizing, organizing, or sequencing activities.

domande.domanda:
A project sponsor informed the project manager that the project must be completed one week sooner than the originally agreed-upon schedule.
What should the project manager do first?

opzioni.A: Crash the schedule
opzioni.B: Fast-track the schedule
opzioni.C: Add duration buffers
opzioni.D: Level out resources

domande.spiegazione: In this scenario, one of two schedule compression techniques must be used: crashing or fast-tracking. Crashing the schedule involves compressing it by adding more resources to the project. However, fast-tracking implies performing originally sequential activities in a simultaneous way instead (PMBOK 8th edition, pages 196-197). When possible, select the least costly option first, which would be fast-tracking.

domande.domanda: Before taking a long leave, a project manager informed the person filling in for them that they should regularly calculate the project’s Earned Value (EV). Among the following options, what is the right description of an Earned Value?

opzioni.A: The difference between the budgeted cost of the performed work and its actual cost.
opzioni.B: The cost of labor spent to date.
opzioni.C: The method of determining how much of the budget should have been spent based on the amount of work accomplished to date.
opzioni.D: The amount of money that has been spent so far on the project.

domande.spiegazione:
Earned Value (EV) is the method used to measure how much of the allocated budget should have been spent in view of the work realized to date (PMBOK 8th edition, page 169).
Option A: This technique allows the project manager to calculate the Cost Variance (CV), which is the difference between the budgeted cost of the performed work (EV) and its actual cost, to eventually find out whether the project is under or over budget (PMBOK 8th edition, page 207).
Option D: The amount of money that has been spent so far represents the Actual Cost (AC) (PMBOK 8th edition, page 169).

domande.domanda:
When the dimensions of the dug canals for the new dam project were compared to the plan, a huge variance was revealed. Therefore, the project manager had to call for a meeting with the team to decide what to do next.
In which of the following focus areas does the project manager’s activity take part?

opzioni.A: Executing
opzioni.B: Closing
opzioni.C: Monitoring and Controlling
opzioni.D: Inspecting

domande.spiegazione:
Reviewing the project performance in comparison to plans is part of the monitoring and controlling focus area. This involves tracking, adjusting, and reporting on the project performance, as well as implementing corrective actions when needed to ensure the project is on track, budget and time-wise (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 72).
Option D: Inspecting is not a focus area; it’s rather a risk identification activity.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is overseeing a citywide initiative to replace outdated street lighting with smart LED systems. Each district has different infrastructure conditions and regulatory approval times, which could affect installation duration. The project has no prior historical data for similar large-scale smart lighting projects, and the engineering team expresses uncertainty about how long some installation activities may take.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Use parametric estimating based on the average time per light fixture installed.
opzioni.B: Apply analogous estimating using data from smaller lighting upgrade projects.
opzioni.C: Gather expert input to develop a range of possible durations for uncertain activities and calculate weighted averages.
opzioni.D: Break down all activities into smaller components and estimate each separately to improve accuracy.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Parametric estimating assumes a reliable relationship between variables (e.g., time per fixture), which may not be true given the variation in infrastructure conditions (PMBOK 8th Edition, pages 184-185).
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Analogous estimating relies on comparable historical projects, and smaller upgrades don’t provide enough similarity or scale accuracy (PMBOK 8th Edition, pages 146-147).
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. When uncertainty exists and there’s limited historical data, the project manager should use an estimation technique that incorporates expert judgment and variability. Gathering expert input to develop a range of possible durations for uncertain activities and calculating weighted averages is three-point or multipoint estimating, which produces more realistic and probabilistic estimates (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 183).
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Bottom-up estimating increases detail, but it doesn’t specifically address uncertainty in activity duration (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 149).

domande.spiegazione: When uncertainty exists and there’s limited historical data, the project manager should use an estimation technique that incorporates expert judgment and variability. Gathering expert input to develop a range of possible durations for uncertain activities and calculating weighted averages is three-point or multipoint estimating, which produces more realistic and probabilistic estimates (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 183).

domande.domanda:
A project manager is assigned to a university complex project that consists of designing and producing 200 wayfinding and directional signs. These signs will be placed and installed near doors, exits, offices, elevators, etc., by another company. After getting the client's approval that the project scope is met, the project manager delivers the signs to the installation company. The latter asks the project manager to help them with the signs’ installation.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Submit a change request to assist with the signs’ installation.
opzioni.B: Do a favor for the installation company and help them out.
opzioni.C: Create a new separate project charter for the signs installation support to make it clear that it’s not part of the initial project.
opzioni.D: Do nothing since the project scope has been officially fulfilled and approved by the client.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The signs production project is completed; therefore, submitting a change request doesn’t make sense.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The signs’ installation is not part of the project, therefore no further steps are required.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. A company is already assigned to install the signs, so there is no need to create a new project charter.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Since they completed their project, which clearly consists of only designing, producing, and delivering the sign, and after getting the client’s official approval of the project's deliverables, the project manager's mission is done.

domande.spiegazione: Since they completed their project, which clearly consists of only designing, producing, and delivering the sign, and after getting the client’s official approval of the project's deliverables, the project manager's mission is done.

domande.domanda:
A project manager got the approval to carry out a significant change that would bring added value to the project. The change has a total cost of $10,000 and will add one month to the project’s duration.
What should the project manager do right after getting the change approved?

opzioni.A: Call for a meeting with the CCB to review the change
opzioni.B: Update the time, cost, and scope baselines to reflect the change
opzioni.C: Perform a change risk assessment
opzioni.D: Update the change control system to reflect the change

domande.spiegazione:
As soon as a change gets approved, the project manager must update the time, cost, and scope baselines to reflect the impact of the change on all project aspects (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 30).
Options A & C: Each change gets through review as well as risk assessment by the Change Control Board (CCB) before getting approved or rejected.
Option D: A change control system represents a description of the way changes to the project scope should be managed. Actual changes are not part of the change control system.

domande.domanda:
A subcontractor is engaged to install the electrical wiring of a construction project. A stakeholder requests a modification in the project's scope, which will result in a change in the subcontractor’s workload.
Which of the following documents will address how the change in the subcontractor's workload will be handled?

opzioni.A: The Change Control System
opzioni.B: The Procurement Management Plan
opzioni.C: The contract
opzioni.D: The project scope

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The Change Control System describes how modifications to the project deliverables and documentation are managed and controlled. However, if the modifications impact the work of a subcontractor, then the project manager should review the change clause of the corresponding contract.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The Procurement Management Plan is used to define the process of what, when, and how to acquire materials or services from third parties. Yet, it doesn’t define the contractual engagement with each of them (PMBOK 8th Edition, pages 124-125).
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Any changes to any of the predetermined contract terms between the subcontractor and the project manager, including the defined scope of work, should be addressed in the contract.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The scope only reflects the change in the workload, but it does not address how this change will impact other aspects (Fee increase, change of completion date, etc.).

domande.spiegazione: Any changes to any of the predetermined contract terms between the subcontractor and the project manager, including the defined scope of work, should be addressed in the contract.

domande.domanda:
At the beginning of the project planning phase, the project manager would always emphasize how important it is for all data to be precise and accurate. During a meeting, a team member asks if there is really a difference between precision and accuracy.
How should the project manager reply?

opzioni.A: Precision and accuracy are mutually exclusive
opzioni.B: Accuracy measures exactness, while precision measures correctness
opzioni.C: Accuracy measures correctness, while precision measures exactness
opzioni.D: Precision and accuracy are actually the same

domande.spiegazione: Accuracy describes how close a measurement is to an accepted value (PMBOK 8th edition, page 265). Precision describes the statistical variability of the produced measurement (it can be far off the accepted value) (PMBOK 8th edition, page 270).

domande.domanda:
A stakeholder is pressuring the project team to make some changes to the product. The project manager informs the stakeholder that the changes cannot be implemented immediately due to the established processes.
What should the project manager refer the stakeholder to?

opzioni.A: The change management plan
opzioni.B: The requirements management plan
opzioni.C: The organizational process assets
opzioni.D: The scope management plan

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. The change management plan is a component of the project management plan that establishes the change control board (CCB), also known as a steering committee. It documents the extent of its authority and describes how the change control system will be implemented (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 116).
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. A requirements management plan describes how requirements will be analyzed, documented, and managed (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 131).
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The organizational process assets refer to plans, processes, guidelines, and knowledge repositories that are unique to and employed by the organization (PMBOK 8th Edition, pages 19-20).
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The scope management plan only explains the scope's definition, development, monitoring, control, and validation procedures (PMBOK 8th Edition, 141).

domande.spiegazione: The change management plan is a component of the project management plan that establishes the change control board (CCB), also known as a steering committee. It documents the extent of its authority and describes how the change control system will be implemented (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 116).

domande.domanda:
A project manager is leading a project that has become so large (multiple teams, long duration, and huge budget) that the sponsor has been replaced by a steering committee.
What should the project manager do to accommodate this new change?

opzioni.A: Acknowledge that the stakeholders’ structure has changed and tailor communication accordingly.
opzioni.B: Work according to the original plan while keeping in mind that the project may now include additional stakeholders.
opzioni.C: Hold a meeting with the new steering committee and continue working on the project.
opzioni.D: Share an updated status report with the new steering committee.

domande.spiegazione: On large projects, one sponsor might not be enough. A Steering Committee is established when a large project involves multiple business units, organizations, or individuals who all have a substantial stake in the project’s success and outcomes. The project manager needs to be proactive and respond to this change. The initial communication plan for a single sponsor may not work for a steering committee. In order to ensure effective communication with the committee, the project manager must understand their communication requirements and preferences.

domande.domanda:
When the execution of a rebranding project was completed, several key stakeholders, including the sponsor, were reluctant to accept deliverables and close the project.
What should the project manager do in this situation? (Select three)

opzioni.A: Identify and resolve any open issues. Then, be firm on formal closure.
opzioni.B: Formally close the project. Stakeholders will get well-acquainted with the new brand by that time.
opzioni.C: Identify and openly discuss the reasons for reluctance.
opzioni.D: Invite earnest feedback from all sides and try to identify any misunderstandings.

domande.spiegazione: The project manager should not close the project when key stakeholders are not satisfied. They should try to discuss, identify, and resolve any issues or misunderstandings first (PMBOK 8th Edition, pages 32-33).

domande.domanda:
During the risk identification phase, the project manager and their team identified more than 100 risks. The project manager believes that the quantitative evaluation of each of these risks will take a lot of time, whereas not all of the identified risks are important enough to justify such a measure.
What should the project manager do next?

opzioni.A: Identify risk triggers, then perform a quantitative analysis of risks that have no triggers.
opzioni.B: Use qualitative risk analysis to qualify and prioritize risks for the quantitative risk analysis.
opzioni.C: Conduct a qualitative assessment of each risk’s probability, then perform a quantitative analysis of risks with a high probability.
opzioni.D: Conduct a qualitative assessment of the potential impact of each risk, then perform a quantitative analysis of risks with a high impact.

domande.spiegazione: Qualitative Risk Analysis is the process of assessing a risk’s occurrence probability and impact. This method helps to focus efforts on only high-priority risks by laying the foundation to perform a Quantitative Risk Analysis (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 96).

domande.domanda:
A project team developed a detailed plan to update the operating system of all of the company's computers. Later on, the project team discovers that not every computer supports the new version of the operating system.
Which of the following statements best describes this scenario?

opzioni.A: The project team made a wrong assumption
opzioni.B: The project team didn't develop an appropriate project plan
opzioni.C: The project team didn’t establish an adequate risk response
opzioni.D: The project team didn’t consider the new version of the operating system as a constraint

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. The project team made the assumption that all of the company’s computers are compatible with the new operating system. Consequently, they planned the project based on this belief. But later on, they found out that their assumption was untrue.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Assumptions should be logged during the project planning phase to take into consideration when creating the project plan, and that’s what the team most probably did since they developed a detailed plan. Therefore, the issue is not a result of poor planning.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Since it wasn’t discovered during the project planning, the encountered issue wasn’t identified as a risk.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The purpose of the project is to implement the new version of the operating system, so it cannot be considered a constraint. Yet, the hardware characteristics of the company’s computers are a constraint since they can hinder the project’s success.

domande.spiegazione: The project team made the assumption that all of the company’s computers are compatible with the new operating system. Consequently, they planned the project based on this belief. But later on, they found out that their assumption was untrue.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is leading a project that was supposed to last 6 months. The project is currently in its second year.
Which of the following statements best describes the situation?

opzioni.A: The project scope was not clearly defined
opzioni.B: The project should have been divided into subprojects
opzioni.C: The project team didn’t protect the scope from changes
opzioni.D: The project should have been halted after 6 months

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. The project took more time than it should have, most likely because the project scope was not clearly defined.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. There is no indication in the described situation that the project should have been broken down into smaller sub-projects.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The project team doesn't usually have the power to approve or disapprove change requests. Changes conducted on the project scope fall under the Change Control Board's (CCB) responsibility.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The fact that the project has exceeded its allocated time means that the sponsor is still supporting the project; therefore, the project should not be halted.

domande.spiegazione: The project took more time than it should have, most likely because the project scope was not clearly defined.

domande.domanda:
A project manager works for a company that does not have an official archiving procedure. The project manager has just finished a project and got the client’s official approval of the final deliverables.
What should the project manager do with all associated paperwork?

opzioni.A: Nothing, since the company doesn’t require the archiving of performed projects
opzioni.B: Archive the project documents following industry best practices
opzioni.C: Discard the archive to comply with the company’s policy
opzioni.D: Ask the client to keep the project’s archive

domande.spiegazione:
Even if there is no official archiving procedure in place, the project manager should still organize, index, and keep the data related to completed projects.
Option C: Project records should be kept for future use; therefore, they should not be discarded by the project manager. Plus, the company doesn’t have an official archiving procedure, which means that they are not calling for archive discard.
Option D: The client should not have access to the project archive since it might contain private, confidential data.

domande.domanda:
In a construction project, the project team reported to the project manager that one of the main concrete mixer trucks had stopped working. Even though they tried to understand the reason behind this unexpected malfunction, the project team didn’t reach any conclusion. Therefore, they suggested referring the issue to a specialized mechanic. The mechanic performed a high-level diagnostic and informed the project manager that he needed 2 to 5 days to fix the problem, adding that he would take care of replacing any spare parts if needed. The project manager accepted the mechanic’s proposal and asked him to prepare an invoice after finishing the truck repair.
What type of contract did the two parties opt for?

opzioni.A: Fixed-price
opzioni.B: Cost-reimbursable
opzioni.C: Time & Material
opzioni.D: Indefinite delivery indefinite quantity

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The two parties didn’t agree on a predetermined cost, thus they didn’t opt for a fixed-price contract.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. In a cost-reimbursable contract, the seller (the mechanic) charges the buyer (the project manager) for all the legitimate expenses that were incurred to complete the work (spare parts), as well as a fixed fee representing the seller’s profit for their work (diagnostic & repair). This type of contract is often used when the project scope is not well defined, such as in this case, where the cause of the truck breakdown is not clear (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 251).
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. In a Time & Material contract, both the buyer and the seller should agree on a daily or hourly rate, which is not the case here.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. An Indefinite delivery indefinite quantity contract implies providing an indefinite quantity of goods or services, with a defined lower and upper limit, within a fixed time period. This is not the case either, since the delivered service is definite (repaired truck) and the delivery time is not fixed (ranges between 2 and 5 days).

domande.spiegazione: In a cost-reimbursable contract, the seller (the mechanic) charges the buyer (the project manager) for all the legitimate expenses that were incurred to complete the work (spare parts), as well as a fixed fee representing the seller’s profit for their work (diagnostic & repair). This type of contract is often used when the project scope is not well defined, such as in this case, where the cause of the truck breakdown is not clear (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 251).

domande.domanda: A project manager is trying to control the costs of the project they are working on. Thus, the project manager decides to calculate the _______________ in order to define the value of the completed work, based on its pre-approved assigned budget.

opzioni.A: Planned Value
opzioni.B: Earned Value
opzioni.C: Schedule Variance
opzioni.D: Cost Variance

domande.spiegazione:
Earned Value (EV) refers to the value of completed work, based on the approved budget assigned to that work (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 169).
Option C: Schedule Variance (SV) is a measure of schedule performance expressed as the difference between the earned value and the Planned Value (PV) (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 208).
Option D: Cost Variance (CV) is the amount of budget deficit or surplus at a given point in time, expressed as the difference between the earned value and the Actual Cost (AC) (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 207).

domande.domanda:
A project manager is working on a project to create and test a new piece of software. The project is following a predictive approach and is currently behind schedule and under budget. The project manager estimated that it would take another 2 weeks to complete the testing activity. The program manager asked the project manager to dedicate only one week to the testing activity.
What should the project manager do in this situation?

opzioni.A: Crash the project to complete the testing activity in one week.
opzioni.B: Fast-track the project to complete testing in one week.
opzioni.C: Submit a change request to complete testing in one week.
opzioni.D: Complete the testing activity in two weeks as planned and inform the program manager that they cannot compromise the testing phase.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Since the project is already behind schedule and under budget, the project manager can consider crashing it by compressing the testing phase and adding more resources (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 196).
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Fast-tracking means performing multiple activities concurrently, so it’s not intended to reduce a certain activity’s duration (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 197).
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The project manager shouldn’t submit a change request to squeeze testing activities into one week, as it will result in lowering the product quality. Even if it means completing the project behind its initial schedule, it is important to perform all of the project aspects that were agreed upon by the customer.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. If crashing is not feasible due to any potentially arising complexity or lack of resources, the project manager needs to decline the program manager’s request and complete the testing in two weeks as previously planned.

domande.spiegazione: Since the project is already behind schedule and under budget, the project manager can consider crashing it by compressing the testing phase and adding more resources (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 196).

domande.domanda:
A Change Control Board (CCB) is composed of 4 members: two members representing the performing organization: the project manager and the functional manager, and two members representing the client: the product manager and the sponsor. During the last week of the project, the product manager and the sponsor requested a change.
What should the project manager do next?

opzioni.A: Refuse to implement the change since it was requested late in the project’s life span.
opzioni.B: Evaluate the change with the project team, then decide whether to proceed with it or not.
opzioni.C: Evaluate and discuss the change internally, then call for a CCB meeting.
opzioni.D: Discuss the change with the functional manager, then decide whether to proceed with it or not.

domande.spiegazione:
No matter how late a change request is made, it should be considered as long as the project is still running.
Option A: Refusing or accepting is beyond the project manager’s authority; it falls under the Change Control Board (CCB) responsibilities.
Options B & D: The project manager should evaluate and discuss the change request with relevant stakeholders before presenting it to the CCB in order to argue whether it should be implemented or refused.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is leading a construction project following a traditional waterfall approach. The project team has gathered requirements from the customer, who is eager to kick off the project promptly. The project manager has a meeting with the business analyst to define the project scope based on the gathered requirements.
What should the project manager do to develop the scope statement?

opzioni.A: Develop the scope description, deliverables, acceptance criteria, and exclusions.
opzioni.B: Develop the scope description, Work Breakdown Structure (WBS), and WBS dictionary.
opzioni.C: Develop the Scope Management Plan, Statement of Work (SOW), and Requirements Traceability Matrix (RTM).
opzioni.D: Develop the Project Charter, Project Management Plan, and deliverables.

domande.spiegazione:
The project scope statement includes the scope description, deliverables, acceptance criteria, and exclusions (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 128). This document is used to define the project scope and ensure that all stakeholders have a common understanding of the project's objectives and boundaries. It is an important project document that guides the project team's work during execution and provides a baseline for evaluating whether requests for changes or additional work are contained within or outside the project's boundaries.
Option B: The WBS and WBS dictionary are not subparts of the scope statement; they are developed after developing the scope statement, and all three artifacts i.e., scope statement, WBS, and WBS dictionary, collectively form the scope baseline.
Options C & D: The Project Charter and the Scope Management Plan should be developed before the scope statement.

domande.domanda:
A project manager decides to obtain the PMP certification in two months. The project manager creates the following exam preparation plan:
Weeks 1 to 4: Watch a preparation course
Weeks 5-6: Take mock practice tests
Week 7: Time off
Week 8: Sit for the exam
However, in week 5, the project manager had to attend a 7-day international conference, which meant pausing the exam preparation for 1 week.
To make up for the lost time, the project manager canceled their week off and worked on mock tests during weeks 6 and 7 instead of weeks 5 and 6. This is an example of:

opzioni.A: Adaptability
opzioni.B: Risk mitigation
opzioni.C: Workaround
opzioni.D: Corrective action

domande.spiegazione: When an unidentified risk occurs, it is addressed through a workaround. A workaround is an unplanned risk response to deal with unexpected risks as well as passively accepted risks during project execution (i.e., when there is no predetermined risk response plan put in place).

domande.domanda:
A project manager is leading a major construction project. During project execution, the contractor, bound by contract to provide regular status reports and participate in progress evaluation meetings, abruptly ceased these obligations, claiming that these activities are excessively time-consuming. The project is at a critical phase with tight deadlines and high stakeholder expectations.
What should the project manager do first?

opzioni.A: Document the contractor's failure to fulfill contractual terms and check the formal claims process outlined in the contract.
opzioni.B: Conduct a thorough assessment of the potential risks associated with the contractor's non-compliance and involve the project sponsor for urgent issue resolution.
opzioni.C: Reach out to the contractor, reminding them of their contractual commitments to attend meetings and submit reports as agreed upon.
opzioni.D: Seek guidance from the organization's legal counsel to explore options for enforcing compliance, such as issuing a formal demand letter urging the contractor to fulfill their obligations.

domande.spiegazione:
Reaching out to the contractor and reminding them of their contractual commitments emphasizes proactive communication and reinforcement of the agreed-upon obligations. By directly engaging with the contractor, the project manager seeks to address the issue collaboratively and re-establish the contractor's participation in project activities without resorting to more drastic measures immediately.
Option A, B, D: Escalating the issue to the project sponsor or legal counsel or initiating formal claims or legal actions may be premature at this stage. These options may become necessary if initial attempts at resolution prove unsuccessful.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is working for a large accounting firm and has been asked to perform a study on the launch of a new offshore site for one of the firm’s clients. The project manager met with all stakeholders, noted down their requirements, and concluded that implementing all these requirements would exceed the allocated budget for the project.
What should the project manager do next?

opzioni.A: Develop the Scope Management Plan
opzioni.B: Develop the Requirements Management Plan
opzioni.C: Develop the Project Scope Statement
opzioni.D: Create the WBS

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The Scope Management Plan outlines how the scope will be defined, validated, and controlled throughout the project, but it is typically developed earlier in the planning phase before the specific scope is defined (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 141).
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The Requirements Management Plan describes how requirements will be gathered, analyzed, and tracked. In this scenario, the requirements have already been gathered, so this plan would have already been developed earlier (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 131).
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. The project manager has already gathered the requirements from the stakeholders and realized that implementing all of them would exceed the budget. The next step is to develop the project scope statement to document what will and will not be included in the project based on constraints like budget.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) is created after the project scope statement. It breaks down the project's deliverables into smaller, manageable components. However, before developing the WBS, the scope needs to be defined and documented in the project scope statement (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 171).

domande.spiegazione: The project manager has already gathered the requirements from the stakeholders and realized that implementing all of them would exceed the budget. The next step is to develop the project scope statement to document what will and will not be included in the project based on constraints like budget.

domande.domanda:
A construction company is building a new hospital in a rapidly growing city. The project must adhere to local building codes and environmental regulations. However, during execution, the project manager discovers that the original design does not fully comply with the latest regulations, which were updated after the project began.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Submit a change request to update the design to comply with the latest regulations.
opzioni.B: Proceed with the original design since the changes occurred after the project started.
opzioni.C: Inform stakeholders that compliance is optional unless explicitly stated in the contract.
opzioni.D: Blame the architects for not anticipating changes in regulations.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Updating the design to comply with the latest environmental regulations and submitting a change request ensures that the project remains aligned with organizational governance requirements.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Ignoring regulatory changes can lead to legal issues and reputational damage. The project manager has a responsibility to ensure compliance throughout the project lifecycle. Continuing with the original design could result in delays and additional costs due to potential fines or rework.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Assuming compliance is optional could expose the organization to legal risks. Compliance is a fundamental aspect of project success.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Blaming the architects avoids addressing the root cause of the issue. The project manager should focus on proactive solutions rather than assigning blame.

domande.spiegazione: Updating the design to comply with the latest environmental regulations and submitting a change request ensures that the project remains aligned with organizational governance requirements.

domande.domanda:
A project manager overseeing the development of a large mining project identifies a potential risk. The risk is documented in the risk register, and a mitigation strategy is documented. However, during the execution phase, the project manager discovers that the mitigation measures will not effectively address the risk if it occurs.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Continue monitoring the risk occurrence.
opzioni.B: Submit a change order to update the mitigation strategy.
opzioni.C: Meet with the project owner to brainstorm a new mitigation strategy.
opzioni.D: Reassess the risk and its mitigation strategy.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Simply observing the situation without proactive adjustments does not resolve the underlying issue and leaves the project vulnerable.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. A change order may eventually be required to implement an updated strategy, but this step should only come after thoroughly reassessing the risk and determining a more effective approach.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Involving the project owner might be necessary in certain situations, but it is not the first step. The project manager should first reassess the risk internally to determine the root cause of the failure and identify potential alternatives.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Reassessing the risk is the most logical first step. This involves revisiting the risk’s probability, impact, and existing mitigation measures to identify why the current strategy is inadequate. By doing this, the project manager can propose a more effective response tailored to the current circumstances.

domande.spiegazione: Reassessing the risk is the most logical first step. This involves revisiting the risk’s probability, impact, and existing mitigation measures to identify why the current strategy is inadequate. By doing this, the project manager can propose a more effective response tailored to the current circumstances.

domande.domanda:
To obtain the human resource requirements of their new project, the project manager published a job offer on a well-known recruitment platform. Days later, over 300 applications were submitted. Going through all of them will take a lot of time and effort.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Use a weighting system to select the best applicants
opzioni.B: Add a section for minimum qualifications in the job description
opzioni.C: Create a screening system to reduce the number of applications to treat
opzioni.D: Randomly select a few candidates and pick the best of them

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Using a weighting system requires a thorough examination of each application since a score will be attributed according to a set of predefined criteria. Hence, this option would be time-consuming. It could, however, be used after applying the screening system.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Altering the job description is not the right action since the job offer had already been published, and applications had been received. Thus, the question addresses the resource selection phase.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. A screening system could be used to short-list applicants based on predefined criteria, such as technical capabilities, years of experience, location, etc. Since the number of applications is high, it would be better to resort to screening. By defining go/no-go criteria, the project manager will be able to reduce the number of applications to treat.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Random selection is not a suitable option because it does not ensure the selection of eligible resources.

domande.spiegazione: A screening system could be used to short-list applicants based on predefined criteria, such as technical capabilities, years of experience, location, etc. Since the number of applications is high, it would be better to resort to screening. By defining go/no-go criteria, the project manager will be able to reduce the number of applications to treat.

domande.domanda:
A project manager learns that they were not assigned the human resources they were promised during the planning phase. Instead, they got a team that did not have the required skills to execute the project work.
Taking into consideration that they work in a weak matrix organization, what should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Issue a change request to get a more qualified team.
opzioni.B: Negotiate with the functional manager in order to obtain the required team members.
opzioni.C: Take the matter to the project sponsor.
opzioni.D: Use their legitimate power by informing the organization that they will not perform the project without the needed resources.

domande.spiegazione: A project manager's power is considerably low in a weak matrix organization. In fact, they are rather considered a coordinator or an expediter (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 22). It’s up to the functional manager to assign resources in such organizations. Therefore, the only solution to obtain the needed resources in this situation is by negotiating your requirements with the functional manager.

domande.domanda:
The stakeholder engagement process involves five steps. What is their logical sequencing according to the figure below? [La figura mostra 4 caselle A-B-C-D in sequenza]
⚠️ Nell'esportazione Udemy manca l'immagine (grafico/tabella) a cui fa riferimento la domanda.

opzioni.A: A. Identify, B. Engage, C. Understand & analyze, D. Monitor
opzioni.B: A. Identify, B. Understand & analyze, C. Engage, D. Monitor
opzioni.C: A. Identify, B. Monitor, C. Understand & analyze, D. Engage
opzioni.D: A. Understand & analyze, B. Identify, C. Engage, D. Monitor

domande.spiegazione:
A. Identify B. Understand & analyze C. Engage D. Monitor
Stakeholder engagement starts by identifying all parties directly or indirectly connected or involved in the project. Next, the identified stakeholders must be fully understood in terms of their beliefs, attitudes, expectations, etc., towards the project in order to be able to analyze each one’s level of power, interest, impact, etc., and prioritize them accordingly. After that, an engagement plan is created according to the findings of the previous steps, where a project manager should ensure clear and constant communication, the satisfaction of stakeholders’ requirements and expectations, and issue resolution when needed. Monitoring stakeholders is the final step in the process, and it entails monitoring any changes in their attitudes or power levels to adapt the engagement plan accordingly.
domande.motivo_incertezza: immagine della domanda non presente nell'esportazione

domande.domanda:
A project is developing a new inventory management system for a regional retail chain with 45 stores. During the planning phase, the regional operations director raises concerns that the identified resources, particularly the number of experienced system integrators, are insufficient to meet the 9-month go-live deadline. Another stakeholder shares the regional operations director's concern and begins to question the viability of the original plan.
What should the project manager do first?

opzioni.A: Review the boundaries of stakeholder negotiations to determine how much flexibility exists in securing additional system integrators from external vendors.
opzioni.B: Reassess the project's core objectives, scope, and schedule to determine which deliverables are essential versus which could be deferred or simplified.
opzioni.C: Initiate negotiations with resource managers to secure the additional system integrators needed to fulfill the original 9-month plan.
opzioni.D: Conduct a comprehensive feasibility analysis comparing the current resource capacity against the full scope, schedule, and quality requirements.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Reviewing negotiation boundaries assumes that additional resources are the solution. However, the project manager does not yet know if additional resources are needed: the feasibility analysis must come first. The project manager should first determine if the plan is achievable at all before jumping to negotiation without understanding the full gap.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Reassessing core objectives, scope, and schedule may be part of the solution, but it is narrower than what is needed. The project manager must assess all dimensions: including resource capacity, quality requirements, and cost, not just scope and schedule.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Initiating negotiations immediately is premature. Sourcing decisions should be based on analysis, not assumptions. The project manager does not yet know if additional resources are needed, what type of resources are required, or whether the schedule or scope could be adjusted instead. This option assumes additional resources are the only solution without conducting the necessary analysis.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. When resource concerns threaten project viability, the project manager must conduct a comprehensive analysis comparing resource capacity against scope, schedule, and quality requirements. A comprehensive feasibility analysis will reveal whether the plan is achievable or whether adjustments are needed.

domande.spiegazione: When resource concerns threaten project viability, the project manager must conduct a comprehensive analysis comparing resource capacity against scope, schedule, and quality requirements. A comprehensive feasibility analysis will reveal whether the plan is achievable or whether adjustments are needed.

domande.domanda:
A project is developing a new patient records system for a regional healthcare network. The quality management plan requires that all software modules undergo a technical quality review at least 5 business days before the scheduled integration deadline. The project manager discovers that four consecutive modules have failed to meet this requirement, with reviews being completed only 1-2 days before integration. The quality manager has flagged this as a recurring breakdown in the quality review process.
What should the project manager do first?

opzioni.A: Generate a cause-and-effect diagram to systematically identify the root causes of the recurring quality review delays across the four modules.
opzioni.B: Revise the quality management plan to reflect more achievable review timelines based on the team's demonstrated performance and current capacity.
opzioni.C: Commission an internal quality audit to assess whether the project's quality processes are being followed consistently across all workstreams.
opzioni.D: Analyze the schedule to identify which upcoming modules are most likely to miss the quality review requirement and implement additional monitoring controls for those modules.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. When a recurring process problem is identified, the project manager should first seek to understand its underlying causes before implementing corrective actions. A cause-and-effect diagram (fishbone diagram) is a quality management tool used to identify and organize potential causes of a problem. It helps the team investigate factors related to people, processes, tools, resources, scheduling, communication, governance, etc. Before changing plans, conducting audits, or adding controls, the project manager should determine why the delays are occurring.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Revising the quality management plan assumes that the quality review requirement is unrealistic. However, the scenario provides no evidence that the 5-day review requirement is inappropriate. The issue may stem from poor planning, resource constraints, late deliverables, ineffective coordination, lack of accountability, etc.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. A quality audit can be useful, but it is not the best first step. An audit evaluates compliance with processes and identifies opportunities for improvement. However, before launching a formal audit, the project manager should first analyze the recurring issue to understand what is causing it. The scenario already indicates that the process is not being followed consistently. The immediate need is to identify why this is happening.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Analyzing the schedule to identify which upcoming modules are most likely to miss the quality review requirement and implementing additional monitoring controls for those modules is proactive and focuses on preventing future occurrences. However, it addresses symptoms rather than causes. Additional monitoring may help detect future delays earlier, but it does not explain why the delays have occurred repeatedly. If the underlying cause remains unresolved, the problem may continue despite increased oversight.

domande.spiegazione: When a recurring process problem is identified, the project manager should first seek to understand its underlying causes before implementing corrective actions. A cause-and-effect diagram (fishbone diagram) is a quality management tool used to identify and organize potential causes of a problem. It helps the team investigate factors related to people, processes, tools, resources, scheduling, communication, governance, etc. Before changing plans, conducting audits, or adding controls, the project manager should determine why the delays are occurring.

domande.domanda:
A construction project manager secured stakeholder agreement on a 20-month project life cycle for a new regional hospital wing. During project execution at month 8, the stakeholders collectively request that the project be completed within 16 months to align with a new government funding deadline. The project is currently on schedule and within budget.
What should the project manager do first?

opzioni.A: Facilitate negotiations with stakeholders to identify which project requirements could be reduced or deferred to make the compressed 16-month timeline achievable.
opzioni.B: Conduct an integrated impact assessment analyzing the effects of the 4-month compression on scope, cost, quality, safety, and contractual obligations.
opzioni.C: Accelerate delivery by adding additional construction crews to critical path activities to increase work capacity and shorten the overall timeline to 16 months.
opzioni.D: Advise stakeholders against modifying the timeline and document the risks and consequences associated with the proposed compression in the risk register.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Reducing scope may ultimately become part of the solution, but it is premature to begin negotiating scope trade-offs before understanding the overall impact of the requested schedule change. The project manager does not yet know whether scope reduction is necessary, how much scope would need to be removed, whether other schedule compression strategies could achieve the objective, or what impacts would occur in other project domains.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. When stakeholders request a significant change to a project baseline, the project manager should first evaluate the impact of the proposed change before determining a response. Reducing the schedule by four months could affect scope delivery, cost, resource requirements, contractual commitments, risk exposure, etc. Before recommending schedule compression techniques, negotiating scope reductions, or accepting/rejecting the request, the project manager should conduct an integrated impact assessment to understand the full implications of the proposed change.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Accelerating delivery by adding additional construction crews to critical path activities means immediately implementing a solution before determining whether it is appropriate. Adding resources (crashing) is a schedule compression technique, but the project manager has not yet assessed cost implications, resource availability, safety impacts, etc. The project manager should evaluate options before selecting and implementing a corrective action.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Advising stakeholders against modifying the timeline assumes the requested change is undesirable before performing an analysis. Stakeholders may have a legitimate business reason for accelerating the project. The project manager's role is not to immediately oppose the request but to evaluate it objectively and provide decision-makers with accurate impact information. Documenting risks may eventually be appropriate, but the first step is understanding the overall impact of the proposed change.

domande.spiegazione: When stakeholders request a significant change to a project baseline, the project manager should first evaluate the impact of the proposed change before determining a response. Reducing the schedule by four months could affect scope delivery, cost, resource requirements, contractual commitments, risk exposure, etc. Before recommending schedule compression techniques, negotiating scope reductions, or accepting/rejecting the request, the project manager should conduct an integrated impact assessment to understand the full implications of the proposed change.

domande.domanda:
Case study I
A manufacturing organization is undertaking a project to retrofit an existing chemical processing facility with new emissions control technology. The project has a budget of $8.5 million and a planned duration of 14 months. The facility operates under multiple regulatory frameworks, including environmental protection laws, occupational health and safety standards, and industry-specific security regulations.
The project charter references a business case that includes compliance as a key success criterion. However, the charter does not specify which compliance categories apply or how compliance will be verified.
Question 1 (Case study I)
The project manager has now begun the planning activities. The project team disagrees on whether a new security requirement (biometric access control for the control room) is a regulatory compliance item or an organizational policy compliance item. The distinction affects budget allocation and schedule priority.
What should the project manager do first?

opzioni.A: Involve the steering committee in the classification decision, since regulatory interpretation requires executive authority.
opzioni.B: Defer the classification decision until after the project is in execution, when more information about security threats will be available.
opzioni.C: Consult EEFs and OPAs to determine whether the requirement is externally or internally mandated.
opzioni.D: Classify the requirement as organizational policy compliance to avoid triggering additional regulatory reporting requirements.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The steering committee can be involved in strategic decisions, but routine classification of compliance requirements is within the project manager's purview. Premature escalation contradicts empowered decision-making at the appropriate level. The steering committee should be engaged for decisions that exceed the project manager's authority or those that have a strategic impact.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Activities planning should be completed before execution to establish baselines. Deferring classification would lead to ambiguous scope, unclear budget allocation, and potential rework. Proactive risk identification is required during planning, not reactive classification during execution.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. The project manager should consult Organizational Process Assets (OPAs) and EEFs to determine whether biometric access control is externally mandated (e.g., by chemical facility security regulations) or internally mandated (organizational security policy). The classification then informs budget allocation, schedule priority, and change control rigor. This approach follows evidence-based decision-making.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Misclassifying a regulatory requirement as an optional organizational policy could lead to regulatory non-compliance, fines, and project shutdown. The project manager should work on accurately identifying and classifying compliance requirements.

domande.spiegazione: The project manager should consult Organizational Process Assets (OPAs) and EEFs to determine whether biometric access control is externally mandated (e.g., by chemical facility security regulations) or internally mandated (organizational security policy). The classification then informs budget allocation, schedule priority, and change control rigor. This approach follows evidence-based decision-making.

Case study I
A manufacturing organization is undertaking a project to retrofit an existing chemical processing facility with new emissions control technology. The project has a budget of $8.5 million and a planned duration of 14 months. The facility operates under multiple regulatory frameworks, including environmental protection laws, occupational health and safety standards, and industry-specific security regulations.
Question 2 (Case study I)
The organization recently signed a sustainability pledge requiring a 25% reduction in facility carbon emissions by the end of next year. The project sponsor has asked the project manager to incorporate this into the project scope, but the pledge has not yet been formalized into organizational policy.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Postpone the sustainability pledge incorporation since it is not yet a formalized policy, and adding it would cause scope creep.
opzioni.B: Postpone the sustainability pledge incorporation until the project completion, since sustainability is not a regulatory compliance category.
opzioni.C: Assess the potential schedule, cost, and design impacts of the sustainability pledge before determining whether it should be incorporated.
opzioni.D: Treat the sustainability pledge as an emerging EEF and initiate a change request to update the scope baseline.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The sponsor is requesting inclusion. Postponing the sustainability pledge incorporation ignores the sponsor's authority and the organization's strategic sustainability commitments. Scope change is not inherently negative if it adds value and is properly managed through change control.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Postponing the sustainability pledge incorporation until the project completion could result in a deliverable that fails to meet organizational commitments.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Impact assessment is an important part of change evaluation, but the project manager should not independently decide whether the pledge should affect the scope. The sponsor has already requested the incorporation of the requirement. The appropriate next step is to initiate the formal change process, during which impact analysis will occur.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Although it has not yet been formalized into policy, the sustainability pledge is an emerging Enterprise Environmental Factor (EEF). Since the sponsor wants the project scope updated, the project manager should follow the formal change management process by submitting a change request and assessing the impact on the project baselines before implementation.

domande.spiegazione: Although it has not yet been formalized into policy, the sustainability pledge is an emerging Enterprise Environmental Factor (EEF). Since the sponsor wants the project scope updated, the project manager should follow the formal change management process by submitting a change request and assessing the impact on the project baselines before implementation.
