opzioni.C: Review the suggestion and set quality checkpoints.
opzioni.D: Allow the team to implement the AI suggestion since it helps optimize workflow efficiency.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Waiting until the final phase may be too late to address strategic misalignment or risks.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Proactive review is needed even if the AI doesn’t flag a problem.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. The project manager should review the suggestion to ensure alignment with project strategy and stakeholder expectations. The project manager must serve as the human-in-the-loop during key decision points, quality checkpoints, and when AI suggestions could impact strategy or stakeholder deliverables (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 243).
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Efficiency doesn’t override the need for managerial oversight on decisions that affect strategic direction.

domande.spiegazione: The project manager should review the suggestion to ensure alignment with project strategy and stakeholder expectations. The project manager must serve as the human-in-the-loop during key decision points, quality checkpoints, and when AI suggestions could impact strategy or stakeholder deliverables (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 243).

domande.domanda:
A project manager is leading a software project using a predictive approach. During execution, a team member developed a new feature that caused regressions on the other features already used by the client.
What should the project manager do? (Select three)

opzioni.A: Submit a change request to fix the resulting regressions.
opzioni.B: Inform the concerned stakeholders about the regressions, their impact, and the proposed solutions.
opzioni.C: Set up a lessons-learned meeting to avoid similar issues in the future.
opzioni.D: Since it’s an internal problem, try to fix it without the customer’s notice.
opzioni.E: Ignore the regressions and focus on completing the project as scheduled.

domande.spiegazione:
When issues occur, the right course of action implies informing the client of what happened, suggesting potential solutions for the issue, and then submitting a change request. This is aligned with the philosophy stating “Don’t bring me problems, bring me solutions” (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 179). Later on, when the issue is fixed, a lessons-learned meeting should be conducted to avoid similar problems in the future.
Option D: Holding the information and not updating the customer on what’s going on with the project can have a bad impact, both on the project and its manager’s transparency.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is responsible for leading a hybrid project with remote team members dispersed across four continents. As a result, the team has experienced communication issues.
What can the project manager do to alleviate the team’s communication challenges? (Select two)

opzioni.A: Set up remote pairing.
opzioni.B: Use an agile approach for the project.
opzioni.C: Colocate the team.
opzioni.D: Create fishbowl windows.

domande.spiegazione:
Fishbowl windows and remote pairing are two techniques used to manage communication in remote teams. The project manager can create fishbowl windows by initiating long-lived video conferences, where team members join in at the beginning of the workday and leave at the end. Remote pairing, on the other hand, is when two or more people join an online event at a specific time to discuss and share screens when needed (Agile Practice Guide, page 46).
Option C: Colocating the team is not always feasible due to many considerations, such as cost, talent availability, regulations, etc. However, when possible, getting the team together in person on a regular basis is a good practice.
Option B: Changing the project life cycle from hybrid to agile won't have any significant impact on communication if team members don't take any specific measures or techniques to improve the way they interact with each other.

domande.domanda:
A project manager developed the Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) by decomposing the work into three levels. The supportive PMO points out that three levels are not enough and recommends breaking down project work into five levels instead.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Take into consideration the PMO’s recommendation and decompose work as needed.
opzioni.B: Establish common ground by decomposing the WBS into four levels instead.
opzioni.C: Since the PMO has a high level of control, the project manager should decompose the WBS into five levels as recommended.
opzioni.D: Since the PMO has a low level of control, the project manager should ignore their request and keep the WBS decomposition levels at three.

domande.spiegazione:
The details and level of decomposition of the Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) depend on the project size, complexity, and level of control needed to effectively manage the project.
Options B, C, D: There’s no standard or predefined number of decomposition levels. A supportive PMO has limited control over the project, meaning the project manager should consider their advice and recommendations, but is not required to follow them.

domande.domanda:
A project manager used the Expected Monetary Value method to determine the contingency reserve for the new industrial project. During the execution phase, the project manager updated the probability of occurrence in the risk register as follows:
According to the project manager’s updates, how much is left in the contingency reserve? [Dati ricostruiti dalla spiegazione: riserva di contingenza totale (somma degli EMV) = $6,000; il Rischio 1 si è già verificato con impatto di $5,000]
⚠️ Nell'esportazione Udemy manca l'immagine (grafico/tabella) a cui fa riferimento la domanda.
domande.spiegazione: According to the risk register table, the project’s contingency reserve is $6,000 (the sum of all risks’ Expected Monetary Values). During the execution phase, this reserve will be used when the identified risks occur. Risk 1 has already taken place, so $5,000 has already been spent (risk impact). Therefore, only $1,000 is left in the contingency reserve ($6,000 - $5,000).
domande.motivo_incertezza: immagine della domanda non presente nell'esportazione

domande.domanda:
A project manager is in charge of a two-hour concert where a playlist of 20 songs will be performed. One hour into the concert, the project manager finds out that the band has only played 8 songs.
What should the project manager do next?

opzioni.A: Ask the band to hurry up so that they can finish performing all 20 songs before the concert ends.
opzioni.B: Ask the band to only play 8 more songs.
opzioni.C: Perform all 20 songs even if it takes longer than expected.
opzioni.D: Gather more data before making any decision.

domande.spiegazione: The project manager needs to gather more data before making any decisions. The fact that only 8 songs were performed doesn’t mean that they are behind schedule since song durations may differ. The project manager is in the process of monitoring and controlling the project work, so they need to deploy the data analysis technique on the gathered data. In this scenario, they should first check the list of remaining songs and their durations in order to verify whether or not the project is on schedule.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is facing some struggles after joining a new company; her superiors noticed that during a kick-off meeting, she had difficulty answering questions about how the project fits in with the organization’s objectives.
What critical skill is the project manager lacking?

opzioni.A: Business acumen
opzioni.B: Ways of working
opzioni.C: Results
opzioni.D: Power skills

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. The competencies that project management team members should possess include: Ways of Working, Power Skills, Business Acumen, Social responsibilities, and Results. A project manager possessing business acumen skills should be able to explain the business value of their project and how it aligns with the organization’s goals (PMBOK 8th Edition, pages 30-31).
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Ways of working competency includes the understanding and application of the standards, methodologies, and frameworks that a project management team may use to execute projects and add value to the organization.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Results is a competency that refers to the actual work and execution of ideas and projects to add value. The ability to accomplish tasks is a central competency that helps ensure the expected value is delivered.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Power skills include all the people skills that a project management team should apply to successfully execute the project (e.g., adaptability and Emotional Intelligence).

domande.spiegazione: The competencies that project management team members should possess include: Ways of Working, Power Skills, Business Acumen, Social responsibilities, and Results. A project manager possessing business acumen skills should be able to explain the business value of their project and how it aligns with the organization’s goals (PMBOK 8th Edition, pages 30-31).

domande.domanda:
During work execution, a project manager faced an issue that required a deviation from the scope. The project manager discussed the matter with the rest of the team and provided the Change Control Board (CCB) with a plan on how to approach the alteration. The CCB recognized the need for the change, but they approved a different implementation method that the project manager didn’t agree with.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Resign from their position and quit the project.
opzioni.B: Refrain from implementing the change.
opzioni.C: Implement the change using the approved method.
opzioni.D: Create a prototype using the rejected method to convince the CCB of its efficiency.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The project manager has to follow the integrated change control processes and should not take the matter personally. Therefore, resigning or quitting the project would be unprofessional.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Since the project manager wasn’t able to convince the CCB through the elaborated and submitted plan, they can’t refrain from implementing the change.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. The CCB’s decision should be respected, and the project manager has to comply with it by implementing the change using the approved method.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Creating a prototype using the rejected implementation method is considered scope creep since this work was neither requested by the client nor included in the scope statement.

domande.spiegazione: The CCB’s decision should be respected, and the project manager has to comply with it by implementing the change using the approved method.

domande.domanda:
During a daily stand-up meeting, the Scrum master heard one of the team members say that they worked on additional functionality that was not described in the user story. The team member went on about how the client would appreciate the extra feature.
What should the Scrum master do?

opzioni.A: Thank the team member for the initiative and inform the client of the newly added functionality.
opzioni.B: Ask the team member to add the extra feature to the sprint backlog as a separate item and mark it as done.
opzioni.C: Ask the team member to remove the functionality and recommend that the project team stick to the requirements.
opzioni.D: Nothing, since the role of a Scrum master is to remove impediments rather than direct the team.

domande.spiegazione:
Regardless of the team member’s intentions, adding functionality that was not included in the initial requirements is considered scope creep. Consequently, the Scrum master should ask the team member to remove the added functionality and make sure that the team is creating the product as per the requirements described in the user stories. Scope creep is not always caused by the client; it can also originate from the team itself, similar to this case, where a task beyond what is required is added because the developer believes it would bring value.
Option D: In addition to removing impediments, the Scrum master has to coach the team and guide them through the right processes and practices. In this case, the team member can create a new item in the product backlog (not the sprint backlog) and the product owner can prioritize it in the upcoming sprints if they approve that it has added value indeed.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is leading a project to launch an AI-powered language learning platform for university students. The remote project team includes a UX designer, a data scientist, a QA engineer, and a marketing strategist. Due to the geographic spread, team coordination proves to be challenging for the project manager.
What should the project manager do? (Select three answers)

opzioni.A: Where possible, use time zone differences to increase overall efficiency.
opzioni.B: Always set team meetings for the first thing in the morning in his location.
opzioni.C: Keep a record of each team member’s time zone and communicate accordingly.
opzioni.D: Involve everyone in setting suitable meeting times, given time zone differences.
opzioni.E: Require every team member to work over the same block of time, regardless of what time it is in their region.

domande.spiegazione:
A. The project manager can use time zone differences to increase overall efficiency; e.g., he can assign tasks so that one team member finishes documentation by the evening according to their local time, and another team member picks it up first thing in their morning, allowing for 24-hour work cycles that boost productivity.
C. By keeping a detailed record of time zones, the project manager ensures that important messages aren’t sent during off-hours, preventing delays in critical communications.
D. When scheduling planning meetings, the project manager should consult all team members to find overlapping windows that respect local working hours.
Option B: Holding meetings early in the morning in one location may force other team members to join late at night, for example, creating frustration and inefficiency.
Option E: Forcing team members to work over the same block of time, regardless of what time it is in their region, would create fatigue and resentment, undermining team morale and violating best practices in remote team management.

domande.domanda:
When they facilitate the sprint planning, the project manager ensures that every story has a checklist that includes the testing activities. However, after a few iterations, the project manager notices that most of the time, the development team does not conduct any testing, causing stories to remain open for a long time.
What should the project manager do first?

opzioni.A: Separate the testing activities from the user stories.
opzioni.B: Have a separate QA team perform the testing at the end of each iteration.
opzioni.C: Discuss the issue with the team during the sprint retrospective meeting.
opzioni.D: Schedule training for the team on how to perform testing activities.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Separating testing activities from user stories is not correct because the “definition of done” could include testing.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Having a separate QA team contradicts the fact that the Agile team should be cross-functional.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. During the sprint retrospective, the project manager goes over what went well during the sprint and what should be improved. It’s best to address any problems during this meeting to identify the root causes and come up with the right action plan (PMBOK 8th Edition, pages 194-195).
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Scheduling training could be an option if the team lacks testing knowledge; however, this should be confirmed after discussing the issue with the team during the retrospective, since the problem could have other reasons, such as inaccurate estimations.

domande.spiegazione: During the sprint retrospective, the project manager goes over what went well during the sprint and what should be improved. It’s best to address any problems during this meeting to identify the root causes and come up with the right action plan (PMBOK 8th Edition, pages 194-195).

domande.domanda:
A project manager is assigned to lead a marketing project for a political party. During a phone call with the party representative, the latter requested adding social media advertisements to the project. The project manager informed the representative that this would cost an additional $8,000, to which the representative agreed. However, when the project manager sent the invoice including the requested service fees, the representative refused to pay the additional cost, claiming that the project had an unacceptable delay that should’ve been penalized.
What should the project manager have done to avoid this situation? (Select two)

opzioni.A: The project manager should have chosen a more appropriate communication channel.
opzioni.B: The project manager should have reduced the scope to balance the cost of the additional service.
opzioni.C: The project manager should have requested a lower price for the additional service.
opzioni.D: The project manager should have requested an extension of the project schedule to accommodate the additional work.

domande.spiegazione:
This situation could have been avoided if the project manager had used formal communication when discussing and approving changes to the contract terms. A phone call is considered informal communication, which means that any decisions made over the phone mainly rely on mutual trust since there is no written record of the discussion or any ensuing decisions.
Furthermore, the project manager only analyzed the impact of the change on cost and did not thoroughly consider its impact on the project’s scope, time, and resources. Therefore, the representative used the project’s “unacceptable delay” as an excuse not to pay for the additional service he requested.

domande.domanda:
A technology firm is developing a new cloud-based platform for small businesses. The project is governed by strict internal policies and procedures, including compliance with data privacy regulations. During a recent audit, it was discovered that one of the project teams had implemented features that did not comply with these regulations, potentially exposing the company to legal risks.
What should the project manager have done differently to prevent this issue?

opzioni.A: Rely solely on the development team to ensure compliance with internal policies.
opzioni.B: Ensure thorough training and awareness of organizational governance policies among all project teams.
opzioni.C: Ignore the non-compliance claims since the project was completed on time and within budget.
opzioni.D: Hold the quality assurance team accountable for not catching the issue earlier.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Relying solely on the development team to ensure compliance is insufficient. Project managers are responsible for ensuring that all teams understand and adhere to organizational governance policies.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Providing thorough training and awareness of organizational governance policies ensures that all project teams understand their responsibilities regarding compliance, ethics, and risk management.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Ignoring non-compliant features exposes the organization to significant legal and reputational risks. Compliance is a critical aspect of project success.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Holding the quality assurance team accountable shifts responsibility away from the project manager, who is ultimately accountable for ensuring compliance throughout the project lifecycle.

domande.spiegazione: Providing thorough training and awareness of organizational governance policies ensures that all project teams understand their responsibilities regarding compliance, ethics, and risk management.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is assigned to lead a big project, with a key portion requiring outsourcing to a service provider. To reduce risk, the project manager wants to ensure that the selected provider is well-suited to the project and quality requirements before granting the whole contract.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Hire an auditor to continuously check the quality of the provider’s work.
opzioni.B: Make the contract flexible in order to be able to replace the provider easily if quality is not met.
opzioni.C: Carefully choose the selection criteria.
opzioni.D: Ask the service provider to do a trial engagement.

domande.spiegazione:
Some projects engage several candidate sellers for initial paid work before making the full commitment to one seller. This allows the buyer to evaluate potential partners while simultaneously making progress on project work.
Options A, B, C: These options could help select the best provider, and manage their work and contractual relationship. However, the scenario is directly related to the concept of doing a trial.

domande.domanda:
During a software development project, the project manager conducts a comprehensive assessment of the project team's performance. The evaluation reveals that several team members have consistently underperformed in their assigned tasks, impacting project progress and outcomes.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Establish a new performance metric based on project requirements to evaluate team members' effectiveness.
opzioni.B: Tailor the team management method based on each member's motivators and skill sets to address performance gaps.
opzioni.C: Implement a standardized feedback mechanism to provide constructive feedback to all team members.
opzioni.D: Provide intensive oversight to the underperforming team members to ensure the efficient completion of their assigned tasks.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Creating a new standard performance measure may not address the root causes of underperformance.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Developing different methods based on team members' motivation and ability helps the project manager provide efficient guidance and support. By understanding each team member's unique strengths, weaknesses, and motivational factors, the project manager can tailor management strategies to address performance issues while fostering a supportive team environment.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. While implementing a feedback mechanism is important for promoting transparency and accountability, a standardized feedback mechanism may not effectively address the specific performance challenges faced by individual team members.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Providing intensive oversight to underperforming team members may lead to micromanagement and undermine trust within the team.

domande.spiegazione: Developing different methods based on team members' motivation and ability helps the project manager provide efficient guidance and support. By understanding each team member's unique strengths, weaknesses, and motivational factors, the project manager can tailor management strategies to address performance issues while fostering a supportive team environment.

domande.domanda:
During the sprint planning meeting, the product owner discovered that only a few user stories were ready for the upcoming sprint, while the rest still needed refinement. The product owner got nervous because the meeting would not be long enough to finish planning the new sprint, which starts the following day.
How could the product owner have avoided such a situation?

opzioni.A: Through setting up backlog refinement meetings with the development team throughout the sprint.
opzioni.B: By requesting the development team to take responsibility for refining user stories before the planning session.
opzioni.C: By requesting the Scrum master to take responsibility for refining user stories before the planning session.
opzioni.D: The product owner did nothing wrong in this situation. They should just include user stories that are ready, and complete refining the remaining stories during the sprint.

domande.spiegazione: It’s the responsibility of the product owner to lead backlog refinement meetings. During one or more mid-sprint sessions, the product owner should collaborate with the team in order to prepare the user stories for the upcoming sprints (Agile Practice Guide, page 52).

domande.domanda:
A project manager is leading a four-year project using a predictive approach. The initial budget of the project is $1,000,000. At the end of the first year, the steering committee asked the project manager to share a diagram showing how much funding was spent each month.
Which data representation technique should the project manager use?

opzioni.A: Burndown chart
opzioni.B: Burnup chart
opzioni.C: Histogram
opzioni.D: Gantt chart

domande.spiegazione:
The project manager can use a histogram as a graphical representation of numerical data (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 268).
Options A & B: The steering committee asked for the amounts spent each month rather than the total spending or the monthly remaining funds. Thus, neither burnup nor burndown charts can be used.
Option D: Gantt charts are used to illustrate the project schedule and not the budget (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 268).

domande.domanda:
A project manager is leading a government-funded healthcare IT project. To save time on stakeholder reporting, a team member suggests using a GenAI tool to automatically generate status updates. The tool can produce polished summaries from raw project data, but it sometimes fills in missing data with unverified content. The sponsor is impressed by the quality of the reports and urges the project manager to continue using them without manual review, claiming “the small details won’t matter.”
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Inform the sponsor that using AI-generated reports without validation risks misrepresenting the project's true status.
opzioni.B: Continue using the tool without review, since it enhances efficiency and stakeholder satisfaction.
opzioni.C: Manually edit only the most important sections of the report to reduce review time while decreasing the risk of inaccuracy.
opzioni.D: Instruct the team to rely on GenAI for future reports and add a disclaimer about potential inaccuracies.

domande.spiegazione:
Informing the sponsor that using AI-generated reports without validation risks misrepresenting the project's true status aligns with PMI’s principles of Honesty (truthful reporting), Responsibility (ensuring ethical use of tools), and Respect (for stakeholders who rely on accurate data).
Options B & C: Continue using the tool without review, since it enhances efficiency and stakeholder satisfaction, or manually editing only the most important sections prioritizes convenience over integrity, risking misleading information.
Option D: Instructing the team to rely on GenAI for future reports and adding a disclaimer about potential inaccuracies shifts responsibility rather than ensuring the output is valid.

domande.domanda:
A project manager gets assigned to a software development project that requires a specialized programming skill set that is currently in high demand in the job market. Additionally, due to the fast-paced evolution of the programming language, finding and retaining skilled individuals has become increasingly difficult.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Opt for an alternative analysis to explore the different options and allocate a sufficient cost reserve to mitigate risks associated with the high turnover rate.
opzioni.B: Develop the software using a more common programming language.
opzioni.C: Mitigate the risk by enrolling the entire team in a bootcamp to learn the specialized programming skill set.
opzioni.D: Raise a risk to project completion due to the threat posed by the required skill set scarcity.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. The project manager is facing high levels of volatility. Volatility exists in an environment that is subject to rapid and unpredictable change. Volatility can occur when there are ongoing fluctuations in available skill sets or materials. Volatility usually impacts cost and schedule. Alternative analysis and use of cost or schedule reserve address volatility. By conducting an alternative analysis, the project manager evaluates different strategies for addressing the skill scarcity challenges. Allocating a cost reserve allows the project to adapt to unforeseen circumstances, such as hiring difficulties or technology changes, without compromising project objectives.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Switching to a different programming language may introduce additional complexity and compromise the project's ability to meet its objectives.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. While investing in team skill development is recommended, this may not be feasible given the urgency of project needs. Additionally, expecting the entire team to acquire a specialized skill set may delay project progress and strain team resources. It also fails to address the immediate need for the skillset and may not be sustainable in the long term.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. While identifying risks is essential, simply raising a risk without proposing mitigation strategies will not effectively address the encountered challenge.

domande.spiegazione: The project manager is facing high levels of volatility. Volatility exists in an environment that is subject to rapid and unpredictable change. Volatility can occur when there are ongoing fluctuations in available skill sets or materials. Volatility usually impacts cost and schedule. Alternative analysis and use of cost or schedule reserve address volatility. By conducting an alternative analysis, the project manager evaluates different strategies for addressing the skill scarcity challenges. Allocating a cost reserve allows the project to adapt to unforeseen circumstances, such as hiring difficulties or technology changes, without compromising project objectives.

domande.domanda:
A project manager who works at a web agency suggests creating a dropshipping e-commerce project since it’s profitable. Her manager, on the other hand, doesn’t fully agree.
What should the project manager do to persuade her manager?

opzioni.A: Calculate the project’s Cost Performance Index.
opzioni.B: Conduct a SWOT Analysis.
opzioni.C: Calculate the project’s Budget at Completion.
opzioni.D: Calculate the project’s Cost-Benefit Ratio.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The Cost Performance Index is a measure of the cost efficiency of budgeted resources, calculated as the ratio of earned value to actual cost. It is used to assess the cost performance of a project that is already in progress. Since the project in question has not yet started, calculating the CPI is not applicable (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 208).
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. SWOT Analysis can provide valuable insights into the potential advantages and challenges of the project (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 204). However, it does not offer a quantitative measure of profitability or financial viability, which is crucial for persuading the manager.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The Budget at Completion (BAC) is the total budget allocated for the project (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 207). While knowing the BAC is important for project planning and control, it does not provide information about the potential benefits or profitability of the project. Therefore, it is not sufficient to persuade the manager about the project's profitability.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. To persuade her manager to select the project, the project manager should use the Cost-Benefit Ratio to demonstrate the project's profitability.

domande.spiegazione: To persuade her manager to select the project, the project manager should use the Cost-Benefit Ratio to demonstrate the project's profitability.

domande.domanda:
An organization is used to following the Scrum framework where sprints are 4 weeks long. One day, the organization’s Chief Technology Officer (CTO) approached the Scrum master and argued that a 4-week sprint was too long and it would be better to reduce it to 2 weeks.
Convinced by the CTO’s suggestion, how could the Scrum Master make this change?

opzioni.A: Announce to the entire Scrum team that the CTO, who has formal power, has decided that the sprint should only last 2 weeks.
opzioni.B: Let the product owner and the team members know about the intention to reduce the sprint length and involve them in the decision.
opzioni.C: Inform the team of the sprint length change during the sprint retrospective and provide them with arguments.
opzioni.D: Engage an agile coach to assist in this transition since having someone external to the team will most likely reduce any resistance.

domande.spiegazione:
The Scrum master needs to make sure to involve the entire team or whoever the change is likely to impact when tailoring a process (Agile Practice Guide, page 120). The buy-in from the team will suffer significantly if one person defines the process, especially if they are from outside the team, such as an agile coach.
Option A: The organization’s CTO gave a personal suggestion and not a formal order.

domande.domanda:
After taking over a project, the project manager noticed that team members were not interacting and collaborating with each other as they were supposed to.
What team-building activities could the project manager opt for? (Select two)

opzioni.A: Purchase gym memberships for all team members and let them choose the gym and training hours that work best for them.
opzioni.B: Buy a ping pong table and allow the team to use it during breaks.
opzioni.C: Go hiking with the project team.
opzioni.D: Offer them tickets to watch new movies.

domande.spiegazione:
Buying a ping pong table or going on a hike are both considered team-building activities. Team building enhances the team’s social relations and builds a collaborative and cooperative working environment (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 205).
Options A & D: If team members go separately to the gym or the movies, there will be no interaction between them, thus interpersonal relationships will not be improved. These activities are just considered motivational factors, not team-building activities.

domande.domanda:
Leading the development of a new mobile banking application for a financial institution, the project manager and a team member, who is responsible for a critical task, have conflicting perspectives on how to approach a key deliverable. The team member feels that he’s being micromanaged, while the project manager believes the team member is not meeting expectations and delivering subpar work. The project manager gets an unexpected email from the sponsor: the latter explains that the team member is seeking her intervention.
What should the project manager do next?

opzioni.A: Sit down with both the team member and the sponsor to collaboratively resolve the issue.
opzioni.B: Ask the sponsor to remove the team member from the project team since he’s not to be trusted with confidential internal issues anymore.
opzioni.C: Discuss the situation with the functional manager to decide on the right disciplinary procedures.
opzioni.D: Initiate a conflict resolution meeting involving relevant stakeholders, including the team member, project sponsor, and other key project team members.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Sitting down with both the team member and the sponsor to collaboratively resolve the issue demonstrates a proactive approach to addressing the conflict. By facilitating an open dialogue and seeking mutual understanding, the project manager can work towards finding a resolution that satisfies both parties and aligns with project objectives.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Asking the sponsor to remove the team member from the project team can only escalate tensions further. Plus, removing the team member should only be considered if all other options for resolving the conflict have been exhausted, and if the team member's behavior is severely detrimental to project success.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The same goes for this option, which suggests discussing the situation with the functional manager to decide on the right disciplinary procedures.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Initiating a conflict resolution meeting involving relevant stakeholders allows for a structured and inclusive approach to addressing the conflict. However, involving other project team members is unnecessary at this point.

domande.spiegazione: Sitting down with both the team member and the sponsor to collaboratively resolve the issue demonstrates a proactive approach to addressing the conflict. By facilitating an open dialogue and seeking mutual understanding, the project manager can work towards finding a resolution that satisfies both parties and aligns with project objectives.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is managing an industrial project. The project manager needs a batch of 1000 custom-made identical filters for the project. Due to their high importance, the project manager chooses a reliable and well-known supplier to produce these filters.
Knowing that a tested filter should be thrown away since it couldn’t be reutilized, what should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Skip inspection since the project manager trusts that the supplier will deliver the filters according to the specifications
opzioni.B: Order more than 1000 filters to perform acceptance sampling on the batch surplus
opzioni.C: Require the seller to provide a conformance certificate of the filter’s raw materials
opzioni.D: Conduct a 100% inspection upon delivery, then order another batch of 1000 filters if he’s satisfied with the quality

domande.spiegazione: When conducting a 100% inspection is not possible, the project manager should opt for the sampling of a certain number from a batch (also known as a lot) of the items and perform an inspection on the sample. Since tested filters cannot be used for the project, the best course of action is to order more than the required items in order to perform the acceptance sampling.

domande.domanda:
During project execution, a team member who was assigned to handle a task informed the project manager that they wouldn’t be able to meet the deadline and that they would need two more days. Upon reviewing the Gantt chart, the project manager determines that the new estimate will have no impact on the critical path or the project cost.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Transfer the task to another team member who can complete it within the allocated time.
opzioni.B: Inform the team member that since the project schedule has already been approved, it won’t be possible to change it.
opzioni.C: Ask the team member to take care of updating the project schedule whenever any inaccuracy in the activities’ estimates is identified.
opzioni.D: Approve the team member’s new estimate of the activity and update the project Gantt chart accordingly.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The project manager won’t have to transfer the task to another team member due to missing the activity’s deadline.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. During the planning phase, estimations might sometimes be inaccurate for a variety of reasons. Thus, updates and adjustments are necessary during execution. If the new estimations have a significant impact on the project, a change request should be issued.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Under a predictive approach, the project manager is responsible for managing and controlling the schedule. So, the project manager should not ask the team member to update the schedule without notice, since the project manager should be aware of all schedule updates.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Since the new activity’s estimate has no significant impact on the project, the best course of action in this situation is to approve it and update the project Gantt chart accordingly.

domande.spiegazione: Since the new activity’s estimate has no significant impact on the project, the best course of action in this situation is to approve it and update the project Gantt chart accordingly.

domande.domanda:
A project manager has recently been assigned to a new project. After checking the requirements, the project manager decided that Kanban is the ideal Agile framework to use. However, the project team is unfamiliar with kanban.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Refrain from using Kanban since the team is not familiar with it.
opzioni.B: Explain Kanban during the first iteration planning meeting.
opzioni.C: Assign training sessions for the team to learn about Kanban in practice.
opzioni.D: Ask team members to learn Kanban practices using their own means.

domande.spiegazione: This situation implies that the project manager has chosen the Kanban framework for their project, which happens to be unfamiliar to their team. If they believe that this particular approach is the best fit for the project, they must ensure that the development team receives the necessary training to properly execute the project. Of the suggested scenarios, setting up training sessions would be the most consistent with servant leadership as well as agile best practices, as it will provide team members with the needed knowledge and mastery to carry out the project.

domande.domanda:
A project manager discovers a serious threat to the project; one of the project contractors might declare bankruptcy. If that happens, the project will be delayed for another two months.
What should the project manager do to mitigate the risk?

opzioni.A: Review the contract to check the consequences of any contract breach.
opzioni.B: Immediately stop working with the contractor.
opzioni.C: Contact an insurance company to secure coverage for potential losses.
opzioni.D: Contact other contractors who can supply the necessary materials.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Reviewing the contract is considered passive acceptance since no proactive action is taken to deal with the risk.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Stopping work with the contractor is not appropriate because the bankruptcy has not been confirmed, and there is no information about any replacement.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Contacting an insurance company is considered a transfer risk strategy rather than a mitigation strategy.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. The project manager should contact different vendors in order to have other alternatives ready in case the risk occurs. By doing this, the possibility of the project’s delay is reduced, i.e., Risk Mitigation.

domande.spiegazione: The project manager should contact different vendors in order to have other alternatives ready in case the risk occurs. By doing this, the possibility of the project’s delay is reduced, i.e., Risk Mitigation.

domande.domanda:
During the project charter development phase, the project manager discovered a gap in the business case; some key regulatory requirements were missing. Non-compliance with these regulations could result in legal issues. Complying with these regulations, on the other hand, could result in drastic scope changes and budget overruns.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Issue a change request to implement the needed changes for meeting regulations.
opzioni.B: Consider these findings a risk and plan a response.
opzioni.C: Start implementing the project and decide later on how to address these requirements when a better solution can be established.
opzioni.D: Inform the project sponsor of their findings.

domande.spiegazione: The project manager should immediately inform the project sponsor of their findings. The PMI's Code of Ethics requires project managers to comply with all laws and regulations. Concealing such information can lead the organization to face legal issues. In the case of a predictive project, change requests can only be issued after setting the project baseline. In the described scenario, the project is neither authorized nor baselined since it’s still in the project charter development phase.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is leading a project that involves installing 120 air conditioners in a corporate building. The project includes too many stakeholders because every office has at least one air conditioner.
What is the best course of action for the project manager to deal with the situation?

opzioni.A: Ask the project sponsor to represent all of the stakeholders.
opzioni.B: Set up an effective way to define the needs of each stakeholder.
opzioni.C: Classify stakeholders and only work with those who have high power and interest.
opzioni.D: Inform their senior management that the project should be divided into sub-projects so that it will be managed as a program instead.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The sponsor may not be available or capable of representing the stakeholders. Plus, assigning a representative for all stakeholders could lead, in some cases, to poor engagement.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. The project manager needs to implement an efficient approach to identify the needs of all project stakeholders in order to minimize any disturbing changes later during the project execution.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. No matter how many stakeholders a project has, they should all be identified and analyzed, along with their needs, as early as possible. This might be a complicated process due to the large number of stakeholders involved in this project.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Having too many stakeholders in the project shouldn’t be the reason for breaking it down into subprojects.

domande.spiegazione: The project manager needs to implement an efficient approach to identify the needs of all project stakeholders in order to minimize any disturbing changes later during the project execution.

domande.domanda:
While reviewing the latest report of the project team's performance, a project manager notices a major drop in their output.
What should the project manager do to raise the team's productivity?

opzioni.A: Increase the pressure on each team member to meet deadlines.
opzioni.B: Conduct daily performance reviews to keep the team focused and motivated.
opzioni.C: Offer a special reward for the best-performing team member.
opzioni.D: Improve and promote trust and cohesiveness among team members.

domande.spiegazione:
Improving feelings of trust and cohesiveness among team members improves productivity. Team cohesion is when people feel fulfilled and driven to achieve a common goal. Therefore, working on increasing cohesion among the team through the establishment of positive relationships, team goals, and shared values increases team members' commitment and helps boost their engagement.
Option B: Conducting daily performance reviews is excessive and time-consuming, taking away from actual work time and reducing productivity rather than improving it.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is using an incremental approach to execute a new project for creating a cutting-edge smartphone. The project is carried out by a colocated team, and work is visualized using a Kanban board. The project is progressing smoothly when a key stakeholder requests that all project activities be placed on hold until he’s provided with a status report.
What should the project manager have done to avoid this situation?

opzioni.A: Centralize project documentation in a shared folder accessible to all stakeholders.
opzioni.B: Schedule weekly meetings with all key stakeholders to provide updates on project status.
opzioni.C: Include all stakeholders in daily standup meetings.
opzioni.D: Invite key stakeholders to check the Kanban board for insights on project status.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. While storing project documentation in a shared folder might promote accessibility, not all project documents should be accessible to everyone since some might be confidential. Additionally, accessibility to project documents does not address the stakeholder's immediate need for status updates regarding ongoing project activities.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Weekly meetings with key stakeholders might be excessive and too frequent. Plus, not all stakeholders have the same availability or communication preferences. Moreover, weekly meetings do not provide timely updates or address urgent requests.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Daily standup meetings are attended by the development team and project manager, as well as the product owner in some cases. Including all stakeholders in daily meetings may not be practical or necessary for all project discussions.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Kanban boards provide clear insight into workflow, bottlenecks, blockers, and overall status. Additionally, the board acts as an information radiator to anyone who sees it, providing up-to-date information on the status of the work of the team (Agile Practice Guide, page 105).

domande.spiegazione: Kanban boards provide clear insight into workflow, bottlenecks, blockers, and overall status. Additionally, the board acts as an information radiator to anyone who sees it, providing up-to-date information on the status of the work of the team (Agile Practice Guide, page 105).

domande.domanda:
A project manager works for an organization that is used to the predictive approach. The organization’s decision-makers attended a conference about Agile and decided to adopt this approach in their upcoming projects. The project manager got worried about losing his job because, as far as he knows, an Agile team is composed of team members, a Scrum master, and a product owner. Thus, the organization will not need a project manager anymore.
Is the project manager’s concern justified?

opzioni.A: Yes, the agile team doesn’t include a project manager.
opzioni.B: Yes, the project manager should either convert to a Scrum master role or look for a new opportunity in an organization following the predictive approach.
opzioni.C: No, the project manager can work as a product owner since both roles are similar.
opzioni.D: No, he can continue working as a project manager but he will be more of a facilitator.

domande.spiegazione: In Agile, there are three common roles: cross-functional team members, product owner, and team facilitator. The team facilitator can also be called project manager, Scrum master, project team lead, or team coach. A team facilitator’s role is to remove impediments, facilitate, and coach the team. In other terms, the team facilitator should have strong servant leadership skills (Agile Practice Guide, pages 40-41).

domande.domanda:
After running a three-week sprint, an agile team examines its burndown chart.
In which area did the team’s progress suffer the most? [Dati ricostruiti dalla spiegazione: burndown diviso nelle fasi A-D; nella fase B il team passa da 27 a 22 story point rimanenti, contro i 15 previsti a fine fase]
⚠️ Nell'esportazione Udemy manca l'immagine (grafico/tabella) a cui fa riferimento la domanda.

opzioni.A: A
opzioni.B: B
opzioni.C: C
opzioni.D: D

domande.spiegazione:
In phase B, the team started with 27 story points as planned and finished with only 22 story points. They are behind by 7 story points since the forecasted progress at the end of phase B is 15 story points. Throughout this phase, the team is behind schedule, and progress is trending out. In all of the other phases, the team’s progress is either ahead of the forecasted progress or very close to the trending line.
Please note that in the real exam, such a question usually comes in the form of “click the area where…”.
domande.motivo_incertezza: immagine della domanda non presente nell'esportazione

domande.domanda:
After a project setback, a project manager observes that the team is reluctant to discuss the root causes in the retrospective meeting. The project manager wants to understand the team's dynamics and foster an environment where problems are discussed openly to prevent future issues.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Focus on process improvements to prevent another setback and maintain team morale.
opzioni.B: Use a combination of anonymous survey feedback and direct observation of team interactions.
opzioni.C: Lead a workshop on the technical causes of the setback to steer the conversation toward objective facts.
opzioni.D: Schedule a series of one-on-one meetings to gather individual perspectives before reconvening the team.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Focusing on process improvements without the team’s honest feedback and input concerning the setback can create an illusion of progress and avoid difficult conversations that might lower morale short term. Skipping a discussion of root causes risks repeating the same problems. Process changes without team buy-in or without understanding human/communication causes are likely incomplete.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. A multi-faceted approach is recommended to diagnose psychological safety. Surveys, observations, and reflection provide a more complete picture of team dynamics. An anonymous survey provides a safe channel for candid input, while observation helps the project manager understand group interaction patterns. This approach is the most comprehensive for diagnosing the root cause of the silence, whether it's a lack of psychological safety or another issue, before implementing a solution.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Technical root-cause analysis can clarify what went wrong from an engineering/process viewpoint and is useful when failures are purely technical. However, if the team is reluctant to discuss causes, the barrier is likely psychological (blame, fear, etc.), not only technical. A technically focused workshop may miss communication, decision, or responsibility issues and won’t create the interpersonal safety needed for open dialogue.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Relying only on one-on-ones is time-consuming and may produce fragmented views that are hard to reconcile. Without anonymity or group validation, some people may still withhold information. Also, private conversations can give rise to perceptions of favoritism if not handled carefully. Best used alongside an anonymous mechanism and observation, not as the sole approach.

domande.spiegazione: A multi-faceted approach is recommended to diagnose psychological safety. Surveys, observations, and reflection provide a more complete picture of team dynamics. An anonymous survey provides a safe channel for candid input, while observation helps the project manager understand group interaction patterns. This approach is the most comprehensive for diagnosing the root cause of the silence, whether it's a lack of psychological safety or another issue, before implementing a solution.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is managing a project using the predictive approach. A Change Control Board (CCB) is formed, in which the project sponsor is a member, to review all change requests. One month after the project launch, the CCB received three change requests; the first was by the sponsor, the second was by a low-power stakeholder, and the third was issued by a senior team member.
Which of these individuals is not allowed to submit a change request?

opzioni.A: The sponsor, since they are a member of the CCB.
opzioni.B: The stakeholder, since they have low power.
opzioni.C: The senior team member, since they are part of the project team.
opzioni.D: All of the above are allowed to submit a change request.

domande.spiegazione: Change requests may be submitted by any stakeholder involved with the project. The project sponsor(s), stakeholders, and the project team are all considered project stakeholders; therefore, they can all make change requests. CCB membership, power level, or involvement in project execution should not be a restriction for someone to request changes.

domande.domanda:
Working in a risk-averse organization, the project manager suggested using the agile approach for a new project that has a high level of uncertainty.
How should risk management be conducted in this case?

opzioni.A: The project manager is responsible for managing the risks.
opzioni.B: Both the project manager and the project team conduct risk analysis, determine risk responses, and update the Risk Register.
opzioni.C: The project team analyzes and addresses risks in all planning meetings.
opzioni.D: Risks are monitored by the product owner during the backlog refinement meeting.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. In Agile projects, the project team owns risk management, while the project manager is only responsible for facilitating the process.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The project team analyzes and addresses risks during planning meetings, then updates the product backlog accordingly. Risk Register is used in the predictive approach.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. When managing an Agile project, risk identification occurs in all types of planning meetings, such as daily stand-ups, release meetings, iteration reviews, and retrospectives.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Even though backlog refinement could be used to address risks, it’s not the only meeting where risks should be monitored.

domande.spiegazione: When managing an Agile project, risk identification occurs in all types of planning meetings, such as daily stand-ups, release meetings, iteration reviews, and retrospectives.

domande.domanda:
A project manager needs to facilitate a virtual brainstorming session with a globally dispersed team to generate solutions for a new market opportunity. The project manager wants to ensure all team members, including those who may be hesitant to speak up, have an equal opportunity to contribute.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Plan a Brainwriting session followed up with a group discussion.
opzioni.B: Set up a Brain-netting session.
opzioni.C: Lead a Reverse brainstorming session.
opzioni.D: Conduct a virtual Round-robin.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Brainwriting implies writing ideas down privately before sharing them with the group, which does not address the hesitation issue described in the scenario.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Brain-netting is a virtual brainstorming technique that uses a digital collaboration platform in order to generate and prioritize ideas, discussing the advantages and disadvantages of specific topics. Anonymous idea sharing can be included as well (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 149). This is the most suitable choice as it is inherently designed for a virtual, dispersed team, and its capacity for anonymity directly addresses the goal of ensuring hesitant members have an equal and safe opportunity to contribute.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Reverse brainstorming is used by teams to create ideas about how to make a problem worse instead of solving it, which is not the appropriate tool for the stated goal of generating solutions for a new market opportunity (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 150).
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. A Round-robin requires each person to contribute in turn. In a virtual setting with hesitant members, this format can create social pressure and anxiety, potentially discouraging candid contributions rather than encouraging them. It does not provide the psychological safety of anonymous contribution that Brain-netting does.

domande.spiegazione: Brain-netting is a virtual brainstorming technique that uses a digital collaboration platform in order to generate and prioritize ideas, discussing the advantages and disadvantages of specific topics. Anonymous idea sharing can be included as well (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 149). This is the most suitable choice as it is inherently designed for a virtual, dispersed team, and its capacity for anonymity directly addresses the goal of ensuring hesitant members have an equal and safe opportunity to contribute.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is facilitating a planning session to define and estimate the duration of a number of activities. 7 members attended the meeting, and Katherine was the most experienced one among them. Upon a disagreement about the duration of one of the activities, the project manager decided to hold a vote and adopt the decision of the majority.
The voting results were as follows:
What should the project manager do next? [Dati ricostruiti dalla spiegazione: 7 votanti; solo 3 su 7 hanno votato '5 days'; media delle stime = 4 days; Katherine ha stimato 3 days]
⚠️ Nell'esportazione Udemy manca l'immagine (grafico/tabella) a cui fa riferimento la domanda.

opzioni.A: Assign the activity a “5 days” estimation since it was the decision of the majority
opzioni.B: Assign the activity a “4 days” estimation as an average of all estimates
opzioni.C: Assign the activity a “3 days” estimation as suggested by Katherine
opzioni.D: Discuss the different estimations and do another round of voting

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. If plurality were adopted instead, the “5 days” estimation would have been selected as a final decision.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. If the average was adopted, “4 days” would have been selected as the activity’s estimated duration.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. If it were an autocratic decision, the estimation of Katherine, for instance, would have been endorsed.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Since only three out of seven members voted for the “5 days” estimation, the majority was not reached. Therefore, the facilitator should discuss the estimations and do another round of voting if they want to stick with the majority as a decision-making method.

domande.spiegazione: Since only three out of seven members voted for the “5 days” estimation, the majority was not reached. Therefore, the facilitator should discuss the estimations and do another round of voting if they want to stick with the majority as a decision-making method.

domande.domanda:
In a consultancy firm, the project manager chooses consultants for a complex project. The project manager identified a potential team member who excels in his role and consistently delivers high-quality work. However, he is an introvert who prefers working independently rather than in large group settings.
How should the project manager adapt the work environment to accommodate the introverted team member?

opzioni.A: Schedule regular one-on-one meetings with the introverted team member to provide opportunities for personalized communication and feedback and to encourage him to share his insights and ideas.
opzioni.B: Organize team-building activities and workshops focused on enhancing communication and collaboration skills to provide the team member with opportunities to interact with his team members in structured settings that promote engagement and relationship-building.
opzioni.C: Assign the team member to solo tasks that align with his strengths and preferences for working independently.
opzioni.D: Integrate technology tools and platforms that facilitate asynchronous communication and virtual collaboration to minimize the need for face-to-face interactions.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. By scheduling regular one-on-one meetings, the project manager creates a supportive space for the introverted team member to comfortably express himself and share his insights and ideas. This approach recognizes the team member's strengths and provides opportunities for personalized communication and feedback, ultimately maximizing his contributions to the project while fostering a positive work environment for all team members.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Encouraging the team member to attend team-building activities and workshops may not fully address his introverted nature or cater to his preferred work style. For introverted individuals, large group settings and interactive workshops may feel overwhelming or draining, leading to discomfort or reduced participation. Plus, this option entails trying to change the introverted personality of the team member rather than adapting the work environment to their character.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. While it's important to consider the team member's preference for working independently, assigning him to solo tasks may not fully maximize his potential or contribute to effective team dynamics. This approach could isolate him from the team and limit opportunities for collaboration and knowledge sharing. Additionally, it may lead to feelings of exclusion or disengagement from team activities, impacting overall team cohesion and morale.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. While integrating technology tools and platforms for asynchronous communication and virtual collaboration can be beneficial for introverted individuals, minimizing face-to-face interactions may harm team dynamics. For introverted individuals, face-to-face interactions may still be valuable for building relationships, clarifying expectations, and fostering a sense of connection with team members.

domande.spiegazione: By scheduling regular one-on-one meetings, the project manager creates a supportive space for the introverted team member to comfortably express himself and share his insights and ideas. This approach recognizes the team member's strengths and provides opportunities for personalized communication and feedback, ultimately maximizing his contributions to the project while fostering a positive work environment for all team members.

domande.domanda:
During the sprint retrospective meeting, team members complained that they were always wasting time going back and forth with the product owner to schedule the backlog refinement meeting. The project manager suggested creating a recurring event to fix the issue.
When should this event take place?

opzioni.A: Right after the sprint retrospective
opzioni.B: Right before the sprint planning
opzioni.C: Right after the sprint planning
opzioni.D: At any time during the sprint

domande.spiegazione: In an iteration-based agile project, the product owner works with the team to refine the backlog and prepare user stories for the next iterations throughout one or multiple sessions, in the middle of the iteration (Agile Practice Guide, page 67).

domande.domanda:
A project manager is conducting a stakeholder analysis using the power/interest grid. Which actions respectively correspond to blocks A, B, C, and D on the matrix? [Dati ricostruiti dalla spiegazione: A = alto potere/basso interesse, B = alto potere/alto interesse, C = basso potere/basso interesse, D = basso potere/alto interesse]
⚠️ Nell'esportazione Udemy manca l'immagine (grafico/tabella) a cui fa riferimento la domanda.

opzioni.A: Monitor - Keep Satisfied - Manage Closely - Keep Informed
opzioni.B: Keep Satisfied - Manage Closely - Monitor - Keep Informed
opzioni.C: Manage Closely - Keep Informed - Monitor - Keep Satisfied
opzioni.D: Keep Informed - Manage Closely - Monitor - Keep Satisfied

domande.spiegazione:
A = Keep Satisfied. Due to their influence, stakeholders with high power and low interest should be kept satisfied. But, because they don’t have a high interest in your project, they can get bored if you over-communicate with them.
B = Manage Closely. Stakeholders with high power and high interest are the most important to your project, and you should make sure to keep them happy by managing them closely.
C = Monitor. Stakeholders with low power and low interest should be kept informed periodically without overdoing it.
D = Keep Informed. You’ll want to keep stakeholders with low power and high interest informed by checking in with them regularly to make sure they are not experiencing any issues or problems.
Please note that in the real exam, such a question usually comes in the form of “drag & drop”.
