opzioni.A: Prepare a comprehensive analysis of team performance and individual contributions to the project progress.
opzioni.B: Present Earned Value Management (EVM) data, such as Cost and Schedule Variance, to give the executives a quantitative assessment of project performance.
opzioni.C: Highlight the adoption of a new project management system and explain how it has improved workflow and collaboration.
opzioni.D: Discuss the key risks faced during the project and the actions taken to efficiently mitigate them.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. While team performance is important, it is not the primary focus for executives. They care about project health, not individual productivity. This option shifts attention to internal team dynamics, which may be irrelevant or distracting at the executive level.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. By presenting the project’s CV and SV, the project manager demonstrates whether the project is under or over budget, whether it is ahead or behind schedule, and how well they’re managing scope and resources. This is the most accurate way to show how progress is being tracked and measured. EVM metrics provide a single, integrated view of cost, schedule, and scope, offering objective, measurable insights into project progress and performance.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. While improvements are valuable, they are secondary to project performance. Executives want to know if the project is on track, not what tools are being used.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Risk reporting is not the primary metric for tracking progress. Risks are part of project health, but they don’t provide a comprehensive view of performance across cost, schedule, and scope. This option focuses on issues, not overall status.

domande.spiegazione: By presenting the project’s CV and SV, the project manager demonstrates whether the project is under or over budget, whether it is ahead or behind schedule, and how well they’re managing scope and resources. This is the most accurate way to show how progress is being tracked and measured. EVM metrics provide a single, integrated view of cost, schedule, and scope, offering objective, measurable insights into project progress and performance.

domande.domanda:
An organization launches a construction project of a new commercial building in a bustling urban area. Due to certain circumstances, there were delays in the project activities. As a result, the completion date should be pushed back by ten days. While analyzing the impact of this delay, the project team noticed that one of the identified project risks has slightly increased, but it remains within acceptable limits.
What should the project manager do next? (Select two)

opzioni.A: Submit a change request to update the project schedule.
opzioni.B: Update the risk register to reflect the increasing risk severity.
opzioni.C: Hold a meeting with the project team to review the impact of the identified risk.
opzioni.D: Capture the change in a project status report and communicate it to key stakeholders.

domande.spiegazione:
A change request is necessary to formally document and update the project schedule to reflect the ten-day delay. This ensures the project remains aligned with governance protocols and maintains transparency with stakeholders. The project manager should also capture the schedule delay in the status report to ensure that stakeholders are informed and aligned.
Option B: While the risk has slightly increased, it remains within acceptable limits. Therefore, updating the risk register is not an immediate priority unless the risk escalates further.
Option C: Reviewing the risk has already been done.

domande.domanda:
An Agile team wants to examine the visual overview of all of the product’s required features and functionality.
What should the project manager suggest the team review?

opzioni.A: Themes
opzioni.B: Epics
opzioni.C: Product backlog
opzioni.D: Story map

domande.spiegazione:
A story map is used by the agile team to get a visual overview of the product development “Big Picture” including an outline of its features and functionalities.
Options A & B: Themes and epics only represent high-level requirements with no specification of the exact features that will be developed.
Option C: The Product Backlog lists all of the product’s required features and functionalities, but they’re not displayed visually.

domande.domanda:
A project manager takes over a project that's fallen behind schedule. The project manager holds a meeting to consult with the team and decide on the appropriate course of action to bring the project back on track. Team members seek the project manager’s guidance on what tasks they should focus on next.
What should the project manager do next?

opzioni.A: Refer to the WBS Dictionary, as it describes work packages and acceptance criteria.
opzioni.B: Review the project schedule, Responsibility Assignment Matrix (RAM), and the resource calendar.
opzioni.C: Break down the project scope into smaller work packages.
opzioni.D: Prioritize the product backlog to provide direction to the team on what they should be working on next.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The WBS dictionary does not include any information about team members' assignments and what they should tackle next.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Along with the project schedule, the project manager should check the Responsibility Assignment Matrix (RAM) and the resource calendar. RAM is used to show project resources their assignment to each work package (the “what”) (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 194). The resource calendar, on the other hand, is used to show the availability of resources (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 132).
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. The project manager took over the project in its execution phase, meaning that the scope had already been broken down into smaller work packages.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The project is most probably following a predictive approach since the scenario mentions schedule issues, and even if it’s following an agile approach, it’s not up to the project manager to prioritize the product backlog since that falls under the product owner’s responsibilities.

domande.spiegazione: Along with the project schedule, the project manager should check the Responsibility Assignment Matrix (RAM) and the resource calendar. RAM is used to show project resources their assignment to each work package (the “what”) (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 194). The resource calendar, on the other hand, is used to show the availability of resources (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 132).

domande.domanda:
During the process of hiring an electrical engineer, the project manager only conducted one behavioral interview. Later on, the project manager discovered that the candidate’s technical skills did not meet the job requirements. Therefore, the project manager decided that going forward, the recruitment process would include a technical test and an additional technical interview.
What risk response strategy did the project manager apply?

opzioni.A: Mitigate
opzioni.B: Accept
opzioni.C: Transfer
opzioni.D: Avoid

domande.spiegazione:
In the described scenario, hiring an unqualified engineer is the risk. Since they were aware of this risk, the project manager took measures to mitigate it. Mitigation involves decreasing the probability of a risk occurrence or lowering its impact when it does occur (PMBOK 8th edition, page 204).
Option D: Even with the addition of a technical test and an interview, there is still a chance that the candidate might not meet the job requirements (the test could be too easy or generic, for instance), that’s why “Avoid” can’t be the right answer.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is leading a software project. The initial requirements are vague, but the sponsor insists on a firm ceiling for development costs. The vendor is concerned that a standard fixed-price contract will lead to excessive change requests.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Use a fixed-price contract to adhere to the budget ceiling and manage scope changes through a formal change control process.
opzioni.B: Propose a cost-reimbursable contract with a fee based on achieving specific performance metrics.
opzioni.C: Adopt a T&M contract with a "not-to-exceed" cap and structured review points for deliverables.
opzioni.D: Draft a firm-fixed-price contract based on the current high-level requirements.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Using a fixed-price contract meets the sponsor's budget need, but it ignores the vendor's valid concern and the reality of vague requirements. This approach is likely to create an adversarial relationship filled with change requests and disputes, undermining collaboration.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. A cost-reimbursable contract contradicts the sponsor's primary concern, as a cost-reimbursable contract does not provide a firm ceiling on costs, only on the vendor's profit.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. By including a cap on a T&M contract, the project manager can balance the project constraints: It respects the sponsor's concern for a firm budget ceiling (the "not-to-exceed" cap), addresses the vendor's concern about the rigidity of a fixed-price contract for vague requirements by using the flexible T&M structure, and incorporates an Agile-like principle of "structured review points" (implied by collaborative models focusing on joint problem-solving) to manage the evolving scope collaboratively, preventing disputes (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 252).
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Creating a detailed scope from vague requirements will inevitably be incomplete or inaccurate. This sets up the project for failure, as the initial specifications will be wrong, leading to massive change orders and cost overruns, thus violating the very budget constraint it tries to protect.

domande.spiegazione: By including a cap on a T&M contract, the project manager can balance the project constraints: It respects the sponsor's concern for a firm budget ceiling (the "not-to-exceed" cap), addresses the vendor's concern about the rigidity of a fixed-price contract for vague requirements by using the flexible T&M structure, and incorporates an Agile-like principle of "structured review points" (implied by collaborative models focusing on joint problem-solving) to manage the evolving scope collaboratively, preventing disputes (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 252).

domande.domanda:
During the project execution, a team member informs the project manager that the electronic equipment used in the project is no longer functioning due to the excessively hot weather.
What should the project manager do to solve the problem? (Select three)

opzioni.A: Identify the problem
opzioni.B: Analyze the problem
opzioni.C: Prevent the problem
opzioni.D: Check the solution
opzioni.E: Keep the solution

domande.spiegazione:
The project manager should use methodical steps to perform problem-solving (PMBOK 8th Edition, pages 187-188). These steps include:
Identifying or specifying the problem.
Defining the problem and breaking it into smaller, manageable problems.
Investigating by collecting data.
Analyzing to detect the root cause of the problem.
Solving by choosing the suitable solution.
Checking the implemented solution to determine whether the problem has been fixed or not.
Option C: Preventing the problem is not correct because the problem already took place in the described scenario.
Option E: After evaluating the solution, it can either be kept or replaced if found ineffective.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is leading a new project to upgrade a company’s supply chain systems. Midway through the project execution, it becomes clear that feedback from the operations division, a key user of the new system, has been omitted during the project planning and execution. As a result, the project outcomes do not align with the operational workflows of the division, leading to dissatisfaction and resistance.
What should the project manager have done to avoid this problem?

opzioni.A: Integrate the overlooked operational insights into the project scope.
opzioni.B: Evaluate whether the project has followed internal guidelines and compliance requirements.
opzioni.C: Check the project’s communications management plan to identify how information flows between teams and why operational input was missed.
opzioni.D: Develop a plan to integrate the unanticipated requirements from the operations division.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. While adjusting the scope may be necessary, it comes after understanding why the feedback was omitted. This option assumes the problem is solved by adding work, but doesn’t address the root cause (poor communication).
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. While policy adherence is important, it’s not the issue here. The problem is stakeholder engagement, not compliance.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. By reviewing the communications management plan, the project manager can identify gaps in stakeholder engagement, improve information flow, and prevent future omissions. This is the best first step because it directly addresses the root cause and enables the project manager to fix the process, not just the outcome.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Developing a plan to integrate the unanticipated requirements is reactive and avoids addressing the systemic issue. A temporary fix won’t prevent similar problems in the future. The goal is to improve the process, not just patch the results.

domande.spiegazione: By reviewing the communications management plan, the project manager can identify gaps in stakeholder engagement, improve information flow, and prevent future omissions. This is the best first step because it directly addresses the root cause and enables the project manager to fix the process, not just the outcome.

domande.domanda:
A project manager joins an agile team that has been working on a product for over a year. The team's velocity has remained steady, but the time required for regression testing and fixing bugs discovered after each deployment has increased significantly. During a retrospective, developers explain that to meet past deadlines, they took shortcuts that have now accumulated as significant technical debt.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Increase the story point estimates for all features to account for the extra time needed to work around the existing debt.
opzioni.B: Initiate a separate, dedicated debt reduction sprint.
opzioni.C: Work with the team to track the debt items and incorporate addressing them into the Definition of Done.
opzioni.D: Halt new feature development to focus on refactoring the problematic code.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Increasing the story point estimates for all new features is a reactive and imprecise solution. It inflates estimates without directly addressing the root cause. It makes new features appear more complicated without a clear plan to deal with the existing debt, and it does not improve the deteriorating health of the codebase.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Initiating a separate, dedicated debt reduction sprint creates a split between new features and code health. Debt reduction should be incorporated into the team's regular workflow, not isolated.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Working with the team to track the debt items and incorporate addressing them into the Definition of Done makes the invisible debt visible and incorporates its management into the team's standard workflow. It is a sustainable, proactive solution that prevents the debt from growing further while allowing for continuous delivery of value, aligning perfectly with agile principles.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Temporarily halting all new feature development is unrealistic from a business perspective. A complete stoppage of value delivery is rarely approved and can be demoralizing for the team. The recommended approach is a balanced, continuous effort (setting aside time for refactoring), not a disruptive "stop-the-line" event that risks creating a new project delay.

domande.spiegazione: Working with the team to track the debt items and incorporate addressing them into the Definition of Done makes the invisible debt visible and incorporates its management into the team's standard workflow. It is a sustainable, proactive solution that prevents the debt from growing further while allowing for continuous delivery of value, aligning perfectly with agile principles.

domande.domanda:
During the execution of an ERP implementation project across three countries, the project manager notices that each regional team is sending updated schedules and status reports by email after weekly meetings. However, the teams often overwrite each other’s spreadsheets, making it hard to track the changes and progress made.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Facilitate training sessions for all teams on version control and proper handling of shared project artifacts.
opzioni.B: Maintain separate document control systems for each region.
opzioni.C: Establish a centralized project repository with version control.
opzioni.D: Develop a new custom document management software tailored for the project’s version control needs.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Facilitating training sessions for all regional teams on version control and proper handling of shared project artifacts might be useful, but it doesn’t solve the root cause, i.e., the lack of a centralized repository. Teaching people how to email files better still leaves room for duplicate versions and overwritten data.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Maintaining separate document control systems for each region can make the situation worse. Having each team maintain its own systems fragments the data further and increases misalignment. The goal is integration, not isolation.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Establishing a centralized project repository with version control directly addresses the problem. A single repository ensures there is one source to track the changes and progress made. Version control allows visibility of updates and reduces the risk of overwriting files. This aligns with best practices in distributed projects.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Developing new software is costly, time-consuming, and unnecessary. Proven off-the-shelf tools like Jira, Confluence, or SharePoint already provide robust document and version control. This would delay progress further.

domande.spiegazione: Establishing a centralized project repository with version control directly addresses the problem. A single repository ensures there is one source to track the changes and progress made. Version control allows visibility of updates and reduces the risk of overwriting files. This aligns with best practices in distributed projects.

domande.domanda:
A government agency is procuring a new public transportation ticketing system. The primary objective is to reduce average passenger boarding time by 15% within one year of launch. The agency's procurement office requires the use of a firm-fixed-price contract to ensure budgetary control. The project manager is concerned that this contract type may not incentivize the vendor to innovate beyond the basic specifications.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Adhere to the procurement office mandate and use a firm-fixed-price contract with detailed technical specifications.
opzioni.B: Propose a cost-reimbursable contract to share the financial risk of innovation with the vendor.
opzioni.C: Suggest a firm-fixed-price contract that includes financial bonuses for exceeding the 15% speed improvement target.
opzioni.D: Propose a Time & Material contract to allow for flexibility in the development process.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Adhering to the procurement office mandate ignores the project manager's legitimate concern. It does nothing to encourage innovation and may result in a vendor delivering only the minimum required, potentially missing the spirit of the project goal.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Proposing a cost-reimbursable contract goes against the fundamental constraint from the procurement office (the use of a firm-fixed-price contract to ensure budgetary control). While it might encourage innovation, it is not a viable option as it disregards a key stakeholder requirement.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. A firm-fixed-price contract that includes financial bonuses for exceeding the 15% speed improvement target is an outcome-based contract within a fixed-price structure. This type of contract "focuses on measurable results rather than prescribed processes" (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 252). By keeping the firm-fixed-price element, it meets the procurement office's requirement for budgetary control. By adding a performance incentive tied to the core objective (boarding time), it directly addresses the project manager's concern about innovation, motivating the vendor to exceed the baseline specification to achieve a shared objective.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Proposing a Time & Material contract also goes against the fundamental constraint from the procurement office. Furthermore, a T&M contract does not inherently guarantee innovation; it simply shifts cost risk to the buyer without a specific mechanism to drive toward the desired outcome.

domande.spiegazione: A firm-fixed-price contract that includes financial bonuses for exceeding the 15% speed improvement target is an outcome-based contract within a fixed-price structure. This type of contract "focuses on measurable results rather than prescribed processes" (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 252). By keeping the firm-fixed-price element, it meets the procurement office's requirement for budgetary control. By adding a performance incentive tied to the core objective (boarding time), it directly addresses the project manager's concern about innovation, motivating the vendor to exceed the baseline specification to achieve a shared objective.

domande.domanda:
To see where each team member stands regarding a certain decision, a project manager uses the Fist of five voting technique. When the team starts voting, one member holds up five fingers.
What does this mean?

opzioni.A: The team member wants to intervene in order to further discuss the decision.
opzioni.B: The team member is totally against the decision.
opzioni.C: The team member totally supports the decision.
opzioni.D: The team member wants to refrain from taking part in the voting.

domande.spiegazione: The Fist of five or Fist to five is a voting technique that agile teams use to help them achieve consensus during decision-making meetings or sessions. This method is used as follows: The facilitator states the decision or action the team is going to vote on and then asks each one of the attendees to hold up a number of fingers that corresponds to their level of support for the stated decision. A closed fist signifies full objection, whereas five fingers mean full support for the decision. Until everyone holds up three or more fingers, the voting goes through multiple rounds to achieve consensus.

domande.domanda:
A product owner who’s new to the agile approach created the following user story: “As a customer, I want a new functionality so that I can achieve a 50% increase in sales”. The project manager found the user story to be deficient.
So, they reached out to the product owner to explain to them that:

opzioni.A: The user story should follow a common structure
opzioni.B: The user story should be specific and testable
opzioni.C: The user story should not include financial values
opzioni.D: The user story should be time-bounded

domande.spiegazione:
The user story written by the product owner is not specific and cannot be tested. Even if it’s written in a user story format, it’s vague and unclear. The product owner must specify what new functionality they are looking to develop (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 143).
Option C: It’s possible to include financial values in a user story as long as they contribute to making it clearer and more understandable.
Option D: A goal can be time-bound, i.e., a SMART goal, but a user story is not bounded by time.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is examining the investment efficiency of two potential projects. However, due to uncertainty, the applicable discount rate is currently unknown and cannot be reliably estimated.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Select the project with the highest ROI
opzioni.B: Select the project with the lowest ROI
opzioni.C: Select the project with the highest NPV
opzioni.D: Select the project with the lowest NPV

domande.spiegazione:
Calculating a project’s Net Present Value (NPV) requires knowing its discount rate (i):
Net Present Value (NPV) = Future payment (F) / [ (1 + Discount rate (i) ) ^ number of periods in the future the cash flow is (n) ]. Since this is not an option in the described scenario, the project manager should rely on the Return On Investment (ROI) and pick the project with the highest value.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is leading an agile project. Their daily 10-minute standup is at 9 am. In the last meeting, the project manager noted a 5-minute delay. Then, the team spent another 5 minutes chit-chatting before they actually started the meeting. After the standup, two team members stayed in the meeting room for another 5 minutes discussing an issue that had surfaced the day before.
What should the project manager do next?

opzioni.A: Request from the team to come to the meeting on time
opzioni.B: Request from the team to stop chit-chatting
opzioni.C: Request from the team to leave the meeting room after the standup
opzioni.D: Change the standup duration to 15 minutes

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Requesting the team to come on time helps maintain discipline and respect for the meeting's timebox.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. After addressing the punctuality issue, the project manager can work on reducing or controlling chit-chatting.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Nothing wrong with the behavior of the team members who decided to dedicate another quick meeting to dive into a particular issue, which permits keeping the standup meeting focused and concise.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The scenario doesn’t include factors that could lead to a change in the standup duration.

domande.spiegazione: Requesting the team to come on time helps maintain discipline and respect for the meeting's timebox.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is leading a project using an adaptive approach. During the sprint review, the product owner asks for an acceptance document to sign off on in order to demonstrate their approval of the deliverables.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Create an acceptance document and share it with the product owner to sign off.
opzioni.B: Ask the product owner to create a task in the product backlog and prioritize it, so that the development team can create the acceptance document.
opzioni.C: Ask the product owner to create the acceptance document and sign it off.
opzioni.D: Inform the product owner that an acceptance document is unnecessary.

domande.spiegazione: A sprint review is conducted to demonstrate the accomplished work, solicit feedback, and foster collaboration rather than seeking formal approval through the sign-off of an acceptance document (Essential Scrum by Rubin, Kenneth S, page 372). Besides, formal approvals are more common in predictive environments.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is leading a team that is not familiar with the adaptive approach. After several weeks, the project has reached a point where there is an accumulation of Work In Progress (WIP).
What should the project manager do to figure out whether the team is properly following procedures?

opzioni.A: Perform a process evaluation
opzioni.B: Review the notes of the previous retrospective meetings
opzioni.C: Check the Kanban board
opzioni.D: Check relevant Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

domande.spiegazione:
Process evaluation involves quality assurance activities and process audits to ensure procedures and processes are being followed and are generating the intended outcomes.
Option B: Process evaluation can also include reviewing the notes of the previous retrospective meetings, as they can reflect the type of issues that were encountered in the past and how they were handled. Therefore, process evaluation involves more than just reviewing the previous retrospective meetings’ notes.
Options C & D: KPIs and the Kanban board can only determine whether WIP is beyond the acceptable level, without identifying the causes. Finally, process evaluation can take place during a retrospective meeting or a lessons learned session, and it can require further investigation that could go beyond those meetings.

domande.domanda:
An organization asked the project manager to send a report on the cost of quality. The report stated that the total cost was $30,000, detailed as follows:
According to the table above, what is the appraisal cost of the project? [Dati ricostruiti dalla spiegazione: la tabella elenca voci di costo tra cui ispezione = $5,000, training, rework, scrap e warranty]
⚠️ Nell'esportazione Udemy manca l'immagine (grafico/tabella) a cui fa riferimento la domanda.
domande.spiegazione: Appraisal costs, also known as inspection costs, are part of the Cost of Conformance as they represent the costs of identifying defective products before they are delivered to clients. This comprises testing, inspecting, auditing, evaluating, and measuring the deliverables, product, or service the project is producing. Appraisal costs are set up to implement a series of activities to determine the work results’ degree of conformance to quality requirements. This means that the project appraisal cost involves inspection costs, which are $5,000. Training falls under prevention activities. Rework and scrap costs, on the other hand, are part of the Internal Failure Costs, whereas Warranty charges fall under External Failure Costs (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 159).
domande.motivo_incertezza: immagine della domanda non presente nell'esportazione

domande.domanda:
Mid-project, a project manager is notified by the information security department that they have just learned about the design changes that were made recently. The information security department also expressed its concern about these changes’ compliance with the organization’s standards since it did not take part when these changes were made.
What should the project manager do to overcome this issue?

opzioni.A: Undo all design changes since the information security department wasn’t involved in the process.
opzioni.B: Allow the information security department team to attend all of the following daily stand-ups to ensure all changes comply with security requirements.
opzioni.C: Ask the information security department to raise the issue with the product owner.
opzioni.D: Conduct a meeting with the information security department to go over all design changes and ensure compliance with the organization’s standards.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. If certain design changes are found to be critical and unfixable, then those should be reverted.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The product owner could be involved in the problem resolution process, but transferring the issue to them wouldn’t work since compliance with the organization’s standards requires understanding security concerns and setting up the appropriate processes by the project manager and their team.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Standup meetings are used for daily work syncing between team members, not for examining changes.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. The project manager should first try to resolve the issue through collaboration by conducting a meeting with the information security department to go over the design changes and implement the appropriate process to ensure compliance with security requirements (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 156).

domande.spiegazione: The project manager should first try to resolve the issue through collaboration by conducting a meeting with the information security department to go over the design changes and implement the appropriate process to ensure compliance with security requirements (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 156).

domande.domanda:
During the sprint review of the project’s final iteration, the product owner expressed their satisfaction with the product and described it as “fit for purpose”. However, a senior team member stated that another iteration is needed to fix some bugs and improve the user experience. The sponsor, who is also attending the meeting, said that further work on the product will resume if more funding is received in the next quarter.
What should the project manager do next?

opzioni.A: Close the project, but keep one developer to fix any major bugs.
opzioni.B: Keep the project open since work could be resumed in the next quarter.
opzioni.C: Continue work on fixing bugs to satisfy the client, then close the project.
opzioni.D: Release all resources.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Properly closing the project entails releasing all resources.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Continuing work on bugs after the project closure is inappropriate.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Working on bugs to satisfy the client is considered gold plating. A project cannot be kept open until receiving new funding. It should be closed and, when funding is obtained, a new project should be launched to fix bugs and do whatever the customer requires.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Since the client requested the project closure, even though they are aware of the bugs and the required improvements, the project manager should proceed with the decision.

domande.spiegazione: Since the client requested the project closure, even though they are aware of the bugs and the required improvements, the project manager should proceed with the decision.

domande.domanda:
The project sponsor informed the project manager that they have doubts about whether the resulting product will satisfy business demands. Therefore, the project sponsor is looking to keep costs to a minimum.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Identify and implement the requirements for making a Minimum Viable Product (MVP).
opzioni.B: Gather all requirements and execute the project using an incremental approach.
opzioni.C: Exclude certain stakeholders from the scope definition process in order to limit requirements.
opzioni.D: Sign a fixed-cost contract with the sponsor to limit project costs.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. The Minimum Viable Product (MVP) is used to define the scope of the first release by identifying the requirements that would deliver value to customers (PMBOK 8th edition, page 269).
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. An incremental approach is not suitable for the described scenario since the client won’t get a usable product until the end of the project.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. It’s not appropriate to exclude certain stakeholders in order to limit requirements. The project manager should involve all stakeholders in the process of collecting and prioritizing product features.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. A fixed-cost contract will not solve the problem in the described scenario since the main concern of the sponsor is verifying the product’s business demand.

domande.spiegazione: The Minimum Viable Product (MVP) is used to define the scope of the first release by identifying the requirements that would deliver value to customers (PMBOK 8th edition, page 269).

domande.domanda:
Mid-project, the project manager noticed that stakeholders’ engagement was fading out and felt the need to measure their satisfaction.
What tools or techniques could the project manager use? (Select two)

opzioni.A: Net Promoter Score
opzioni.B: Mood chart
opzioni.C: Power/interest grid
opzioni.D: Engagement assessment matrix

domande.spiegazione:
Stakeholder satisfaction can be measured with surveys or by looking at related metrics such as Net Promoter Score (NPS) and Mood chart. The Net Promoter Score is a numerical measure of the stakeholder’s satisfaction with your product, service, or workplace and their willingness to recommend it to others (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 269). The score ranges from -100 to +100. A high promoter score reflects high business loyalty and job satisfaction. Mood charts, on the other hand, are used to track the daily mood of certain key stakeholders, where they can use colors, emojis, or numbers to express how they’re feeling. This method can help the project manager anticipate and identify potential issues and work on improving certain areas, such as in the described scenario where engagement is fading.
Option C: The power/interest grid is created in order to categorize stakeholders based on their power or influence levels and has nothing to do with measuring their satisfaction.
Option D: The Engagement Assessment Matrix is a stakeholder management technique that is used to monitor the engagement levels of stakeholders and therefore identifies involvement issues. This tool might have helped the project manager detect the stakeholders’ engagement problem, but it can’t help them figure out satisfaction levels.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is leading the second phase of a project using a hybrid approach. During the first phase of the project, the project manager faced some challenges with defining the requirements. Therefore, at the beginning of the new phase, the project manager wants to proactively manage stakeholders’ expectations in order to find common ground and diminish any differences.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Send a questionnaire to all of the involved stakeholders in order to determine the project requirements.
opzioni.B: Set up a meeting with each stakeholder to identify their needs.
opzioni.C: Invite all concerned stakeholders to a requirements workshop to develop user stories.
opzioni.D: Conduct a survey of the project’s current users.

domande.spiegazione:
The project manager wants a way to proactively manage stakeholders’ expectations and find a common ground while collecting requirements for the second phase of his hybrid project. For that, the project manager should invite all concerned stakeholders to a requirements workshop to develop user stories. Facilitating a workshop is the best option in this situation to identify the project requirements and diminish stakeholder differences. The interaction occurring during a workshop can help everyone involved find common ground and reach consensus when it comes to project requirements.
Options A, B, D: Sending a questionnaire, setting up one-on-one meetings, and conducting surveys could help collect data and get insights, but stakeholders should communicate with one another to bridge any disagreements.

domande.domanda:
A customer informed their project manager that they are going to launch a new project, and they will assign it to the same product owner of the current ongoing project.
How should the project manager react in response to the customer’s decision?

opzioni.A: Ask the customer to reconsider their decision since a product owner should handle one product at a time.
opzioni.B: Ask the customer to reconsider their decision to avoid a conflict of interest situation.
opzioni.C: It’s ok to have the same product owner for both products as long as they can fulfill their duties.
opzioni.D: Ask the customer to add another product owner to the current project as a backup.

domande.spiegazione: A product should only have one product owner, considering they’re the one responsible for deciding which features to build and in which order (Essential Scrum by Rubin, Kenneth S, page 15). When multiple products are being developed, it’s possible to either have a product owner for each of them or have one product owner for all of them. This depends on the projects’ size as well as other factors such as the connection between projects. But, in all cases, the product owner should fulfill their role and be available to respond to queries from the development teams.

domande.domanda:
During product validation, a key stakeholder refuses to sign off on the acceptance document, claiming that some of the functionalities do not meet their expectations.
What should the project manager have done to avoid this situation?

opzioni.A: Involve the key stakeholder during the quality control phase
opzioni.B: Involve the key stakeholder during the project initiation phase
opzioni.C: Involve the key stakeholder during the planning phase
opzioni.D: Involve the key stakeholder during all project phases

domande.spiegazione: Stakeholders need to get involved early on during project planning and sometimes during the project initiation as well. Key stakeholders should also be involved during the quality control phase so that they can assess the project deliverables and recommend any changes before the official acceptance. Since the concerned key stakeholder is responsible for signing off on the acceptance document, their power is considered high. Therefore, stakeholders who are identified to have high power using the power/interest grid should be managed closely and/or kept satisfied throughout the whole project.

domande.domanda:
While working on identifying risks, a project manager noticed that there was a disagreement among team members concerning the appropriate way to execute an important work item.
What can the project manager do to mitigate this risk?

opzioni.A: Outsource the concerned work item.
opzioni.B: Enroll the team in training about the technologies related to executing that work item.
opzioni.C: Let the team self-organize and figure out how to execute the work item.
opzioni.D: Escalate the issue to the functional manager.

domande.spiegazione:
Providing training on the technologies related to the work item will help the team fully understand how to execute it. This strategy aims to mitigate the risk by reducing conflict between team members.
Option A, C, D: The other options involve transferring the risk by outsourcing the work item, accepting it by letting the team figure out a solution on their own, or escalating the risk to the functional manager.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is in charge of a software development project that follows an Agile approach. During the project execution, the project manager receives a request from the customer to alter a requirement.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Block the change request
opzioni.B: Welcome the change request
opzioni.C: Avoid the change request
opzioni.D: Take the change request to the Change Control Board (CCB)

domande.spiegazione:
Flexibility is one of the most important aspects of the Agile approach; the scope of work can change in response to new requirements. An Agile, adaptive, or change-driven approach encourages collecting feedback from stakeholders on a regular basis.
Option D: Unlike the predictive approach, the Agile approach doesn’t involve a Change Control Board (CCB).

domande.domanda:
A project manager joins a project to replace the former project manager who has abruptly left the organization. During the first week, they noticed that team members do not trust or support each other's ideas and that the work climate is counterproductive.
According to Tuckman's model, at which development stage is this team?

opzioni.A: Adjourning
opzioni.B: Norming
opzioni.C: Forming
opzioni.D: Storming

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. In the adjourning phase, tasks are completed, the team breaks up, and members move on to other assignments.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The norming stage comes after storming; this is when team members begin to work together and trust each other. In the performing phase, teams begin to function as a unit; they get the job done smoothly and effectively without inappropriate conflicts or the need for supervision.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Forming is the first stage of a team’s development, where members start to know each other and form first impressions. Team members usually avoid controversies or conflicts in this phase.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. The project manager’s team is in the storming phase. Tuckman’s team development ladder identifies five stages: forming, storming, norming, performing, and adjourning (PMBOK 8th edition, page 211). Storming is the most difficult and critical stage a team can go through. Different personalities emerge during this phase, resulting in conflict and rivalry. At this point, the team's performance will suffer tremendously since their energy is diverted to disputes and arguments.

domande.spiegazione: The project manager’s team is in the storming phase. Tuckman’s team development ladder identifies five stages: forming, storming, norming, performing, and adjourning (PMBOK 8th edition, page 211). Storming is the most difficult and critical stage a team can go through. Different personalities emerge during this phase, resulting in conflict and rivalry. At this point, the team's performance will suffer tremendously since their energy is diverted to disputes and arguments.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is in charge of leading a ground-breaking medical research project. During a meeting with the sponsor, the project manager discusses how he’s going to handle the project, explaining that he wants to encourage self-awareness, listening, and coaching. The project manager adds that helping the project team grow is among his top priorities.
What type of leadership does the project manager intend to adopt?

opzioni.A: Servant leadership
opzioni.B: Authentic leadership
opzioni.C: Transactional leadership
opzioni.D: Transformational leadership

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. The project manager intends to adopt a servant leadership style. The Agile Practice Guide distinguishes servant leadership with the following characteristics: promoting self-awareness, listening, serving teammates, assisting people in their development and growth, coaching rather than controlling, and promoting security, respect, and trust. Servant leaders prioritize the needs of others, helping them reach their best performance and potential (PMBOK 8th edition, page 197).
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Authentic leaders focus on the self-development of themselves and their followers.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Transactional leaders focus on supervision, organization, and performance, using incentives and penalties as motivation tools.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Transformational leaders focus on motivation as well as creating an atmosphere of innovation and creativity.

domande.spiegazione: The project manager intends to adopt a servant leadership style. The Agile Practice Guide distinguishes servant leadership with the following characteristics: promoting self-awareness, listening, serving teammates, assisting people in their development and growth, coaching rather than controlling, and promoting security, respect, and trust. Servant leaders prioritize the needs of others, helping them reach their best performance and potential (PMBOK 8th edition, page 197).

domande.domanda:
A project manager who works in a national bank decides to use the power/interest grid to plan stakeholder engagement.
How should he deal with an interested stakeholder with little authority?

opzioni.A: Monitor
opzioni.B: Manage closely
opzioni.C: Keep informed
opzioni.D: Keep satisfied

domande.spiegazione:
The project manager should keep stakeholders with high interest and low authority informed. He should proactively plan how to regularly communicate the project status to this group of stakeholders and check in with them to make sure they are not experiencing any issues or problems.
Options A, B, D: The project manager should closely manage stakeholders with high levels of power and interest, keep stakeholders with high power and low interest satisfied, and monitor stakeholders with low levels of power and interest.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is managing a branding project for a fast-food restaurant chain. During the project, two team members had an argument about a design task. The project manager decides to have a meeting with the two members. Upon discussing the issue, they all came to the conclusion that the best course of action would be to outsource this activity.
Which conflict resolution technique did the project manager use?

opzioni.A: Forcing
opzioni.B: Collaborating
opzioni.C: Compromise
opzioni.D: Smoothing

domande.spiegazione:
Since the project manager chose to meet with the concerned team members to discuss their conflict and make the best decision accordingly, the situation implies problem-solving or collaboration, which leads to a win-win situation (PMBOK 8th edition, page 157).
Options A, C, D: Other problem-solving techniques include:
Forcing: which leads to a win-lose situation.
Smoothing: which leads to a yield-lose situation.
Withdrawing: which leads to a lose-leave situation.
Compromising: which leads to a lose-lose situation.
Reference: Guan, D. (2007). Conflicts in the project environment. Paper presented at PMI Global Congress 2007.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is leading a globally distributed IT security team with members across different time zones. Four months into project execution, the project manager notices that the team struggles with inconsistent productivity and unclear expectations.
What should the project manager do? (Select two answers)

opzioni.A: Avoid giving negative feedback in person.
opzioni.B: Give team members freedom to define and adapt their own roles.
opzioni.C: Set up regular meetings to discuss performance and expectations.
opzioni.D: Learn about the skills each team member has and address gaps through targeted training.
opzioni.E: Give feedback via instant messaging to maintain a proper written record.

domande.spiegazione:
Regular, structured check-ins provide consistent opportunities to align on expectations, address issues, and track progress in virtual settings where informal feedback opportunities are limited. Virtual teams require proactive skills management since organic knowledge-sharing is reduced. Identifying and bridging competency gaps ensures all members can contribute effectively. Performance feedback requires context that instant messaging lacks. Complex or sensitive feedback should use richer channels (video calls, documented reviews).
Option A: Video calls (the virtual equivalent of "in person") are actually preferred for delivering constructive feedback to ensure clarity and allow dialogue.
Option B: While some autonomy is good, virtual teams often need clearer role definitions to prevent overlaps/gaps in responsibilities.
Option E: Feedback should be timely, constructive, and contextual, not transactional. Delivering performance feedback over instant messaging lacks nuance, tone, emotional intelligence, and opportunity for dialogue. It reduces a human-centered process to a text-based transaction, which can lead to misinterpretation. While maintaining records is good practice, the medium matters. The correct approach is to provide feedback in a private, real-time conversation and follow up with a summary email or note for documentation. This balances clarity and empathy during delivery and record-keeping through formal channels for accountability.

domande.domanda:
A project team is working on a highly innovative product where requirements are expected to evolve. The project manager wants to create an environment where team members feel comfortable proposing unconventional solutions and experimenting with new approaches without fear of blame if an idea fails.
Which stage of psychological safety is the project manager trying to cultivate?

opzioni.A: Inclusion Safety
opzioni.B: Learner Safety
opzioni.C: Contributor Safety
opzioni.D: Challenger Safety

domande.spiegazione:
There are four stages of psychological safety that “reflect a growing level of inclusion, engagement and team maturity”:
Inclusion Safety: members feel safe to belong to the team. They are comfortable being present, do not feel excluded, and feel like they are wanted and appreciated.
Learner Safety: members are able to learn through asking questions. Team members here may be able to experiment, make (and admit) small mistakes, and ask for help.
Contributor Safety: members feel safe to contribute their own ideas, without fear of embarrassment or ridicule. This is a more challenging state, because volunteering your own ideas can increase the psychosocial vulnerability of team members.
Challenger Safety: members can question others’ (including those in authority) ideas or suggest significant changes to ideas, plans, or ways of working.
The scenario's goal, to encourage proposing unconventional solutions and experimentation, directly aligns with the “Challenger Safety” stage, which enables innovation and constructive change.

domande.domanda:
Shortly after starting a new project, a project manager noticed that a team member who was also on the last project was not as productive as she used to be. The project manager invited her to a one-on-one meeting, where she admitted that her frustration was due to the fact that she had expected a performance bonus in the last project, but did not receive it.
What should the project manager do first?

opzioni.A: Explain to the team member that performance bonuses are outside of the project manager’s control.
opzioni.B: Escalate the issue to the HR department for further resolution.
opzioni.C: Acknowledge her frustration and provide recognition for her contributions to the last project.
opzioni.D: Explain to her how performance was evaluated and how bonuses were awarded in the last project.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. While bonuses could be outside the project manager's control, deflecting responsibility doesn't address the emotional aspect of the team member’s frustration.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Escalating to HR is possible in case the project manager finds out that the team member deserves a performance bonus. This step could be done after showing empathy, listening to the team member, and reviewing the grounds and the correctness of the bonus decision.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Acknowledging her frustration shows empathy, and offering recognition helps to re-engage her in the current project. While the bonus issue may not be within the project manager's control, providing recognition for ongoing work can boost morale and productivity (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 86).
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The project manager should clarify any misunderstanding, but this should be after acknowledging her frustration and providing recognition for her contributions to the last project.

domande.spiegazione: Acknowledging her frustration shows empathy, and offering recognition helps to re-engage her in the current project. While the bonus issue may not be within the project manager's control, providing recognition for ongoing work can boost morale and productivity (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 86).

domande.domanda:
One month into project execution, the project manager notices that the sponsor is always late for their weekly meetings. However, the project manager chooses not to address the sponsor’s behavior. Instead, the project manager documents the frequent tardiness in the meetings’ notes.
Which conflict resolution technique is the project manager using?

opzioni.A: Problem-solving
opzioni.B: Smoothing
opzioni.C: Information recording
opzioni.D: Withdrawal

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The situation does not imply problem-solving since the project manager didn’t point out the issue to the sponsor in order to find a solution.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The project manager didn’t smooth the conflict either since there was no discussion with the sponsor to diminish their differences.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Information recording, taking notes, or documenting the situation is not a conflict resolution technique.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. The unwillingness to deal with a conflict is referred to as withdrawing. This conflict resolution technique is acceptable when some time to cool off is needed in order to achieve a better understanding of the situation, or when the other party is unassailable or uncooperative (PMBOK 8th edition, page 157).

domande.spiegazione: The unwillingness to deal with a conflict is referred to as withdrawing. This conflict resolution technique is acceptable when some time to cool off is needed in order to achieve a better understanding of the situation, or when the other party is unassailable or uncooperative (PMBOK 8th edition, page 157).

domande.domanda:
A project manager is in charge of an educational project. After analyzing the power level of each of the project’s four stakeholders, the project manager finds out that Monica and Markus have high power, while Ravi and Sergio have low power. For a deeper insight, the project manager created the stakeholder engagement assessment matrix below.
Based on this analysis, which stakeholder should be prioritized in terms of engagement? [Dati ricostruiti dalla spiegazione: Monica = alto potere, Neutral; Markus = alto potere, Unaware; Ravi = basso potere; Sergio = basso potere, Resistant]
⚠️ Nell'esportazione Udemy manca l'immagine (grafico/tabella) a cui fa riferimento la domanda.

opzioni.A: Monica
opzioni.B: Markus
opzioni.C: Ravi
opzioni.D: Sergio

domande.spiegazione:
The priority in engagement should be given to stakeholders with a high level of power. Monica and Markus have high power, but Monica is Neutral, while Markus is unaware. Having an unaware stakeholder with a high level of power is more dangerous than a neutral stakeholder with a high level of power, since the first type can cause a lot of trouble when they become aware at a late stage of the project. The project manager should prioritize engaging Markus by sharing the project details with him. Then, they should try to win his support and bring him to the leading level if possible.
Options A & D: Monica and Sergio should be the project manager’s second priority. It’s preferable to have either supportive or leading high-power stakeholders. So, the project manager needs to make more effort to bring Monica to one of these two levels. On the other hand, even though Sergio has low power, the project manager needs to work on moving him out of the resistant level since his level of power can change at any time throughout the project.
domande.motivo_incertezza: immagine della domanda non presente nell'esportazione

domande.domanda:
An organization in need of accounting software conducts a make-or-buy analysis. The organization decided to go for in-house development since the analysis shows a payback period of fewer than 3 years. However, when acquiring resources, the project manager finds out that the developer's rate included in the make-or-buy analysis is only half the current rate in the market.
What should the project manager do first?

opzioni.A: Submit a change request.
opzioni.B: Inform the sponsor about the findings.
opzioni.C: Nothing; as long as the project’s SPI and CPI are on track, this shouldn’t be a problem.
opzioni.D: Update the make-or-buy analysis report.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. If the sponsor agrees to carry on the project and increase its budget according to the new findings, then a change request should be issued. However, when following an adaptive approach, no change requests, SPI, or CPI are used. In this case, the project manager should inform the sponsor or the product owner about their findings and discuss whether it’s still possible to achieve the project goals or not.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. The project manager should notify the sponsor of any identified risks that may impact the business value of the project. Business value measurements are used to ensure that the project deliverables remain consistent with the business case and benefits realization plans. Business value can be tangible or intangible (PMBOK 8th edition, page 14).
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. If the project is following a predictive approach, it can show assuring SPI and CPI, especially at the beginning of its execution. However, since the developer’s rate was underestimated, the project will get off track in terms of cost later on.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. A make-or-buy analysis is considered a tool for measuring financial business value. The project manager should not update the make or buy analysis report without consulting or referring to the sponsor first. The sponsor can determine whether to continue the investment or not if the payback period turns out to be more than 3 years after updating the make-or-buy analysis.

domande.spiegazione: The project manager should notify the sponsor of any identified risks that may impact the business value of the project. Business value measurements are used to ensure that the project deliverables remain consistent with the business case and benefits realization plans. Business value can be tangible or intangible (PMBOK 8th edition, page 14).

domande.domanda:
Two agile teams are working on developing the same product. Team A is made up of 5 members and uses 2-week sprints, while Team B involves 4 members and uses 3-week sprints. Team A completed all sprint backlog items with a velocity of 50 story points. Team B, on the other hand, reached 70 story points without completing all of the sprint’s backlog.
Which team has better performance?

opzioni.A: Team A, since they completed all sprint backlog items
opzioni.B: Team A, taking into consideration their velocity, can achieve 75 story points in a 3-week sprint, which is better than what Team B achieved
opzioni.C: Team B, since they have a better velocity
opzioni.D: Team B, since they achieved more story points with fewer team members

domande.spiegazione:
The team that has better performance is the team that fulfills its sprint engagement by completing all of its backlog items. This means that the performance of Team A was better than the performance of Team B.
Options B & C: Velocity should not be used to compare teams’ performance.
Option D: The number of completed user stories per sprint and team size can not indicate whether a team’s performance is good or not.

domande.domanda:
During a project status meeting, the project manager updated the sponsor on the project performance by informing them that the SPI is 0.75 and the CPI is 1.05.
What does this indicate?

opzioni.A: The project is over budget but on schedule
opzioni.B: The project is within budget but behind schedule
opzioni.C: The project is on schedule and within budget
opzioni.D: The project is behind schedule and over budget

domande.spiegazione: A Schedule Performance Index (SPI) of less than 1 indicates that the project is behind schedule. A Cost Performance Index (CPI) greater than 1 means that the project is within the predetermined budget (PMBOK 8th Edition, pages 208-209).

domande.domanda:
A product owner and team members have different interpretations of a particular user story. To resolve the disagreement, the project manager suggests the creation of personas.
What’s the most probable reason for creating personas?

opzioni.A: To use it as a wireframe to help clarify project outcomes
opzioni.B: To engage stakeholders who don’t know much about the project
opzioni.C: To help the development team empathize with the users of the solution
opzioni.D: To identify and describe real users of the solution

domande.spiegazione:
A persona is a fictional representation of the ideal potential users of a product or service. This description helps the team understand and empathize with the users’ needs for the solution. Thus, the team can better adapt the solution to help and satisfy its users in real-life situations.
Options A & B: Persona does not have a role in stakeholder engagement, nor is it a wireframe for clarifying project outcomes.
Option D: Even though a persona involves a set of real-life characteristics, it does not identify or describe the real users of the solution.

domande.domanda:
After introducing a new foreign developer to the team, the project manager noticed that a senior team member seemed to be avoiding any interaction with the new developer.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Talk to the senior team member privately to try and find out the reason behind their behavior and reinforce that exclusion or discrimination is unacceptable.
opzioni.B: Address the issue formally through HR procedures in the next performance review cycle.
opzioni.C: Nothing, since no conflict between the two has occurred, and addressing this can only create unnecessary tension.
opzioni.D: Bring up the situation in a team meeting as a general reminder about inclusivity and collaboration without mentioning names.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. The project manager should talk to the senior team member privately to get to know the reason behind their behavior. Besides, the project manager should be clear about not tolerating any kind of discriminatory behavior towards the new team member and the potential consequences and disciplinary procedures the senior team member will face in case their behavior persists.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Waiting for a formal review delays necessary action and allows the behavior to continue, potentially harming team culture and trust. Ethical concerns should be addressed immediately.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Such behavior should not be ignored, even when it seems to have no tangible impact on work progress.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Raising the topic publicly without understanding the facts risks embarrassing both members and making the team defensive. Private resolution is more professional and effective.

domande.spiegazione: The project manager should talk to the senior team member privately to get to know the reason behind their behavior. Besides, the project manager should be clear about not tolerating any kind of discriminatory behavior towards the new team member and the potential consequences and disciplinary procedures the senior team member will face in case their behavior persists.

domande.domanda:
After the organization’s recent transition to the agile approach, the project manager expected the project team to become self-organized. However, team members still wait for the project manager to assign them work.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Take a few weeks off to force the team to act on their own
opzioni.B: Mentor the team on how to make their own decisions
opzioni.C: Ensure that the team includes different functional expertise
opzioni.D: Support the team by removing encountered impediments

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Taking a vacation is a passive approach to dealing with the problem, and it won’t solve it since the team will get back to relying on the project manager as soon as they come back.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. The project manager can help their team get self-organized by mentoring them on how to make their own decisions. This will empower them to pick their own tasks without waiting for assignments or asking for permission or direction from the project manager every time.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Ensuring that the team includes different functional expertise will help the team be cross-functional rather than self-organizing.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Supporting the team by removing encountered impediments is part of the agile project manager’s duties and won’t help make the team self-organizing.

domande.spiegazione: The project manager can help their team get self-organized by mentoring them on how to make their own decisions. This will empower them to pick their own tasks without waiting for assignments or asking for permission or direction from the project manager every time.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is leading a multi-year software project. After a few months, a senior team member started losing motivation and complaining that their assigned work could be easily done by a junior team member.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Incentivize the senior team member by increasing their salary or rate.
opzioni.B: Increase the engagement of the senior team member by holding team-building activities.
opzioni.C: Be proactive and start looking for a replacement for the senior team member.
opzioni.D: Find more challenging tasks for the senior team member to tackle.

domande.spiegazione:
The reason behind the team member’s demotivation is intrinsic. The senior team member is looking for challenging work and will respond well to stretch goals and problem-solving (PMBOK 8th edition, page 182).
Options A & B: Increasing their salary or holding team-building activities will not help address the original problem.
Option C: Looking for a replacement should be the last resort if all other options fail to motivate the concerned team member.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is facilitating a meeting attended by his project team as well as key stakeholders to prioritize all product backlog items according to their business value and risk level.
Where should each category of items be placed in the product backlog (from top to bottom)? [Dati ricostruiti dalla spiegazione: A = alto valore/alto rischio; B = alto valore/basso rischio; C = basso valore/alto rischio; D = basso valore/basso rischio]
⚠️ Nell'esportazione Udemy manca l'immagine (grafico/tabella) a cui fa riferimento la domanda.

opzioni.A: A, B, C, D
opzioni.B: B, A, D, C
opzioni.C: A, B, D, C
opzioni.D: D, C, B, A

domande.spiegazione:
Items of high value and high risk should be on top, as completing them sooner generates more new knowledge, which eliminates uncertainty and reduces costly failures later on. “High-risk items should be explored and implemented first to avoid rear-loading the risk. If a high-risk item will cause the product or its development to fail (an issue that cannot be resolved), Scrum teams learn about it early. If something is going to fail, you want to fail early, fail cheap, and move on to a new opportunity that has value.” (Agile Project Management for Dummies, Page 178).
Items of high value and low risk should be tackled next. These items are great for achieving quick wins. The project team can then consider working on low-value and low-risk items. Finally, items of low value and high risk should be put off and placed at the bottom of the product backlog since they are not worth the effort. To sum up, the right order is: A, B, D, and then C from top to bottom.
domande.motivo_incertezza: immagine della domanda non presente nell'esportazione

domande.domanda:
A project manager on a new agile project is conducting the team's kickoff meeting. The team is composed of members from development, quality assurance, and UX design who have not worked together before.
What should the project manager do first?

opzioni.A: Facilitate a session for the team to define and agree on the project's primary purpose and goals.
opzioni.B: Discuss with the team the adequate agile framework.
opzioni.C: Assign initial tasks to each team member based on their functional expertise.
opzioni.D: Establish individual performance metrics to track each member's contribution to the project.

domande.spiegazione: Supportive leadership entails focusing on Purpose, People, and then Process. By starting with the "why," the project manager helps the team "engage and coalesce around the goal," which is the foundational step for enabling high performance. Focusing on process or individual metrics is premature.

domande.domanda:
During the last three daily standup meetings with the team, the project manager noticed that a new team member was struggling with one of their assigned tasks, as he seemed to be making no progress towards completing it.
What should the project manager do? (Select two)

opzioni.A: Reassign the task to another team member who has completed similar work before.
opzioni.B: Check whether other team members can help their new colleague with the task after the standup meeting.
opzioni.C: Encourage the new member to improve his performance by setting a clear completion target for the next standup.
opzioni.D: Suggest the new member review similar tasks completed by the team in the past to find a solution.

domande.spiegazione:
Instead of providing the answer, the project manager can start by guiding the team member to available resources (past work, documentation, repositories). This empowers the individual to learn and grow, aligning with the principle of developing team member competence. It is a coaching-oriented approach that helps the team member become self-sufficient in the long run. If that doesn’t work, the project manager can try a more direct and collaborative approach, asking another team member to help mentor the new member and guide them through getting their task completed. Since the member is new and they might lack certain skills or experience dealing with certain types of tasks, they will get the chance to learn and overcome any impediments by collaborating with more experienced team members (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 31).
Option A: Assigning someone else to get the task done will only have a bad impact on their self-esteem and motivation and make them miss out on a learning opportunity.
Option C: Encouraging the new member to improve his performance without proper guidance is ineffective. The project manager should provide the team member with practical guidance to help them overcome their struggle with the assigned task.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is leading a project within a functional organization. Halfway through the project implementation, a team member left the organization.
What should the project manager do first?

opzioni.A: Collaborate with the functional manager to get a replacement
opzioni.B: Update the project’s resource breakdown structure
opzioni.C: Reassign their workload to the project team member
opzioni.D: Evaluate the impact of the team member’s departure on the project

domande.spiegazione:
First, the project manager should understand the impact of the team member's departure on the project. It might have a big impact; therefore, the leaving member needs to be promptly replaced with an experienced member. Or, their departure might have a limited impact, and the project can proceed without their contribution.
Options A & C: Based on the evaluation findings, a decision should be made; whether to get a replacement or reassign the workload.
Option B: The project’s resource breakdown structure should be updated later on to reflect the new changes.

domande.domanda:
Before starting the project, and after identifying all of the individuals and groups involved or affected by the project, the project manager took a step further by classifying stakeholders according to their level of power, interest, and influence.
This step is referred to as:

opzioni.A: Stakeholder analysis
opzioni.B: Stakeholder identification
opzioni.C: Stakeholder monitoring
opzioni.D: Stakeholder engagement

domande.spiegazione:
Since the question states that stakeholders were already identified and that the project hasn't started yet, stakeholder analysis is the right answer. Stakeholder analysis refers to the classification of all project stakeholders in order to ensure efficient engagement later on (PMBOK 8th Edition, pages 199-200).
Option D: Stakeholder engagement takes place in the execution focus area, and it involves: communicating and collaborating with stakeholders to meet their expectations, addressing issues, and fostering appropriate stakeholder involvement (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 70).
Option C: Stakeholder monitoring implies assessing stakeholders’ satisfaction and whether their engagement plan is effective or needs to be updated (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 73).

domande.domanda:
A project manager is developing the business case of a green transportation project. To do so, they decide to use the SWOT technique.
How should the project manager apply this technique?

opzioni.A: Follow a Plan-Do-Check-Act cycle (PDCA Cycle)
opzioni.B: Assess the business model using expert judgment
opzioni.C: Identify the project's strengths and weaknesses
opzioni.D: Conduct a benefit/cost analysis

domande.spiegazione:
SWOT stands for Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, and Threats. It’s a tool that project managers use to assess the opportunities and threats they might face, as well as their projects’ strengths and weaknesses (PMBOK 8th edition, page 204).
Option A: The PDCA cycle is a quality management technique to control and continuously improve processes and products (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 158).
Options B & D: Assessing the project’s business model or conducting a benefit/cost analysis could be part of developing the business case, but both methods have a different purpose from the SWOT technique.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is managing an online e-learning platform. The project team is following the Scrum framework, and every few weeks, they release a new version that includes more features, user interface changes, bug fixes, security patches, etc. In order to avoid confusing users with the continuous changes, the project manager decides to make all release information accessible to the platform members under the “News” section on the website.
What type of communication does the project manager plan to use?

opzioni.A: Push communication
opzioni.B: Interactive communication
opzioni.C: Pull communication
opzioni.D: Proactive communication

domande.spiegazione:
Pull communication is a communication type where access to the information is provided; however, the receiver must proactively seek out and retrieve this information. When the communication is solely for informative purposes, pull communication should be used. It will have little to no impact on the project if the recipients do not read it. According to the PMI process groups guide: “Pull communication is used for large complex information sets, or for large audiences, and requires the recipients to access the content at their own discretion. These methods include web portals, intranet sites, e-learning, lessons learned databases, or knowledge repositories.” (PMI Process groups Guide, page 253)
Option D: PMBOK defined three types of communication: interactive, push, and pull (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 152). Proactive communication is a made-up term.

domande.domanda:
During the construction of a small infrastructure project, the project manager decided to cancel the scheduled lessons learned review meeting due to time constraints and the pressure to move forward with project closure.
What direct consequence might result from this decision?

opzioni.A: Future projects could face low stakeholder satisfaction.
opzioni.B: Future projects may encounter the same issues.
opzioni.C: Future projects could face increased risks.
opzioni.D: Future projects may incur higher costs.

domande.spiegazione:
Lessons learned reviews provide an opportunity to identify and document recurring issues and implement preventive measures. Canceling the review means these insights are not captured, increasing the likelihood of similar issues arising in future projects, particularly those that could lead to claims or inefficiencies.
Options A, C, D: Stakeholder dissatisfaction and increased risks or costs can be the consequence of the recurring issues; they are not the most immediate or direct result of canceling the lessons learned meeting.
