opzioni.C: Ask other team members to take over the affected team member’s tasks until the issue is resolved.
opzioni.D: Coordinate with the IT department to ensure the issue is addressed as a priority.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Asking the team member to reach out to the IT department directly might be a logical first step. However, it lacks urgency and doesn’t reflect servant leadership. The project manager should remove impediments for the team.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The product owner handles product value and backlog prioritization, not internal technical support issues. Escalating this to the product owner is inappropriate.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Asking other team members to take over the affected team member’s tasks may temporarily help, but it does not resolve the root issue. It also risks overloading others without addressing the blocked team member’s productivity.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. According to the Agile Practice Guide, one of the key responsibilities of the agile project manager as a servant leader is to remove obstacles that block team progress. Ensuring quick resolution of technical issues is a core part of that role.

domande.spiegazione: According to the Agile Practice Guide, one of the key responsibilities of the agile project manager as a servant leader is to remove obstacles that block team progress. Ensuring quick resolution of technical issues is a core part of that role.

domande.domanda:
Leading a construction project with a diverse team, the project manager recently noticed rising tensions and decreased morale, with some team members feeling their concerns are not being heard. The project manager has been under a lot of pressure and realizes that he may have been less approachable.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Reflect on his behavior, acknowledge the issue to the team, and invite open feedback to address concerns.
opzioni.B: Focus on deliverables, and the situation will improve on its own.
opzioni.C: Assign a team member to handle morale issues and focus on technical tasks.
opzioni.D: Focus on meeting deadlines as a top priority.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. Demonstrating self-awareness by reflecting on your actions and inviting feedback aligns with the value that effective leaders can make a connection between their feelings, thoughts, and actions. This self-awareness helps professionals build relationships to accomplish results. This approach also supports enhanced team performance and increased trust and morale as outcomes of accountable leadership (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 46).
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Ignoring the issue risks further decline in team performance and morale.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Assigning a team member to handle morale issues without personal involvement fails to show humility and availability.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. While meeting deadlines is important, ignoring team morale and rising tensions will likely harm performance and increase risks. A project manager’s role isn’t only to track deadlines, it’s also to lead the team, resolve conflicts, and maintain a healthy work environment. In the long run, deadlines are more at risk if the team is disengaged or demotivated.

domande.spiegazione: Demonstrating self-awareness by reflecting on your actions and inviting feedback aligns with the value that effective leaders can make a connection between their feelings, thoughts, and actions. This self-awareness helps professionals build relationships to accomplish results. This approach also supports enhanced team performance and increased trust and morale as outcomes of accountable leadership (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 46).

domande.domanda:
A project manager is in the phase of identifying and evaluating the risks of a construction project. One of the identified risks is so complex and ambiguous that the project manager decides to transfer it to the program manager so the latter can make the appropriate decision.
How did the project manager respond to the risk?

opzioni.A: Transfer
opzioni.B: Mitigate
opzioni.C: Escalate
opzioni.D: Avoid

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Transferring the risk entails shifting the threat ownership and responsibility to a third party, which may involve payment of a risk premium to the third party assuming the threat.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Risk mitigation implies decreasing the threat probability of occurrence and/or impact.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. In the described scenario, the project manager has escalated the risk to the program manager. When a threat is considered to be outside the project scope or when the appropriate response exceeds the project manager’s authority, risk escalation is the suitable risk response strategy. Risk escalation involves passing the risk to the right owner (the program manager in this case) to ensure that it is recognized, understood, and managed appropriately (PMBOK 8th Edition, pages 203-204).
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Avoiding the risk means eliminating the threat or protecting the project from its impact.

domande.spiegazione: In the described scenario, the project manager has escalated the risk to the program manager. When a threat is considered to be outside the project scope or when the appropriate response exceeds the project manager’s authority, risk escalation is the suitable risk response strategy. Risk escalation involves passing the risk to the right owner (the program manager in this case) to ensure that it is recognized, understood, and managed appropriately (PMBOK 8th Edition, pages 203-204).

domande.domanda:
A project manager is overseeing the integration of a new CRM system across sales, marketing, and customer service departments. The integration requires frequent data synchronization between legacy systems and the new platform. Midway through execution, the team reports that the process is significantly slower than expected due to a recently introduced IT security protocol.
What should the project manager do next?

opzioni.A: Provide training to help the team better understand and use the new IT protocol effectively.
opzioni.B: Hold a brainstorming session to explore temporary solutions that maintain security while improving integration speed.
opzioni.C: Hold a meeting with the project team to study potential alternatives to replace the IT security protocol.
opzioni.D: Hold a meeting with the IT department and the project team to understand the protocol’s implementation.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Training does not resolve the core issue: the protocol itself is causing systemic delays. The team may understand the process perfectly, but if the protocol requires excessive steps for each data transfer, no amount of training will eliminate the bottleneck. This option treats a process inefficiency as a knowledge gap, which is misaligned with root cause analysis.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Holding a brainstorming session to explore temporary solutions risks encouraging workarounds that could bypass security controls, even unintentionally. Security protocols are typically mandated for compliance or risk mitigation. Proposing temporary fixes without understanding the full scope and intent of the protocol may lead to non-compliance or technical debt. This is not a sustainable or ethical approach.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Holding a meeting with the project team to study potential alternatives to replace the IT security protocol is an overreach. The project manager and team do not have the authority to replace an organization-wide security protocol. Such decisions are made by IT governance and cybersecurity leadership. Attempting to bypass or replace a mandated control undermines organizational policies.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Holding a meeting with the IT department and the project team to understand the protocol’s implementation is the best first step because it engages the IT department which designed and implemented the protocol, builds shared understanding of its purpose, scope, and constraints, and opens a collaborative channel for identifying approved optimizations. By seeking to understand the protocol first, the project manager ensures that any proposed changes are compliant, secure, organizationally acceptable, and risk-informed.

domande.spiegazione: Holding a meeting with the IT department and the project team to understand the protocol’s implementation is the best first step because it engages the IT department which designed and implemented the protocol, builds shared understanding of its purpose, scope, and constraints, and opens a collaborative channel for identifying approved optimizations. By seeking to understand the protocol first, the project manager ensures that any proposed changes are compliant, secure, organizationally acceptable, and risk-informed.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is leading a large infrastructure project. Early in the planning phase, the project manager realized that focusing solely on engineering deliverables may overlook environmental impacts and community concerns. Some team members suggest sticking to the technical plan to avoid delays.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Proceed with the technical plan and address environmental and community issues when they arise.
opzioni.B: Integrate environmental and stakeholder considerations into the project plan.
opzioni.C: Assign responsibility for environmental issues to a separate consultant and focus only on technical tasks.
opzioni.D: Wait for regulatory authorities to raise concerns before making any changes.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Ignoring interconnected aspects increases project risk and undermines sustainability. The project manager should proactively address environmental and community issues instead of waiting until these issues arise.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Integrating environmental and stakeholder perspectives from the start exemplifies a holistic view, aligning with the principle of considering all project components and their interdependencies for sustainable and resilient outcomes (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 39).
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Assigning responsibility for environmental issues to a separate consultant leads to siloing responsibilities, preventing integrated decision-making, and leading to misalignment and missed risks.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Waiting for regulatory authorities to raise concerns before making any changes is reactive management, which fails to anticipate risks and does not foster resilience or adaptability.

domande.spiegazione: Integrating environmental and stakeholder perspectives from the start exemplifies a holistic view, aligning with the principle of considering all project components and their interdependencies for sustainable and resilient outcomes (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 39).

domande.domanda:
A project manager wants to assess four potential suppliers by ranking them based on three main aspects: the quality of their products, their production capacity, and their costs.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Apply a screening system to eliminate suppliers who do not meet minimum standards.
opzioni.B: Use evaluation criteria to list the general attributes required from suppliers.
opzioni.C: Use a weighting system to assign importance to evaluation factors and rank suppliers accordingly.
opzioni.D: Initiate contract negotiations with the top-ranked supplier based on general preference.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The project manager should not use a screening system since they are not eliminating sellers who do not meet particular conditions.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. The project manager has already chosen the evaluation criteria they’re using (i.e., the quality of products, production capacity, and costs). Now, they need a tool that includes weighting or detailed ranking based on these evaluation criteria.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Since the project manager wants to rank suppliers through the use of specific criteria (aka evaluation criteria), they should use a weighting system to score each supplier’s performance on each criterion (PMBOK 8th Edition, pages 249-250).
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The project manager has not reached the contract negotiation phase yet.

domande.spiegazione: Since the project manager wants to rank suppliers through the use of specific criteria (aka evaluation criteria), they should use a weighting system to score each supplier’s performance on each criterion (PMBOK 8th Edition, pages 249-250).

domande.domanda:
A project manager is in charge of a public project under a fixed-price contract of $220,000, inclusive of 10% VAT. During the project execution, a new law was passed that increased the VAT rate from 10% to 15%.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Submit an invoice of $220,000, inclusive of 10% VAT.
opzioni.B: Submit an invoice of $220,000, inclusive of 15% VAT.
opzioni.C: Submit an invoice of $230,000, inclusive of 15% VAT.
opzioni.D: Submit a claim since the VAT change reduces the profit margins of the project.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. It’s illegal to violate tax laws by underreporting VAT. Since the new law (15% VAT) is in effect, the contractor must issue invoices with the updated rate to avoid tax penalties.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. If the claim is denied, the fallback is to invoice $220,000 with 15% VAT, legally complying with the new rate while absorbing the reduced profit.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Unilaterally increasing the invoice to $230,000 would breach contract terms unless a formal change order or amendment is approved.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. Since the change in VAT is due to a legal or regulatory change beyond the contractor’s control, the project manager should submit a claim under the contract’s change clause or force majeure/governing law clause, depending on the contract terms.

domande.spiegazione: Since the change in VAT is due to a legal or regulatory change beyond the contractor’s control, the project manager should submit a claim under the contract’s change clause or force majeure/governing law clause, depending on the contract terms.

domande.domanda:
A fintech company is building a banking app for foreign workers. 70% of coding is complete when a competitor reveals plans for a similar app that will help foreign workers make money transfers to their home countries.
What should the project manager do next?

opzioni.A: Accelerate launch to beat the competitor to market.
opzioni.B: Inform stakeholders about remittance needs and discuss adapting the app.
opzioni.C: Abandon the project to avoid direct competition.
opzioni.D: Sue the competitor for intellectual property theft.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. An accelerated launch means rushing without considering all aspects, which might risk launching an inferior product.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. The competitor’s move highlights an important market requirement: remittance functionality. Project managers should ensure that projects deliver value aligned with stakeholder and market needs. By raising the issue with stakeholders, the PM can drive a conversation about whether the app should pivot or expand its scope to address remittance. This maintains strategic alignment and adaptability in a dynamic market.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Abandoning the project is an overreaction to competition rather than adapting to unforeseen changes. This means wasting 70% of completed work, showing poor resilience and adaptability.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Taking legal action misallocates resources to non-productive efforts and doesn't address the core competitive threat.

domande.spiegazione: The competitor’s move highlights an important market requirement: remittance functionality. Project managers should ensure that projects deliver value aligned with stakeholder and market needs. By raising the issue with stakeholders, the PM can drive a conversation about whether the app should pivot or expand its scope to address remittance. This maintains strategic alignment and adaptability in a dynamic market.

domande.domanda:
During the risk identification process, attrition of resources was identified as a major risk. As a response, the project manager decided to opt for financial incentives to motivate the project team.
What type of risk response is the project manager following?

opzioni.A: Acceptance
opzioni.B: Mitigation
opzioni.C: Transference
opzioni.D: Avoidance

domande.spiegazione: The project manager is mitigating the risk of resource attrition. This type of risk response aims to diminish the probability and/or impact of a threat (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 204).

domande.domanda:
A project manager works in an organization that adopts the predictive approach. The project they’re currently leading is running over budget, so they won’t be able to complete it without obtaining more funds. After updating the management on the project status, and after being asked to present a new budget assessment, the project manager estimates that they need an additional amount of $35,000.
This is an example of:

opzioni.A: Forecast analysis
opzioni.B: Status report
opzioni.C: Change request
opzioni.D: Progress report

domande.spiegazione: The project budget might change as the project progresses. In this case, the project manager informed management about the new forecasted budget; (BAC + $35,000), which is known as EAC (Estimate at Completion).

domande.domanda:
A project team shifting from predictive to agile delivery is experiencing frequent production issues, especially during handoff to the operations team. The project manager wants to reduce these support problems in future releases.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Invite the operations team to participate in retrospectives and demos and apply their feedback to project activities.
opzioni.B: Prioritize backlog items related to support needs, such as documentation and user manuals.
opzioni.C: Encourage early involvement of stakeholders during backlog refinement discussions.
opzioni.D: Invite the operations team to daily standups to stay updated on progress.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. The project manager should invite the operations team to participate in retrospectives and demos and apply their feedback to project activities. Including operations in reviews and retrospectives helps build shared ownership, improve handoffs, and reduce post-release issues.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Prioritizing backlog items related to support needs doesn’t address the root cause: lack of collaboration with operations. This is a partial solution and does not ensure operational alignment or feedback loops.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Involving stakeholders in backlog refinement doesn't specifically address the transition-to-operations issue or support problems.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Daily standups are for the development team to coordinate work. Operations joining daily may not be practical or valuable. Involvement in reviews and retrospectives is more impactful for transition improvement.

domande.spiegazione: The project manager should invite the operations team to participate in retrospectives and demos and apply their feedback to project activities. Including operations in reviews and retrospectives helps build shared ownership, improve handoffs, and reduce post-release issues.

domande.domanda:
A project manager has joined a team delivering a customized ERP solution. During development, the team identifies a potential design flaw and suggests a new design to avoid future deployment issues. However, the original design has already been formally approved, and the team is not confident about the new design.
What should the project manager do next?

opzioni.A: Submit a formal change request to run a proof of concept.
opzioni.B: Submit a formal change request to change the original design.
opzioni.C: Run a proof of concept to validate that the new design resolves the issue.
opzioni.D: Change the project development approach to agile to make design changes more flexible.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. The team is uncertain whether the new design will work. Therefore, it would be premature to approve a full design change without validation. The best next step is to submit a formal change request, not to change the design immediately, but to authorize a Proof of Concept (PoC). This allows the team to test feasibility, manage risk, and gather evidence before making a larger design decision.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Submitting a formal change request to change the original design is premature. The team is not confident in the new design. Approving a design change without validation may introduce greater technical and schedule risk.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Running a proof of concept without submitting a formal change request is considered scope creep since it violates the governance and control procedures established after design approval.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Changing the project development approach to agile to make design changes more flexible is unrealistic mid-project, and unrelated to resolving the current design concern. Changing the entire delivery approach introduces new risks and doesn’t address the immediate issue.

domande.spiegazione: The team is uncertain whether the new design will work. Therefore, it would be premature to approve a full design change without validation. The best next step is to submit a formal change request, not to change the design immediately, but to authorize a Proof of Concept (PoC). This allows the team to test feasibility, manage risk, and gather evidence before making a larger design decision.

domande.domanda:
A project manager has been assigned to manage the development of a large healthcare facility. The project follows a Lean Construction methodology, emphasizing collaboration, waste reduction, and continuous improvement. During the early phases of the project execution, the project manager discovers that the subcontractor responsible for structural steel lacks experience with Lean Construction practices.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Do nothing since the project is already underway.
opzioni.B: Terminate the subcontractor’s contract due to their lack of transparency.
opzioni.C: Instruct the subcontractor to begin Lean training immediately.
opzioni.D: Identify areas requiring immediate support to align the subcontractor with Lean practices.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Ignoring the issue could lead to inefficiencies, misalignment with Lean principles, and further complications during project execution.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Terminating the contract is an extreme measure that would likely cause significant project delays and increase costs. The subcontractor’s lack of Lean experience does not necessarily indicate intentional non-transparency.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Requiring training without assessing specific gaps and providing targeted guidance risks delaying project progress and might not address the subcontractor’s immediate needs effectively.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. This approach enables the project manager to address specific deficiencies and provide targeted assistance, ensuring the subcontractor can contribute effectively to the project while adhering to Lean Construction principles. It promotes collaboration and minimizes disruption.

domande.spiegazione: This approach enables the project manager to address specific deficiencies and provide targeted assistance, ensuring the subcontractor can contribute effectively to the project while adhering to Lean Construction principles. It promotes collaboration and minimizes disruption.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is leading an Agile app development project. During a sprint review, a key stakeholder requests adding a new feature that is similar to one developed in a prior sprint. The stakeholder asks for a quick estimate of how this addition might affect the project’s timeline and budget.
What should the project manager do next?

opzioni.A: Collaborate with the development team to estimate the new feature based on its complexity.
opzioni.B: Work with the product owner to determine how the new feature might affect the project’s schedule and costs.
opzioni.C: Review the user stories and velocity metrics from the previous sprint related to the similar feature to estimate the effort required for the new addition.
opzioni.D: Initiate a detailed risk analysis to identify potential schedule overruns and budget implications of incorporating the new feature.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Collaborating with the development team to estimate the new feature based on its complexity misses a key opportunity to leverage historical data. While involving the team is essential, ignoring comparable past work contradicts Agile best practices like relative estimation and empirical forecasting. The team should use previous velocity and user stories as a baseline, not start from scratch. This option represents a missed efficiency and fails to provide a quick estimation as requested.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. While the product owner is involved in prioritization, they are not responsible for estimations.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. The project manager should review the user stories and velocity metrics from the previous sprint related to the similar feature. By reviewing past performance, the project manager can estimate story points or effort based on similar scope and provide a quick, credible, data-backed response to the stakeholder’s request.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. While risk analysis is valuable, it’s overkill for a quick estimation. The stakeholder wants a preliminary estimate, not a full risk report. This option delays response and may overwhelm the request with unnecessary detail.

domande.spiegazione: The project manager should review the user stories and velocity metrics from the previous sprint related to the similar feature. By reviewing past performance, the project manager can estimate story points or effort based on similar scope and provide a quick, credible, data-backed response to the stakeholder’s request.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is facilitating a workshop for a construction project aimed at improving cost-efficiency without compromising essential functionality. During the session, a team member proposes replacing a critical structural component with a less expensive alternative that slightly reduces performance but offers significant cost savings.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Accept the team member’s recommendation since it lowers the total project budget.
opzioni.B: Dismiss the team member’s idea since it compromises the component’s performance.
opzioni.C: Assess whether the decrease in performance affects the project’s core functionality compared to the financial benefits.
opzioni.D: Proceed with the change if no further approvals are needed from stakeholders.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. While cost reduction is a goal of Value Engineering, it must be balanced with functionality and value. Approving a change solely for cost savings may compromise the project’s purpose, violating the core principle of maximizing value, not just minimizing cost.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Dismissing the idea rejects innovation without analysis. Value Engineering encourages creative solutions, even if they involve trade-offs. The key is to evaluate whether the performance decrease is acceptable relative to the savings.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C:
Correct. The project manager should assess whether the decrease in performance affects the project’s core functionality compared to the financial benefits. This is the correct application of Value Engineering principles, which focus on:
Function-first thinking: What is the component’s essential function?
Cost-performance balance: Is the cost saving worth the functional trade-off?
Value optimization: Does the change improve the ratio of function to cost?
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Even if approval isn’t required, the change must still be evaluated for impact. Skipping analysis risks unintended consequences and undermines project integrity.

domande.spiegazione:
The project manager should assess whether the decrease in performance affects the project’s core functionality compared to the financial benefits. This is the correct application of Value Engineering principles, which focus on:
Function-first thinking: What is the component’s essential function?
Cost-performance balance: Is the cost saving worth the functional trade-off?
Value optimization: Does the change improve the ratio of function to cost?

domande.domanda:
A project manager is leading the development of a new data analytics platform using an Agile approach. The project is subject to strict regulatory and organizational quality standards. A formal quality audit has just been completed, and the audit team has identified several gaps.
What should the project manager do next?

opzioni.A: Provide the audit team with access to all project records and ask them to validate the completeness of the audit findings.
opzioni.B: Prepare the team to clarify any aspects of the audit findings upon request.
opzioni.C: Meet with the audit team to understand the root causes of the findings and develop a corrective action plan.
opzioni.D: Hold a team meeting to assess the audit results and start fixing the issues.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. The audit has already been completed. Re-submitting documents does not address the findings. It treats the audit as an inspection, not a continuous improvement opportunity.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. While readiness is important, preparing the team to clarify any aspects of the audit findings upon request delays action. The project manager should not wait for follow-up questions; they should initiate corrective actions immediately after receiving and understanding the results.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Meeting with the audit team to understand the root causes of the findings and develop a corrective action plan is the best next step because it promotes shared understanding of the issues and ensures that corrective actions are accurate and aligned with standards. By working with the audit team, the project manager turns findings into actionable improvements, not just compliance checkboxes.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. While internal review is useful, acting without alignment with the audit team can lead to rework or failed verification. The best practice is to collaborate first, then act.

domande.spiegazione: Meeting with the audit team to understand the root causes of the findings and develop a corrective action plan is the best next step because it promotes shared understanding of the issues and ensures that corrective actions are accurate and aligned with standards. By working with the audit team, the project manager turns findings into actionable improvements, not just compliance checkboxes.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is leading an urban development project for a city government. Midway through execution, the lead structural engineer announced his departure due to personal reasons. The project is already on a tight timeline. The project team expresses concern about the increased workload and potential delays.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Assign the lead engineer’s responsibilities to other team members to compensate for his departure.
opzioni.B: Contract external experts to handle high-priority work that cannot be delayed.
opzioni.C: Work with the team to identify resource needs and hire a replacement to maintain project momentum.
opzioni.D: Request an extension of the project deadline due to unexpected personnel changes.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Assigning the lead engineer’s responsibilities to other team members increases stress and risk of burnout. It may also reduce quality if team members are overburdened. This approach avoids addressing the root issue: resource depletion.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. While outsourcing can help, it should not be the first step. It assumes that external resources are available and affordable, which may not always be the case. Also, integrating third parties takes time and may introduce coordination risks.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. By working with the team, the project manager ensures that new hires have the right skills, knowledge transfer is planned, and team morale remains stable. This is the best proactive measure because it addresses the root cause (loss of critical human resources), involves the team in solution-building, and supports long-term sustainability by replacing talent rather than just patching gaps.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Requesting an extension of the project deadline is a reactive approach. It also accepts failure to meet the set deadline rather than seeking solutions. The project manager should explore options to keep the schedule before requesting an extension.

domande.spiegazione: By working with the team, the project manager ensures that new hires have the right skills, knowledge transfer is planned, and team morale remains stable. This is the best proactive measure because it addresses the root cause (loss of critical human resources), involves the team in solution-building, and supports long-term sustainability by replacing talent rather than just patching gaps.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is leading a major upgrade to an existing mobile app. During task estimation, the development team expresses differing opinions on the effort required for a particular feature that has varying levels of technical complexity and integration challenges.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Propose building a small-scale prototype to gain clarity on the technical requirements and effort needed.
opzioni.B: Allow the team to further investigate the feature and revise their individual estimates.
opzioni.C: Ask each team member to explain their reasoning and assumptions behind their estimate, then guide the team toward a shared understanding.
opzioni.D: Involve the product owner to further explain the feature’s properties to help the team better understand the required effort level.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Prototyping might help if the differences stem from uncertainty, not assumptions, which is not the case. This can only delay decision-making and add unnecessary work.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Giving team members extra time to investigate the feature and revise their individual estimates will delay progress. The goal is not to wait, but to align.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Asking each team member to explain their reasoning and assumptions behind their estimate is the best approach because it helps the team identify shared assumptions, clarify technical challenges, and reach a consensus-based estimate, ensuring that the final estimate is well-informed, realistic, and collectively owned.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. While the product owner owns the what (requirements), they do not own the how or how much. Effort estimation is the responsibility of the development team, not the product owner. Bringing in the product owner may clarify functional intent, but it won’t resolve technical disagreements. The core issue isn't unclear scope; it’s differing technical interpretations among developers.

domande.spiegazione: Asking each team member to explain their reasoning and assumptions behind their estimate is the best approach because it helps the team identify shared assumptions, clarify technical challenges, and reach a consensus-based estimate, ensuring that the final estimate is well-informed, realistic, and collectively owned.

domande.domanda:
From past experience, the project manager of a construction project knows that there is a risk of not receiving the needed sand supply on time. Therefore, the project manager included this potential threat in the risk register. If this risk were to occur, the project manager would have to purchase the sand from another supplier. But, in this case, there may be some differences in the sand quality.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Order the sand ahead of time to avoid delays.
opzioni.B: Reject the lower-quality sand of the new supplier.
opzioni.C: Keep ordering from different suppliers until finding a reliable supplier with good sand quality.
opzioni.D: Check the sand quality and ask for quality guarantees before ordering.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. This option changes the agreed risk response strategy. Ordering early may avoid delays but could create storage or cost issues, and doesn’t address the real concern, which is quality differences from the alternative supplier.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Rejecting the sand after it arrives is reactive and may cause delays. Quality concerns should be addressed before ordering through proper evaluation, not after delivery.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. This trial-and-error method is inefficient. It indicates poor planning and can result in cost overruns and delays. Proper quality checks should be done before selecting a supplier.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. The risk has already been identified and documented in the risk register, with an appropriate contingency plan (using an alternate supplier). Since there’s a known risk of quality variation, the correct response is to proactively verify the alternative supplier’s quality standards and request guarantees before proceeding.

domande.spiegazione: The risk has already been identified and documented in the risk register, with an appropriate contingency plan (using an alternate supplier). Since there’s a known risk of quality variation, the correct response is to proactively verify the alternative supplier’s quality standards and request guarantees before proceeding.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is assigned to lead a project abroad. At the start of the project execution, the project manager gets worried about the country’s high levels of violence in public. The project manager gets approached by a local police officer who pledges to keep the project team safe during their stay in return for a private money transfer.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Not pay the police officer and ignore this incident.
opzioni.B: Not pay the police officer and rather follow the chain of command.
opzioni.C: Pay the police officer and consider it a facilitation payment.
opzioni.D: Pay through a 3rd party, considering how suspicious the situation is.

domande.spiegazione: In such situations, the project manager should not pay and should instead follow the chain of command and solicit their support in providing security to the project team. This situation is considered bribery or at least palm greasing. Nevertheless, the project manager should act proactively and take all security measures.

domande.domanda: Despite creating an agenda and timeboxing the meetings, the project manager struggles to engage all attendees. What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Make meetings shorter to prevent boredom.
opzioni.B: Limit the interventions of the most talkative attendees to allow others to participate.
opzioni.C: Change to remote meetings to make everyone feel more comfortable.
opzioni.D: Encourage all attendees to participate and share their thoughts by asking for their opinions on the discussed matters.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Simply reducing meeting duration does not address the core issue of disengaged attendees. The goal is to actively involve everyone in the discussion.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Focusing solely on controlling dominant participants may not fully resolve the issue. Encouraging contributions from quieter attendees is a more effective strategy for balanced engagement.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Changing to remote meetings doesn’t guarantee improved engagement. The issue lies in fostering active participation, regardless of the meeting format.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. As a facilitator, the project manager must ensure that all attendees take part in the meeting by encouraging them to share their ideas and opinions and engaging them in the discussed topics. It’s among their responsibilities as a facilitator to ensure that everyone takes part in the decision-making, problem-solving, brainstorming, etc., activities that take place during meetings. Promoting participation and maintaining the ideas and discussions flow during such events is an indication of efficient facilitation (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 170).

domande.spiegazione: As a facilitator, the project manager must ensure that all attendees take part in the meeting by encouraging them to share their ideas and opinions and engaging them in the discussed topics. It’s among their responsibilities as a facilitator to ensure that everyone takes part in the decision-making, problem-solving, brainstorming, etc., activities that take place during meetings. Promoting participation and maintaining the ideas and discussions flow during such events is an indication of efficient facilitation (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 170).

domande.domanda:
A project manager oversaw the construction of a new highway interchange that was completed 5% under budget. However, during final inspections, engineers discovered the off-ramp dangerously narrows at a critical curve, violating safety standards. The transportation ministry orders a full redesign, requiring demolition of the $8.2 million structure. Stakeholders are furious, but the construction firm insists they followed the approved plans exactly.
What should the project manager do first?

opzioni.A: Involve a 3rd party to determine who bears the incurred loss.
opzioni.B: Initiate a joint review with designers and contractors to determine whether specifications were unclear or implementation was flawed.
opzioni.C: Fast-track the demolition to demonstrate decisive action, then bill the design firm for all rework costs.
opzioni.D: Convene an independent safety audit while pausing all similar interchange projects.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Before assigning responsibility, the project manager must first understand what happened. Jumping straight to determining fault skips the root cause analysis and undermines collaboration. A 3rd party is either a mediator or an arbitrator, who gets involved to facilitate an agreement between disputing parties. This isn't the appropriate first step; the project manager should try negotiation and collaboration to find a solution before moving on to alternative dispute resolution.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Budget adherence doesn't compensate for a flawed deliverable (outcome failure). The project manager must investigate why efficient execution (meeting budget) failed to deliver a safe, usable interchange (strategic value). A joint review identifies whether design specifications were inadequate (planning failure), contractors misinterpreted plans (execution failure), or inspection processes missed the defect (quality control failure). Transparent collaboration with all parties maintains trust while solving the problem.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Billing the design firm for all rework costs before investigation represents blame-shifting, violating ethical principles.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Pausing all similar interchange projects without data is an overreaction since these projects are unrelated.

domande.spiegazione: Budget adherence doesn't compensate for a flawed deliverable (outcome failure). The project manager must investigate why efficient execution (meeting budget) failed to deliver a safe, usable interchange (strategic value). A joint review identifies whether design specifications were inadequate (planning failure), contractors misinterpreted plans (execution failure), or inspection processes missed the defect (quality control failure). Transparent collaboration with all parties maintains trust while solving the problem.

domande.domanda:
A project manager has been brought on to a project in the very early stages and has been asked to write its charter. Over the past week, the project manager met with a number of stakeholders, received their input, and is now ready to have the charter signed.
Who can sign the project charter? (Select three)

opzioni.A: Project Sponsor
opzioni.B: Project Steering Committee
opzioni.C: Project Manager
opzioni.D: Project Management Office (PMO)

domande.spiegazione:
Projects get authorized by someone external to the project, such as the sponsor, PMO, or steering committee.
Option C: The project manager cannot sign the charter to authorize himself to start executing the project.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is leading a global Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system development. The system is scheduled for release in one year and must comply with strict regulatory requirements, such as data privacy laws. The project manager had meticulously planned the project, wanting to ensure the system’s quality and avoid any critical delays or rework.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Hold regular review sessions with stakeholders to ensure alignment with user needs.
opzioni.B: Since the project is meticulously planned, testing can be done at the final phase.
opzioni.C: Conduct comprehensive testing after developing all features to validate the whole system’s functionality.
opzioni.D: Conduct continuous testing to detect and fix defects before they escalate.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. While regular reviews are valuable, they focus on validation, not verification and quality assurance. They help confirm that the product meets stakeholder expectations, but they don’t ensure technical quality or compliance.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Even with a well-defined plan, testing is essential. Skipping testing increases the risk of undetected bugs, compliance failures, and rework.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Delaying testing until late in the project means defects are harder and more expensive to fix, regulatory compliance may be missed, and delays are likely if major issues are found.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. By conducting continuous testing, the project manager embeds quality into processes and deliverables. Regular testing allows the team to identify issues early, reduce technical debt, ensure compliance with regulations, and avoid costly rework and delays.

domande.spiegazione: By conducting continuous testing, the project manager embeds quality into processes and deliverables. Regular testing allows the team to identify issues early, reduce technical debt, ensure compliance with regulations, and avoid costly rework and delays.

domande.domanda:
During a project to develop a new platform, the company replaced the original product owner with a new one who has a limited understanding of the product. As a result, the team starts disregarding the new product owner's input and instead looks to the project manager for direction.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Assign decision-making to the most experienced team member until the new product owner gains more expertise.
opzioni.B: Arrange a team-building workshop and encourage the team to value the new product owner’s input.
opzioni.C: Temporarily take on the responsibilities of the product owner while they get up to speed.
opzioni.D: Take time to share knowledge about the product and project context with the new product owner.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Assigning decision-making to the most experienced team member, even if it’s a temporary solution, undermines the role of the Product Owner; the Product Owner must remain the single source of product backlog decisions. Shifting authority to a senior team member dilutes accountability, confuses the team, and delays the new PO’s integration into the role.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Arranging a team-building workshop and encouraging the team to value the new product owner’s input does not address the root cause, i.e., the product owner’s lack of product knowledge. Respect is built through competence and trust, not just interpersonal activities.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Temporarily taking on the responsibilities of the product owner while they get up to speed undermines agile roles and creates confusion. The project manager should not assume responsibilities that belong to another defined role.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. The project manager should schedule time to share insights with the new product owner about the product and project information. This aligns with the servant leadership role of the project manager in agile. Providing timely support helps empower the product owner and restores their authority in the team.

domande.spiegazione: The project manager should schedule time to share insights with the new product owner about the product and project information. This aligns with the servant leadership role of the project manager in agile. Providing timely support helps empower the product owner and restores their authority in the team.

domande.domanda:
A government agency is overseeing the development of a new public transportation system in a major city. The project involves multiple stakeholders, including federal regulators, local authorities, and private contractors. During execution, several key decisions were delayed due to unclear authority boundaries between the project manager and functional managers.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Make joint decisions with key stakeholders.
opzioni.B: Rely on informal communication to resolve governance issues quickly.
opzioni.C: Review and reinforce the governance framework defined in the project charter.
opzioni.D: Run issues by the executive sponsor to ensure timely resolution.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Making decisions with only key stakeholders violates the principles of effective project governance, which emphasize collaboration, transparency, and shared accountability.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Informal communication may help in some cases, but relying on it exclusively undermines formal governance processes and can lead to confusion and inconsistency.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Revisiting the governance framework ensures that roles and responsibilities are clearly understood and followed. It also allows the project manager to align team actions with organizational objectives and maintain structured decision-making. This supports accountability, transparency, and control, which are central to project governance (PMBOK 8th Edition, pages 8-9).
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Escalating every issue to the executive sponsor bypasses lower-level decision-makers and creates bottlenecks. Effective governance requires clarity in delegation and escalation paths, not over-reliance on executive intervention.

domande.spiegazione: Revisiting the governance framework ensures that roles and responsibilities are clearly understood and followed. It also allows the project manager to align team actions with organizational objectives and maintain structured decision-making. This supports accountability, transparency, and control, which are central to project governance (PMBOK 8th Edition, pages 8-9).

domande.domanda:
A project manager is managing the development of a sports arena. During the final inspection phase, the professional observes that the quality of the retractable seating system does not meet the agreed-upon specifications outlined in the contract with the supplier. The supplier disputes this claim, insisting that the delivered product adheres to the agreed quality standards.
How should the project manager support their claim to the supplier?

opzioni.A: Rely on verbal agreements with the supplier regarding quality expectations.
opzioni.B: Provide documented inspection results and the agreed-upon quality specifications.
opzioni.C: Reference issues from previous projects that involved similar suppliers.
opzioni.D: Refer the supplier to the claims clause in the mutually signed contract.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Verbal agreements are not legally binding in most cases and fail to provide the solid, documented evidence needed to support a claim.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. By presenting factual evidence such as inspection reports and contractual specifications, the project manager builds a strong, objective case. This ensures the claim is based on factual, contractual evidence.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Past performance does not address the specific quality issues related to this project. It is irrelevant to the current claim.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Referencing the claims clause in the contract does not directly address the quality issue at hand. The supplier needs specific evidence, such as inspection reports and agreed-upon quality specifications, to validate the claim.

domande.spiegazione: By presenting factual evidence such as inspection reports and contractual specifications, the project manager builds a strong, objective case. This ensures the claim is based on factual, contractual evidence.

domande.domanda:
A manufacturing company is launching a project to create an innovative product. The details of the components of work packages have been defined, and constraints for each component have been identified. Top management requested a precise cost estimate of the project.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Use top-down estimating to provide an estimate based on the overall scope.
opzioni.B: Use relative estimating to compare the effort of tasks against each other based on complexity.
opzioni.C: Perform bottom-up estimating based on the detailed work packages.
opzioni.D: Use analogous estimating based on costs from a previous similar project.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Top-down estimating is less accurate and is used early in the project when details are limited. It would not satisfy top management's request for a precise estimate.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Relative estimating (e.g., story points or T-shirt sizing) is often used in Agile projects where tasks are compared to each other rather than assigned fixed values. While it helps with prioritization and estimation in uncertain environments, it does not produce the precise cost estimates required by top management in this case.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. The Bottom-up estimation technique is used when project requirements are decomposed into small, feasible work elements, which are then aggregated to estimate the cost of the entire project. The Bottom-up technique can be used to provide a precise estimate of both the project cost and duration (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 149).
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Analogous estimating relies on historical comparisons and is quick but imprecise, especially inappropriate when accurate and detailed breakdowns already exist (PMBOK 8th Edition, pages 146-147).

domande.spiegazione: The Bottom-up estimation technique is used when project requirements are decomposed into small, feasible work elements, which are then aggregated to estimate the cost of the entire project. The Bottom-up technique can be used to provide a precise estimate of both the project cost and duration (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 149).

domande.domanda:
A software team spanning 3 different countries struggles with missed deadlines. One team is reluctant to say "no", the second team frequently changes priorities, and the third team insists on perfect details before starting work.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Standardize all workflows to the third team’s approach for quality.
opzioni.B: Host cross-cultural workshops to align on behavioral norms.
opzioni.C: Extend all deadlines to accommodate cultural differences.
opzioni.D: Assign tasks only within time zones to minimize friction.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Standardizing all workflows to the third team’s approach for quality suppresses the different perspectives that make global teams valuable, makes other teams feel micromanaged and/or pressured, and violates flexibility to customize organizational frameworks.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Cross-cultural workshops help address these challenges. They focus on skill development and provide tools to navigate different work styles and the lack of in-person interaction. They also help teams create agreements and set behavioral parameters. For example, they define how to politely say "no," what level of flexibility is appropriate, and how much detail is truly needed to start work.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Extending all deadlines doesn't address root interpersonal skills gaps, reduces efficiency contrary to effective and constructive goals, rewards inefficiency rather than teaching cultural navigation, and could frustrate high performers who adapt quickly.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Assigning tasks only within time zones to minimize friction prevents knowledge of organizational structures across regions, leads to missed opportunities for 24-hour productivity in global teams, and encourages an "us vs them" mentality contrary to unity in shared objectives.

domande.spiegazione: Cross-cultural workshops help address these challenges. They focus on skill development and provide tools to navigate different work styles and the lack of in-person interaction. They also help teams create agreements and set behavioral parameters. For example, they define how to politely say "no," what level of flexibility is appropriate, and how much detail is truly needed to start work.

domande.domanda:
A construction company is building a new eco-friendly office complex. The project aims to achieve the Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED) certification by incorporating sustainable materials and energy-efficient designs. However, during execution, the project manager realizes that some subcontractors are using materials that do not meet the required sustainability standards. This could delay the certification process and affect the project’s overall success.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Proceed with the current materials and focus on completing the project on time.
opzioni.B: Replace the non-compliant materials immediately, even if it causes delays or cost overruns.
opzioni.C: Communicate with the subcontractors to understand the situation and work together to find compliant alternatives.
opzioni.D: Penalize the subcontractors for not complying with the sustainability standards.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Using non-compliant materials undermines the project’s sustainability goals and risks failing to achieve the LEED certification.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. While replacing materials is necessary, doing so without understanding the root cause may lead to further issues. The project manager should focus on collaboration and problem-solving rather than taking immediate action.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Communicating with subcontractors to understand the situation and finding compliant alternatives demonstrates a proactive and collaborative approach to dealing with the issue. This ensures alignment with sustainability goals and fosters better relationships with stakeholders.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Penalizing the subcontractors for not complying with the sustainability standards does not address the root cause of the issue. The project manager must take responsibility for managing risks and ensuring compliance throughout the project lifecycle.

domande.spiegazione: Communicating with subcontractors to understand the situation and finding compliant alternatives demonstrates a proactive and collaborative approach to dealing with the issue. This ensures alignment with sustainability goals and fosters better relationships with stakeholders.

domande.domanda:
A project manager identified a risk that has a very low occurrence probability, but if it does occur, it can have a severe impact on the project. In the past, the project manager accepted this kind of risk, but this time, the project manager followed the organization's culture and planned to hedge the risk.
The risk attitude of the project manager’s organization is best known as?

opzioni.A: Risk seeker
opzioni.B: Risk averse
opzioni.C: Risk neutral
opzioni.D: Risk mitigator

domande.spiegazione: Averse means opposing. A risk-averse organization is not very supportive or creative towards risks. Such organizations usually try to avoid risks unless there is a good reason to accept them.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is leading a software development project. During sprint 3, he notices that one team member consistently dominates stand-up meetings, frequently interrupting others, steering discussions toward their own ideas, and discouraging input from quieter members. As a result, collaboration suffers, task progress slows, and team morale declines.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Set up a confidential channel for team members to share their views anonymously on how meetings are being run.
opzioni.B: Assign the team member tasks that require less involvement from other team members to reduce their domination in group discussions.
opzioni.C: Transition to asynchronous communication using daily reports to minimize verbal dominance in meetings and ensure active participation of all members.
opzioni.D: Schedule a one-on-one discussion with the team member to address how their conduct during daily standups.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. While feedback is valuable, it avoids direct action. It may delay resolution and could lead to passive-aggressive communication. The project manager should address the issue directly rather than collecting anonymous feedback.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Assigning the team member tasks that require less involvement from other team members is punitive and avoids addressing the root cause. It may damage the team member’s confidence and create resentment. The goal is not to isolate, but to improve behavior.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Transitioning to asynchronous communication may reduce dominance, but it undermines face-to-face interaction and collaborative problem-solving. It also avoids fixing the behavior, which may persist in other contexts.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. By having a private conversation, the project manager avoids public confrontation, encourages self-awareness, and fosters accountability and improvement. This is the best approach because it promotes respectful, focused dialogue, allows the project manager to communicate the impact of this behavior, and supports psychological safety and team cohesion.

domande.spiegazione: By having a private conversation, the project manager avoids public confrontation, encourages self-awareness, and fosters accountability and improvement. This is the best approach because it promotes respectful, focused dialogue, allows the project manager to communicate the impact of this behavior, and supports psychological safety and team cohesion.

domande.domanda:
A project manager is leading a critical technology implementation project. During execution, extensive and unforeseen changes to the project scope have caused significant delays. These changes were identified during the project’s initial risk assessment but were not fully anticipated in terms of magnitude or impact. The team now proposes requesting an extension from key stakeholders due to the delays.
What should the project manager do next?

opzioni.A: Review the current schedule with the team to assess how the scope changes have affected progress and identify potential recovery paths.
opzioni.B: Verify that all scope modifications have been documented and their effects on cost, schedule, and resources have been evaluated.
opzioni.C: Adjust the project timeline to accommodate the additional work required by the scope changes.
opzioni.D: Initiate discussions with stakeholders to renegotiate deliverables and deadlines based on the new realities.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. While reviewing the timeline is important, it comes after ensuring that all changes are properly tracked. Without a clear record of what changed and why, any reevaluation lacks foundation.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. By confirming that changes are logged and assessed, the project manager ensures that decisions are data-driven, risks are understood and managed, and stakeholders can make informed decisions. This is the best next step because it ensures traceability and accountability, it supports transparency and integrated change control, and it provides a solid basis for future actions and stakeholder negotiations.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Adjusting the project timeline assumes the delay is acceptable. Extending the schedule without formal approval risks scope creep and stakeholder dissatisfaction. This action should come after documentation and stakeholder engagement.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. The project manager must first ensure that changes are documented and assessed before negotiating with stakeholders.

domande.spiegazione: By confirming that changes are logged and assessed, the project manager ensures that decisions are data-driven, risks are understood and managed, and stakeholders can make informed decisions. This is the best next step because it ensures traceability and accountability, it supports transparency and integrated change control, and it provides a solid basis for future actions and stakeholder negotiations.

domande.domanda:
On a project to upgrade airport security systems, a technical issue arises during the installation of the biometric gates. The project manager mentions that a similar issue occurred in a previous airport project and was successfully resolved. However, the current team doesn't have access to that project’s lessons learned register. Therefore, one team member proposes a new solution.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Grant the team access to the lessons learned register to evaluate the past resolution.
opzioni.B: Apply the newly proposed solution immediately to gain time.
opzioni.C: Organize a root cause analysis to decide on the best way to resolve the issue.
opzioni.D: Create a workaround to resolve the issue and document it for future projects.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. The project manager should grant the team access to the previous project’s lessons learned register to evaluate the past resolution. Accessing historical lessons learned helps avoid reinventing the wheel and wasting time.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Immediately implementing a new solution without evaluating a proven past resolution may introduce unnecessary risk or rework.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. While root cause analysis is useful, the issue is already known to have occurred and been resolved in a past project. Reviewing past lessons is more efficient in this context than repeating the analysis.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Creating a workaround skips validation of a known solution. This may lead to rework or suboptimal results, and does not align with leveraging historical knowledge first.

domande.spiegazione: The project manager should grant the team access to the previous project’s lessons learned register to evaluate the past resolution. Accessing historical lessons learned helps avoid reinventing the wheel and wasting time.

domande.domanda:
On a project to implement a contactless payment system for municipal parking, the project manager notices that a developer consistently arrives late to the daily standup meetings. This delay frustrates the rest of the agile team and disrupts their cadence.
What should the project manager do first?

opzioni.A: Remind the team member of the team’s ground rules during the next standup.
opzioni.B: Remind the entire team of the agreed-upon ground rules during the next standup.
opzioni.C: Facilitate a discussion to consider changing the standup meeting time to better accommodate all team members.
opzioni.D: Ask the team member to submit written status updates on days they can’t join the standup on time.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Addressing the team member during the standup and not privately may appear to single them out and could affect them.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. The project manager should start by reminding the entire team of the agreed-upon ground rules during the next standup. This reinforces shared ownership and team norms without targeting any individual.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Adapting the schedule for one member without clear justification may create unnecessary changes and disrupt the team’s rhythm. Before considering a schedule change, it's important to confirm whether the issue is systemic or isolated.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Asking the team member to provide written updates bypasses the collaborative purpose of the daily standup. It may also set a precedent for skipping meetings, which weakens team communication and cohesion.

domande.spiegazione: The project manager should start by reminding the entire team of the agreed-upon ground rules during the next standup. This reinforces shared ownership and team norms without targeting any individual.

domande.domanda:
A new developer joins the team during the second sprint and suggests using a different testing method. However, the rest of the team is resistant to the idea.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Instruct the new team member to focus solely on development tasks.
opzioni.B: Guide the new team member to use the project’s existing testing process.
opzioni.C: Set up a meeting with the new team member to understand the proposed testing method.
opzioni.D: Tell the new team member to follow the established testing method for now.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Instructing the new team member to focus solely on development tasks limits team collaboration and discourages initiative. Agile encourages cross-functionality and openness to new ideas, especially when they may improve team performance.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. While it maintains consistency, guiding the new team member to use the project’s existing testing process discourages innovation without first understanding the potential value of the proposed method.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Correct. Setting up a meeting with the new team member to understand the proposed testing method demonstrates the servant leader mindset: listening, learning, and evaluating ideas before making decisions. It encourages and supports continuous improvement.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Telling the new team member to follow the established testing method for now may maintain stability, but it misses the opportunity to improve the process and doesn’t address the root cause of the resistance.

domande.spiegazione: Setting up a meeting with the new team member to understand the proposed testing method demonstrates the servant leader mindset: listening, learning, and evaluating ideas before making decisions. It encourages and supports continuous improvement.

domande.domanda:
During the construction of a state-of-the-art aquarium complex, the lead marine biologist consultant, who has been integral to designing water filtration systems and marine habitat layouts, announces their departure due to personal reasons. This poses a potential risk to the project's specialized design and installation phases. Although the client has praised the project's progress so far, the departure of this expert could disrupt critical tasks.
What should the project manager do to mitigate the impact of this key resource's departure?

opzioni.A: Notify the client of the departure and adjust timelines accordingly.
opzioni.B: Allocate additional funds to hire another marine biologist consultant immediately.
opzioni.C: Offer a contract extension or additional incentives to retain the consultant.
opzioni.D: Establish a transition plan to ensure knowledge-sharing.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Informing the client about internal team changes does not actively mitigate the impact of the resource leaving.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Allocating a budget without ensuring knowledge transfer does not address the immediate risk of lost expertise.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Attempting to retain the resource is not always feasible, especially if the individual is leaving for personal reasons or a better opportunity.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Correct. This approach minimizes the risk of losing critical knowledge by ensuring that the departing structural engineer transfers their expertise to other team members. It ensures continuity and reduces potential disruptions to the project (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 26).

domande.spiegazione: This approach minimizes the risk of losing critical knowledge by ensuring that the departing structural engineer transfers their expertise to other team members. It ensures continuity and reduces potential disruptions to the project (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 26).

domande.domanda:
During the daily standup, a developer mentions that they must take unplanned leave for a few days and won’t be able to complete a backlog item. This item is essential for a feature that users expect in the upcoming sprint review.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Collaborate with the product owner to reprioritize the sprint backlog.
opzioni.B: Coordinate with the product owner to notify users about the feature delay.
opzioni.C: Assign a temporary replacement.
opzioni.D: Request the developer to delay their leave until the task is completed.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. In Agile, unexpected changes (like team availability) should be addressed through collaboration and flexibility. The product owner owns the backlog, so working together to reprioritize items helps the team adjust to the change while staying focused on delivering value.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. Informing users is reactive and doesn’t address the current sprint planning. The first step should be to see if the work can be adjusted before committing to a delay.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Agile teams are self-organizing and cross-functional. Bringing in someone from outside disrupts team cohesion and doesn’t align with Agile principles unless it’s a last resort agreed on by the team.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Requesting the developer to delay their leave until the task is completed is not a respectful or sustainable solution. Agile promotes individual well-being and team adaptability. The right approach is to adapt the plan, not push personal boundaries.

domande.spiegazione: In Agile, unexpected changes (like team availability) should be addressed through collaboration and flexibility. The product owner owns the backlog, so working together to reprioritize items helps the team adjust to the change while staying focused on delivering value.

domande.domanda:
During a predictive project to automate inventory management for a regional warehouse, two senior developers disagree over the best way to integrate a barcode scanner module. After several heated exchanges, the debate turns personal, and progress stalls.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Decide on the integration approach so the dispute does not escalate further.
opzioni.B: Facilitate a structured discussion to reach a solution.
opzioni.C: Split the work so each developer implements their own version.
opzioni.D: Focus the team on other tasks until tempers cool.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Incorrect. Deciding on the integration approach means using the Forcing/Directing conflict resolution technique; by imposing a decision, the PM may achieve a quick fix but risks resentment, lowers morale, and doesn’t resolve underlying issues; personal tension could resurface.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Correct. Facilitating a structured discussion to help both developers openly share their reasoning and reach a mutually beneficial solution. Collaborating/Problem‑solving encourages open dialogue, addresses root causes, and produces a win‑win outcome (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 157).
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Splitting the work so each developer implements their own version is a compromise; each side gives something up, but duplicating effort wastes resources and still may not address the personal rift.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Downplaying the conflict by focusing the team on other tasks until tempers cool presents the use of the Smoothing/Withdrawing conflict resolution technique; by doing this, the PM avoids confrontation temporarily, underlying disagreement and personal animosity remain, risking future breakdowns.

domande.spiegazione: Facilitating a structured discussion to help both developers openly share their reasoning and reach a mutually beneficial solution. Collaborating/Problem‑solving encourages open dialogue, addresses root causes, and produces a win‑win outcome (PMBOK 8th Edition, page 157).
domande.nota: Opzione C ricostruita: nell'esportazione il testo dell'opzione era sostituito dalla sua spiegazione.

domande.domanda:
On a smart water metering project, a key stakeholder frequently becomes temperamental and disruptive during team meetings, making team members uncomfortable and less willing to speak up. The project manager wants to maintain a healthy team environment and ensure effective stakeholder collaboration.
What should the project manager do?

opzioni.A: Provide the team with emotional intelligence training.
opzioni.B: Encourage the team to work on their conflict resolution skills so they can handle stakeholder confrontations.
opzioni.C: Provide the team with agility training to help them adapt to the evolving stakeholder needs.
opzioni.D: Meet privately with the stakeholder to address their behavior and its impact on the project.

spiegazioni_opzioni.A: Correct. The project manager should provide the team with emotional intelligence training to help them manage interactions with difficult stakeholders. Emotional intelligence training improves the team's ability to manage emotions, stay calm under pressure, and engage constructively with temperamental stakeholders (PMBOK 8th Edition, pages 169-170). This aligns with the emphasis on interpersonal skills and emotional intelligence in stakeholder engagement.
spiegazioni_opzioni.B: Incorrect. While conflict resolution skills are useful, the issue here is rooted in emotional reactions and communication, not necessarily structured conflicts. Emotional intelligence training is a more proactive and targeted response.
spiegazioni_opzioni.C: Incorrect. Agility training focuses on adaptive planning and iterative delivery, not interpersonal challenges or emotional management.
spiegazioni_opzioni.D: Incorrect. Direct confrontation with a stakeholder can risk damaging the relationship, especially if done prematurely or without a broader stakeholder engagement plan. It also appears to assign blame, which contradicts the collaborative and facilitative approach for managing stakeholders.

domande.spiegazione: The project manager should provide the team with emotional intelligence training to help them manage interactions with difficult stakeholders. Emotional intelligence training improves the team's ability to manage emotions, stay calm under pressure, and engage constructively with temperamental stakeholders (PMBOK 8th Edition, pages 169-170).
